title: Self character model never loads: LookComp churn starves dispatch_look_driven_models, cyan placeholder orb rides the player
description:
The player's own character renders as the cyan self_pc placeholder orb (scene.rs:149) with no model at all, for the whole session. Reproduced on a clean GM char (Verilamp, San d'Oria) against the local LSB stack at HEAD+working tree, and observed by the user on a remote server (char Oldman, zone 248).

Not a load failure and not the kick-time drop: across 3 runs there are zero 'ffxi actor load failed' lines, and dispatch_look_driven_models never emits a LoadActorRequest for self at all (18 dispatches per zone-in, none for self).

Mechanism, proven with temporary probes:
- The wire snapshot's self entity carries look = None, so sync_entity_looks_system (scene.rs:662-663) hits the (None, Some) arm and REMOVES self's LookComp. A probe on that arm fired 16 times, for entity 17455719 (self) and no other entity.
- ensure_self_lookcomp_system (scene.rs:634-640) re-seeds it from the launcher-time SelfAppearance because it is absent.
- The two fight every dirty frame: 54 of 56 'look changed for entity' debug lines are self; every other entity changes exactly once.
- dispatch_look_driven_models (look_resolver.rs:659, registered in the dat_mmb chain) is scheduled in the gap and never observes self with a LookComp. A probe placed at its dedup check never fired for self.
- With no LoadActorRequest, poll_load_actor_tasks never runs the remove::<Mesh3d>() at ffxi_actor_render.rs:2453-2456, so the resting placeholder ball is never consumed.

Regression: the same character in the same zone rendered its model correctly on 2026-08-05 (artifacts/verify/morph-ball-fix.png, captured at cc5d1fe). Prime suspect is 0bda240 'Tag the player as self even when their entity arrives first', the only later commit touching self identity in this system: it inserts IsSelf on the sync_entities_system UPDATE arm, which switches ensure_self_lookcomp_system on for self and creates the churn. Not yet bisected.

The deeper defect underneath is that self's entity in the wire snapshot has look = None at all; the ordering fight is only what makes it fatal.
design:
Two independent fixes, both probably wanted:
1. Stop the churn. Either do not remove LookComp on a (None, Some) transition (a look that stops being reported is not a look that changed), or exempt self from the removal arm, or have ensure_self_lookcomp_system and sync_entity_looks_system agree on a single owner for self.
2. Make self's snapshot look non-None so the server-driven path owns it like every other PC (wire_translate.rs:634 maps e.look; find why the session's self entity drops it on pos-only updates).

Guard test candidate: a Bevy-schedule test asserting that an entity whose wire look goes None keeps a LookComp visible to dispatch_look_driven_models, i.e. that a self entity present for N frames produces exactly one LoadActorRequest.
acceptance_criteria: Zone in on the local stack as any character; the self model renders and no cyan orb remains attached. Log shows exactly one 'actor dispatch (pc)' for the self entity id and zero removals of self's LookComp.
notes:
2026-08-07: FIXED the fatal half in 8e4c4bc (sync_entity_looks_system no longer clears LookComp when the wire look goes None) + guard test scene::tests::look_going_none_keeps_the_last_known_lookcomp, which fails against the old arm. Verified live: artifacts/verify/orb-fixed.png shows the model, self dispatch fires.

STILL OPEN, and why this stays open rather than closing: self's entity in the wire snapshot still reports look = None on pos-only updates (only self does). That is the upstream defect -- find why the session's self entity drops it (wire_translate.rs:634 maps e.look straight through) and make self's look as stable as every other PC's. Until then the launcher-seeded appearance is what renders when the server look is absent, so a gear change made before the server re-sends CHAR_PC for self may not show.
2026-08-11 VERIFIED LIVE (local LSB, GUI zone 103, artifacts/verify/session-2026-08-11.log): exactly one 'actor dispatch (pc): entity_id=17455719' for self, zero LookComp removals, zero self_pc placeholder lines. The upstream defect is closed: self's look no longer comes from the launcher seed but from the two packets that actually carry it (0x00A GrapIDTbl, 0x051 GRAP_LIST) -- LSB skips the owning char in every entity broadcast, so a 0x00D for self never arrives. The feared double-dispatch (launcher seed then server look) did not occur.
close_reason: Closed

title: Event VM: 56 opcodes are neither implemented nor safely skippable — every cutscene using one is auto-released
description:
56 of 216 event opcodes hit `StepResult::Unimplemented` (ffxi-event/src/vm.rs:53-75, :342-349), which makes kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:1620-1638 auto-release the **entire** cutscene with a "not yet supported" line.

The set includes the load-bearing ones: 0x7F (dialog-select wait), 0x63 (play-anim-and-wait), 0x26 / 0x58 (yield), 0x53-0x55 (scheduler waits).

EVIDENCE: research/XiEvents/OpCodes/*.md — disassembly-grounded (tier 2). The 56-opcode diff was scripted against ffxi-event/src/opcode_meta.rs.
notes:
2026-08-05: four opcodes landed (501b706), driven by the chocobo rental rather
than by working the 56 as a list.

Method worth reusing: ffxi-event/examples/zz-event-drive.rs runs one event
offline and prints where it stops -- no live session needed. Upper Jeuno
rental is zone 244 event 10003 (vendor/server .../Upper_Jeuno/npcs/Couvoullie.lua,
startEvent(eventSucceed, price, currency, lowLevel)).

Implemented, all as retail's own actors-not-resolved early exit, the same
shape the LOADEXTSCHEDULER pair already used:
  0x53 WAITSCHEDULOR, 0x54 WAITMAPSCHEDULOR, 0x55 WAITLOADSCHEDULER
  0x7E CHOCOBO -- variable width from its case byte (6/8/16/18), added to
       opcode_meta::sub_size. Cases 3 and 6 carry PopulateCustomProperties,
       which is where retail reads the chocobo's colour (vals[0] = colour+32);
       relevant to kuluu-6wf.1's hardcoded yellow.

Also found and fixed a latent hang, not a stop: EventVm::step looped without
bound, so a script whose loop condition this VM cannot move spun the thread
forever. Now budgeted (OPCODE_BUDGET_PER_STEP) and reported as Unimplemented.
The corpus sweep found this by hanging on it.

Corpus baseline for the next person, from ffxi-event/examples/zz-event-sweep.rs
(all zones, every event): 51078 end, 11381 stop, 5 run past end. Top remaining
blockers by frequency: 0x80 (2584), 0x76 (1387), 0x3E (1178), 0xB6 (922),
0x47 (796), 0x9D (734), 0x75 (697), 0x6E (651), 0x6C (485), 0x34 (345).
Work that list top-down and re-run the sweep to measure.
2026-08-11: 25 opcodes implemented (f833e33) + the input-poll correction (a512f1c). Sweep: ended 51078 -> 60598, stopped 11381 -> 1530. Method that worked: work research/XiEvents/OpCodes pseudo-code BODIES (never the header 'OpCode Size' row) by corpus frequency, re-running zz-event-sweep to measure. Corrected two wrong fixed sizes (0x71 10 -> 16, 0x9D 0 -> 23) and added 14 sub-byte dispatched families to sub_size. Note the 1530 conflates refusals with budget exhaustion: ~800 are already-implemented opcodes the VM spun on (0x0B, 0x15, 0x01, 0x02, 0x1C). STILL OPEN: ~31 of the original 56 remain, 0x26 among the bead's own load-bearing set is still unimplemented, and 0x9D is the largest genuine refusal at ~366. Two spin-offs filed: the input-wait host surface, and the 5 -> 33 ran-past-end regression.

2026-08-27: CORRECTED BASELINE + the work-slot arithmetic family (kuluu-cjct).

The earlier "top blockers by frequency" list in these notes was measured off an
oracle that conflated two failure modes, and it named the wrong work.
StepResult::Unimplemented was returned both for a genuine refusal AND for
OPCODE_BUDGET_PER_STEP exhaustion, where the reported opcode is merely whatever
the VM sat on when a loop burned 100k opcodes. Split into Unimplemented vs Spun;
host behaviour unchanged (both -> DialogStep::Stopped).

Under the split, this note's claim that "0x9D is the largest genuine refusal at
~366" is FALSE: all 357 of 0x9D's appearances were spins. So were 0x0B (370),
0x15 (196), 0x02 (84), 0x01 (81), 0x3C (54). Genuine refusals totalled 273, not
1469 -- the opcode backlog was ~5x smaller than recorded, and the real mass was
looping, not refusing.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE LOOPING: the work-slot arithmetic family (0x05-0x19, 0x3C) was
only being SKIPPED BY WIDTH. 0x0B is work[1] += 1 -- a loop counter. Advancing
past it without applying it is exactly what turns an authored for-loop into a
spin. Implemented the family against the research/XiEvents/OpCodes pseudo-code
bodies: 0x05/0x06 set 1/0, 0x07/0x08 add/sub, 0x09/0x0A bit set/clear, 0x0B/0x0C
inc/dec, 0x0D/0x0E/0x0F and/or/xor, 0x10/0x11 shl/shr, 0x14/0x15 mul/div, 0x19
swap, 0x3C bit-array set. All wrapping (retail is C++ int on x86; a panicking
client is worse than a wrong scene). setworkofs grew the shift parameter 0x3C
needs.

MEASURED A/B, both arms under the identical harness policy:
                  before   after
  ended           60598    60687
  cancelled         838     1819
  refused           273      393
  spun             1196       38
  step-limited      132      100
Non-terminating events 1328 -> 138, a 90% cut. "refused" RISES because events
that used to spin now progress far enough to reach a real refusal; "cancelled"
rises because menu loops now iterate properly and take the harness's back-out
path.

HARNESS FIX in the same pass: the sweep answered every menu with option 0
forever, so any shop whose option 0 is "browse again" scored as non-terminating
-- 1325 events. It now backs out after MENU_REVISITS_BEFORE_CANCEL visits to the
same message id, the way a player would.

CORRECTED WORK LIST (genuine refusals, by corpus frequency):
  0x71 94, 0xD4 82, 0xCE 60, 0xFF 27, 0xA7 19, 0x31 16, 0xA0 15, 0x26 13,
  0x5A 11, 0xF0 8, 0xBC 7, 0xF8 6, 0x82 5, 0xC6 4, 0x8C 3, 0x9B 3.
0x71 is the largest and is the player-input poll -- blocked on kuluu-dmkp's host
input surface, not on decoding. Remaining non-terminating: 38 spun, 100
step-limited (58 looping on message, 42 on wait).

NOT DONE HERE: 0x12/0x13 (rand) -- see kuluu-q602.

2026-09-09 transport fix (kuluu-fldn / kuluu-919z): identical before/after zz-event-sweep results: ended 60,687 (42 past-end), cancelled 1,819, refused 393, spun 38, step-limited 100. This harness supplies empty parameters and no scene context, so this comparison only guards that existing mode; it does not establish real server-parameter or actor-scene behavior. Separate installed-DAT tests drive funded/unfunded Lucia, Mhaura Felisa, and Port Jeuno Zedduva through attached scene context. Evidence: artifacts/verify/transport/sweep-before.txt and sweep-after.txt.

title: markers.json: one failed read wipes every character's saved map markers
description:
Found by 4 independent review agents in the v0.3.0..v0.4.0 post-release review.

marker_store.rs:56 — save_for() rebuilds the ENTIRE file from load_all().unwrap_or_default(), so any read/parse error turns the atomic tmp+rename into 'file = this character only'; all other characters' sections are silently dropped.

It self-escalates: marker_store.rs:95-105, on load error sync_markers() does markers.by_zone.clear() but still sets loaded_for = Some(id). The clear() trips Bevy change detection, so the NEXT frame takes the markers.is_changed() save branch and persists the empty set. Corruption becomes permanent loss with no user action.

Trigger is mundane: MarkerFile is a bare HashMap with no schema version (marker_store.rs:12), so adding a MapMarker field without a serde default is an unparseable file. A transient EACCES/EINTR does it too. Only trace is one tracing::warn! the player never sees.

Fix: replace loaded_for: Option<u32> with a three-state enum (Idle | Loaded(u32) | Failed(u32)) so a failed load can never permit a save; propagate the error out of save_for instead of unwrap_or_default(); refuse to write when the existing file can't be read. Add a schema version to MarkerFile.
acceptance_criteria: A corrupt/unparseable markers.json leaves existing on-disk markers untouched; a test asserts save_for does not drop other characters' sections when load_all fails.
close_reason: Every element of the proposed fix landed in commit 9ebf75e (2026-07-30), two days after the bead was filed: three-state MarkerLoad enum, save_for propagating the load error instead of unwrap_or_default, a schema version on MarkerFile, and the exact acceptance-criteria test by name.

title: BATTLE2 cmd_arg for MagicStart is the routine FourCC, not a spell id — cast routine + interrupt both misread
description:
CONFIRMED against LSB source. For ActionCategory::MagicStart (8), LSB packs the cast routine's FourCC into BATTLE2 cmd_arg, NOT the spell id. The spell id is in the first target result's `param`.

vendor/server/src/map/ai/states/magic_state.cpp:101-109:
    .actiontype = ActionCategory::MagicStart,
    .actionid   = static_cast<uint32_t>(m_PSpell->getFourCC()),
    ...
    .results = {{ .param = static_cast<int32_t>(m_PSpell->getID()), ... }}
vendor/server/src/map/enums/four_cc.h:39-45: BlackMagicCast = 0x6B626163 "cabk", WhiteMagicCast "cawh",
BlueMagicCast "cabl", SongMagicCast "caso", NinjutsuMagicCast "canj", SummonMagicCast "casm",
GeomancyMagicCast "cage", TrustMagicCast "cafa". Interrupts (four_cc.h:47-54) are "spwh"/"spbk"/... and
interrupts.cpp:268-284 broadcasts them ALSO as ActionCategory::MagicStart.

CONSEQUENCE 1 — kuluu-ky8c's fix is inert on real packets. scheduler_runtime.rs dispatch_cast_routine_started
treats action_id as a spell id; SpellSuffixCache::suffix does SpellTable::lookup(action_id as u16) and
ffxi_proto::magic::cast_suffix does u16::try_from(action_id), both of which reject a 32-bit FourCC. suffix is
always None, action_routine falls back to the generic DatId "cast", and the ner1 aura never spawns.

CONSEQUENCE 2 — interrupts are misread as fresh casts. An interrupt arrives as category 8 with "spbk", so
dispatch_cast_routine_started and dispatch_action_overlay both classify it as a cast START: the looping cast
pose is re-armed for CAST_TIMEOUT_FRAMES (60s) and the aura restarts, instead of tearing down.

FIX: for action_kind 8, read cmd_arg AS the routine FourCC (it is literally the DAT routine name in ASCII, LE)
and use it directly as the DatId — no spell-DAT magicType lookup needed. Distinguish "ca*" (start) from "sp*"
(interrupt) on the prefix and route the interrupt to teardown + the sp<suffix> stop-cast clip (kuluu-u2of).
Take the spell id from the first result's param where a spell id is genuinely needed (cast bar naming).

NOTE this supersedes part of the earlier SpellSuffixCache approach: the server already hands us the exact
routine name, so deriving the suffix from ROM/118/114.DAT magicType is redundant for the ANIMATION path (it is
still needed for cast TIME). Corroborated independently by research/XiPackets/world/server/0x0028/README.md:148-157.

TENSION TO RESOLVE LIVE: a live session on 2026-07-24 showed the Poison cast animation looking correct, which
this analysis says should have fallen back to the generic "cast" routine. Verify on the LSB dev stack what
cmd_arg actually arrives as before assuming either story.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped in v0.4.0 (commits 104d3ea/a867f9b). Independently re-verified in the v0.3.0..v0.4.0 protocol-conformance review against vendor/server @ c39004ce: magic_state.cpp:102 .actionid = getFourCC() and :109 .param = getID() confirm the premise; CSpell::getFourCC (spell.cpp:412-437) returns only ca**/sp** for all eight groups; interrupts.cpp:272/311/352 reuse ActionCategory::MagicStart with getFourCC(true) -> sp*, so the prefix-based interrupt discriminator matches LSB's encoding exactly. All three Rust call sites (session.rs:1698, ffxi_actor_render.rs:2277, scheduler_runtime.rs:875/882) gate on CATEGORY_MAGIC_START before calling magic_start_routine, so the non-magic ca/sp FourCCs (cate/spte/cait/spit/calg/splg) cannot collide. Residual nits filed as kuluu-4vqu (item 9: precondition enforced only by caller discipline) and kuluu-7rmt (citation line drift in magic.rs:36-40,84).

title: Bevy 0.19: shadow rendering ~6x more expensive at 4096/3-cascade (60->10fps); +96-step vol fog stacks to 7fps
description: Live GUI smoke on branch bevy-0.19 (Bastok Mines, char Bevyprobe, local LSB): steady-state ~7fps after all asset churn settled (churn img+0 mesh+0 zone+0 skin+0). perf_hud breakdown: CPU baseline 8.4ms (fine) and every named CPU render span sub-ms (early prepass ~0.4ms, main_opaque_pass_3d ~0.2ms, clustering ~0.1ms), yet rprep ~80ms + rgraph ~60ms ~= rtotal ~140ms. rprep includes swapchain acquire, rgraph is encode+submit+present; the ~0ms remainder rules out bevy_framepace sleep capping frames. => render thread is GPU-present-bound, not our CPU code. Consistent with upstream Apple-Silicon 0.19 regression bevy#24448 (flagged in migration plan risk register). Rendering itself is CORRECT (zone textured, skinned actor posed) — this is perf only. Definitive A/B vs 0.18 needs main to build (currently red: FfxiLightingUniform time_params, fixed only on branch). Evidence log: /tmp/bevyprobe-gui.log. Relates to pre-existing kuluu-xf8 (periodic ~70ms GPU spikes) which this makes constant.
notes:
ROOT-CAUSE LOCALIZED via feature-toggle matrix on 0.19 branch (Bastok Mines, Bevyprobe). Earlier 60->7fps A/B was CONFOUNDED: vol-fog commit 32d6710 is branch-only (absent on main), so I'd compared 0.18-no-fog vs 0.19-with-fog. De-confounded matrix (all same zone/char/camera, exclusive GPU):
  0.19 minimal (fog off, shadow 512, bloom 0):        60fps, rtotal ~5-8ms
  0.19 shadow 4096 only (fog off, bloom 0):           ~10fps, rtotal ~95ms
  0.19 fog off (shadow 4096 + bloom 0.12):            ~10fps, rtotal ~95ms
  0.19 full (fog 96-step ON + shadow 4096 + bloom):   ~7fps, rtotal ~140ms
  0.18 full config (shadow 4096, fog code ABSENT):    60fps, rtotal ~10ms
CONCLUSIONS: (1) NOT a flat upstream 0.19 GPU wall — 0.19 minimal = 60fps identical to 0.18. bevy#24448 likely NOT the cause. (2) SHADOWS are the dominant regression: shadow_map_size 4096 / 3 cascades / 200u ran 60fps on 0.18 but ~10fps on 0.19 => Bevy 0.19 made 4096 shadow rendering ~6x more expensive (~50ms/frame). Shrinking to 512 restores 60fps. Prime suspects: 0.19 shadow-cascade/PCF changes, or our migration's shadow rewiring (shadows_enabled->shadow_maps_enabled, fetch_directional_shadow frag_coord_xy signature). Relates to kuluu-xf8 (shadow cascades already suspected). (3) The 96-step volumetric_fog (branch-only feature 32d6710, actively being tuned in weather.rs) adds ~45ms/frame on top (10->7fps) — separate, feature-cost, not a 0.19 bug; consider lowering fog_step_count. Logs: /tmp/bevyprobe-{minimal,shadow,nofog,gui}.log + /tmp/bevyprobe-018.log.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: STATUS UPDATE (audit 2026-07-31, static): two mitigations landed after this bead's last note and are still in the tree.
(1) 175bb55 (2026-07-16 23:30, i.e. after this bead's last update) forces GpuPreprocessingMode::None on macOS — kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs:295-311, FFXI_GPU_PREPROCESS=1 opts back in; the commit measured 12.8fps GPU path vs 34.3fps CPU path, resolution-independent.
(2) 43a5a50 (2026-07-17) re-enabled PipelinedRenderingPlugin by default — mod.rs:273-283; ~38fps serial -> stable 60fps at native res with vsync on.
kuluu-tjas (created 2026-07-17) records the post-fix state: 'Bastok Mines holds a stable 60fps at low settings (shadows 1024/2-cascade, AA off, native res)' and warns 'raising shadows/AA/cascades will re-cap below 60'.

CONSEQUENCE for this bead's CONCLUSIONS: the regression those fixes attribute is GPU-driven mesh preprocessing, not shadow-pass cost. This bead's '0.19 made 4096 shadow rendering ~6x more expensive' conclusion was measured BEFORE preprocessing was forced off and has not been re-measured since — it is neither confirmed nor retracted. The open question is now narrow: with preprocessing forced to CPU and pipelining on, does shadow_map_size 4096 with 4 cascades still cost ~50ms/frame? Re-run the same toggle matrix on today's main to answer it. The vendored shadow-pass GPU spans needed for that measurement are still in place (vendor/bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs:2836-2865, 'KULUU PATCH').

Also note: the cited runtime config '4096 / 3 cascades / 200u' matches NO preset in the tree — Low is 1024/2/200, Medium 2048/3/300, High 4096/4/700, Ultra 4096/4/1100 (kuluu-render/src/graphics/settings.rs:488-589), and High has been 4096/4/700 since before this bead (ed50499, 2026-07-15). Whatever supplied that combination (a persisted graphics.json or in-GUI toggling) is not recorded, so any re-run must state the exact config it used.

The two blockers this bead recorded are both stale: 32d6710 (vol fog) is an ancestor of HEAD, not branch-only, and main builds on Bevy 0.19 (Cargo.toml:95).

P0 may be over-priority now that 60fps is reported at low settings; consider P1 pending the shadow re-measure at the shipping preset.

title: c2s datagram seq-window violation silently deafened sessions (Horizon MH dead interactions, fresh-char c2s ignored)
description: Two independent counters (sub_seq/bundle_seq) violated the LSB dispatch window (vendor/server/src/map/map_networking.cpp:419-428): a subpacket is dispatched only when client_packet_id < sync <= datagram header, so after the second multi-subpacket bundle every c2s was silently skipped while the session looked healthy. 7dac9be's SendResRdy keepalive piggyback triggered it on every zone-in — on HorizonXI all MH interactions (Moogle talk, /logout, /mhexit, door exit) went dead. Fix: header = last subpacket sync (session.rs::datagram_header_id), single counter, guard test modeling the server window. Companion fix: zone-in cutscenes ride 0x00A LOGIN (EventPara@0x60, presence = PosHead.server_status==4) and must be answered with 0x05B End or the char sticks InEvent (0x05E/0x0E7 rejected) and the CS re-fires every relog — decode::ZoneInEvent + begin_server_event routing. Verified live on local LSB: fresh char completes intro CS 503 + MH expo CS 30000, enters MH via zmr0, Moogle spawns + Mog Menu opens (0x02E), zmrq exit works, logout in MH instant (0x00B state=1), relog clean.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e015c4; live-verified on local LSB (fresh char full MH loop)

title: Client version targeting: profile installs and route version-dependent constants through it
description: Kuluu's DAT constants, code comments, and format assumptions were verified against one install: the HorizonXI tree in vendor/game-files (a ~2023 retail client with mods, FFXiMain.dll SHA-256 f4f90fbd...). Retail moved on; the September 2026 update grew every item DAT block from 0xC00 to 0x1400 bytes. Latest retail is the primary target going forward; other client generations (HorizonXI) stay usable through the same mechanism rather than parallel code paths. Umbrella for: a ClientProfile probe in ffxi-dat (FFXiMain.dll hash + DAT-layout heuristics), named install targets under vendor/game-files/targets/<name> selected by FFXI_CLIENT_TARGET, per-generation layout enums that version-dependent parsers dispatch on, and a sweep of HXI-era assumptions onto the profile.
notes: 2026-09-10: mechanism landed. ffxi-dat/src/client_profile.rs (ClientProfile::probe, KNOWN_CLIENTS with horizonxi-2023 = vendored install, ItemBlockLayout::{Legacy,Retail2026} stride detection); DatRoot::profile(); item_dat ItemTable probes layout per file and fails closed on Retail2026; FFXI_CLIENT_TARGET + vendor/game-files/targets/<name> (cargo xtask game --target/--list, Parallels /Volumes/[C] drive detection); kuluu logs the profile at startup and warns on unknown builds; README 'Client versions' section; example dat-client-profile. No retail install on this host yet: next real step is installing/patching retail in the Parallels VM and adding its KNOWN_CLIENTS row. Children: kuluu-47cq (0x1400 decode), kuluu-t818 (assumption sweep).

title: Smooth event-scripted passenger walks across session and native render cadence
description: User recording shows Lucia admission and exit walking as short teleports. Trace event VM movement, session publication, native prediction/interpolation and animation; fix cadence without changing server-owned event coordinates or completion.
design: Event scene movement publishes at SESSION_TICK_PERIOD (100 ms), while native dispatch previously snapped each snapshot and reset movement intent to idle. CodeMOVE in research/XiEvents/OpCodes/0x001F.md establishes frame-scaled continuous motion. Native dialog movement now interpolates over the exported session cadence and derives scripted speed/gait without modifying the user walk toggle or emitting player Move packets. Event exit preserves the exact authoritative endpoint; large discontinuities, zone changes and logout clear interpolation. This buffering adds up to 100 ms visual latency; the exact retail rendering policy remains unobserved. The unchanged gait helper lives in the cross-platform combat_stance module and retains its native re-export.
acceptance_criteria: Scripted walks visibly interpolate and animate at render cadence, keep VM-authoritative terminal positions, and mandatory regressions reject stepping or stale-motion lifecycle failures.
notes: Completed and verified with Lucia admission and Catus exit. Walking leg animation is visible, and final authored coordinates are preserved. Lucia median rendered step is 0.021505 (maximum 0.025143) versus baseline maximum 0.129283; Catus median is 0.021667 (maximum 0.039724) versus baseline maximum 0.130001. Mandatory scripted_walk_render_contract uses a deterministic 60 Hz clock and checks every movement sample, animation intent, no Move emission, final position and lifecycle. Deliberate snapping and idle-animation mutations fail assertions. Affected library suites pass: kuluu 457, kuluu-render 1129 and kuluu-session 450; the ignored event contract runs explicitly in the mandatory gate. Final harness/comments/fmt/contracts/clippy/wasm and release build pass. Live proof uses final2; final3 only changes citations and relocates the unchanged gait helper. Fixture restoration and session/process cleanup are complete. Evidence: artifacts/verify/ferry-followup/summary.json, checks.json and fixed-lucia/fixed-catus motion recordings and analyses.
close_reason: Implemented, live verified, and protected by mandatory mutation-tested contracts. Final checks and release build pass; evidence and observation limits recorded in notes.

title: Honor invisible dock gate collision from retail RID data
description: User recording after 75616ab1 shows the Selbina ship cabin can be entered while dock NPC says next ship is eight Vana minutes away. Trace static hull shell, animated transport visibility, sub-area activation and collision so absent or moving vessels cannot expose a stationary enterable interior.
design: The inspected FFXiMain.dll is identified by SHA-256 f4f90fbd080c05448aab3f866b127d7c1675b3cc15c8beaa57bfc584064b7e7c, not installation date or generic file version. title: Zone-static particle generators never render in most zones: name whitelist + missing global effect-dir lookup
description:
Braziers, lanterns, chimney smoke and every other zone-static auto-run particle generator fail to render in most zones even though their sibling 0x47 point lights do (Selbina screenshot 2026-09-09: guard-shack lantern lit but no flame/glow).

Two stacked defects in kuluu-render/src/zone_particles.rs:

1. The spawner only admits generators whose chunk NAME matches fir*/fih*/sma*/smk*/smf*/kas* (or whose MMB texture reads as water). Real zones use hundreds of other directory/name vocabularies: Selbina (file 348) carries its lantern glows as t_se/effe/ligh/lt01..lt17 + lfr1..lfr8 (D3m ltcu) and its chimney smoke as t_se/effe/smok/sk00..sk10 (sheet bsmk). Corpus survey (ffxi-dat temp probe over all 298 zone DATs): 46,378 timed auto-run generators outside weat/, top directories ligh(3425) ramp(1685) ligt(953) mizu(815) hi01(764) fire(681) taki(639) ... a whitelist cannot cover them.

2. spawn_zone_particle_generator is called with global=None, so any generator whose mesh ships in the global effect dir (ROM/0/0.DAT, syst/effe/) resolves to nothing and is silently dropped. The campfire flame sheet hi12 lives ONLY there, which is why even the whitelisted fir1..fir8 in Selbina fail: the client log reads 'zone_particles: DAT 348 -> 0 zone-static particle generator(s)' beside 'zone_point_lights: DAT 348 -> 7 faithful point light(s)'. weather_particles.rs already passes the GlobalEffectDir and keys its rebuild on its arrival; zone_particles never did.

Retail policy (tier 2, research/XIClient): World/Zone/XiZone.cpp SetCurrentArea links every Generator resource in the zone container and Unlinks only those under 'taew' (weat/), which WeatherTransition.cpp ActivateWeatherGenerators activates per weather; World/Generator/CYyGenerator.cpp reads the auto-run bit from flags & 0x1000 and clears it under 'taew'. No name filter anywhere. research/xim Scene.kt registerEffectsRecursively is the same: every autoRun EffectResource under the zone root.
design: Retail policy (tier 2, research/XIClient): XiZone.cpp InitWeather unlinks only the 'taew' generators at zone load; CYyGenerator runs everything else on flags & 0x1000 (auto_run). No name filter. Life==0 singletons stay with dat_mzb (sea sheets) / zone_clouds (canopies) — see follow-up kuluu bead for the rest of that set. Dedup: byte-identical repeats keyed by (name, mesh, base position) collapse (806 same-position repeats corpus-wide, e.g. West Ronfaure effe/fir1 twice); like-named emitters at distinct positions (4,562) all run. UNVERIFIED INFERENCE: retail may draw the same-position repeats stacked; collapsing them is the low-risk reading pending a retail observation. Perf: the 0x0A section-1 emit cull (CYyGenerator::Idle 'Check distance to camera'; xim GeneratorCullUpdater) is parsed as ParticleGeneratorDef::emit_cull and applied in sync_particle_meshes from the camera eye (max 0 -> DrawDistance.world, retail XiZone::GetDrawDistance); camera-relative generators are exempt (they sit at the eye). Applied universally (actor/routine generators too), matching retail; only zone statics were measured.
acceptance_criteria: Selbina lantern shows flame (fir*) + glow (lfr*/lt*), chimney smoke (sk*) rises; client log reports >0 zone-static generators for 348; every auto-run life>0 generator outside weat/ spawns; hi12-style global-dir meshes resolve; real-DAT guard tests pin both defects; checks pass.
notes: Landed in be919d01. Evidence: Selbina (348) client log before: 'zone_particles: DAT 348 -> 0'; harness after: 41 generators, 0 unresolved; headless render at hour 22 shows fir7 flame + lfr7 glow at the shop lantern (/tmp/selbina-lamp3.png, session artefact). Corpus survey (temp probe, deleted): 298 zones, 46,378 timed auto-run non-weat generators, 18,866 life==0 singletons; 43,563 carry 0x0A (max hist peaks 20/25/30/40/50/60/80; 115 at 0; unlink bit never set). Frame time file 110 (782 emitters), vsync-floored harness: before cull 21.5 ms vs 16.7 floor; after cull 16.6. Tests: zone_particles (5, real-DAT pins for 348/200/197 + global-dir hi12), particle_gen emit_cull (2), particle_sim culled (2). Not done: live in-game confirm against the LSB stack; sub-area interior DAT generators (separate follow-up).

title: Walker falls through the world off steep bank faces (Selbina dock stairs south edge); retail's floor/wall cutoff is 45 deg, ours is 60
description: Repro (deterministic, offline): cargo build -p kuluu --example zz-field-walk --features native-window; ./target/debug/examples/zz-field-walk 248 38 -2 -6.5 51.98 3.43 1 — at tick ~120 (wire 47.14, 1.01, feet -9.79) the walker goes Airborne and free-falls forever; live it reproduced with the FFXI_STAIR_DRIVE channel (warp yaw -1.2 from !pos 38 -6.5 -2): the character is pushed back at DEPEN_MAX_PUSH (0.15/tick) while sinking through the stairs, ending 100 yalms below the zone. Geometry (zz-collision-column 248 47.141 1.013 -9.787): the south edge of the staircase is a sloped bank whose faces carry normal.y 0.35..0.6. The tread the walker stood on is a 0.596 face (a FLOOR under FLOOR_NORMAL_MIN = 0.5); one 8cm step later every support column hits only 0.43-0.50 faces (walls), so support_probe misses, step() enters Airborne, and landing_floor ignores the same wall-class faces, so nothing ever catches the fall. Retail: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Zone/Terrain/CollisionManager.cpp CollisionManager::InterpolatePosition splits candidates at |ObjectNormal.y| <= 0.708 (45 deg): steeper faces push the movement sphere out horizontally (y scaled 0.2), flatter ones set the height; the sphere query never tunnels. Two fixes: (1) FLOOR_NORMAL_MIN 0.5 -> 0.708 (cited), so the bank is a wall the sweep stands the body off from, as retail does; (2) a no-tunnel landing guard: an airborne tick whose swept band crosses an up-facing steep face at the feet column lands on it instead of passing through (down-facing faces stay excluded, kuluu-0nnl). This is very likely the 'weird sliding around going down the stairs near the boat NPCs' report.
notes:
Diagnosis (2026-09-09): FFXI_STAIR_CAPTURE + FFXI_STAIR_DRIVE live run and the offline zz-field-walk replay agree tick for tick. Straight descents at depth -4/-7/-7.6 and a camera-pan descent are clean (monotone dz at the 0.083/tick rate limit, zero lateral drift, render position == wire position). The oblique run (yaw -1.2) reaches (47.14, 1.01, feet -9.79): Poof d=-0.13, then Airborne, then depenetration pushes -0.15/tick while gravity integrates through the stairs. zz-collision-column at that footprint: centre and all four ring columns hit only faces with normal.y 0.35..0.50 (wall-class under the 0.5 cutoff); the tread just behind is a 0.596 face. Retail (CollisionManager::InterpolatePosition) puts the wall/floor split at |normal.y| <= 0.708.

Fix: dat_mzb::FLOOR_NORMAL_MIN 0.5 -> 0.708 with the citation (the bank becomes a wall the sweep stands the body off, as retail does); MzbCollisionGeometry::highest_up_facing_hit_in_slab + step.rs landing fallback so an airborne tick never passes through an up-facing steep face (down-facing stays excluded, kuluu-0nnl). Tests: live_tests face_just_past_45_degrees_blocks_like_a_wall, steep_bank_descent_never_tunnels; field test moved to 40/65 degrees (a 50 degree rise spans two sample pairs and reads as two risers). Offline replay after: oblique run slides along the bank and reaches the dock with 0 airborne ticks; straight run unchanged (ends -14.559).

title: Event VM sweep oracle conflates budget-spin with genuine opcode refusal, mis-ranking the kuluu-u7r5 work list
description:
StepResult::Unimplemented(op) is returned for two unrelated reasons: (a) a genuine refusal -- the opcode jumps/sets_ret/is invalid/has an unknown sub, so the VM has no width it may safely take (vm.rs:511,639,680,685,688,698); and (b) OPCODE_BUDGET_PER_STEP exhaustion (vm.rs:412-421), where the reported opcode is merely whatever the VM was sitting on when a loop it cannot leave burned 100k opcodes.

kuluu-u7r5's NOTES tell the next person to 'work that list top-down by corpus frequency'. That list is the sweep's stop tally, and its top entry is 0x0B (370) followed by 0x15 (196), 0x02 (84), 0x01 (81) -- all already implemented, all spins. Working the list as written starts on four opcodes that have nothing to implement.

The host behaviour for the two cases is identical (DialogStep::Stopped -> release the scene), so this is purely a diagnostic defect -- but it is a defect in the acceptance ORACLE for a P0, which is the same class of mistake as kuluu-i82r.
design: Add StepResult::Spun(u8), returned only from the budget check. runner.rs maps it to the same DialogStep::Stopped(op) as Unimplemented, so host behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. zz-event-sweep tallies the two separately and prints two ranked lists. Re-record the kuluu-u7r5 baseline from the refusal list only.
acceptance_criteria: zz-event-sweep prints separate 'refused' and 'spun' tallies; the refusal ranking contains no opcode that has an implemented arm in vm.rs; kuluu-u7r5 NOTES updated with the corrected ranking.
close_reason: Split StepResult::Spun from Unimplemented; zz-event-sweep now ranks refusals and spins separately and models a player backing out of a repeated menu. Corrected ranking recorded on kuluu-u7r5 -- the old list named 0x9D/0x0B/0x15 as top blockers and all three were spins.

title: Launcher Browse folder picker crashes the app on Windows
description: Reported on the v0.5.2 aarch64-windows build in a Parallels Win11-ARM VM: clicking Browse in the DAT-setup/Settings screens kills the client. rfd feature flags ruled out (win_cid file-dialog backend is not feature-gated; common-controls-v6 affects message dialogs only — verified in rfd 0.15.4 source). Root-cause hypothesis: the blocking rfd::FileDialog::pick_folder() runs on the winit main thread; on Windows that thread's COM apartment / message pump belongs to winit and a blocking IFileDialog there crashes (macOS is the only platform that REQUIRES the main thread; Windows is safest off-thread). Fix: run the dialog on a worker thread on Windows and join — also converts any dialog panic into a cancelled pick instead of a dead launcher. Secondary: both pickers use env HOME as the fallback start dir, which is unset in plain PowerShell launches — use dirs::home_dir(). Exact crash message still uncapture d (run from PowerShell with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 and click Browse to confirm the panic once a fixed build is in hand). Related observation, separate issue: under Parallels, wgpu selects Microsoft Basic Render Driver (CPU) because the VM driver has no DX12 — VM limitation, real Snapdragon hardware unaffected.

title: Windows exes dynamically link VCRUNTIME140.dll — fresh Windows-on-ARM machines fail at launch
description: Rust MSVC targets link the CRT dynamically by default (crt-static off), and the ffxi-nav-recast C++ bridge guarantees the vcruntime140/msvcp140 dependency. On x86_64 the VC++ redist is ubiquitous so it never surfaced; the v0.5.1 aarch64-windows exe fails on any machine without the ARM64 redist (fresh Snapdragon laptops, Parallels Win11-ARM VMs) with the missing-VCRUNTIME140.dll dialog. The arch subtlety: the x64 redist does not satisfy a native ARM64 exe. Fix: RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+crt-static' on BOTH windows release legs (embeds the runtime; standard for standalone Rust Windows distribution; safe because .cargo/config.toml scopes rustflags to aarch64-apple-darwin only). Verify by absence of vcruntime140.dll in the shipped exes' PE import tables. The x86_64 zip carries the same latent dependency, masked by redist ubiquity — fix both.
close_reason: Shipped in v0.5.2: RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+crt-static' on both Windows release legs. Rehearsed on the publish-disabled branch first; verified on both the rehearsal artifacts AND the published v0.5.2 exes by PE scan — zero CRT DLL imports (vcruntime140/msvcp140/ucrt) in either arch, machine types 0x8664/0xAA64 correct. No VC++ redistributable needed on any Windows machine.

title: Nameplate glyphs went translucent/background-tinted: straight-alpha mip chain
description: The kuluu-nre2 mip chain box-filtered straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA, so minified glyph strokes averaged with transparent/outline texels: letters turned semi-transparent and took on the background (dim+mottled over sky/trees, clean over dark walls). Fix: premultiply RGB by alpha in linear space before mip build (premultiply_linear), AlphaMode::Premultiplied on the plate material, pulse fade scales the whole texel via LinearRgba(a,a,a,a). Verified live in Port Windurst: glyph avg (124-127,164-168,124-128) identical across stone/trunk/sky backgrounds with bloom 0.16 active; outline pure black on all three (artifacts/verify/premult-1.png). title: Self height (wire z) wedges permanently once >1yalm off the MZB floor — /pos z=0.00 at a -9.28 riverbed, inflating all 3D distances
design:
Diagnosis from a live HorizonXI session (Oldman, West Ronfaure zone 100, ffxi x=-390.20 y=-437.21):

EVIDENCE
- /pos reported z=0.00. Offline probe (zz-collision-column 100 -390.20 -437.21 0) against the retail MZB: the ONLY floor in that column is ffxi_z=-9.279. No floor exists at z=0.
- LSB mob_spawn_points for the adjacent mobs agree with the terrain: River Crab 17187219 at pos_y=-10.374, Goblin Fisher 17187211 at -9.215. Entities are fine; the zone is NOT mis-positioned.
- /debug distances are full 3D over wire coords (slash_commands.rs::sq_dist). Crab 17187219: horizontal ~3.3y, delta-height ~10.4 -> 3D ~10.9 (session showed 14.1 with wander). "Adjacent mob reads 8-10y" = the height gap.
- Self z feeds c2s 0x015 (session/codec.rs::build_subpacket_pos), so the server persists/broadcasts the bogus height; 0x00A LOGIN then re-seeds z=0 next session. Self-sustaining.

MECHANISM (the wedge)
- input.rs grounds via ground_step(xz, -basis_pos.z, MAX_GROUND_STEP_UP=1.0) and falls back to holding basis_pos.z on None ("let the server correct" — but the server never corrects mid-session).
- dat_mzb.rs::ground_step rejects hit_y > feet_y + max_rise. With feet_y=-z=0 and the floor at bevy +9.28, the floor is out of reach -> None forever.
- Repro offline: zz-ground-walk 100 -390.2 -437.2 0.0 <dest> — every step "NO FLOOR (kept bevy_y=-0.000)". With a correct seed (z0=-6 from the terrace) the same walk descends smoothly to -9.279.
- Note: the kuluu-0nnl commit text says "descent stays unbounded", but in the production mapping (feet=-z_wire; game-down = bevy +y) the bound is what rejects >1yalm drops; gentle descents only work because per-tick drops are <1. The bound's side vs intent needs a re-audit (roof-snap protection may be protecting the wrong side).

SECOND WEDGE SOURCE
- reactor.rs::step_point preserves from.z and never grounds (no MZB access) — /follow, /pathto, engage drag z across height changes.

FIX DIRECTIONS
1. Recovery in input.rs: when ground_step returns None, retry ground_nearest (or a bounded per-tick fall) instead of holding z forever; "server will correct" is false.
2. Seed repair: after 0x00A/CHAR_PC self seed, snap z to ground_nearest when no floor is within reach of the seed.
3. Ground reactor-driven movement, or hand z correction back to a shared grounder.
4. Re-audit MAX_GROUND_STEP_UP one-sidedness against kuluu-0nnl's Jeuno repro before changing the bound.

SIDE EFFECTS OF THE WEDGE (all from the 3D gap)
- /debug + melee/engage range inflated (blocks melee while horizontally adjacent — debug_heights.rs comment already documents this failure class).
- Self model/camera anchored ~9.3y off the real floor -> other PCs look mis-positioned; our z=0 is also broadcast so others see us floating.

- "client-side z does appear to change, perhaps server-side it isn't" — it IS going server-side: c2s 0x015 carries the wedged z and the server accepts/persists it (that is how the wedge survives relogin). There is no server-side terrain validation to catch it; retail correctness comes from the retail client refusing to produce those positions.

- Since the Jeuno fix (ab7258d): can walk through walls (known interim state, kuluu-q5sn — navmesh wall-slide was removed with the navmesh grounding) and hop up/down ledges. Neither is retail: retail caps step-up and has falling.

MzbCollisionGeometry::ground_or_recover falls back to ground_nearest only when the walker is under EVERY floor in its column (unreachable by walking, so always safe and inert otherwise); recover_self_ground_system is the single recovery authority, gated on LoadMzbInFlight so an async interior swap cannot roof-snap the player (kuluu-0nnl); the correction rides a new AgentCommand::GroundCorrection so it no longer cancels /follow or /pathto and is not dropped under a forced-move override; reactor::step_point interpolates z instead of freezing from.z. MAX_GROUND_STEP_UP audited and left at 1.0 -- the bead NOTES had the bound's side inverted, the climb side is what's bounded.
WHAT LIVE VERIFICATION DID AND DID NOT SHOW (local LSB, GUI zone 103): self z grounded at -5.319, the real MZB floor, and held there across driven movement (debug_drive + debug_heights, artifacts/verify/session-2026-08-11.log) -- no wedge. The RECOVERY path itself was NOT exercised: agent-socket 'move' would not place the character at a wedged z (x never changed either), so the under-floor seed could not be forced from outside. Reproducing it needs either the HorizonXI character that reported it or a client-side test hook that seeds a bad z.

Seeding a bad height server-side ('!pos 142.407 0 -151.001') reproduces the bead's headline symptom exactly: debug_heights reports server_z=0.0 while player_bevy_y=5.319, i.e. /pos says 0.00 while the character stands on the real floor. MECHANISM THE REPRO EXPOSES: the wedge lives in SessionState.self_pos.z (which is what debug_heights prints as server_z, what c2s 0x015 carries, and what the 3D distance math uses), NOT in LocalPlayerPrediction. The rendered/predicted position was correctly grounded the whole time. recover_self_ground_system reads prediction.pos when initialized, so it looks at the already-correct value and never sees an under-floor player -- it can only catch a wedge that the PREDICTION shares. And self_pos.z tracks whatever the server last asserted (proven by the restore), so nothing reconciles it against the grounded prediction.

The ground_or_recover / LoadMzbInFlight / GroundCorrection machinery from 1eda363+55d6415 is sound and unit-pinned; it is aimed at the wrong copy of the position.

title: Event cue channel: cutscenes execute but nothing can render them
description:
The event VM runs a cutscene's bytecode to completion and NOTHING reaches the renderer, because the channel is closed at four successive boundaries: ffxi_event::StepResult (AwaitMessage/AwaitMessageAck/AwaitChoice/Done/Cancelled/Unimplemented) -> ffxi_event::DialogStep (Frame/Ended/Stopped) -> event_dialog::Begin/Advance -> AgentEvent (EventDialog/EventEnded) and ViewerEvent (no cutscene variant). Choreography opcodes fall into EventVm::step's _ arm and advance with zero side effects.

Compounding: retail marks 0x1C/0x27/0x2A/0x53/0x7E sets_ret, so a scene spends frames returning to EventIdle. We collapse them to advances, so Advance::Ended fires on the same tick the player answers, 0x05B goes out immediately, and the scene has literally zero duration.

THREE PARTS, in dependency order:
(a) EventCue channel end to end: vm.rs (StepResult::Cue or take_cues), runner.rs DialogStep, event_dialog.rs Begin/Advance, state.rs AgentEvent, kuluu-snapshot ViewerEvent, wire_translate.rs. Cue set the chocobo rental needs: CameraControl (0x46), ScreenFade (0x45), ActorMotion (0x2C), ActorEventHide (0x4E), MountVisual (0x7E case 1/2), music volume (0x5D, reuse AgentEvent::MusicVolumeChanged). Move those opcodes out of the _ arm. The 4CCs are an emitter->matcher contract: exported consts with the emitter plus a guard test.
(b) Make the VM spend time: honour sets_ret for 0x1C/0x27/0x2A/0x53/0x54/0x55 as a Wait satisfied from the 200ms reactor tick; hold 0x05B until EXECEND.
(c) Renderer: full-screen black fade quad + cutscene mode (hide HUD, take camera). New module in kuluu-render. Vanilla parity, no feature gate.

RETAIL GROUND TRUTH (capture 2026-08-04 12.37.09, frames 22-26): the mount cutscene is a ~2s fade to black then fade in already mounted in the same spot. A screen fade, not choreography.

CITATIONS BY SYMBOL: research/XiEvents/OpCodes/0x0046.md (SetViewMode(0) + DisableUserControlCamera + KaListBox_DisableDraw), 0x0045.md (FUNC_LoadStartScheduler, DAT id 30704 + DatIdHelper(work)), 0x002C.md (CMoSchedularTask), 0x004E.md (Render.Flags0 event-hide bit), 0x005D.md (YmMusicServer_Volume), 0x007E.md.

RISKS: widening StepResult/DialogStep/AgentEvent/ViewerEvent crosses the kuluu-snapshot snapshot boundary (PROTOCOL_VERSION bump + wasm rebuild). Making waits yield changes EVERY event in the corpus: the kuluu-u7r5 sweep baseline moves, and any event yielding on a wait the host fails to satisfy becomes a HANG rather than a silent skip (OPCODE_BUDGET_PER_STEP bounds opcodes within one step and does NOT protect against this - a wall-clock release valve is required). Delaying EVENT_END keeps the char InEvent server-side; LSB rejects zonelines and logout while InEvent, and PENDING_EVENT_END_GRACE plus the walk-away release will force-release a legitimately waiting cutscene mid-fade. Both must become cutscene-aware.

CONTESTED, settle before coding (c): 'fdo0' = fade out / 'fdi0' = fade in is an INFERENCE from the 4CC. XiEvents documents 0x45 only as passing the u32 to FUNC_LoadStartScheduler. Open the scheduler DAT that id addresses and see whether the 4CC is a resource key inside it - do not build a fade keyed on a guessed string. Also: this event issues 0x46 case 1 (disable camera) with no matching case 0 in the reachable body; getting the teardown wrong leaves the camera permanently locked after a rental, strictly worse than today.
acceptance_criteria: Renting a chocobo fades to black and fades back in mounted; the sweep baseline is re-recorded; no event can hang the client.
notes:
2026-08-07 IMPLEMENTED in c8f3390. Offline only -- NOT verified live.
Cue channel (EventCue + take_cues drain), VM emits 0x2C/0x45/0x46/0x4E/0x5D/0x7E;
ViewerEvent widened (PROTOCOL_VERSION 18->19); kuluu-render/src/cutscene.rs
reads fdo0/fdi0 from ROM/62/110.DAT via a new scheduler ScreenColorDrive stage.

POST-REVIEW FIXES (three reviewers; the first two were real bugs shipped by the
implementers and caught only by adversarial review):
- CutsceneScope::push had no open check while end() returned before emitting
  CutsceneEnded when closed. Server CancelEvent closes the scope but leaves the
  runner alive, so the next drive published a fade into a dead scope and latched
  the screen black with no driver. Now tracked by a `published` flag.
- FadeProgram::ends_clear() compared all four channels to [1.0;4], but the
  authored fdi0 ends at ALPHA 0, so it was always false: the release fade-in was
  dead code and a scripted fade-in in flight got hard-cut. Now judged on the RGB
  mean the compositor actually uses.
- Added SCREEN_FADE_MAX_HOLD_SECS = 90 backstop in ScreenFade::tick. The release
  rides a broadcast channel that drops under lag at two hops (NativeSource::
  drain_events discards on Lagged), so a dropped CutsceneEnded left the player
  frozen behind an opaque overlay. 90s is safe because the longest single
  authored 0x1C WAIT in the whole corpus is 3370 units = 56.2s.

STILL OPEN (follow-ups, not blockers):
- A1b: wait/yield semantics. The VM still advances through 0x1C/0x53/0x54/0x55,
  so a scene's cues all land in ONE tick with no pacing. The fade will therefore
  snap rather than play until this lands. THIS IS THE NEXT PIECE.
- Proper fix for the dropped-release hole: carry the cutscene latch in
  SceneSnapshot and reconcile per frame, so it self-heals. Needs another
  PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. The 90s ceiling is a backstop, not this.
- 0x5D fade_frames dies at the AgentEvent boundary (MusicVolumeChanged has no
  fade field); renderer eases with audio::BGM_FADE_SECS instead.
- CutscenePlugin registers on wasm but load_fade_programs is native-only, so the
  browser viewer consumes cues and draws no fade.
- Remaining cues unrendered: ActorHide, ActorMotion, Mount, actor-aimed Scheduler.
  cutscene::apply_cue is the hook.
- 0x46 case 2 (query camera state into a work slot) still unimplemented.
- MUSIC_SLOT_COUNT should become a vendor-scrape of music_slot.h.

ACCEPTANCE MUST RUN IN A CITY. The choreographed rental only exists in the six
zones LSB warps the player out of (230, 234, 241, 244/245/246). Outdoor renters
are dialog + a single 0x45 'chco' -- no fade, no camera lock, by design.
Live check: zone 230 event 599, ~0.5s to black, mount swap, ~0.5s back, HUD returns.

2026-08-27 LIVE: THE FADE RENDERS. Acceptance is met on the visual leg.
Observed by jw driving the real flow by hand in zone 230 (Camereine): pick the
default "yes" -> short fade to black -> zone change screen -> mounted on a

written -- it is short, but it is visible and correctly ordered. A1b is still
worth doing for pacing fidelity; it is NOT a blocker on this bead.

"fades back in mounted in the same spot" description does not mention; the
2026-08-04 retail capture was of the mount cutscene, not the renter's warp.

A SOCKET-DRIVEN ATTEMPT THE SAME DAY WRONGLY SCORED THIS AS FAILING, and the
reason is worth keeping. AgentCommand::EndEventChoice has two misleading field
names: `event_id` must carry the dialog's npc_id (not the socket's event_id) and
`event_num` must carry the dialog's event_para (599, not 0) -- see

Everything below the driving layer did hold up: talking to an NPC over the

TWO METHODOLOGY TRAPS, both now folded into
.agents/skills/verify/references/drive-gui.md:
1. GM !cs <id> CANNOT verify a cutscene -- it starts the event on the PLAYER
   entity, so the client misses the NPC's block and falls back to the zone
   master block, running a different copy. Log signature: "event_dialog: event
   id is not on the entity's own block; resolved elsewhere
   source=ZoneMasterBlock". Trigger through the NPC.

Also: verification should run the --release binary. The dev profile zones in at
0.5-0.6fps with 1.5-2.5s frame spikes, which is why a short fade was unsamplable
here. launch.sh now defaults to target/release/kuluu.
2026-09-08 LIVE RE-VERIFICATION (re-confirmation, not new ground -- no commits have touched cutscene.rs/the cue channel since the 2026-08-27 pass this repeats): rented a chocobo from Camereine (npcid 17719343, zone 230) against the live LSB stack using target/release/kuluu --agent-listen auto play verilight/TestPass!1234/Verilamp. Yes/No dialog appears; answering that second dialog (same npc_id/act_index/event_num=599, choice=0) is what actually drives the cue sequence. title: AH search-server protocol: framing + list/history packets
description: Implement the FFXI search-server TCP protocol in ffxi-proto (or a new module): length-prefixed frames, blowfish over MD5-derived key (static 24-byte base key scraped at build time from vendor/server/src/search/search_handler.h per the vendor-scrape skill — never hand-copied), IXFF magic, MD5 integrity hash at len-0x14, trailing 4-byte per-packet key. Requests: TCP_AH_REQUEST/_MORE (category id @0x16, sort-param count @0x12, u32 params @0x18+8i; sort ids 2=level 5=damage 6=delay 9=name), TCP_AH_HISTORY_SINGLE/STACK (itemid @0x12, stack @0x15). Responses: 0x95 item list (count @0x0E, 20 items/packet, 10 bytes: u16 itemid, u32 single price, u32 stack price, 0x80 @0x0A = final) and history (last 10 sales: date/seller/buyer/price). Cite search_handler.cpp / auction_list.cpp / auction_history.cpp.
