title: [bug] Sky/cloud canopy shows a per-texel dither checkerboard
description:
The weat/<type>/ cld1/cld2 cloud canopy renders with a fine per-texel light/dark checkerboard across the whole sky (screenshot: overcast night sky in a city zone). FFXI stores partial transparency as a dither/stipple, not smooth alpha; a modern renderer turns that stored pattern into a visible one.

Suspected root cause: ffxi_dat::texture::ffxi_alpha_remap expands the DXT3 4-bit alpha nibble as (raw>>4)*255/8. FFXI's 'opaque' 0x80 is not representable in 4 bits, so DXT3 encoders alternate nibble 7 (decoded 119) and nibble 8 (decoded 136) to average 128. The remap turns that 17/255 (6.7%) source ripple into 223 vs 255 (12.5%) — it AMPLIFIES the dither instead of resolving it. Both nibbles mean 'opaque'.

Reference notes from another dev: /Users/jon/Downloads/ffxi-sky-dither.md (order of work: histogram, move alpha cutoffs to <=0.5, mips+trilinear, CPU undither for sky/cloud textures, verify half-scale alpha test).
design:
1. Diagnose: alpha histogram of the actual cld1/cld2 textures to confirm the {0,119,136} DXT3 signature vs {0,255} DXT1.
2. Snap the dithered-opaque band: both nibble 7 and nibble 8 mean opaque, so the remap must not leave a 12.5% gap between them.
3. Sky/cloud-specific CPU undither at upload if the stipple is genuinely in the art (DXT1).
acceptance_criteria: The cloud canopy renders without a visible per-texel checkerboard at the camera distances the sky is drawn at; the fix is pinned by a unit test over the DXT3 dithered-opaque nibble pair.
close_reason: Fixed: DXT3 ordered-dither resolution on the sky shells + continuous half-scale alpha remap. Verified before/after with zone-render-headless (f_ro/331, weat/clod, hour 20): cloud checkerboard and star-dome stipple both gone; daytime zone render pixel-diff mean |delta| 0.106/255, visually identical. Commit 3250c01.

title: [bug] Retail minimap loads an uncalibrated map for the 94 zones with no sub-zone 0
description:
The retail minimap picks its image from the POLUtils-scraped MAP_DAT_TABLE by a dense 0-based map_index, then asks FFXiMain.dll for calibration with dll.zone_map(zone, 0). Those are two different key spaces: the DLL keys on sub_zone_id, and 94 of the 384 zones in the DLL table have no sub_zone 0 at all (every multi-map zone — Windurst Waters 238 has only sub 1 and 2). For those zones zone_map() returns None and retail_aabb silently falls back to state.aabb (the top-down bake's extent), so the retail image is drawn against an unrelated world box and every marker lands off the map.

Windurst Waters is worse still: MAP_DAT_TABLE idx 0 for zone 238 is file 5486, which the DLL has no record for at all, while the DLL's two records are (sub 1, file 5501) and (sub 2, file 5502) — so the wrong image is loaded AND it cannot be calibrated.

Verified against the retail install: the DLL zone-map record carries its own map DAT file id (bytes 8-9 fileTableOffset plus a jTableIndex-selected base, research/xim ZoneMapTable.kt), and that file id agrees with the scraped table for 178 of the 195 zones present in both. Driving image + AABB from the same DLL row removes the cross-table index assumption entirely.
design: Add file_id to ZoneMapRecord and a MainDll::zone_maps(zone) enumerator; have the minimap and the Map screen's Change Map preview select a record and take BOTH the image file id and the AABB from it. With no record, fail retail mode to the TopDown bake rather than draw an uncalibrated image. Record choice on zone-in: first record whose AABB contains the player, else the first — retail actually keys off the player's collision mapId (xim MapDrawer.getCollision), which we do not surface yet.
acceptance_criteria: In Windurst Waters (238) the map image matches the zone and the player marker sits where the player stands. No zone can draw a retail map image against an AABB that did not come from the same DLL record.
close_reason: Fixed in f30d78b, verified live in Windurst Waters: loader now takes file 5501 from the FFXiMain sub-1 record and the grid readout matches that record's AABB exactly at two positions (K-11 and K-10, both predicted). Follow-up left open below.

title: Target-action ability submenu never scrolls — rows past the 7th are unreachable
description: On BST/THF, Charming a pet appends the pet-command rows to the ability list and pushes Sneak Attack / Steal out of view with no way to reach them. hud/target_action_menu.rs spawns MAX_ROWS=7 row entities and renders rows.get(row.slot) with no viewport offset, so any list longer than 7 is silently truncated — the cursor can still move onto the hidden entries but nothing shows. The main menu pane already solves this (hud/menu.rs resolve_viewport keeps the cursor centred in a DYNAMIC_VISIBLE_ROWS window).
design: Give the target-action menu the same cursor-centred viewport as menu::resolve_viewport, applied to both the ability-group sub list and the top-level entry list, and show an overflow marker so the truncation is visible. Mouse hover/click must map slot -> viewport_start + slot the way menu_mouse_hover_system does.
acceptance_criteria: With more ability rows than fit, scrolling the cursor to the last entry keeps it on screen and Sneak Attack/Steal stay reachable with a charmed pet.
close_reason: Cursor-centred viewport added to the target-action menu for both the ability sub list and the top-level entries, with mouse hover/click mapping slot -> viewport_start + slot. No overflow glyph: hud::menu's own scrolling panes do not draw one, and inventing one here would be the only such marker in the HUD.

title: Job-ability/weaponskill effect DAT is keyed by ability id, not the packet's animation field — Sneak Attack plays a stranger's animation
description: Sneak Attack (abilityId 44, abilities.sql animation 17) plays what looks like a ranged-attack/weaponskill routine. scheduler_runtime::action_dat_file_id resolves the completion-effect DAT as 0x113C + abilityId (ffxi-proto/src/action_anim.rs ability_file_id) — 0x113C+44 = file 4456, root routine 'mdy3' (15 generators, no textures) — where the ability's real effect is 0x113C + animation = file 4429, root 'huiu', which carries a 'hit0' sub-routine and three textures. The body motion rides the same DAT (its Motion stages drive begin_completion_motion), so a wrong file gives a wrong animation too. Category 3 is worse: abilities with abilities.sql actionType=3 (Steal, id 41 / animation 181) arrive as ActionCategory::SkillFinish and get fed to weapon_skill_animation_index(41), which is a different weaponskill's index entirely.
design: s2c 0x028 already carries the right index: LSB sets actionResult.animation = PAbility->getAnimationID() / PWeaponSkill->getAnimationId() / PSpell->getAnimationID() (0x028_battle2.cpp:71 packs it as the 12 bits after resolution(3)+kind(2)). Decode it for every category in decode_battle2_header instead of only CATEGORY_BASIC_ATTACK, plumb it through AgentEvent/ViewerEvent::ActionStarted, and key action_dat_file_id off it: cat 3 = race base + animation, cat 4 = 0xAF0 + animation, cat 6 = 0x113C + animation. Matches research/xim AbilityTable.kt getAnimationId, which branches on the same LSB actionType and adds animationId (never the ability id).
acceptance_criteria: Sneak Attack resolves file 4429 ('huiu'), Steal resolves race base + 181, and a spell still resolves 0xAF0 + its spell_list animation.
close_reason: s2c 0x028's per-result animation index is now decoded for every category and plumbed through ActionStarted (wire v12); action_dat_file_id keys off it. Confirmed against the retail DATs: the 0x113C block spans ~339 entries (max abilities.animation = 338) and 0x113C+343 does not resolve at all, so it cannot be ability-id indexed; 0x113C+17 is Sneak Attack's cm0?/cm1? strike with a hit0 particle sub-routine and mdam, while 0x113C+44 is a 10-generator projectile show. The old comment's Boost evidence was a misattribution — 0x113C+39 is Familiar's aura (abilityId 24, animation 39).

title: [bug] The minimap self marker points where the camera looks, not where the character faces
description: update_minimap_overlay passes ChaseCamera.yaw into sync_marker_layer (minimap/overlay.rs:262, hud/map_screen.rs:876), so swivelling the camera spins the player marker while the character stands still. The marker must follow the character's own heading. self_marker_rotation() is already correct — its tests feed it camera::yaw_for_heading(heading) — only the call site is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Swivelling the camera leaves the player marker's nose alone; turning the character rotates it. Verified live.
notes: Fixed in e2f0c37: rotation now derives from the actor's own Transform (facing_xz(rotation)) and ChaseCamera is no longer a parameter of either marker system. Unit tests pin tip==facing across headings and that the transform convention matches camera::yaw_for_heading. LIVE LEG OWED (console locked): capture the minimap at headings 0/64/128/192 and confirm the pin turns with the body, then swivel the camera and confirm it does not.
close_reason: Fixed in e2f0c37 and verified live (artifacts/verify/minimap-*.png): map edge lands within 0.5px of the marker mapping's prediction at an overhanging window, pin tip tracks the actor's heading through all four quadrants, and fills resolve from the real retail ncol table.

title: Job-ability battle lines print LSB's ".." comment placeholder verbatim ("Oldman uses ..")
description: Using Sneak Attack logs 'Oldman uses . .' instead of 'Oldman uses Sneak Attack.'. Abilities with abilities.sql message1=0 fall back to MsgBasic::UsesJobAbility=100 (vendor/server/src/map/entities/charentity.cpp:1945). ffxi-proto's msg_basic table is scraped from the trailing comment in vendor/server/src/map/enums/msg_basic.h, and LSB writes '..' rather than a named token wherever retail's mesbasic string substitutes the action name or a number: 14, 31, 100, 101, 102, 103, 136, 137, 317, 324 (plus the 420-427 roll family). The scrape has no way to know which token a bare '..' is.
design: Extend TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES in ffxi-client/src/session/mod.rs (already established for msg 116 and 565) with the action-name family, mapping each '..' to the token the substituter already knows: <ability> for the 'uses' lines, <number> for the shadow-count lines. Leave the 420-427 Corsair roll family out — they need two numbers plus a status the substituter cannot supply from data1/data2 alone. The durable fix is scraping retail's own mesbasic table (ROM/27/72.DAT); tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Sneak Attack logs 'Oldman uses Sneak Attack.'; Charm logs 'Oldman uses Charm. The Goobbue Farmer is now under Oldman's control.'; no battle line renders a bare '..'.
close_reason: TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES extended with the '..' action-name family (100/101/102/103/136/137/317/324) and the two shadow-count lines (14/31). msg 100 now renders 'Oldman uses Sneak Attack.' Corsair rolls 420-427 left out and tracked in kuluu-v8uc.

title: Mob TP moves / weaponskills log as "skill #NNN" — <skill> resolves against the combat-skill table
description: s2c 0x028 battle lines carrying msg_basic <skill> (43 readies, 185-189/224-226/238/242/243/362/370 uses) render as 'Goobbue Farmer readies skill #584' / 'uses skill #160'. Two faults in substitute_battle_placeholders (ffxi-client/src/session/mod.rs:4414): (1) <skill> is looked up in ffxi_proto::skill_names, which is the COMBAT skill table (Hand-to-Hand, Dagger) — the right source is the weaponskill / mob TP move name space; (2) it reads data1 (the result param = damage) instead of the resolved action id, so 'uses skill #160' was literally the 160 damage. Only msg 38/53/310 (skill-up lines) legitimately take a combat skill id from data1.
design: Scrape a merged TP-move name table into ffxi-proto at build time from vendor/server/sql/mob_skills.sql (id, mob_skill_name) unioned with weapon_skills.sql (weaponskillid, name) — the two agree on all 175 overlapping ids and weapon_skills supplies 34 ids <256 that mob_skills omits. Keep <skill> for 38/53/310 on skill_names(data1); route every other <skill> message to the new table via the resolved action id (battle2 already computes it: param for start categories, cmd_arg for finish). msg 326 ReadiesSkill is emitted only by ability_state/petskill_state with param = ability id, so it resolves as an ability. Retail's own table is ROM/27/80.DAT (research/xim MobAbilityTable.kt:10, BasicStringTable xor 0x80) — a later fidelity upgrade, tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: A mob TP move logs 'Goobbue Farmer readies Uppercut.' and 'Goobbue Farmer uses Uppercut. Oldman takes N points of damage.'; skill-up lines still read 'Your Dagger skill rises'.
close_reason: Merged mob_skills+weapon_skills name scrape into ffxi_proto::tp_move_names; <skill> now resolves by resolved action id, with 38/53/310 kept on the combat-skill table and 326 on the ability table. Verified by unit tests (mob skill 584 -> Uppercut for both the readies param path and the uses cmd_arg path).

title: [bug] Minimap markers drift from the map image whenever the view window clips the map edge
description: crop_pixel_rect (ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/mod.rs:508) clamps the requested pixel sub-rect to the image bounds (.max(Vec2::ZERO) / .min(image_size)), but the marker overlay maps world->UV against the UNCLAMPED visible AABB (minimap/overlay.rs:317, hud/map_screen.rs:864). Whenever the player-centred window pokes past the edge of the zone map image — which is what 'zoomed out enough' means near a zone border — the drawn image covers a different world span than the markers assume, so every dot (including the player) sits offset from the terrain under it. Bug grows with how far the window is clipped.
acceptance_criteria: A marker's screen position matches the map feature under it at every zoom level and every position in the zone, including hard against a zone border. Unit test pins image placement and marker UV against the same visible AABB.
notes: Fixed in e2f0c37: MapImagePlacement replaces crop_pixel_rect on both surfaces; the image is sized/offset in percent against the same visible AABB the markers use, with Overflow::clip on the surface. Unit tests pin the agreement over an overhanging window (minimap/mod.rs). LIVE VISUAL LEG STILL OWED: macOS console was locked for the whole verify window (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked=1), which blanks GPU capture. Repro set up and ready: zone 110 map AABB is x[-1402.5,1157.5] z[-1317.5,1242.5] (FFXiMain zone-map record, size 2560), so teleporting Verilamp to server x=1140 puts the default r=50 window 32.5 yalms past the map's right edge. Expected: player pin stays centred, map's right edge lands at 67.5% of the widget with backing beyond it.
close_reason: Fixed in e2f0c37 and verified live (artifacts/verify/minimap-*.png): map edge lands within 0.5px of the marker mapping's prediction at an overhanging window, pin tip tracks the actor's heading through all four quadrants, and fills resolve from the real retail ncol table.

title: Chat merge key is re-derived from array index every snapshot, so new server lines never land at the bottom
description:
Two producers feed the chat log and they have no common clock: session-thread lines (AgentEvent::ChatLine -> state.rs:1236 self.chat.push, carried inside the wire snapshot) and renderer-local toasts (/debug, /copy, SFX, skybox - pushed via SceneState::push_local_toast, never leave the render process). server_ts is 0 on every client-authored line, so kuluu-render/src/snapshot.rs:163 rendered_chat merges the two streams on local_seq instead.

local_seq is supposed to be a monotonic arrival counter. It is not. kuluu/src/view_native/bridge.rs:124 NativeSource::drain_deltas returns an empty Vec - native play is full-snapshot only - so stamp_new_server_chat (snapshot.rs:63) never runs, and snapshot.rs:139-147 re-derives local_seq from array position on EVERY poll: server chat gets 0..n, toasts get n..n+m. The real interleaving is destroyed each frame and every toast is pinned below every server line, permanently.

Symptom: with any local toasts on screen, a newly arriving server line is inserted ABOVE the whole toast block instead of at the bottom of the log. Reproduced live with an [event] auto-skip line landing above a /debug + /copy + SFX toast block.
design: Make the sequence authoritative at creation instead of re-derived. Session assigns a monotonic u64 to each ChatLine when it appends (state.rs:1236 and the AgentEvent::Error path at :1284), carried across kuluu-snapshot alongside server_ts. On ingest, allocate a renderer local_seq only for lines whose session seq is newer than the highest already seen; toasts keep taking next_chat_seq at push time. That is stable across full-snapshot resync AND across CHAT_HISTORY_CAP draining, which index-derived seqs are not. Alternative considered and rejected: sorting on server_ts - it is 0 for all client-authored lines, which is most of the ones that misplace.
acceptance_criteria: A local toast pushed between two server lines renders between them, and stays there across subsequent full snapshots. A guard test drives ingest_system with repeated full snapshots plus interleaved toasts and asserts rendered_chat order is arrival order. History-cap draining does not reorder surviving lines.

title: Event VM drops the server's num[8] params and text-table zone, so vendor/conquest events render unresolved markers
description:
kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:4593 decode_event_0x034 already decodes nums (8 x i32 at data 0x04), event_num (the server's zone), event_num2 (the text table) and mode. kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:4636 event_trigger_ids then collapses the whole DialogState to (npc_id, act_index, event_para) and throws the rest away, and event_dialog.rs:168 starts the VM with Vec::new() for params - the comment there claims a 0x32 trigger carries no numerics, which is true for 0x32 but NOT for 0x33/0x34, and all three opcodes route through the same call site (session/mod.rs:3454).

Live consequence: the conquest outpost vendor. vendor/server/scripts/globals/conquest.lua:1461 calls startEvent(vendorEvent, nation, fee, 0, fee, player:getCP(), 0, 0, 0), which vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x034_eventnum.cpp:44-50 packs into num[0..7]. With an empty params array every {Num:N} marker in the vendor dialog stays unresolved, so the player sees no price and no CP balance.

Second half: we load the string DAT for current_zone_id (event_dialog.rs:127 ensure_zone), but 0x034_eventnum.cpp:56-64 sets EventNum2 to eventInfo->textTable when it is not -1, else the char's zone. A server that redirects the text table gets the wrong strings from us. EventNum likewise carries the server's authoritative zone, which is the more trustworthy key than our tracked current_zone_id (cf. the Mog House case where zone_id stays the surrounding city).
design: Widen event_trigger_ids to return the decoded DialogState (or a small struct carrying nums, event_num, event_num2) and pass params into DialogSession::begin. Keep the event DAT keyed on the zone the event actually belongs to; load strings keyed on event_num2 when it differs from the event zone, which means ensure_zone must cache the two independently rather than as one loaded_zone.
acceptance_criteria: A 0x034 trigger carrying non-zero num[] renders its {Num:N} markers with those values; an event whose EventNum2 names a different zone loads that zone's strings. Guard test builds a 0x034 to the 0x034_eventnum.cpp layout and asserts the params reach the VM.
notes:
2026-08-05: found a concrete consequence while diagnosing the chocobo rental.
EventVm::start initialises work_zone: [0; WORK_ZONE_LEN] and never seeds it from
the trigger packet's num[8]. Zone 230 event 599's IF at offset 150 is 'if gil <
price goto the cannot-afford tail'; both sides read 0, 0 < 0 is false, so we
answer YES, RENT for a player who cannot pay. Probe: driving '230 599 115 10 0'
still ends at pc 325, the rent branch.
Citation: GP_SERV_COMMAND_EVENTNUM (vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x034_eventnum.cpp).

CONTESTED, settle before coding: the Work_Zone[N+2] = num[N] base is inferred
from three mutually consistent IF sites inside ONE event. A wrong base silently
mis-branches every parameterised event. Settle by driving the conquest outpost
vendor event (8 params) offline with zz-event-drive and confirming the same base
explains its comparisons, or pin against XIClient's RecvEventCalcNum.

GATE: re-run zz-event-sweep and record the new baseline on kuluu-u7r5 in the
same commit — this WILL flip branches in events that currently take the
all-zeros path, and several already-'working' dialogs will change text.

2026-09-09: Confirmed the N+2 parameter mapping against independent retail Selbina Lucia event 221 affordability and Southern San d'Oria event 599 rental comparisons. Seed eight full-width parameters into Work_Zone[2..9], keeping result slots 0 and 1 intact. Script writes update dialog numeric parameters too. Installed-DAT tests cover Lucia balances 99, 100, and 1,300,000, and decline. Live funded Lucia charged exactly 100 gil and awarded FERRY_TICKET; decline and insufficient funds left balance/tickets unchanged. Movement and airship work tracked in kuluu-919z. Corpus baseline recorded on kuluu-u7r5.
close_reason: Seeded all eight event parameters into retail numeric work slots; installed-DAT affordability and live Lucia purchase verified.

title: 0x0E name extraction misses LSB dynamic-entity spawn layout (targid >= 0x700, name at 0x44)
description:
ffxi-proto/src/decode/entity.rs:96 try_extract_name knows exactly one CHAR_NPC name layout: name at packet 0x34, shifted to 0x35 when the byte at 0x34 is 0x01. That matches vendor/server/src/map/packets/entity_update.cpp:563-587 (the isRenamed re-send path, which sets ref<uint16>(0x34)=0x01 and nameOffset=0x35 for targid < 1024).

LSB has a SECOND layout we do not handle. entity_update.cpp:539-560: when type == ENTITY_SPAWN and isRenamed and look.size == MODEL_EQUIPPED and targid >= 0x700, the packet grows to 0x56, updatemask is forced to 0x57 (Name bit SET), look_t is memcpy'd over 0x30, and the name is written at 0x44 with ref<uint8>(0x18)=0x01 as the marker.

So for every dynamic entity - server-added NPCs, trusts, fellows - our decoder passes the NAME_FLAG check, then reads look_t bytes as a name. read_name_slot rejects them as non-ASCII, so the spawn name is silently dropped. This is the range HorizonXI's dynamic_entity_renamer addon keys off (addons/dynamic_entity_renamer/dynamic_entity_renamer.lua register_dynamic_entity: targid >= 0x700, name at data 0x34+4).

Existing tests cover only the low-targid shift (try_extract_name_char_npc_renamed_low_targid_shift at :1036).
design: Discriminate on the 0x18 marker (packet 0x18 = body 0x14) rather than on targid, since the packet is what we hold: when body[0x14] == 0x01, read the name from body 0x40 (packet 0x44); otherwise keep the existing 0x30/0x31 logic. Verify the marker is not aliased by the UPDATE_POS moving field at the same offset - entity_update.cpp:322 writes ref<uint16>(0x18) = loc.p.moving under UPDATE_POS, so the two CAN collide and the discriminator must also require the spawn-shaped size (0x56).
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic 0x0E built to the entity_update.cpp:539-560 spawn layout yields the correct name; the existing low-targid and PC cases still pass; a moving entity whose loc.p.moving happens to be 0x0001 is not misread as the dynamic layout.

title: DAT overlay search path: honour Pivot-style overrides before the base install
description:
Private servers ship client-side DAT changes as an overlay directory, not by editing the retail install. HorizonXI uses XI-Pivot: config/pivot/pivot.ini names a root_path plus an ordered overlay list (horizonmusic, horizonoverrides, xiview), and polplugins/DATs/<overlay>/ROM*/<dir>/<file>.DAT shadows the base install at fopen time. Measured in vendor/game-files: 22 override files across 3 overlays (file ids 71607-109786 plus xiview 12/87/39542/39551).

We resolve every file id straight to the base install (ffxi-dat/src/archive.rs DatRoot::resolve -> location.path_under(root)), so none of that is visible to us. Supporting it is the single highest-leverage private-server change: one resolver learns an ordered list of overlay roots, checks each for the resolved ROM subpath, and falls back to the base install.

Note the overlays are keyed by ROM subpath (ROM/26/46.DAT), not by file id, so the overlay check happens AFTER VTABLE/FTABLE resolution and needs no table of its own. Some overlays carry variant filenames (xiview ships '51 (normal).DAT' and '51 (widescreen).DAT' alongside 51.dat) that Pivot does not select automatically - ignore non-canonical names.
design:
Decided 2026-08-04: be compatible with the configs private servers already ship, and make the overlay list hot-swappable rather than a startup-only env read. This SUPERSEDES the earlier note in this field saying do NOT parse pivot.ini — the opposite is now the requirement, because a user pointing us at a HorizonXI install should just work without re-declaring what Pivot already declares.

Resolution order for the overlay list (first source that yields one wins):
1. an explicit setting from our own config, settable at runtime;
2. FFXI_DAT_OVERLAYS (platform path separator), a startup override;
3. auto-discovery of Pivot's own config next to the install.

Pivot discovery: our DAT root is <Game>/SquareEnix/FINAL FANTASY XI, so <Game> is two levels up, and Pivot keeps config/pivot/pivot.ini plus polplugins/DATs there. pivot.ini has [settings] root_path= and an [overlays] section of N=name lines. root_path in a real install is a WINDOWS path (measured: 'C:\Program Files (x86)\HorizonXI\HorizonXI\Game\polplugins\DATs') and is useless off Windows, so prefer the local <Game>/polplugins/DATs and only honour root_path when it resolves locally.

Hot-swap: DatRoot is shared as Arc<DatRoot>, so the overlay list needs interior mutability (RwLock) and a set_overlays(&self) that works through the shared Arc — rebuilding DatRoot would re-read every VTABLE/FTABLE and force the Arc to be replaced everywhere. A read lock per DAT open is negligible against the file I/O. Callers that cache DAT-derived data must invalidate on change; see the dual-wiring gotcha where each *DatRoot resource must be inserted in BOTH view_native/mod.rs and settings.rs.

UNVERIFIED: Pivot's precedence between overlapping overlays. pivot.ini indexes them 0..N but the shipped pivotSettingsHolder.ini comment does not match its own entries, and we have no Pivot source vendored. Moot for the measured install — horizonmusic (sound only), horizonoverrides (ROM/350,351,353) and xiview (ROM/0,119,280) do not overlap on a single path — so implement ascending index = search order, first match wins, and say so rather than imply it is confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: With an overlay root configured, a file id whose ROM subpath exists under the overlay reads the overlay bytes; a file id with no overlay entry reads the base install. A unit test with a synthetic two-overlay tree pins precedence order and base-install fallback. Zero overlay roots configured is byte-identical to today.
notes:
COMPLETE and fully verified. Commits 32a9c3a (resolver + 150-site path_under migration) and 0b7fb50 (config surface).

Config surface: overlay_store persists to config/kuluu/dat_overlays.json; absent = discovery decides, present = authoritative including empty (how a player disables the server's overlays, distinct from reset). apply_saved is wired at BOTH DatRoot construction points -- main.rs resolve_dat_root and launcher_ui/settings.rs -- per the dat-root dual-wiring gotcha. Nothing else needed re-inserting: every *DatRoot resource holds an Arc clone of the SAME DatRoot and set_overlays takes &self, so one call reaches all of them. /overlay list|add|remove|clear|reset drives it live.

Tests, all passing: 15 in ffxi-dat archive (overlay precedence, .DAT/.dat spellings, base-install fallback, pivot.ini parse and index order, discovery dropping names with no directory, live swap through a shared Arc, and a real-install guard that reads the installed pivot.ini and asserts discovery matches it -- it ran non-vacuously on the HorizonXI install, finding horizonmusic/horizonoverrides/xiview); 5 in overlay_store (round trip, empty-is-not-absent, clear, malformed-is-an-error); 4 in slash_commands (parse_overlay defaults, paths with spaces, clear/reset/remove distinct, bad input explained not acted on). Note the parser tests live in the BIN crate, so they need --bins, not --lib.

Still open, deliberately out of scope: nothing invalidates DAT-derived caches on swap, so already-decoded assets keep their old bytes until a zone change or reload. Each mutating /overlay verb says so rather than implying the swap is total.

title: [bug] Camera-anchored sky layers sort to distance 0 and blend over every other transparent object
description:
Nameplates, particle effects (brazier fire), and any other alpha-blended object seen AGAINST THE SKY are washed out / dimmed by the cloud canopy, while the same object over a wall or terrain renders correctly.

Mechanism:
- Bevy 0.19 sorts Transparent3d by the mesh AABB centre's view-space Z (bevy_core_pipeline core_3d/mod.rs:485-492, fed by bevy_pbr material.rs:1327-1341). View Z increases toward the camera; the sort is ascending, i.e. back-to-front.
- zone_clouds.rs:539 (cloud canopy) and zone_clouds.rs:748 (star dome) are camera-anchored: transform translation = camera position, mesh AABB centre ~ local origin. Their sort depth is therefore ~0 — the NEAREST possible value — so they are drawn LAST in the transparent pass, over every other transparent object in the scene.
- Transparent objects do not write depth. Where sky is visible the depth buffer holds the opaque gradient dome at SKYBOX_RADIUS=5500, so the 5400-rim canopy passes the depth test and blends over the nameplate/particle already drawn there. Over world geometry the canopy is depth-rejected, which is why the SAME nameplate is bright over a building and grey over the sky.
- Same defect ordered the additive sun disc (cam + dir*SKY_RADIUS, sort depth -4000) BEFORE the canopy, contradicting zone_clouds.rs:26-28 which states the sun must shine through the clouds.
design: Camera-anchored sky layers cannot be sorted by their AABB centre — it sits on the camera. Each declares the view depth it should sort at via Material::depth_bias (bevy_pbr material.rs:173-179, added straight to the sort distance and used for nothing else). Depths are derived from SKYBOX_RADIUS so no visible world geometry — all of which is inside the opaque dome — can sort behind them, and ordered back-to-front among themselves: stars, then canopy.
acceptance_criteria: A nameplate/particle seen against the sky renders at the same brightness as one seen against a wall. Guard test pins the sky layers strictly behind SKYBOX_RADIUS and in back-to-front order.
close_reason: Fixed: camera-anchored sky layers now declare a Material::depth_bias anchored at SKYBOX_RADIUS instead of sorting at their camera-coincident AABB centre. Verified live (Rolanberry rain): nameplate glyph peak 144-151 unfixed (n=10) vs 169-170 fixed (n=5), against a 172 over-opaque-rock reference. Commit f1e119e.

title: Chat lines carry coloured spans so item names render green like retail
description:
Retail renders the item name inside a drop/obtain line in a distinct colour (green) while the rest of the line stays the log-mode colour — see the 2026-08-03 screenshots on the epic. Today ffxi_viewer_wire::ChatLine is a flat {channel, sender, text} and hud/chat_panel.rs only splits colour on autotranslate braces, so any per-substitution colouring is impossible to express.

Give ChatLine structured spans across the wire boundary and have chat_panel colour them. The span pool per row already exists (SPANS_PER_ROW = 16). segment_chat_line's autotranslate path must keep working.
acceptance_criteria: A drop line renders as >=3 spans with the item-name span a different colour from its neighbours; autotranslate colouring unchanged; span count for a worst-case line stays under SPANS_PER_ROW.
close_reason: Closed

title: ffxi-dat: parse the client system-message DialogTable (ROM/27/76.DAT)
description:
Add a SysMesDat reader alongside EmoteTextDat (dmsg.rs), for ROM/27/76.DAT — the client's system-message DialogTable (326 entries; entry 262 self-identifies as 'sysmes262', entry 40 as 'mes40'). This is where retail's treasure wording lives, so the strings are DATA, not English literals in our source.

Grammar beyond what decode_dialog_text already handles:
- leading 0x1F <log-mode>: the retail chat-log colour selector (121 normal / 123 error / 127 obtain / 136 countdown / 138 trade / 141 moogle / 200 debug / 208 examine / 9,10,13,14 chat-channel echoes). Must be surfaced, not dropped.
- 0x1C <n>: generic string parameter (player/entity name). POLUtils calls 0x1C 'ChocoboName'; in sysmes it is plainly a name slot.
- 0x12 <n>: a second numeric-parameter family alongside 0x0A CC_NUM.
- 0x01 0x01 <slot>: bare slot refs — 0x01 is the a/an article, 0x11 the target entity name (matches the emote table's caster/target 0x10/0x11).
- 0x7F 0xB4 <n>: gil amount. 0x7F 0x86 <n>[second/seconds] and 0x7F 0x92 <n>[/s]: plural alternates. 0x7F 0x88 <n>[the /]: article alternate (already known as AUTO_EMOTE_TARGET_ARTICLE). 0x7F 0x80 0x01: capitalise-next-substitution.
- inline item tags carry more kinds than the five currently named: observed 0x04, 0x23, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27, 0x28, 0x29, 0x33, 0x37 — grammatical variants of the item-name substitution.
acceptance_criteria: Parses the NA install's ROM/27/76.DAT; entry 16 composes to 'You find a <item> on the <mob>.' and entry 18 to '<name> obtains a <item>.'; the 0x1F log-mode is returned, not swallowed; tests self-skip when no retail install is present.

title: EPIC: Treasure pool — drops in chat (retail colouring) + pool UI + lot/pass
description:
Kuluu never decodes s2c 0x0D2 GP_SERV_COMMAND_TROPHY_LIST or 0x0D3 GP_SERV_COMMAND_TROPHY_SOLUTION, so nothing about item drops reaches the chat log: no 'You find a <item> on the <mob>.', no '<name> obtains a <item>.', no lot announcements, no gil-found line. There is also no treasure pool UI and no c2s lot/pass, so pool items cannot be acted on at all.

Retail evidence (user-supplied screenshots, 2026-08-03): the drop and obtain lines render MULTICOLOURED — the item name is a distinct green span inside an otherwise white line:
  'You find a [pair of bounding boots] on Leaping Lizzy.'
  'Macnugget obtains a [pair of bounding boots].'
with the bracketed item name green. The colour boundary is exactly the item-name substitution slot, not an inline 0x1E colour code (ROM/27/76.DAT carries no 0x1E at all).

Wording is data, not English literals: ROM/27/76.DAT is the client system-message DialogTable (entry 262 literally reads 'sysmes262'). Treasure entries: 16 (find on), 218 (find in container), 17 (lot), 18 (obtains), 19 (obtains gil), 130 (you cast lots), 131 (you obtain), 15/31 (does-not-meet-requirements + lost), 164 (was lost), 115/116 (quartermaster pool). Each entry leads with 0x1F <log-mode> selecting the retail log colour (121 normal, 123 error, 127 obtain, 141 moogle, ...).

Remaining under this epic: kuluu-tzm3 (retail lowercase log name) and pinning retail's default font-colour RGB via the retail-observe skill — the item-name green is currently a theme-consistent approximation.

title: [bug] Sun renders as a flat disc and flashes rapidly near the horizon
description: Live at sunrise and again during rain (recordings 2026-08-03 10:10 / 10:12): the sun is a bare flat yellow/red disc with no core+halo+streak glow, and it strobes on/off at high frequency when near the horizon. The flat-disc look is the Enhanced sun profile; MEMORY retail-sun-sky-style-vanilla records that retail's sun is the Vanilla painterly lens flare and that the Enhanced default was already flipped to Vanilla once -- so either that flip regressed or this build is on the Enhanced path. The strobing is separate and is the more likely defect: lens-flare visibility is a continuous BVH raycast (per the cexi audit, cexi's own is a binary occlusion query read a frame late), and a near-horizon sun ray grazes terrain and the newly-spawned cloud canopies, so the occlusion result likely flips every frame. Check whether the raycast now hits CloudMesh entities -- clouds are camera-follow and sit at the dome rim, directly between the camera and a horizon sun.
acceptance_criteria: Sun shows the Vanilla flare by default and does not strobe when grazing terrain or cloud canopies.
notes:
2026-08-05, headless zone-render-headless --sky at file 201:

THE FLAT DISC IS NOT A SKY-STYLE REGRESSION. sun_moon.rs only draws the sun as a textured billboard when moon_material::SunSprite resolves, and extract_sun_sprite_sheet matches a 0x21 sheet whose texture category is "suns"/"suny" — which exists in ZERO of the 298 zone DATs. The sun's art is an MMB (mesh 'suns'/'sun2' on the weat/<w>/sun0|sun1 generator), not a sprite sheet, so SunSprite is always None and the disc is always the procedural emissive ico-sphere. Either drop that dead path or resolve the sun billboard from the MMB (blocked on kuluu-fjd3's vertex-scale bug).

The FLARE half is fixed: it was drawing at roughly a quarter strength because the chain ignored retail's texture-stage gains and each element's authored vertex colour. lens_flare now runs the D3m stage chain (research/xim gl/XimLensFlareShader.kt, XIClient CMoD3m.cpp:16-104) with the per-element colour, so the core saturates and the ghosts ramp down the chain.

The STROBING is untouched — no repro headless (SunOcclusion defaults to 1.0 with no BVH there). Still needs the live check on whether the raycast hits CloudMesh.
2026-08-11: the reach clamp shipped in this session's first pass was a NO-OP at the shipping default -- view_distance.min(SKY_RADIUS) with the High preset's 6100 resolves to SKY_RADIUS, byte-for-byte the pre-fix cast distance. Fixed in c9c9dda: occlusion_reach = min(placement spawn radius, the zone DAT's fog visibility, SKY_RADIUS), plus an area-sampled disc (3 equal-area rings x 8 taps at the sun's real angular radius) replacing the 5-tap cross. STILL UNVERIFIED LIVE: the strobe itself. A GUI session was up on 2026-08-11 but the macOS console was locked, so GPU captures came back black. Re-run wants: outdoor zone, hour ~6.2, walk along a ridge and watch flare_params.w slide rather than flip.
2026-08-16: the flat-disc half is confirmed fine in the shipping (gate-off) configuration -- artifacts/verify/sun-hour8-gateoff.png shows a clean core plus soft glow plus a faint downward streak, i.e. the Vanilla flare, not a bare disc. The STROBE remains unverified: it needs a live GUI session watching flare_params.w across frames near the horizon, and both attempts (2026-08-11, 2026-08-16) died on the macOS console auto-locking, which blanks every GPU capture. Headless cannot reproduce it (SunOcclusion defaults to 1.0 with no BVH). Next attempt should disable the screen lock for the duration.
2026-09-08: Live GUI attempt against the local LSB stack (zone 105 Batallia Downs [S], verilight/Verilamp). Confirmed a real resync gotcha: GM !addtime only moves the server's earth-clock offset (vendor/server SetTimeOffset), and kuluu's client-side sky only re-syncs VanaClock from the zone-in LOGIN packet's game_time (kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:908) -- so !addtime has no visible effect on the rendered sky until you re-!zone into the same zone id to force a fresh vana_time_synced (proof: artifacts/verify/kuluu-nykm/scan2/hour9_none.png stale-night vs hour9_resync.png correct-daytime after the same offset). Beyond that, this attempt could not reach the bead's core observable at all: the chase camera cannot be aimed from the agent socket. AgentCommand::Move's heading and DebugDrive's forward/strafe (kuluu-session/src/state.rs, debug_control.rs) never reach input.rs::camera_polish_system, which reads yaw/recenter only from literal ButtonInput<KeyCode> (CameraYawLeft/Right) and mouse-drag -- verified empirically: 8 headings sent via move produced byte-identical framing (scan2/h000..h224.png), and a 6s DebugDrive forward walk moved the character without rotating the view (scan2/drive_fwd*.png). The documented fallback (osascript System Events key-code presses per drive-gui.md) was attempted and rejected outright by this sandbox's own permission classifier before any keystroke was sent, for both a single key code and a repeat loop. Net result: the character was stuck facing a fixed castle-wall bearing at the Batallia Downs zone-in point for the whole session and the sun was never brought near the horizon in frame, so the strobe itself remains exactly as unverified as after the 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-16 attempts -- but the blocking cause this time is camera-aiming tooling, not the console auto-lock (which did not occur; caffeinate -d -u held the display awake the whole session and captures worked once the window was raised). Recommend either a human-in-the-loop repeat of this recipe (the resync gotcha above will save real time) or adding a socket-level camera-yaw AgentCommand before trying this class of check headlessly again. title: [bug] Cloud canopy disappears on a weather change and only returns after a relog
description: Observed live at sunrise (recording 2026-08-03 10:10): clouds vanish, sky goes flat, sun renders as a bare disc. Logging out and back in restores them. CONTENT IS RULED OUT -- measured weat/fine and weat/suny in both zone DATs the session loaded (202 and 209) and every one authors both cld1 and cld2 canopy generators, so the tag the weather resolves to is not the problem. That leaves state: rebuild_zone_clouds (ffxi-viewer-core/src/zone_clouds.rs) writes state.key = key and drains state.entities into a fade-out BEFORE the four early-return paths that follow (file_id, DatRoot, resolve, fs::read, find_weat_type). Any of those returning leaves the old set removed, the key updated, and no retry until the key changes again -- which a relog supplies. Suspect ordering; confirm which return fires by instrumenting before changing the flow.
design: Do not set state.key until the new layer set is actually built, and log when a rebuild aborts after teardown. Also check the fade-out despawn path does not reap newly spawned entities that share a component.
acceptance_criteria: A weather change swaps canopies without a gap; a failed rebuild retries rather than latching empty.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (f43df5d clouds/fog bit, 9009533 weat generators, cc201af vertex-colour decode + per-stage saturate); gate green, 1359 unit tests + 2 real-DAT integration tests pass. NOT yet verified in a running client.

title: Event lookup never falls back to the zone master block, so cross-nation outpost guards auto-skip
description: Live repro: zone=109 unique_no=0x0106D287 act_index=647 event_id=32763 -> 'NPC block has no such event id'. Diagnosis: 0x0106D286 (17224326) is Mesachedeau, R.K. -- the San d'Oria outpost guard, and the DAT authors event 32763 in ITS block. 0x0106D287 (17224327) is Souun, I.M., the Bastok guard, at identical coordinates (all three nations' guards share one spot; only the controlling nation's is visible). LSB's own Souun_IM.lua declares guardEvent 32761, yet the server dispatched 32763 on Souun -- so the event id and the NPC block disagree by design or by server policy. Measured: the only two blocks in zone 109 that resolve 32763 are 0x0106D286 and 0x7FFFFFF0, the ZONE MASTER block, which resolves it via a 0xFFFE wildcard entry. kuluu-session/src/event_dialog.rs::begin only ever consults dat.block_for_actor(unique_no) and gives up, so it never reaches the master block. Hypothesis: retail resolves an event id against the NPC's own block and then the zone master block. 467 wildcard entries across 292 zones suggests the master block is a real catch-all tier, not decoration.
design: Verify the lookup ORDER against XiEvents' event-entry search before implementing -- do not assume. If confirmed, begin() tries block_for_actor(unique_no) then zone_block(), and UndriveableReason::NoEventEntry only fires when both miss.
acceptance_criteria: Talking to a non-controlling-nation outpost guard opens the real menu instead of auto-skipping; a guard test pins the NPC-then-master order.
notes: Fix implemented and green, NOT yet committed: the three-line block_for_actor gate is gone from event_dialog.rs::begin, UndriveableReason::NoBlockForActor removed with it (now unreachable), and ffxi-dat gained an_actor_with_no_block_of_its_own_still_resolves pinning that an actor with no block of its own resolves via SoleOwnerElsewhere and via the zone master block.

title: Weather is never received on zone-in: 0x00A carries it and we do not decode it
description: LSB constructs GP_SERV_COMMAND_WEATHER (0x057) in exactly one place -- vendor/server/src/map/zone.cpp:672, inside the weather-CHANGE broadcast to CHAR_INZONE. A character zoning in is therefore never sent a 0x057, and our ffxi-client/src/state.rs:990 clears current_weather on zone change, so ZoneWeather sits on the unknown default (suny) until the zone's weather happens to change -- which on a Vana schedule can be a long wait. That, on top of kuluu-e9he, is why weather looks wrong right after zoning. Weather IS delivered on zone-in, inside 0x00A LOGIN: vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x00A_login.h:107-111 declares WeatherNumber u16, WeatherNumber2 u16, WeatherTime u32, WeatherTime2 u32, WeatherOffsetTime u32, immediately after EventMode and before ShipStart. Our decoder (ffxi-proto/src/decode/login.rs ServerLogin) reads unique_no/act_index/zone_no/game_time/pos_head/music_num/myroom/zone_in_event and stops short of them -- it already reads MusicNum, which sits 4 fields earlier in the same struct, so the offset walk is most of the way there.
design: Add weather_number (+ the 2/time/offset fields, which the cross-fade work in the audit backlog will need) to ServerLogin, and emit AgentEvent::WeatherUpdated from the 0x00A handler the same way the 0x057 handler does. WeatherNumber2/WeatherTime2 look like the incoming-weather slot for a transition already in flight -- confirm before wiring them to anything.
acceptance_criteria: Zoning into a zone with non-default weather shows that weather immediately, with no 0x057 required.
notes: 2026-08-11 VERIFIED LIVE: 'ffxi_client::session: 0x00A LOGIN carries zone-in weather weather_number=2 weather_time=776648868 previous_weather_number=0 has_previous=false' on zone-in, with no 0x057 involved. WeatherTime/WeatherTime2 now decoded too; previous_weather_* confirmed as the previous slot (not incoming) against XIClient 0x00A.cpp:90-96, and LSB leaves it zero pending its own '// TODO: Previous weather'.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Weather table fix regressed clouds: id 0 used as an unknown-weather sentinel
description: Regression from kuluu-68os (commit a66fc22). Three sites indexed the weather table with 0 to mean 'the server has not told us yet' (zone_clouds.rs cloud + star spawn, weather.rs weather_type_fourcc). That only worked while the old 9-tag table collapsed ids 0 and 1 onto suny; retail row 0 is fine, so the default state started asking for weat/fine. Measured over the install: 72 of the 298 weat-bearing zones ship suny but NOT fine, and find_weat_type was exact-match with no fallback, so those zones lost their cloud canopy entirely. Fixes: (1) weather_type_id_or_default(Option<u16>) in ffxi-dat makes 'unknown' distinct from id 0 and resolves it to WEATHER_TYPE_FALLBACK; all three sites use it. (2) find_weat_type now takes retail's single suny hop on a miss (XIClient WeatherTransition.cpp:52-54) -- the same fallback the 0x2F record path already had, never applied to the weat container walk. That also fixes weathers the zone does not author at all: rain ships in only 56 of 298 zones, so /weather rain was silently cloudless in most of the world. Also drops a hardcoded b"fine" or_else in the star-dome path that re-typed a tag literal.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown weather resolves to suny, id 0 still resolves to fine, and every weather id yields a container in any zone that ships any weat dir.
close_reason: Fixed in 1a4b481: weather_type_id_or_default separates unknown from id 0; find_weat_type takes retail's suny hop; guard test added

title: Waist/skirt companion motion DAT is never loaded -- joints 38-47 stay in bind pose
description: load_pc pushed only skel_file_id and +1, so nothing opened the waist motion set. Measured on the retail install: for HumeM base 7072, +0 has 130 clips (lower body), +1 has 7 (upper body, wlk1 over 41 joints spanning 3..89), +3 and +4 have 69 each and their wlk2 drives joints 38-47 -- disjoint from everything else. Those hip-hung cloth joints therefore held bind pose during every idle, walk, run, strafe, jump and death. Retail: waist = base_skeleton_no_tab[race] + max(waist_type,1) + 2 (XIClient SkeletalMeshActor.cpp:3165 via ReadStdMotionRes at :3014), waist_type from the BODY slot's CIB (:1659); upper body = base + is_shield + 1 (:3175), is_shield from the SUB slot's CIB (:1682). NOT a hardcoded +3: measured per-race, +3 and +4 ship different clip counts (Elvaan 71 vs 72, race 7 67 vs 70), so the CIB selector is load-bearing. Also corrects ffxi-dat Cib byte 0x05 from weapon_unknown to is_shield, matching XIClient include/CYy/Model/KzCib.h.
acceptance_criteria: Waist and upper-body motion DATs are selected from CIB bytes; guard tests assert the joint sets are disjoint and that the two waist variants differ for some race.
notes: Rider NOT taken: the slot-eviction loop clears any slot absent from the new match set, and emote DATs ship no ?2 clips, so the waist snaps to bind during emotes. Excluding slot 2 from eviction is plausible but not retail-confirmed -- needs retail-observe. Strictly no worse than before, where the waist never animated at all.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (9ad88be, deb4c4b, 4840779); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guard tests

title: Variable-width opcodes advance by their widest case, desyncing ExecPointer
description: OPCODE_META carries one size per opcode, so for variable-width opcodes it holds the MAX case. vm.rs's fallback skips valid && !jumps && !sets_ret opcodes by that size, so where the data encodes a narrower form the ExecPointer lands mid-instruction and the VM executes operand bytes as opcodes -- silently, because the skip looks successful. XiEvents lists multi-valued 'OpCode Size' for these; 0x46 and 0x79 are ~97 percent of the occurrences. Rules transcribed from the retail pseudo-code: 0x46 is 4 only when sub==2 else 2 (0x0046.md); 0x79 is 12 when sub==1 else 10 (0x0079.md); 0x5C is 4 for sub 0x00-0x07, 6 for 0x80-0x87 and 0xA0/0xA1, and returns without advancing otherwise -- a hang, so authored data cannot contain it (0x005C.md); 0xC2 is 4/6/2 for sub 1/2/other (0x00C2.md).
acceptance_criteria: sub_size(op, sub) returns the tier-2 widths for 0x46/0x79/0x5C/0xC2; the VM consults it in both the fallback and advance().
notes: NOT implemented: 0xAE, 0xB7 and 0xD8 also vary, but their width is entangled with a runtime actor lookup (e.g. 0xD8 advances 6 on lookup failure regardless of sub), so they keep their current behaviour rather than being guessed at. Fold them into kuluu-u7r5's per-opcode arms.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (9ad88be, deb4c4b, 4840779); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guard tests

title: Sky ring elevations are polar-angle fractions, not sines
description: skybox.wgsl set the lookup parameter to raw ray.y and bracketed the DAT ring elevations against it, treating each elevation as a SINE. Retail builds the dome as a lathe: angle = elevation * (PI/2), ring vertex at cos(angle)*radius horizontally and sin(angle)*radius vertically (research/XIClient/.../World/Zone/XiZone.cpp:90-92, constant at Constants/Floats.cpp:7 ANGLE_PI_OVER_2, struct at include/World/Weather/WorldParameters.h:19-20). A view ray's y IS sin(angle), so the parameter is the angle recovered from it: asin(clamp(ray.y,0,1)) / (PI/2). Error at e=0.5 is 45 degrees vs our 30, against a 50-degree vertical FOV. Coupled edit: the default altitude table in skybox.rs spanned -1..1 and had to move into the [0,1] domain.
design: Verified the domain independently over the shipped corpus: 6130 non-empty records, 0 out of [0,1], 0 non-monotonic, ring 0 exactly 0.0 and ring 7 exactly 1.0 in every one. Pinned as a real-DAT guard test in ffxi-dat/src/weather.rs.
acceptance_criteria: Shader brackets against the polar-angle fraction; default table in [0,1]; guard test asserts the corpus invariant.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (9ad88be, deb4c4b, 4840779); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guard tests

title: Placement Euler rotations compose in the wrong order (EulerRot::XYZ -> XYZEx)
description: ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mzb.rs:1130 uses EulerRot::XYZ, which glam documents as intrinsic Rx*Ry*Rz. Retail builds Identity -> scale -> RotateX -> RotateY -> RotateZ -> translate in D3D row-vector convention (research/XIClient/.../Rendering/ZoneRenderer.cpp:430-443; Matrix4.cpp:200-204 MultiplyRight = this*r, :508-511 out = v*M), which transposes to column-vector T*Rz*Ry*Rx*S = glam's EulerRot::XYZEx. Self-proven by the order-reversed inverse chain at ZoneRenderer.cpp:459-466, repeated at UnderscoreAtStruct.cpp:44-59. Nothing upstream compensates: ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:1175 reads the triple verbatim from PL_ROTATION 0x1C, and the to_bevy left-multiply (dat_mzb.rs:1134-1140) is a proper rotation (det +1) applied outside the TRS, so winding and the mirrored key are untouched.
design: One edit site only. Do NOT touch dat_mzb.rs:1279-1287 -- that rotation comes from the 0x0B Generator chunk's 0x09 opcode (particle-system data); XIClient has no disassembled effect-system Euler composition and cexi routes 0x05 effect geometry away from its own TRS helper. Quarantine it with particle_sim.rs:441,524.
acceptance_criteria: dat_mzb.rs:1130 uses EulerRot::XYZEx; a guard test pins the composition order against a hand-computed T*Rz*Ry*Rx*S matrix.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (a66fc22, 203d16c, c02f435, 5080ce6, 0a0ecea); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guards

title: Weather id->tag: replace the 9-tag collapse with retail's 20-row WeatherTable1
description: ffxi-dat/src/weather.rs:244-265 collapses 20 LSB weather ids onto 9 weat/<tag> dirs (12 of 20 rows wrong). Retail ships a literal indexed array read with no bounds check: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Weather/WeatherCondition.cpp:9-13 (WeatherTable1), indexed at World/Zone/XiZone.cpp:400-403 with the raw server weather number. Correct rows: fine suny clod mist dryw heat rain squl dust sand wind stom snow bliz thdr bolt aura ligt fogd dark. All 20 ship as real weat/ child dirs. Also trim the four-deep fallback ladder at ffxi-viewer-core/src/weather.rs:63 to retail's single suny hop (WeatherTransition.cpp:52-54). Cite WeatherCondition.cpp, NOT WeatherKeyframeLibrary.cpp -- the latter is a FourCC-keyed load list whose row 7 literal carries a 'sqal' typo. Transcribe in DAT byte order, not XIClient's reversed int literals. Row 0 is fine, not a None special case.
design: Replace WEATHER_TYPE_IDS wholesale; update the test at weather.rs:947-958 which currently pins the wrong rows.
acceptance_criteria: All 20 rows match WeatherTable1 in DAT byte order; test asserts each row; fallback ladder is a single suny hop.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (a66fc22, 203d16c, c02f435, 5080ce6, 0a0ecea); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guards

title: Fix kuluu-p52e's no-op test-name acceptance oracle, and audit other beads for the same mistake
description: 'cargo test -p ffxi-proto --features native-window -- --list' FAILS with 'the package ffxi-proto does not contain this feature: native-window' -- ffxi-proto has no [features] section at all; only kuluu/kuluu-render do. title: [bug] The DAT celestial billboards render black — per-vertex colour multiplies to zero
description:
Blocks kuluu-b98u. The Moon-attached `moon` generator is a 12-frame SpriteSheet particle. Every input to it is correct at runtime (FFXI_TRACE_CELESTIAL=1, zone DAT 210, hour 21):

  Moon billboard mesh=moon verts=6 live=1 origin=Vec3(602.2, 868.8, 0.0)
                 scale=Vec2(20,20) rgb=Vec3(1.0, 0.553, 0.553) frame=11

and the template it draws resolves too:

  frame=11 verts=6 pos0=(-2,-2,0) pos3=(-2,1.94,0) uv0=(0.75,0.50) uv3=(0.75,0.746)
  brightness=(1,1,1) vert_alpha=1 sprite_frames=12

That is a 4x3.94 quad at init_scale 20 = ~80 units at the 900-unit celestial distance, i.e. ~5 degrees, ~140px in a 1280px/45-degree frame. The texture resolves as well: the 0x21 sheet asks for ("moon","moonshap") and the DAT's Img chunks index exactly that under both the qualified and local-name tiers.

Yet nothing draws. Rendering zone-render-headless aimed dead-on at the traced world position (--enhanced-sky so the lens flare cannot be mistaken for it) shows only the faint oversized `kasa` MMB edge, never a lunar disc. The moon texture itself is fine — dumped from ROM 210 it is the expected 256x256 sheet of 12 detailed lunar phases.

Not the alpha encoding: 5a1600a fixed decoded_texture_to_image to expand FFXI's top-nibble alpha (0x88 -> 0xFF) and the disc is still absent. Not the MMB scale bug (kuluu-fjd3) either — that one affects the StaticMesh-linked sun and halo, while this is the SpriteSheet path.
design:
RULED OUT: the first-frame ordering race. 95c74bb orders the celestial systems
before sync_particle_meshes so the clock and origins are set before the mesh
bakes; the billboard still draws black. Keep the ordering (the race was real),
but look elsewhere for the colour.

Remaining suspects, in order:
1. rebuild_mesh's per-vertex colour vs what particle_draw returns. The trace and
   mesh_key call particle_draw with the same clock on the same frame and report
   rgb=(1.0, 0.553, 0.553), yet a magenta unlit opaque material still renders the
   quad black — so either the colours written into ATTRIBUTE_COLOR are not the
   ones particle_draw returns, or Bevy is not consuming that attribute the way
   d3m_material assumes. Dump the actual buffer contents at the insert_attribute
   call rather than inferring from particle_draw.
2. MeshKey latching: confirm an all-zero build cannot compare equal to a later
   coloured one (colour quantum is 1/256, so 0 vs 0.6 should differ — verify).
3. Whether StandardMaterial's vertex-colour path needs an explicit opt-in in
   Bevy 0.19 that d3m_material is missing; the MMB-path particles that DO show
   (fire, water) may be getting their colour from the texture instead, which
   would hide the same defect everywhere.

Bisect recipe that produced the finding: temporarily make d3m_material return an
opaque magenta unlit material and re-render. Geometry then appears (a correctly
sized square quad for the moon sprite, a thin spindle for the oversized kasa MMB),
which is how "invisible" was reclassified as "black".
acceptance_criteria:
- The moon disc renders at ~5 degrees showing the retail lunar surface, phase-correct
- A headless render at a known hour is the regression guard
notes:
NEW EVIDENCE (2026-08-01): this is NOT "doesn't render" — it is "renders black".

Bisected by temporarily forcing d3m_material to an opaque magenta unlit material
(no texture, alpha_mode Opaque) and re-rendering zone 210 at hour 21 aimed at the
traced moon position. Both celestial billboards then appear:

  - a square quad ~120px, which is the moon sprite at exactly its expected size
    (4 units x init_scale 20 = 80 units at the 900-unit celestial distance, ~5 deg)
  - a tall thin spindle, which is the oversized `kasa` MMB (kuluu-fjd3)

So geometry, position, size, billboard orientation, entity lifetime and depth are
all correct, and the earlier "invisible" reading was wrong. What is wrong is
colour: under a MAGENTA base colour the quads still draw BLACK, which means the
per-vertex colour rebuild_mesh writes multiplies to ~0.

That contradicts the FFXI_TRACE_CELESTIAL line from the same function on the same
frame, which reports rgb=(1.0, 0.553, 0.553) for that generator — the trace calls
particle_draw with the same `clock` that mesh_key/rebuild_mesh use. Resolving that
contradiction is the whole bug.

Prime suspect: a first-frame ordering race. sync_particle_meshes and
track_celestial_bodies have no relative ordering (in the harness OR in the client —
SchedulerRuntimePlugin registers the sim systems, CelestialParticlesPlugin the
tracker). On frame 0 the simulator's CelestialClock is still Default, so
day_fraction = 0; the moon's time-of-day alpha curve `k000` is a linear 0->1 ramp,
so alpha = 0 and the whole draw multiplies to black. If built_key then latches that
mesh and needs_rebuild somehow fails to fire on later frames, the black sticks.
Check whether MeshKey's colour quantisation or the Empty-vs-Live discrimination is
letting an all-zero build compare equal to a later coloured one.
2026-08-11: the bead's premise is REFUTED -- the celestial billboards do NOT render black, and none of the three listed suspects (ATTRIBUTE_COLOR buffer contents, MeshKey latching, a missing Bevy vertex-colour opt-in) was at fault. The lunar crescent was drawing correctly all along at the right position, size and phase; it was SWAMPED by the kasa lunar-halo MMB rendering as a saturated ~20-degree pink disc in front of it. Root cause: particle_sim applied the 0x4E day-of-week and 0x4F moon-phase tint tables as an RGB-only 2x modulate, discarding table[3]. Retail modulates all four channels (research/xim Particle.kt:217-218 modulateInPlace vs the adjacent modulateRgbInPlace), and that discarded alpha lane is exactly the halo's gate: kasa's 0x4F alphas are 0.00 everywhere except phases 5/6/7, while the moon sprite's never drop below 0.42. Fixed in 84df6b3. A sibling defect found alongside it -- sprite-sheet D3DCOLOR stored in file order but read as RGBA, swapping red and blue -- is fixed in 7f2fdb0. STILL OPEN: the AC asks for a headless render at a known hour as the regression guard; the guard is currently two unit tests (one synthetic, one DAT-driven) plus a manually inspected PNG, because the repo has no GPU render-test harness.
2026-08-16 VERIFIED WITH PIXELS (artifacts/verify/moon-hour21.png, zone DAT 210 hour 21, FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS=1, zone-render-headless --sky --client-sun): the moon renders as a phase-correct CRESCENT showing the lunar surface, ~78px of a 1280px frame (~2.7 deg at a 45-deg fov). Not black, and no longer swamped by the kasa halo -- at a crescent phase the halo's 0x4F alpha lane is 0, which is exactly what the alpha-modulate fix restored. AC 1 met. AC 2 ('a headless render at a known hour is the regression guard') is met in spirit by the DAT-driven unit test zone_210_lunar_halo_is_dark_except_near_full_moon rather than by a rendered-image guard -- the repo has no GPU render-test harness, and that gap belongs to a harness bead, not this one. NOTE the flag is now --sky, not the --enhanced-sky the bead's recipe cites.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Particle-linked MMB billboards decode ~100x too large — the DAT sun/halo cover the whole sky
description:
Blocks kuluu-b98u (retail-accurate sun/moon). The weather-tree celestial billboards link an MMB (0x2E) rather than a D3M, and particle_sim's MMB fallback draws them at the wrong geometric scale.

Measured (dat-celestial-probe, file 201, weat/suny):
  sun0 -> mesh "suns", MMB, 81 verts, extent [11.354 x 49.950 x 49.519], init_scale 70
  kasa -> mesh "moon", MMB, 49 verts, extent [0.831 x 16.379 x 16.379], init_scale 20

At the retail celestial distance of 900, 50 x 70 = 3500 units across — the sun renders as an angular blob covering half the frame (verified with zone-render-headless --enhanced-sky --hour 8, which disables the lens flare so only the DAT billboard draws).

For a ~3 degree sun at 900 units the drawn size should be ~47, i.e. the mesh should measure ~0.5 units before the authored 70x. So the decoded positions look ~100x too large, which points at ffxi_dat::mmb::parse_models reading these particle MMBs with the wrong vertex layout (it picks stride 48 vs 36 off decrypted[4]; a fixed-point/int16 position layout would produce exactly this class of error).

Retail applies particle scale as a plain multiplier on the linked mesh — research/xim ParticleInitializers.kt:846-857 ScaleInitializer, Particle.kt:341-353 particleTransform.scaleInPlace — and a StaticMesh link resolves straight to the ZoneMeshResource (ParticleLinkedDataProviders.kt:189-204). So the scale path is right and the geometry is wrong.
design:
Settle the vertex layout against tier 1-2 sources (research/XIClient, the FFXiMain disassembly), NOT by dividing by a fudge factor. Compare a particle MMB ("suns", "moon") against a zone-geometry MMB that already renders correctly to find what differs in the header.

Verification loop that does not need a server:

  FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS=1 cargo run -p kuluu-render --example zone-render-headless -- \
    --file 201 --enhanced-sky --hour 8 --client-sun --cap 60 --cam 0 200 0 --tgt 900 700 0 --out /tmp/sun.png

--enhanced-sky disables the lens flare, so anything drawn is the DAT billboard. FFXI_TRACE_CELESTIAL=1 logs each celestial particle's origin, scale, colour and sprite frame.
acceptance_criteria:
- The DAT sun subtends a retail-plausible angle (compare against a retail-observe capture at matching hour/weather)
- FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS gate removed from celestial_particles.rs and the hand-authored discs retired
- A real-DAT test pins the decoded extent of / so the layout cannot regress
notes:
2026-08-11: the bead's premise is REFUTED and the title is now wrong. Nothing decodes ~100x too large: for zone 201 suns/moon, decrypted[4]==0x01 selects the 36-byte stride and the decoded vertex AABB equals the MMB's OWN header AABB byte-for-byte (suns x:[0,11.354] y,z:+/-24.97/24.76). Those extents are AUTHORED. The internal names are 'sunsphere'/'moonsphere', they carry no texture, and their vertex alpha ramps 128 at centre to 0 at rim -- they are the glow DOME and lunar halo, not the sun disc. The real defect was collapsing retail's two billboard modes into one bool, drawing a 3-D axial dome as a flat screen sprite with its symmetry axis at screen-right (84df6b3); 7f2fdb0 then restricted that axial path to solid meshes, since 98 of 1276 Camera generators in DATs 100-500 link exactly-flat templates that draw edge-on under it. Pinned by real-DAT extent + stride tests. REMAINING for this bead: AC 1 (the DAT sun subtends a retail-plausible angle) needs a retail-observe capture at matching hour/weather -- the dome washes the frame pale near the sun and nobody has judged that against retail; AC 2 (remove the FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS gate, retire the hand-authored discs) is untouched.
2026-08-16 PIXEL MEASUREMENT, zone DAT 201 hour 8, camera (0,200,0) -> (900,700,0), zone-render-headless --sky --client-sun, 1280px frame:
  FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS=1 (artifacts/verify/sun-hour8.png): sun core 97px = ~3.4 deg
  gate off        (artifacts/verify/sun-hour8-gateoff.png): sun core 84px = ~3.0 deg
AC 1 IS NOW MET: retail's sun is ~3 deg and the DAT sun subtends 3.4. The 'angular blob covering half the frame' is gone -- so is the hard-edged sail, which was the collapsed billboard mode, not a decode error.

WHAT BLOCKS AC 2 (removing the FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS gate and retiring the hand-authored discs): the glow DOME washes the sky out. Sampling a 400x380 patch in the lower-left corner, far from the sun, mean luminance is 222.8 with the gate on vs 134.8 with it off -- +65%, and the blue sky and cloud contrast visible in the gate-off render are gone in the gate-on one. This confirms the fjd3 implementer's disclosed residual risk 1 with pixels. The dome subtends ~125 deg by construction (radius 25 x init_scale 70 at the 900-unit celestial distance), so the open question is its brightness/blend, not its geometry: what tint and blend mode retail draws sunsphere/moonsphere with. Needs a retail-observe capture at matching hour/weather to settle. Keep the gate OFF until then.

title: Generator water sheets rendered as specks: 0x0F scale / 0x09 rotation ignored, tint /255 instead of /128 identity
description: Zone 245 (and every generator-sheet zone) had no sea: parse_model_spawn dropped the section-1 0x0F ScaleInitializer and 0x09 RotationInitializer (research/xim ParticleGeneratorParser.kt:170,176), so the lowsea/2lowsea tiles (MMB AABB ±1.4) spawned unscaled instead of 500× — a ~3-unit speck. Tint was also /255 where FFXI effect color identity is 0x80 (research/xim MeshBuffers.kt:41 ByteColor.half; corroborated by zone_clouds.rs /128 and every static generator shipping 0x80 neutrals), halving sheet brightness and opacity. Fixed in ffxi-dat generator.rs (parse + MODEL_TINT_IDENTITY + pinned tests) and dat_mzb.rs build_zone_mmb_spawns (T·R·S compose). Also fixes the empty fountain-basin (the scaled sheet fills it, surface ~3 units below plaza). Evidence: artifacts/verify/jeuno-sea-{pre,post}-fix.png same camera, live-jeuno-sea-post-fix.png live client.
