title: Actor collision radius from model locator 44, not the mesh AABB
description:
Retail's per-actor collision radius is 0.8 x the XZ magnitude of model locator 44, read through GetLocatorWorldPosition and scaled by the actor's model scale (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp ControllableActor::GetCollisionSize, SkeletalMeshActor::GetElemLocal).

We parse no locators at all today (no hits for 'locator' anywhere in ffxi-dat/ffxi-actor/kuluu-render), so walker/obstacles.rs snapshots the mesh AABB's wider ground-plane half-extent instead, and walker/step.rs contact_blocks stands the sweep BODY_RADIUS in for the player's own size. A mesh AABB is wider than the retail circle for anything with outstretched arms, wings or a tail, which makes those actors block earlier than retail.
design: Add locator/element parsing to ffxi-dat's skeleton path, expose locator 44 on ffxi-actor's skeleton instance, and have snapshot_mob_block_radius read 0.8 x |locator44.xz| instead of the AABB. Player side: same value for self rather than BODY_RADIUS.
acceptance_criteria: MobBlockRadius derives from locator 44; a wide-silhouette mob (e.g. a bird or crab) blocks at the same distance as a humanoid of equal body width, not at its wingspan.

Raw disassembly and complete runtime hashes unavailable here; revalidate these reports rather than treating them as verified upstream truth. Contributor build instructions moved into README Optional DLSS builds.
PR #521 supplied contributor forensic dumps, now recoverable at immutable commit 8fe705fcc5265df5fad34c0e2ed206d8e0d14dd0:DLSS_docs/logs/ (including nr_full_disasm.txt, nr_dispatch.txt, nr_createfeature.txt, and ngxlib/params_disasm.txt); this supersedes the earlier statement that raw disassembly was unavailable. Architecture.md and History.md at the same commit retain contributor interpretations and build history. These are investigation evidence, not independently verified NVIDIA API contracts. The stacked readiness work removes the duplicated documentation/dumps from the active tree, keeps build instructions in README, and separately gates NR with enhanced-neural-uplift. Hardware validation remains open.

title: Dust Storm emission hemisphere rotates with third-person camera
description: In Valkurm Dunes Dust Storm, the cameraAttachedBase particle origin was rotated by the live camera transform. The authored +Z offset therefore stayed on the far side of the player from the camera, so particles appeared only beyond the character and flipped sides when the camera orbited. cexi-viewer runtime establishes that cameraAttachedBasePosition adds the base offset in fixed world axes and samples it only at particle birth.
acceptance_criteria: Dust Storm emission origin remains fixed in world axes as the third-person camera orbits; existing particles keep their birth origin; focused regression tests and a live opposite-heading camera check pass.
notes: Verified 2026-09-04 at exact Valkurm F-8 under Dust Storm: cameraAttachedBasePosition now adds its authored base in fixed world axes, while existing particles retain their birth origins. Opposite third-person headings both show dust distributed around/through the character. Evidence: artifacts/verify/valkurm-f8-dust-translated-bias-slope-{north,opposite}.png.
close_reason: Corrected camera-attached particle origins to fixed world axes and passed opposite-heading live Dust Storm verification.

title: Retire superseded Bevy 0.19.0 light patch and restore pbr diagnostics on Bevy 0.19.1
description: Bevy 0.19.1 fixes the directional-light cascade queue crash upstream by resizing every thread-local queue before collection, so vendor/bevy_light and its patch entry are stale. The Bevy 0.19.1 lockfile also leaves vendor/bevy_pbr unused, unintentionally dropping Kuluu shadow-pass GPU timing. Remove the obsolete light fork and stale guidance; either rebase the pbr diagnostics patch onto 0.19.1 or explicitly retire it if the instrumentation no longer has a consumer. Add a guard that prevents required path patches from silently becoming unused after dependency updates.
acceptance_criteria: cargo metadata/tree emits no unused-patch warning; no stale guidance claims the local bevy_light crash fix is active; the bevy_pbr diagnostics decision is implemented and documented; focused checks pass.
notes: Bevy 0.19.1 cleanup completed: removed the obsolete vendor/bevy_light override; rebased vendor/bevy_pbr to pristine 0.19.1 plus only Kuluu's shadow-pass GPU diagnostic span; added a harness failure for Cargo.lock [[patch.unused]]. Stock bevy_light passed the 120-frame 2->3->4 cascade-count runtime repro. Cargo tree resolves stock bevy_light and the active local bevy_pbr patch with no unused warning. Full fmt, clippy, test, and build gates pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; full workspace gates pass.

title: cargo-guard false-fires on cold-cache CI: tree_cpu_secs flatlines while the build is progressing
description:
scripts/cargo-guard.sh reports 'WEDGE DETECTED -- no CPU progress for 180s' and SIGKILLs a healthy cargo on cold-cache GitHub runners. Root cause of the measurement failure is NOT yet known.

EVIDENCE (two runs, identical signature):
  - run 32397132673 (dependabot/cargo/tokio-1.53.1, 2026-08-20) test job
  - run 33635418305 (PR #512 wip-UI-Updates92, 2026-09-02) test job, died at 13m29s
Both fired at exactly 180s (= DEFAULT_STALL_SECS, i.e. last_progress never
advanced past start). Both name bevy_pbr with ~3min cumulative CPU alongside
rustc processes seconds old (32397132673: syn 00:20, tokio 00:11, cxx_build
00:02 | 33635418305: glam_matrix_extras 00:09, parry3d 00:04, obvhs 00:00).

PROOF IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE: in 33635418305 cargo printed 'Compiling obvhs' at
21:26:49.955 and the guard fired at 21:26:50.334 -- 0.4s later -- claiming 180s
of no progress. cargo was dispatching new units continuously through the window
it called stalled. Re-running the SAME commit did not trip the guard; the test
job instead failed 101 on a real compile error, which the guard had been
masking.

Note the detection path is tree_cpu_secs() (cumulative ps TIME summed over the
pid tree), NOT the %CPU column shown in the wedge report -- so the report's
'99.4' figures are cosmetic and cannot be used to argue either way.

HYPOTHESIS (unverified): tree_cpu_secs returns a constant (likely 0), so
'[ $cpu -gt $last_cpu ]' is never true and last_progress is pinned at start,
guaranteeing a fire at exactly stall_secs. Would explain the exact-180s timing
in both runs. Candidate causes: the ps/awk ppid walk failing to reach the cargo
root on that runner, or 'ps -Ao pid,ppid,time=' behaving differently there.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CI: if the measurement is broken it is latent locally
too, where the guard SIGKILLs real builds -- and locally there is no second
data point to notice it, since the advertised remedy is 'just re-run'.
design:
Mitigated in CI first (separate, already landed): ci.yml sets
CARGO_GUARD=0 + timeout-minutes, because the guard's premise is contention from
a second cargo (agent session, rust-analyzer, pre-push hook) and an ephemeral
runner has exactly one. That removes the blast radius but does NOT fix the
measurement, which is what this bead tracks.

Fix direction: make tree_cpu_secs falsifiable rather than silently degrading.
  1. Reproduce: log the sampled value each SAMPLE_SECS under a debug env knob
     and run on ubuntu-latest with a cold cache.
  2. Distinguish 'measured zero progress' from 'failed to measure'. An empty or
     unparseable sample must NOT be read as a stall -- today ${cpu:-0} silently
     converts a measurement failure into wedge evidence. Treat N consecutive
     failed samples as inconclusive and decline to kill.
  3. Pin it with a unit test feeding tree_cpu_secs synthetic ps output (Linux
     and macOS column layouts, header row present/absent, HH:MM:SS and
     DD-HH:MM:SS TIME forms).
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause of the flatline identified and stated, not guessed.
- A measurement failure can no longer be mistaken for a stall (the guard either
  measures progress or declines to act; it never kills on absent data).
- Test over synthetic ps output covering both platforms' column layouts and
  TIME formats, including the two captured CI signatures.
- Guard re-enabled in CI (drop CARGO_GUARD=0 from ci.yml) only if it earns its
  place there; otherwise close that out explicitly with the reasoning.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (reproduced locally 2026-09-02) -- tree_cpu_secs is not
monotonic, and the guard compares it against a high-water mark.

tree_cpu_secs sums 'ps' TIME over LIVE processes only. When a rustc unit exits,
its accumulated CPU time leaves the sum, so the total can DROP. But
cargo-guard.sh:115-118 only ever raises last_cpu:
    if [ "${cpu:-0}" -gt "${last_cpu:-0}" ]; then last_cpu=$cpu; last_progress=$now; fi
last_cpu is therefore a high-water mark, and last_progress stops advancing until
the live-tree sum EXCEEDS the widest-parallelism peak the build ever reached.

REPRODUCTION (6 CPU-burning children that exit, then one long-running child):
    t=3s  tree_cpu_secs=11   <- 6 children live; high-water mark set
    t=4s  tree_cpu_secs=0    <- children exited, their CPU left the sum
    t=9s  tree_cpu_secs=5    <- single child at 100% CPU, still under the mark
From t=4 the guard sees 'no progress' while the tree burns a full core.

WHY THIS MATCHES THE CI SIGNATURE EXACTLY:
  - Cold cache => wide parallel dep build sets a high mark; those units exit;
    the tail is a few long units. Current sum < mark forever => fires at
    precisely stall_secs (180s), which is what both captured runs show.
  - Explains why bevy_pbr is always named: it is simply what is still running
    in the taper.
  - Explains why warm-cache runs never trip it (few units, no high mark).
  - Explains why 'gh run rerun --failed' passes: different unit scheduling.

RULED OUT for the CI case -- this is NOT kuluu-yob2's lock queueing:
  - Run 32397132673 shows NO 'another cargo invocation is already running'
    startup notice, so others_running() was empty; note() demonstrably worked
    (the wedge lines printed).
  - Lock holder pid 3416 < every rustc pid (13458..15097), consistent with 3416
    being the guard's OWN cargo that spawned them.
  One cargo, its own tree, actively compiling. Same symptom as kuluu-yob2,
  different mechanism -- and this mechanism would also produce kuluu-yob2's
  release-gate failure without requiring two concurrent cargos, so that bead's
  stated cause should be re-examined against this one.

FIX: compare against the LAST sample, not the running maximum, and track
per-pid cumulative time so exited processes' CPU is retained (or sum
/proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime including reaped children via cutime/cstime).
Distinguish 'measured no progress' from 'failed to measure' while there.

2026-09-04: FOURTH occurrence, same signature, on a re-run of PR #512's CI
(run 33635418305, test job 101107478482) AFTER the CARGO_GUARD=0 fix had landed
on origin/main (19fdd66). Fired at exactly 180s again, naming bevy_render at
01:08 alongside bevy_light 00:26 / bevy_text 00:23 / bevy_core_pipeline 00:18 --
i.e. three units seconds old, so cargo was demonstrably still dispatching.
Note the named long unit is bevy_RENDER this time, not bevy_pbr: it is whatever
survives the taper, exactly as the high-water-mark mechanism predicts. That is
now four independent confirmations of the tree_cpu_secs diagnosis.

CI-SCOPE FINDING (matters for fork PRs): re-running an existing pull_request run
does NOT pick up a ci.yml fix that has since landed on the base branch -- gh run
rerun replays the original workflow file and merge ref. So a base-branch fix
cannot rescue an already-created fork PR by re-run alone; the fix has to be in
the PR's own branch. UNTESTED and do not assume: whether a FRESH run, triggered
by a new push to the fork branch, would pick up base ci.yml via a recomputed
merge ref.

title: cargo-guard kills a build queued behind another cargo's file lock (false WEDGE, failed the v0.6.0 release gate)
description: Release run 32769025619 (v0.6.0) CI-gate test job died exit 125: scripts/cargo-guard.sh declared 'WEDGE DETECTED - no CPU progress for 180s' while its own dump showed rustc at 99% CPU (bevy_pbr, 3m40s cumulative) and 'Holder of the build lock: pid 3597 (cargo)'. The guard samples cumulative CPU of ITS OWN cargo's process tree (tree_cpu_secs); a cargo queued behind another invocation's target-dir lock accrues none while the lock holder does all the work, so lock queueing is indistinguishable from the jobserver wedge it was built to catch. The pre-existing-cargo warning only fires for cargo processes alive at guard startup - a racer that starts after is invisible. Same trap as the workflow-worktree memory: lock contention is latency, not death.
notes:
Fix directions (pick one): (a) inside the stall branch, check whether another 'bin/cargo (build|test|check|...)' process exists and is accruing CPU - if so, reset last_progress and keep waiting (lock queueing, not wedge); (b) attribute progress from ANY rustc process, not just the watched tree; (c) find why two cargos ran concurrently in the release test job at all - the guard's advice 'no other cargo should be running concurrently' suggests the workflow step layout is the real bug. Immediate remedy used 2026-08-24: gh run rerun --failed, which passed.

2026-09-02 (from kuluu-52q3): this bead's stated cause -- a SECOND cargo queued
on the target-dir lock -- may not be needed to explain the v0.6.0 failure.
kuluu-52q3 reproduces a mechanism that produces the identical signature with
only ONE cargo: tree_cpu_secs sums live processes only, so exiting rustc units
REMOVE their CPU from the total, while last_cpu is only ever raised (a
high-water mark). After the wide parallel phase peaks and those units exit, the
sum can sit under the mark indefinitely while the build burns a full core --
firing at exactly stall_secs and naming whatever long unit remains (always
bevy_pbr). Re-check the v0.6.0 run for the 'another cargo invocation is already
running' startup notice: if it is ABSENT, there was no second cargo and this is
kuluu-52q3, not lock queueing. Fixing 52q3 may close this outright.

title: Discord report: PC renders decapitated (face/hair DAT missing) on Linux/retail install
description:
Sir Youda (Discord, 2026-08-23): character renders with no head on Linux (NVIDIA 4060ti, Vulkan backend), retail client files; headgear renders when equipped, so only the face/hair model is missing. jw has separately seen heads not load when pointing at HorizonXI's client files.

Investigation 2026-08-24: the face model is a single DAT pushed by resolve_face() in kuluu-render/src/look_resolver.rs and loaded like any equipment file in load_pc (kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs). Three ways it can vanish: (1) resolve_face returns None (face byte outside the per-race band) - this was SILENT until now; (2) read_dat fails (file missing/unreadable in the user's install) - warns 'equipment files resolved but unrendered'; (3) DAT reads but collect_skel_meshes()==0 - same warn. A full local retail install passes a survey of all 8 races x 32 faces (new diagnostic: ffxi-dat/examples/dat-face-survey.rs) except TarutaruF 24-31 (tracked separately), so the report is install- or server-value-specific, not reproducible here.
notes:
Sweep results 2026-08-24 (harness: actor-render-headless + pixel oracle, /tmp/face-sweep + /tmp/combo-sweep):
- All 8 races x 32 faces render correctly in isolation on a full retail install, EXCEPT HumeM face 16 (fid 7096 is a retail placeholder DAT: 0 usable vertices) and TaruF 24-31 (fids are ranged-motion DATs). Retail loads those same dead files, so those combos are headless on retail too - parity, not our bug.
- TaruM (the Discord report's race): all 32 faces pass alone AND 16 faces x 5 armor sets pass with a face-vs-no-face image-diff oracle. In-range faces cannot decapitate on a complete retail install.
- Root-cause divergence found in XIClient SkeletalMeshActor.cpp:489-494: retail CLAMPS an out-of-range model id to model 0 ('wrong GRP number') - a bad face byte renders face 0, never a missing head. Kuluu returned None and silently dropped the part. FIXED: resolve_face/resolve_equipment_slot now clamp like retail, with a warn on the face clamp.
- 'Base model without a head' (jw's observation): armor model id 0 always resolves to base clothing files while the face was the only silently-droppable part, so [valid race + zeroed/garbage armor + unresolvable face] rendered exactly that. Also default_pc_equipment includes face 0, which goes headless if the install cannot serve that fid (era-mismatched HorizonXI client files - their FFXiMain table differs from our baked modern bases).

FIELD UPDATE 2026-08-27: Sir Youda reports v0.6.0 (which contains both fixes above) did NOT resolve it - 'still have transparent head'. So the out-of-band-face clamp was not his root cause. Assumption audit found and addressed:
1. OBSERVABILITY GAP CLOSED: warns only reach stderr (EnvFilter default 'info'); a desktop-launched user never sees them and we never got logs. Added /actordiag [target]: chat-reports the full look->fid->path->bytes->meshes->textures chain incl per-texture max_alpha vs the 69/255 discard, plus root+overlay list. One screenshot now diagnoses any decapitation report.
2. LINUX CASE HOLE FIXED: base-install DAT resolution was exact-case ('.DAT' only) while overlays already probed both spellings. Retail's Windows fopen is case-insensitive, so a wine/launcher-assembled Linux install with lowercase '.dat' files is valid to the real client but was invisible to us. path_of now probes both spellings in the base install too (test: base_install_matches_a_lowercase_extension; fails on Linux CI without the fix, vacuous on macOS).
3. SILENT INVISIBILITY PATH IDENTIFIED (not yet ruled in/out): collect_textures drops Img chunks whose decode fails WITHOUT any warn; and a face texture that decodes with all alpha < 69/255 renders a present-but-fully-discarded mesh - literally a 'transparent head' with zero log output. /actordiag surfaces both (DECODE FAILED / max_alpha verdict).
4. Ruled out: hair/headgear visibility selection (we have none - all face meshes always drawn); actor LRU cache trapping a face-drop (key includes the face fid; a transient read failure could cache a headless look until restart, but his issue persists across restarts).
Local repro attempts stay negative: the dev install (itself HorizonXI-launcher-managed, 3 pivot overlays discovered) passes /actordiag clean for TaruM.
Next: ship in next release, ask reporter for /actordiag screenshot + whether install is HorizonXI-launcher-downloaded vs a true retail copy + whether GL mode differs.

title: Wide Scan list: bottom rows scroll under the clipped panel edge — cursor invisible at list end
description: With the fixed panel height (kuluu-xavp) and wrapped two-line rows, only ~20 of the 24 pooled rows fit; the scroll window's end-clamp (start.min(total-PANEL_ROWS)) pins the window to the last 24 rows near the end, letting the cursor walk to visual row 23 — below the clipped bottom edge (user video, Valkurm ~21-row list). Fix: remove the end-clamp so the cursor never sits lower than the window's middle row; the list end shows fewer trailing rows instead, which always fits the frame.
close_reason: panel_scroll_start keeps the cursor at/above the window middle (no end-clamp); verified live — wrapping to the last row shows the cursor fully inside the fixed panel with blank space below (list_end_cursor.png), wrap back to top intact (list_top_cursor.png). Commit 16a7160.

title: Map panel list height jitters while scrolling — fix it to a constant fraction of the viewport
description: The Wide Scan / Change Map / Markers panel is content-sized, so as the scroll window slides past rows that wrap to two lines the box height jumps every step. Retail's list box is a fixed-size frame. Fix: fixed Val::Percent height for the list submodes (command submenu stays auto-sized), overflow clipped.
close_reason: Fixed 55%-viewport panel height for list submodes (bottom edge pixel-identical at y=974 across cursor rows 0 and 5, height_row0/5.png) + command_cursor park/restore so Esc from Wide Scan lands on the Wide Scan row (cursor_restored.png). Generic MenuStack already keeps per-level cursors; Map screen was the lone offender. Commit 1ad3a4f.

title: Snapshot ingest cadence stalls ~150ms then bursts - root cause of self-motion leaps
description: self_sync trace (kuluu-render scene.rs, RUST_LOG=self_sync=trace) shows dirty-snapshot ingests during movement normally arrive per frame (~20ms) but stall for 100-270ms then deliver the accumulated displacement in one ingest (5 events in a 10s debug_drive). Likely the same hitch family as the render-thread SceneSnapshot deep-clone stutter (see perf program memory; /devhud instruments it). The self visual smoothing (see the jiggle bead) masks the symptom; the cadence stall itself is unfixed. Probes: camera_boom=trace and self_sync=trace.

title: Wide Scan retail layout: list panel on the LEFT, left/right pages the list, selection is an orange crosshair
description: Retail reference (user screenshot, North Gustaberg): the Wide Scan list is a left-edge panel (command submenu buttons stay top-right); left/right page the long list; the selected row is marked on the map with a large orange crosshair centered on the entity, not a ring. Our list sits top-right for all submodes, left/right are dead in the list, and the selection marker is a hollow ring. Fix: flip the panel to the left in WideScan submode only; page cursor by PANEL_ROWS on NavLeft/NavRight (clamped) in WideScan and Change Map; restyle MapWidescanCursorMarker as a retail-style crosshair (two thin bars).
close_reason: Landed in 02d241e: PANEL_LEFT_PX flip for WideScan submode, page_cursor (PANEL_ROWS, clamped) on NavLeft/NavRight in WideScan+ChangeMap, WIDESCAN_CURSOR_CROSS crosshair replaces the ring. Verified live vs the user's retail reference: layout_widescan_left.png / layout_paged*.png.

title: Weather HUD icon: replace tofu emoji with retail usgaiji element sprites
description: The weather widget rendered Unicode emoji (U+1F32A etc.) through the bundled FiraMono subset, so every icon was a tofu box. Retail draws weather as the eight element icons in the 'font    usgaiji ' UI-element group (one icon for single weather, two for its double, research/xim Compass.kt:69-96; group name confirmed in research/XIClient Constants/Strings.h:24). Also: UI DATs now resolve via VTABLE/FTABLE file ids (13/39542/39551/39560) instead of hardcoded ROM paths, so installs at other patch levels with a shuffled physical ROM layout still resolve; shared read_ui_dats() replaces four per-consumer path loops.
close_reason: Closed

title: De-ship ffxi-nav-recast from the distributed client (recast-nav feature; agent/dev only)
description: User direction 2026-08-20: recast exists for /pathto (a dev-ease command) and should not ship in the default player binary — it belongs with the 'botty' surfaces (kuluu-mcp / agent) or a dev/QoL flavor. Evidence: only consumers are kuluu-session/src/reactor.rs (pathto/goal pathing; loads meshes exclusively from dev-checkout paths vendor/server/navmeshes, research/Phoenix/navmeshes, or FFXI_NAVMESH_DIR — a distributed player has none, and the reactor already falls back to straight-line when no mesh loads) and kuluu/src/view_native/navmesh_overlay.rs (debug overlay). kuluu-render/minimap no longer references it (CLAUDE.md 'minimap culling' note is stale — fix while here). Design: make ffxi-nav-recast an optional dep of kuluu-session behind a recast-nav feature; default OFF for the shipped kuluu binary, ON for kuluu-mcp and dev builds. Decide interaction with the single-feature-set principle (CLAUDE.md build section), checks.sh invocations, release legs, and deck-build-sync. Payoff: smaller player binary, botty machinery out of the player client, and deletion of the C++-bridge CXXFLAGS overrides threaded through all six release legs / docker / .cargo/config.toml (ring/blake3 C deps do not need them). Note: does NOT replace crt-static (kuluu-ddgn) — the C deps still import the CRT.

title: Release: native aarch64 legs for Linux and Windows
description: Add two release.yml build legs on GitHub's free-for-public-repos native ARM runners: ubuntu-24.04-arm producing kuluu-<tag>-aarch64-linux.tar.gz and windows-11-arm producing kuluu-<tag>-aarch64-windows.zip. Audiences: Asahi Linux / ARM SBCs / headless-agent ARM cloud boxes (linux), Snapdragon laptops + the retail-observe Parallels Windows-on-ARM VM on this host (windows — currently runs the x86_64 build under Prism emulation). Both runners build natively so no cross toolchain; CXXFLAGS must be blanked like the sibling legs so the Recast C++ bridge builds. Verification: linux-arm binary smoke-tested in the colima aarch64 VM; windows-arm in the Parallels VM. Publish gate includes both legs.
close_reason: Shipped in v0.5.1: kuluu-v0.5.1-aarch64-linux.tar.gz + kuluu-v0.5.1-aarch64-windows.zip built natively on ubuntu-24.04-arm / windows-11-arm, both gating publish. Rehearsed on a publish-disabled branch first, which caught the windows-arm Cranelift component wedge (fixed via RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN bypass). aarch64-linux binary runtime-verified natively in the colima arm64 VM (clap usage printed); aarch64-windows checksum-verified only — Parallels VMs currently 'invalid', run-proof deferred. Updater arch-selection requirement recorded on kuluu-fwz.

title: CI gate never compiles wasm32 — wasm breaks only surface on the release leg
description: v0.5.0's first release run failed on the Build (browser WASM) leg: new consumers (camera far plane via skybox::camera_far, nameplate mip raster via zone_texture::image_with_mips, look_resolver::dispatch_mount_models registration) referenced natively-gated modules from ungated code. scripts/checks.sh fmt/clippy/test/build never target wasm32-unknown-unknown, so the breakage was invisible until the release pipeline (delayed the v0.5.0 release by ~1.5h; recovery = delete tag, fix, re-push per cut-release skill). Fix: add a cheap 'cargo check -p kuluu-render -p kuluu-viewer-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown' stage to checks.sh (and the CI gate) so the boundary is enforced at push time. The fix commit is 4f03d0b; the recovered release is v0.5.0.
notes:
2026-09-09 adversarial done-check (triage flagged it as landed): NOT fully done. Evidence: The bead's fix asks for a `cargo check -p kuluu-render -p kuluu-viewer-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` stage in scripts/checks.sh "(and the CI gate) so the boundary is enforced at push time."

What exists in /tmp/kuluu-wt/probe (= main, matches /Users/jon/src/ffxi):
- scripts/checks.sh:256-258 has a `run_wasm()` stage: `cargo check -p kuluu-viewer-wasm --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (only `-p kuluu-viewer-wasm`, not also `-p kuluu-render`; though kuluu-viewer-wasm depends on kuluu-render per kuluu-viewer-wasm/Cargo.toml:54, so kuluu-render is still transitively type-checked).
- scripts/checks.sh:294 wires it into the stage dispatcher (`wasm) ... run_wasm`).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:115-129 adds a separate `wasm` job that installs the wasm32 target and runs `scripts/checks.sh wasm` — this landed in commit d2be7b36 ("build(dlss): pin optional SDK and stage release runtim
Remaining: Add `scripts/checks.sh wasm` (or equivalent) to `.githooks/pre-push` so a wasm32 break is caught locally before push, matching the bead's "enforced at push time" language — likely gated similarly to clippy (skippable under PREPUSH_FAST since it requires a target/toolchain that may not be installed) or documented as a known gap if intentionally deferred to CI-only. Also consider making `run_wasm()` explicitly check `-p kuluu-render` alongside `-p kuluu-viewer-wasm` per the bead's literal proposal, even though it's currently covered transitively.

title: Gamepad left-stick X does nothing on any preset - routed via StrafeLeft/Right, which no preset binds
description:
kuluu/src/view_native/gamepad_input.rs:175-181 resolves left-stick X through bound_key(&bindings, Action::StrafeLeft / StrafeRight). Every shipped preset leaves both unbound - kuluu-render/src/keybinds/presets.rs:177-178 (Compact1), :196-197 (Compact2, the default), :222-223 (Standard) all assert get(StrafeLeft/StrafeRight) == None; keyboard A/D are TurnLeft/TurnRight instead (presets.rs:104-105, 121-122, 138-139). bound_key returns None, so the stick-X branch synthesizes nothing: pushing the left stick sideways is silently dropped on every preset. Stick Y works because MoveForward/MoveBackward are bound everywhere.

Repro: default preset, any pad - push left stick fully left; the character neither turns nor steers. (Static analysis 2026-08-20; confirm once live on hardware.)

Near-term fix: fall back to TurnLeft/TurnRight when Strafe is unbound - matches retail unlocked movement, where horizontal input is camera-relative steer (exactly what resolve_move_inputs does with TurnLeft/TurnRight when not locked, input.rs:157-188). Real fix: the direct analog injection in kuluu-uos3.5 removes the key round-trip entirely. Either way, add a regression test asserting every preset yields a usable stick-X mapping.
close_reason: Fixed by direct analog injection: left stick feeds PadStickIntent consumed by dispatch_movement_system as f32 axes (pf/ps + merge_dir), no longer routed through StrafeLeft/Right key synthesis, so it works on every keyboard preset.

title: Retail-faithful gamepad bindings: adopt retail's 27-function pad model with Pattern-E/PS2 defaults and direct analog axes
description:
Current layer: kuluu/src/view_native/gamepad_input.rs (369 lines, Steam Deck era) is a hardcoded button->synthetic-keyboard shim: sticks digitized at STICK_DEADZONE=0.35 into held movement/camera keys, South/East/West/North = confirm/cancel/lock-on/menu, d-pad = nav (Right doubles as CycleTarget in world), bumpers = camera zoom, R2 = OpenChat. Unmapped physical inputs: L2, Start, Select, L3/R3. Unreachable retail functions: autorun, first/third-person toggle, heal/lock on stick click, select-active-window, screenshot, logout window, hide-all-windows, and both macro palettes.

Retail model (researched 2026-08-20; sources in NOTES): pad config is external to the game (FFXiPadConfig.exe, launched from the title config menu; the client suspends pad input while its window exists - research/XIClient .../Input/GamepadConfigMonitor.cpp) and stored in the registry as padmode000 (6 flags: enable gamepad / force feedback / sliders / hat switches / when-inactive / XInput; XInput added in the Nov 10 2015 update together with the "Pattern E" preset) and padsin000: 27 comma-separated slots, one per game FUNCTION, each holding a button/axis id, -1 = unassigned (documented at docs.ashitaxi.com/usage/configurations/; live examples in vendor/game-files/config/boot/horizonxi.ini:527-538 and ashita.ini:102).

The 27-slot retail function table:
0 toggle autorun | 1 CTRL macro bar | 2 first/third person | 3 ALT macro bar | 4 toggle /heal + lock target | 5 cancel | 6 main menu | 7 confirm | 8 select active window | 9 hide all windows | 10 menu-nav-with-move-stick (held) | 11 camera-with-move-stick (held) | 12 logout window | 13-16 movement axes | 17-20 camera axes | 21-24 menu movement / field targeting (d-pad) | 25 screenshot | 26 controls-operate toggle.

Pattern E (XInput) value 8,9,13,12,10,0,1,3,2,15,-1,-1,14,-33,-33,32,32,-36,-36,35,35,6,7,5,4,11,-1 decodes to the canonical PS2 layout: Cross/A confirm, Circle/B cancel, Square/X main menu, Triangle/Y select active window, L1/LB autorun, R1/RB screenshot, L2/LT CTRL macro palette, R2/RT ALT macro palette, L3 heal/lock, R3 view toggle, Start logout, Select/Back hide windows, d-pad menu+targeting, left stick move (partial deflection = walk; no backpedal - stick-down turns the character around), right stick camera (Y inverted).

XIClient (research/XIClient .../Input/InputManager.{h,cpp}) confirms the runtime shape: DirectInput8 pad polled beside keyboard/mouse in one InputManager::Process(); a shared action table where each action carries separate pad and keyboard analog handlers and GetAnalogKey (InputManager.cpp:1023-1057) resolves pad-vs-keyboard by larger magnitude.
design:
1. Model bindings as retail FUNCTIONS, not keys: a PadAction enum mirroring the 27-slot table (digital functions + three analog groups: movement / camera / menu). PadBindings resource = BTreeMap<PadAction, GamepadButton> plus per-group deadzone/invert scalars, persisted as gamepad.json via a store cloned from kuluu/src/keybinds_store.rs. Presets: Retail (Pattern-E layout expressed against gilrs/Bevy's Xbox-logical names) as default, plus Custom overrides - same preset+sparse-overrides shape as PersistedKeybinds.
2. Retire the synthetic-keyboard shim in two steps. Digital: dispatch PadActions straight into the existing Action layer / InputMode handlers instead of synthesizing KeyCode/KeyboardInput (removes the logical_key_for hazard class entirely - kuluu-obha). Analog: inject stick vectors directly into dispatch_movement_system beside ResolvedMoveInputs (precedent: the debug_ctrl.active_drive override, input.rs:736-743) so magnitude drives walk/run (retail: partial deflection = walk) and camera rate, replacing the 8-held-keys digitization at 0.35 deadzone. When pad and keyboard both produce an analog value, retail's rule applies: larger magnitude wins (XIClient GetAnalogKey).
3. Fill the retail default map including the currently missing functions: autorun (Action::ToggleAutorun exists), first/third person (ToggleFirstPerson), L3 heal/lock (ToggleLockOn already has the contextual heal semantics), Y select active window (TogglePassiveCursor/SelectActiveWindow), RB screenshot, Start logout window, Back hide-all-windows (needs a HUD-visibility action if absent). Slot 26 (controls-operate toggle) is PlayOnline-era; explicitly out of scope. Slots 10/11 (menu-nav/camera with move stick while held) are for single-stick pads; defer.
4. LT/RT macro palettes (slots 1/3) are blocked on kuluu-mco (no macro system exists); wire the two PadActions once it lands - retail semantics per kuluu-mco NOTES (hold/toggle bar, d-pad selects, confirm fires, trigger+up/down pages).
5. Config UI: the Gamepad tab this epic (kuluu-uos3) lists as unscoped - enable pad, invert camera Y, deadzones, per-function rebind with press-to-detect, preset select. Menu help bar gains pad glyphs (pad variant of Bindings::key_label; retail ships Xbox button icons as ROM/119/50.DAT "abxy360" per research/cexi-docs/ui/export.md:249).
6. Optional, enhanced, later: import an existing padsin000/padmode000 (registry dump or HorizonXI/Ashita ini) via the Ashita-documented XInput id table for players migrating from retail.
7. Backend: bevy_gilrs is already enabled (bevy "default_platform", Cargo.toml:100-118) and covers XInput on Windows plus Steam Deck (Steam Input presents an XInput/SDL device) - no Steamworks Input API needed. Keep the PrimaryGamepad single-device guard (gamepad_input.rs:28-51, Deck dual-mirror workaround) and add the GamepadAxisHeld-successor state to the OnExit(InGame) drain (bevy-lifecycle-symmetry; second defect in kuluu-obha).
acceptance_criteria: With a default profile on an Xbox-layout pad: every Pattern-E function above dispatches its retail semantic (d-pad targets in field / navigates in menus, Y cycles active window, LB toggles autorun, A with no target opens the action window, stick partial-deflection walks, stick-down turns around rather than backpedaling); pad input works identically regardless of which keyboard preset is active; unit tests pin the Retail preset table, the pad-vs-keyboard larger-magnitude rule, and lifecycle drain on leaving InGame.
notes:
Sources: docs.ashitaxi.com/usage/configurations/ (padmode000/padsin000 + XInput id table); forum.square-enix.com/ffxi/threads/49065 + /50091 (Nov 10 2015 XInput update, official setup); ffxiclopedia Controller + Troubleshooting: Controls (PS2 defaults); research/XIClient Input/ (InputManager, GamepadConfigMonitor); vendor/game-files/config/boot/{horizonxi,ashita,lsb}.ini (live padmode/padsin profiles); research/xim GamepadManager.kt (non-authoritative precedent). Kuluu-side map from 2026-08-20 exploration: gamepad_input.rs (existing shim), keybinds_store.rs (persistence template), input_mode.rs MenuStack (menu model already pad-drivable), text_input/mod.rs modal router.
2026-08-20 first increment landed: PadAction/PadBindings retail model (kuluu-render/src/keybinds/pad.rs) with Pattern-E defaults pinned by test; gamepad.json store (kuluu/src/padbinds_store.rs, sparse overrides over retail defaults); synthetic-keyboard shim replaced by PadPressed direct Action dispatch + PadKeyEvent side-channel for the modal router; sticks are true analog (PadStickIntent) with radial deadzone 0.20, retail larger-magnitude pad-vs-keyboard merge (pick_mag), continuous camera-relative run direction, stick-back autorun cancel, rest-break edges, camera-recenter integration. Retail roles live: A confirm, B cancel, X main menu, Y active window, LB autorun, RB screenshot, L3 heal/lock, R3 view toggle, Back hide windows, d-pad menu-nav + field target cycling (+ fishing reel). Interim deviation: RT=OpenChat until kuluu-mco lands (then RT->AltMacroBar); LT/Start parsed but inert. Remaining: macro palettes (blocked on kuluu-mco), logout window on Start, Gamepad config tab UI + pad glyphs in help bar, walk-on-partial-deflection (needs walk-gait wiring, deferred), padsin000 import.

title: Widescan track has no directional pointer outside the map — retail shows a tracking arrow on the compass
description: After WidescanTrack (0x0F5 stream), retail draws an arrow on its compass dial pointing at the tracked entity. Our compass is an N/NE text chip (kuluu-render/src/hud/compass.rs) with no dial. Adaptation: a small rotated pin next to/in the compass chip, visible only while tracked, pointing toward the target relative to the camera facing (camera-forward XZ from OperatorCamera GlobalTransform; target from local entity transform else raw 0x0F5 coords with the LSB y/z swap). Reuse the minimap pin idiom (pin_border_radius + PIN_TIP_BEARING) and TRACKED_MARKER_COLOR so it matches the map's tracked marker.
close_reason: Compass track pointer: rotated pin beside the compass chip pointing at the 0x0F5 target camera-relative; track survives map close (retail c2s 0x0F6 semantics) and Esc-cancel clears it locally (fa450b0 — server answers END with silence, not Lose). Verified live (after_cancel.png, cancel_cleared_*.png). Commits 445a661 + fa450b0.

title: Wide Scan cursor selection is not highlighted on the map
description: Moving the cursor through the Wide Scan list gives no map feedback; retail highlights the selected hit's dot. Add a cursor ring marker on the full-screen map at the selected row's entry position (local entity transform when spawned, rel_x/rel_z otherwise), shown only in the WideScan submode, styled with the list cursor color so selection reads across both surfaces.
close_reason: Cursor ring (WIDESCAN_CURSOR_RING_PX, theme::CURSOR) follows the selected row's entity on the map; verified live (ws_cursor_row0/row3.png). Commit 445a661.

title: Widescan rows show generic 'Mob' on real servers — resolve names client-side from the zone NPC-name DAT like retail
description: Observed on HorizonXI (66.85.159.114): a 36-entry 0x0F4 burst renders as generic 'Mob' rows. Retail semantics (research/XiPackets/world/server/0x00F4/README.md): the client resolves Type 1/2 (npc/mob) names ITSELF from the ActIndex; sName is only an override, and a Type 0 (char) entry with no sName is hidden entirely (no row, no dot). The client-side source for unspawned entities is the zone NPC-name DAT that ffxi-dat::npc_names already parses and kuluu-session's NpcNameResolver already lazy-loads. Fix: (1) compose_id(zone, act_index) helper in ffxi-dat (inverse of split_id); (2) enrich empty-name non-char 0x0F4 entries in handle_sub_packet via NpcNameResolver before emitting WidescanEntryReceived; (3) retail-hide unnamed kind-0 entries in widescan_rows and update_map_widescan_dots; (4) kind constants exported from ffxi-proto so 0/1/2 isn't retyped.
close_reason: Session enriches empty-sName 0x0F4 entries from the zone NPC-name DAT (compose_id(zone, act_index) -> NpcNameResolver), matching retail's client-side resolution (XiPackets 0x00F4); unnamed CHAR entries now hidden like retail. Verified live: artifacts/verify/widescan_names.png shows 17/17 real names.

title: Missing retail Config page: Mouse/Cam 4-way inversion + sensitivity (hardcoded)
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. Retail's Config menu has horizontal+vertical inversion toggles for both Camera and Mouse; Kuluu has none (grep invert/sensitivity: no hits) and sensitivity is hardcoded (kuluu-render/src/mouse.rs:9-11 MOUSE_YAW_SENS/MOUSE_PITCH_SENS=0.005). The in-game Config menu is keybind presets only (hud/menu.rs:249-255). This is a missing-vanilla feature, and it is also the escape hatch if the camera-relative movement reading (kuluu-client/src/view_native/input.rs:150-186, argued faithful from a 2026-07-20 HorizonXI capture) turns out wrong - that dispute needs a retail capture, not a code read.

title: Status-ribbon countdown timers are unflagged non-retail (the adjacent tooltip IS gated)
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. kuluu-render/src/hud/status_ribbon.rs:157-171 draws remaining-time text under every buff chip, registered unconditionally at hud/mod.rs:262; the code itself notes 'Retail draws no timer here at all.' Meanwhile the buff TOOLTIP is behind enhanced-buff-tooltips - inconsistent. Gate the timers the same way (or fold both into one runtime Enhanced toggle per the DynamicLights pattern).
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (00e599a5, 52ad563b) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Review-fix commit 388fef0c on wt/kuluu-m9hj. The enhanced-buff-timers gating exposed a pre-existing gap: no check stage ever compiled ANY enhanced-* feature, so enhanced-buff-tooltips, enhanced-cast-bar, enhanced-mob-hp-under and enhanced-job-display had been type-check-free too. scripts/checks.sh now has an `enhanced` stage (workspace clippy -D warnings + workspace test under native-window + every enhanced-* feature kuluu declares except enhanced-neural-uplift, which needs the DLSS SDK), wired into ci.yml as a dedicated `enhanced` job with cache-key ci-enhanced. The feature list is scraped from kuluu/Cargo.toml so it self-maintains. Deliberately excluded: the pre-push hook (speed; it stops at clippy) and the `debug-menu` dev-only feature, which remains ungated -- worth a follow-up bead if dev-menu rot is a concern. Also of note: the whole enhanced family currently compiles and tests clean, so the new leg is green from day one.
Unknowns left open: The first full `scripts/checks.sh enhanced` run failed in the kuluu doctest target with E0463 can't find crate for kuluu_render/kuluu_session. Re-running the doctest leg with identical features passed (exit 0), and the same leg passes on the vanilla feature set, so this reads as an artifact race in  | ci.yml was not machine-validated as YAML on this box (no PyYAML, no yq); the new job block was written to mirror the existing test/wasm jobs exactly and reviewed by eye. | The new CI job adds a third full workspace compile+test to every PR (its own dep cache key ci-enhanced). Wall-clock impact is parallel with clippy/test, but it is a real runner-minutes cost that may want trimming later (e.g. clippy-only, or -p kuluu-render scope).
close_reason: Landed on main 00e599a5, 52ad563b after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Minimap is an unflagged always-on radar: mob/NPC/PC dots, default-visible, plus duplicate compass
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. Retail has a summoned map, not a persistent minimap, and its map is not a live entity radar. kuluu-render/src/minimap/mod.rs:27-32 MinimapVisible defaults true; minimap/overlay.rs:125-131 MarkerFilters::default() enables Npc|Mob|Pc|Pet dots; hud/compass.rs is spawned twice (minimap/mod.rs:366 AND hud/mod.rs:116). Model on the DynamicLights pattern (graphics/settings.rs:88-117 - runtime Vanilla/Enhanced enum, #[default] Vanilla): minimap+radar become an Enhanced runtime setting defaulting off/party-only; /minimap stays as the toggle.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (747c16af, 17ffb107, 8b0e0211) after adversarial review (rounds: needs_fix, needs_fix, approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
2026-09-09 round-3 pass (commit 838fa9b8 on wt/kuluu-7cqw).

Round-2 review returned needs_fix with three issues; all three premises were verified against the source and all three are fixed. No finding was refuted.

WHAT LANDED

(1) Correctness: the vanilla mask was dropping party dots on selection. marker_category() (overlay.rs) resolves the Target role BEFORE Party; sync_marker_layer filtered on that resolved category and then despawned every dot not in `seen`. So targeting or locking on a party member reclassified her as Target - a bit VANILLA_CATEGORIES_MASK does not set - and her dot disappeared from both the minimap and the Map screen. That is the ordinary healer flow, and the round-2 test missed it because it only targeted a Mob.

Fix: new marker_visible() decides visibility from the underlying kind/party category, with the role strictly additive -
  filters.is_visible(marker_category(kind, is_party, false))
    || (is_role_target && filters.is_visible(MarkerCategory::Target))
A selection can now only ADD a dot, never subtract one the player's own filter already shows. marker_category() keeps its role-first order, which is still what colours the fill and ring; only the visibility decision changed.

(2) Documentation grounding: the "legend toggles are the player's manual override" claim was unbacked. There is no legend UI anywhere in the tree - MarkerFilters::set/toggle and MarkerCategory::swatch_color have zero non-test callers. Removed the claim from overlay.rs (MarkerFilters doc), minimap/mod.rs (apply_minimap_radar_setting doc), the assertion message in the radar_setting_owns_the_defaults test, and the marker_category doc line. They now say the categories are settings-owned until a per-category UI exists, and that /minimap show|hide|toggle is the only genuine manual override today. The identical claim in the earlier commit message (5ec82378) is retracted in 838fa9b8's message rather than by rewriting branch history.

(3) hud/mod.rs's single-CompassLabel comment credited update_compass_track_pointer with a single_mut() it does not use - compass.rs:129 is iter_mut() over CompassTrackPointer. Only update_compass (compass.rs:82) backs the invariant; the comment now says so.

HOW VERIFIED
- cargo test -p kuluu-render: 1041 lib + all integration suites, 0 failed (output showed Compiling from /private/tmp/kuluu-wt/kuluu-7cqw, so it is this worktree).
- cargo test -p kuluu: 417 pass, 0 failed.
- clippy -D warnings clean on kuluu-render and kuluu; cargo fmt --all --check clean; scripts/checks.sh style clean.
- Mutation check (the important one): temporarily reverting marker_visible to the old resolved-category behaviour makes BOTH new tests FAIL - targeting_never_hides_a_dot_its_own_category_shows and the extended sync_marker_layer_skips_filtered_category. The tests genuinely pin the fix.
- Shared-target-dir gotcha: a stale cross-worktree ffxi-dat rlib made kuluu-render fail to compile (extract_lens_flare_sheet vs ..._sheets). Fixed by touching ffxi-dat/src/lib.rs to force a rebuild from this worktree - not a branch defect.

STILL OPEN
- Party in VANILLA_CATEGORIES_MASK remains an UNVERIFIED INFERENCE. The grounded retail fact on record is the negative (a summoned static map, not a live entity radar); whether retail's map screen plots party members has not been observed. The mask comment says so explicitly. A retail-observe session on the map screen would settle it and is the last grounding gap on this bead.
- MarkerCategory::Target's swatch_color and MarkerFilters::set/toggle still have no production callers; they are the surface a future per-category filter UI would consume.
Unknowns left open: Party remains an unverified inference for the vanilla mask - no retail map-screen observation has been made confirming that retail's summoned map plots party members. The mask comment already says so; a retail-observe session would settle it. | MarkerCategory::Target's swatch_color and MarkerFilters::set/toggle still have no production callers. They are the surface a future per-category UI would use, but until then Target's bit is only ever set by MinimapRadar::Enhanced. | The commit message of 5ec82378 still contains the retracted legend claim; it is corrected in the new commit rather than amended, since rewriting the branch was judged riskier than a follow-up retraction. | kuluu test count is 417 here vs the reviewer's reported 424 - both runs report 0 failed; difference not investigated (likely a differing set of self-skipping live-server fixtures).
Correction from user retail screenshot and primary Square Enix manual (2026-09-09): retail DOES have a persistent lower-left compass radar above chat. The summoned map/terrain minimap distinction must not suppress this compass. Its dots use their own palette (PC blue, NPC green, party pink, pets yellow, eligible-job monsters red); the existing MarkerFilters only describe the separate map surfaces. Follow-up implementation and exact evidence: kuluu-k8lj.
close_reason: Landed on main 747c16af, 17ffb107, 8b0e0211 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed, how it was verified, and what stays open.

title: Four debug chat lines use ToastEvent::system and bypass the devhud filter
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. kuluu-render/src/debug_chat.rs:38,40,75,77 (engaged-by/low-HP/speed emoji lines), sun_moon.rs:521,536,553 (sunrise/moonrise lines), hud/vana_clock.rs:101 (day rollover), weather.rs:353 (DAT-loader telemetry) all emit ToastEvent::system, so they print in normal player chat. The dev_hud filter (snapshot.rs chat_line_visible) already suppresses ToastEvent::debug lines. Fix: switch all four sites to ToastEvent::debug.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (18e8a36e) after adversarial review (round-1 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Fixed on branch wt/kuluu-ka0m, commit 22dced5c9cd7be26e9f56484c285d374ee06d10c. All seven emitters called out in the description now use ToastEvent::debug instead of ToastEvent::system: debug_chat.rs (engaged-by / low-HP / zone-change in report_engagement_events_system, and speed suppressed/restored in report_speed_state_system), sun_moon.rs (sunrise/sunset, moonrise/moonset, moon-phase), hud/vana_clock.rs (Vana'diel day rollover) and weather.rs (zone-weather DAT loader telemetry). They therefore now fall under the existing dev-HUD gate in snapshot.rs:120, chat_line_visible(channel, dev_hud) = dev_hud || channel != ChatChannel::Debug, and no longer print in normal player chat. To make the sun_moon/vana_clock/weather lines testable without a full render App, the three inline format! + write calls were lifted into small toast constructors (sun_transition_toast, moon_transition_toast, moon_phase_toast, vana_day_rollover_toast, zone_weather_loaded_toast); the systems now just write the constructor's result, so behavior and text are unchanged. Verified by five new unit tests that use a real oracle rather than a name check: debug_chat's two tests run the actual Bevy systems plus drain_toast_events over a minimal App and assert each drained ChatLine is invisible at dev_hud=false and visible at dev_hud=true; the other three assert both the exact rendered text and chat_line_visible in both directions for the extracted constructors. cargo test -p kuluu-render passes (lib 1039/0, all integration targets green), cargo clippy -p kuluu-render --all-targets -D warnings is clean, cargo fmt --check and scripts/checks.sh style pass. No wire/snapshot/AgentCommand contract touched; no retail grounding needed (product-only debug tooling). Follow-up candidate found while grepping: kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:505 still emits the "Now playing: ..." BGM line as ToastEvent::system, which looks like the same class of client telemetry; hud/auction.rs:1013 and kuluu/src/view_native/screenshot.rs:55 also still use ::system but are plausibly deliberate player-facing feedback. Operational note: the shared /tmp/kuluu-wt-target is being clobbered between concurrent worktrees, so only cargo runs that print "Compiling kuluu-render ... /tmp/kuluu-wt/kuluu-ka0m/kuluu-render" reflect this branch.
Unknowns left open: Three ToastEvent::system call sites remain outside this bead's scope and were left alone: kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:505 (the "Now playing: <track> by <composer> [track #N, slot=...]" BGM line), kuluu-render/src/hud/auction.rs:1013, and kuluu/src/view_native/screenshot.rs:55. The audio one looks like | No retail oracle was consulted: triage marks this not_applicable (product-only devhud/debug-chat filtering). The only vanilla-parity claim relied on is the negative one already stated in the bead - these client-generated lines have no retail equivalent and so must not appear in the player chat log. | The debug chat strings keep their existing non-ASCII glyphs (arrows, U+2694, U+2764, U+270B, U+2600, U+263E, U+1F4C5, U+26C5, em dash). That predates this change and checks.sh style only hard-fails under kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/, so it was left as-is; whether these render as tofu in the ch
close_reason: Landed on main 18e8a36e after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Nameplates blend under lens flare / particles: missing Transparent3d sort bias
description: Plates are AlphaMode::Blend with default depth_bias 0, so camera-anchored transparent quads (lens flare AlphaMode::Add, weather) rank nearest in Bevy's view-Z Transparent3d sort and draw over the names; fire particles near a mob can also outrank the plate. Retail draws names in a late screen-space pass (CXiActorNameDraw) over effects. Fix: uniform positive Material::depth_bias on plate materials so plates outrank all unbiased world transparents while keeping plate-vs-plate order and opaque depth testing (same mechanism as the kuluu-w4jf sky-layer fix).
close_reason: NAMEPLATE_SORT_BIAS (= SKYBOX_RADIUS) on the plate StandardMaterial; plates now sort after lens flare/weather/particle quads in Transparent3d. Same mechanism as the kuluu-w4jf sky-layer fix; pinned by plates_outrank_camera_anchored_transparents test. Live flare-over-plate eyeball pending next GUI session.

title: Nameplate legibility: bigger plates, thicker opaque outline, depth-scale floor, mipmapped plate texture
description: Nameplates track retail closely but retail's 640x480-era sizing reads too small/thin/low-contrast on modern displays. User asked for plates readable at any distance and in all circumstances. Deliberate legibility nudges layered on the retail-faithful ramp (precedent: NAMEPLATE_LEGIBILITY_SCALE): raise legibility scale, floor the depth ramp, thicken + opacify the outline, faux-bold the glyphs, and mip the plate texture so minified names stop aliasing.
close_reason: Landed: legibility scale 1.15->1.3, depth-ramp floor 0.45 (retail ramp function untouched, tests pinned), outline 5px->7px fully opaque, faux-bold 2px dilate, mip-chained plate texture (was aliasing under minification). Verified via raster preview composited over light/mid/dark at simulated 1440p on-screen sizes.

title: Fullscreen map washes out over bright scenes — add backdrop scrim + raise map alpha
description: MAP_IMAGE_ALPHA=0.86 alone lets ~14% of the scene bleed through the parchment; over a bright sunlit scene (Valkurm sand, PC silhouette) the map loses contrast and legibility varies with whatever is behind it. Fix: draw a semi-transparent black backdrop between the 3D scene and the map image so scene luminance is damped uniformly, and raise the image alpha slightly; scene remains faintly visible (retail keeps the world visible behind the map — xim MapDrawer draws the map UI element at Color(1,1,1,0.5), tier-6 evidence only). Exact retail compositing could not be observed: the Parallels VM is invalid (Sidecar volume retired), and XIClient does not implement the map UI. Re-calibrate against retail via retail-observe when the VM is restored.
close_reason: Black scrim (alpha 0.40) spawned under the map image, MAP_IMAGE_ALPHA 0.86 -> 0.90; scene contribution drops from a scene-dependent 14% to a steady ~6%. Retail calibration deferred until the Parallels VM is restored.

title: Focusing the chat input cancels auto-run
description: Toggling auto-run and then opening the chat input line (e.g. typing '/') stopped the character. dispatch_movement_system lumped InputMode::Chat in with the modal screens (Dialog/DeliveryBox/Check/Bazaar/Auction) and cleared AutoRun::phantom_forward. Retail keeps auto-run running while the input line is focused.
acceptance_criteria: With auto-run engaged, opening the chat input keeps the character running; keystrokes typed into the buffer do not drive movement or camera.
close_reason: Chat is no longer in the autorun-cancel set; while focused its keystrokes are hidden from movement/camera via an inert ButtonInput and phantom_forward keeps driving. Pinned by mode_cancels_autorun/mode_swallows_keys tests.

title: Fullscreen map markers drift west: Bevy 0.19 ImageNode Auto contain-fits instead of stretching
description: Bevy 0.19 bevy_ui_render draws NodeImageMode::Auto images aspect-preserved contain-fit centered in the node box (bevy_ui_render-0.19.0 src/lib.rs:539), regardless of the node's layout size. The Map screen's MapScreenImage is laid out 100%x100% of the viewport but the square 512x512 map texture renders as a centered height-fit square, while the marker overlay percent-positions dots across the full viewport width — so every marker lands west of its true map location for points west of center (east of, for points east). Vertical is coincidentally correct because the fit square's height equals the viewport height. Fix: image_mode NodeImageMode::Stretch on MapScreenImage (and MinimapImage for the same latent mismatch), matching the placement math which assumes the drawn image exactly fills the node.
close_reason: ImageNode image_mode set to Stretch on MapScreenImage and MinimapImage; Bevy 0.19 Auto contain-fit was detaching the drawn map from the percent-placed marker overlay

title: Widescan is silently capped at entity spawn range: unnamed 0x0F4 entries dropped from list, never plotted as map dots
description:
The full protocol loop is faithful (c2s 0x0F4 SendFlg=1 on Wide Scan submode entry, s2c 0x0F6 ListStart / 0x0F4 entries / 0x0F6 ListEnd accumulated in SessionState.widescan, 0x0F5 track updates), and LSB serves the real widescan radius — getWideScanRange (vendor/server/src/map/utils/charutils.cpp:7507) gives 150 for sub RNG9, up to 350 for RNG80+, max(main,sub). But the client display throws the beyond-spawn-range majority away, so widescan looks capped at ~50 yalms:

1. LIST: widescan_rows (ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/map_screen.rs:286) drops any entry whose sName is empty and whose act_index has no locally-spawned entity. LSB always sends sName empty (vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x0f4_tracking_list.cpp — memcpy is a commented-out TODO), so the name fallback is the local entity table, which only covers the ~50y spawn range. Every entry beyond spawn range is filtered out. This was the deliberate kuluu-bi1s.6 call ('#<index> placeholder rows are noise'), but its side effect is that widescan degenerates to spawn range.

2. MAP DOTS: the Wide Scan submode never plots the 0x0F4 entries at all. update in map_screen.rs:872 draws overlay::sync_marker_layer over the LOCAL entity set; only the tracked target (0x0F5) uses widescan data. Retail plots scan results as dots at self+(rel_x,rel_z) out to full radius.

Fix sketch: (a) plot widescan entries as kind-colored dots at self_pos + (rel_x, rel_z) in Wide Scan submode (rel values are horizontal-plane server units; note LSB packs p.x/p.z diffs); (b) for the list, either keep named-only but stop implying completeness, or give unnamed rows a generic label (e.g. 'Lv24 Mob') so distant entries stay trackable — retail shows rows for everything because retail servers fill sName. (c) Guard test: an entry with empty name and no local entity must still produce a map dot.
notes: Implemented 2026-08-19: (1) widescan_rows no longer drops unnamed entries — generic kind label fallback (widescan_kind_label: Character/NPC/Mob) keeps beyond-spawn-range hits listed and trackable; (2) new update_map_widescan_dots system + MapWidescanDots resource/MapWidescanDot component plots 0x0F4 entries without a local entity as kind-colored dots at self + ffxi_to_bevy(rel_x, rel_z, 0), active only in the WideScan submode, drained when inactive, InGameEntity for zone-exit cleanup; (3) fixed the 0x0F5 tracked-marker fallback axis swap (raw LSB y=height was fed into the wire-convention transform, putting the horizontal coord on Bevy's up axis for beyond-range tracked targets). Guard tests: widescan_unnamed_entries_get_generic_kind_labels, widescan_dot_world_maps_rel_offsets_onto_the_map_plane. Also unblocked the shared clippy gate: allow(clippy::unneeded_struct_pattern) on the two additive-only sentinels in ffxi-session/src/state/tests.rs (new nightly lint vs the deliberate uniform { .. }).
close_reason: Verified live: Wide Scan submode in Valkurm Dunes (Verilamp, ALL_JOBS_WIDESCAN 150y) lists 16 generic 'Mob (LvXX)' rows for unnamed beyond-spawn-range hits and plots them as mob-colored dots around the self marker (artifacts/verify/widescan_map.png). Landed in commit b0854b0.

title: Split C: extract ffxi-hud from kuluu-render (HUD is a 22k-line near-pure sink)
description: Recon (2026-08-18): hud/ (21,450 lines, 47 files) + hud_hide/ui_font/ui_element_atlas/debug_chat is referenced from outside by only 10 call sites: input_mode.rs:403-427 and picking.rs:422-436 (into hud::action_model/overlay/menu -- layering inversions of the vana_clock/kuluu-a7c1642 shape, fix FIRST), minimap/mod.rs:7,363 + minimap/overlay.rs:223, cutscene.rs:21 + nameplate.rs:32 (hud_hide). HUD outbound: snapshot 45, components 33, minimap 20 (map_screen <-> minimap couple; minimap likely moves WITH hud). Waist stays in viewer-core: snapshot, components, camera, scene. wasm shell imports only 7 root re-exports incl. HudPlugin -- would re-point to ffxi-hud. kuluu references ::hud 171x (mechanical sed). Blockers to resolve: (a) the 10 inbound refs -> invert via events/resources or move the model bits down; (b) ViewerCorePlugin::build cross-cluster .before/.after orderings naming hud systems -> public SystemSet labels; (c) hud/style.rs is intra-HUD hub (fine, moves). NOT fundable: splitting ZONE from ACTOR (64-edge couple, dat_vos2->combat_stance 32); splitting materials apart (cross-shader include_str! invariant tests in ffxi_zone_material.rs:654 / skinned_ffxi_material.rs:686 / lens_flare.rs:338).

title: session/mod.rs partition: relocate tests, then move message-decode concerns out (treasure.rs precedent)
description:
Why: session/mod.rs is 9,199 lines and is where protocol work lands (state.rs
took 45 commits in 6 months; keepalive_loop is 2,184 lines, handle_sub_packet
1,091 with ~15 &mut cache params). Funded on navigability/design correctness,
NOT build speed - kuluu-p5a5 measured the edit loop at 4-12s regardless of
module shape, and this plan makes no compile-time claim.

Ground facts (verified 2026-08-18 by import grep):
- There is NO module cycle. supervisor -> reactor -> session -> {auth_client,
  lobby_client, map_client} -> state is a DAG; state.rs and map_client.rs
  import none of the other five. The one reactor->session edge is
  reactor::run spawning session::run (reactor.rs:1239), a real downward call.
  Do not plan work around 'breaking the cycle'; there isn't one.
- Test share of the hot files: session/mod.rs 3,114/9,199 lines (34%,
  #[cfg(test)] at 6085), state.rs 1,732/5,390 (32%, at 3658), reactor.rs
  1,988/3,312 (60%, at 1324).
- Domain clusters already sit as contiguous top-level helper runs in
  session/mod.rs (battle-message decode ~4373-5157 incl. BattleBitReader/
  Battle2Header; zone+system+fishing messages 4171-4370; event/dialog decode
  5158-5308 + 5448-5525; shop 5309-5359; emotes 4961-5027; status icons/
  recast 5360-5447). session/treasure.rs is the in-repo precedent for the
  move shape (rank-2 in refactor-economics: whole concern -> named module).
design:
Slices, each independently green + committed, oracle diffed per slice:

1. CHEAPEST INCREMENT (offer stopping after): relocate the #[cfg(test)]
   modules to sibling files - session/mod.rs -> session/tests.rs
   (#[cfg(test)] mod tests; picks the file up; `use super::*` keeps private
   access), state.rs -> #[path]-declared state_tests.rs, reactor.rs likewise.
   Pure relocation, zero token-cost claim (rubric: test co-location measures
   zero) - funded on: the hot file halves in the editor, and rg over
   non-test protocol code stops hitting test fixtures.
2..n. One concern per slice out of session/mod.rs, treasure.rs-shaped:
   battle_msg (decode_battle_message/Battle2*/synth_check/placeholders),
   zone_msg (ZoneMessage/emit_zone_message_chat/system messages/fish lines),
   event decode (decode_event_0x032/33/34, eventucoff, emit_event_dialog),
   shop, emotes+EmoteTextResolver, status_icons/recast. Code verbatim,
   citations carried, visibility widened only as the compiler demands.

Oracle: sorted fully-qualified `cargo test -p kuluu --lib -- --list`
names before/after each slice; leaf names must be byte-identical, module-path
deltas enumerated and intended (the 126910e/a7c1642 bar). Verify the list is
non-empty before trusting it (kuluu-i82r). After any slice touching decode
paths: protocol-conformance-reviewer on the diff.

REJECTED (do not re-derive):
- Context-struct rewrite of keepalive_loop/handle_sub_packet signatures now:
  Extract Class with no file boundary measures zero; only do it as committed
  setup once a handler-split target file list is written down.
- Extracting handle_sub_packet match arms into same-file helpers: the S5
  shape, worst-measured move.
- Unifying the three decode_event_0x03x fns or any similar-looking decoders:
  wire boundary, similar is not identical.
- Splitting kuluu into crates: settled by kuluu-p5a5 measurements.
- Splitting keepalive_loop itself before the concern moves shrink its
  helper surface: re-plan after slices 2..n land.
notes: Slice 1 (test relocation) landed as cb0d40c 2026-08-18: session/mod.rs 9199->6086, state.rs 5390->3659, reactor.rs 3312->1325; oracle 454 test names byte-identical, bodies token-identical vs HEAD (two rustfmt trailing commas the only delta). Recipe that worked: move the body indentation-preserved with sed, let cargo fmt renormalize (rustfmt never touches string-literal internals), then prove token-identity with whitespace-stripped comparison against git HEAD. Next: concern moves per --design, one per slice, protocol-conformance-reviewer after each.

title: Build-time investigation: edit loop is 4-12s; crate splits rejected, harness is the real cost
description:
Investigated 'long Rust compile times' and whether splitting the large crates (kuluu 61k lines, kuluu-render 70k) would help.

MEASURED (2 independent rounds, real content edits, quiet tree between each; cargo build --workspace --locked --features native-window):
  no-op ............................................  1s
  view_native/perf_hud.rs (BIN target) .............  4s
  kuluu-session/src/state.rs .........................  8s
  kuluu-render/src/hud/style.rs ................ 10s
  kuluu-render/src/scene.rs (core of 35-mod SCC) 11s
  ffxi-dat/src/lib.rs (bottom of stack) ............ 11-12s
  cargo test -p kuluu-render --lib (Edit hook) ..  8s
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets (warm) .... 10s
Identical whether the edit adds a private const or a pub fn (which invalidates
downstream metadata). Crate size, module cycles, and the bin/lib boundary have
NO measurable effect on the edit loop.

THE REAL COST IS THE TAIL, NOT THE LOOP:
  - Jobserver wedge: 4 rustc at 0.0% CPU blocked on cargo jobserver pipes
    (lsof fds 3-6) for 16-20 min, including ffxi-nav-recast (437 lines).
    Two more cargo processes blocked 25+ min on target/debug/.cargo-lock.
  - target/ reached 241 GB, then was cleaned to 28 GB mid-session -> cold
    rebuild. Settle build alone measured 304s.
  - Feature-unification divergence: cargo test -p <crate> (no --features
    native-window) diverges from the workspace build on 19 units incl. bevy
    itself (missing bevy_feathers) -> 195/461 units (42%) must populate a
    SECOND artifact universe. Costs disk, not per-edit time (measured 8s), but
    it is what drives the bloat -> clean -> cold-rebuild loop.
design:
CONCURRENCY (measured, not assumed): cargo now takes 3 locks
(.cargo-lock, .cargo-build-lock, .cargo-artifact-lock). Experiment with two
concurrent builds, one using a separate build.build-dir:
    A (shared build-dir):    10s   held .cargo-build-lock exclusively
    B (separate build-dir): 387s   never blocked, but rebuilt everything, 7.4 GB
Separate build-dirs give true parallelism at a 39x cost. Worktree-per-agent is
the same trade or worse. sccache requires CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, which would
destroy the measured 4-12s loop -- the earlier 0.32%-hit-rate rejection stands
and is now right for a stronger reason.
=> SINGLE-FLIGHT is correct: serializing costs ~10s; every isolation
   alternative costs minutes and gigabytes.
notes:
=== RESEARCH SWEEP (compile-time techniques not yet tried) ===
LANDED:
  * resolver.feature-unification = "workspace" (.cargo/config.toml).
    Verified on the unit graph: forced-fresh share 42% -> 19%. Neutral-to-
    slightly-better on wall clock; the win is disk/cold-rebuild pressure.
  * -Z no-embed-metadata (.cargo/config.toml [unstable]): metadata only in
    .rmeta, shrinks target/. One-time whole-cache invalidation, paid 2026-08-18
    bundled with the Bevy feature trim below.
  * Bevy feature trim (root Cargo.toml): default features expanded by hand,
    minus bevy_gltf + gltf_animation + bevy_world_serialization (zero source
    references; unit-graph critical-path depths 21 and 19). Verified on the
    unit graph after the trim: 653 -> 647 units, bevy_gltf / gltf* /
    bevy_world_serialization all at 0 units. Re-derive the expansion at the
    Bevy 0.19 -> 0.20 upgrade (kuluu-qsfj).

REJECTED after research (2026-08-18, do not re-derive):
  * -Z fine-grain-locking: the bead's own gate fails. Its "waiting job blocks
    all other jobs" fix (cargo#16657) was NEVER merged - still open with
    conflicts as of 2026-03; only the foundational lock-split (cargo#16708,
    merged 2026-03-06) is in our cargo 1.98.0-nightly (2026-05-26). Per the
    tracking issue (cargo#4282) only non-artifact commands (check) can run
    in parallel; our remaining contention is concurrent builds/tests, which it
    cannot parallelize, and the rust-analyzer use case is already solved by
    RA's separate target dir (.zed/settings.json). Expected win ~0, and the
    known failure mode is exactly the queue-blocking wedge cargo-guard.sh
    exists to bound. Revisit if/when a successor to cargo#16657 merges.

DEAD ENDS (measured/checked, do not re-derive):
  * -Zthreads (parallel frontend): composes with cranelift, but CPU time rises
    10-30% with thread count to buy wall clock -- a losing trade on a box
    already oversubscribed. Also rust#133873 is a jobserver deadlock CAUSED by
    -Zthreads. Revisit only on a quiet machine.
  * -Zgc / cache.auto-clean-frequency: global ~/.cargo cache ONLY, never
    target/. Target-dir GC is cargo#13136, accepted but unimplemented.
    'cargo clean --stale' does not exist. Hence scripts/target-hygiene.sh.
  * mold/wild on macOS: Linux/ELF only. Already on ld64.lld.
  * -Zshare-generics: off at opt-level=2, needs a global RUSTFLAG, documented
    ICE risk with dynamic linking (bevy#5505). Bad risk/reward on cranelift.
  * split-debuginfo, codegen-units, -Zcheck-cfg, debug=0: already optimal or
    no measurable win.
  * cargo-hakari/workspace-hack: superseded by resolver.feature-unification.
  * sccache: needs CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, which would destroy the 4-12s loop.

CRITICAL PATH (cargo --unit-graph, 653 units, longest chain 29 deep): levels
17-26 are all Bevy at width 1-7. Our code is only the last 3 levels.
kuluu-render sits at depth 27 width 1 -- a real single-threaded stall, but
worth only ~6-10s of a 304s cold build, and splitting an SCC into a chain
LENGTHENS the critical path rather than widening it. Confirms the split refusal.

HUD LAYERING INVERSIONS (follow-on from 126910e, landed a7c1642 2026-08-18):
fishing_spot -> hud::equipment_screen::EquipmentIndex, ffxi_actor_render ->
hud::self_hud::resolve_self, dat_mmb + zone_lights -> hud::mesh_debug::
MmbDebugInfo. All three fixed with the same shape (domain half moved out,
presentation stays, 954-test leaf-name oracle). Funded on layering; no
compile-time claim.
close_reason: Re-verified 2026-09-09 by an adversarial done-check: Verified against the current tree (probe checkout c443301a): all three LANDED techniques the bead names are present in code — resolver.feature-unification = "workspace" and -Z no-embed-metadata in .cargo/config.toml, and the hand-trimmed Bevy default-feature list (minus bevy_gltf/gltf_animation/bevy_world_serialization) in root Cargo.toml — each traceable to a landing commit (23f8c294, fedd0ee5). Every REJECTED/DEAD-END technique the bead lists (-Z fine-grain-locking, -Zthreads, -Zgc, mold/wild, -Zshare-generics, sccache, cargo-hakari) is correctly absent from the build config, matching the bead's own "do not re-derive" verdicts. Supporting tooling referenced in the notes (cargo-guard.sh, target-hygiene.sh) also exists. The only outstanding action item — re-deriving the Bevy feature trim at the 0.19->0.20 upgrade — is explicitly assigned by the bead's own text to a separate tracked bead (kuluu-qsfj), so it is not unfinished work under this one. This is an investigation/design bead whose deliverable was the measurement writeup plus these landed config changes, and both are confirmed in place; closing as done is correct.

title: Esc during an event VM timed wait is deferred, and dropped if no message wait follows
description: DialogRunner::cancel sets the invalid-message flag then run()s, but EventVm::step returns Waiting before observing any cancel while a 0x1C/0x6F wait is held, so the session's Advance::Waiting arm swallows the Esc: no EVENT_END, no EventEnded, no UI feedback. The flag survives until the script next reaches a MESWAIT (vm.rs OP_MESWAIT handling), so the cancel lands late; if the remaining bytecode has no message wait (e.g. WAIT -> END) it is dropped entirely and the event ends as if Esc was never pressed. Decide whether retail defers or cancels immediately (check XiEvents 0x001C RetFlag/cancel interaction), then either latch cancel-requested and apply it when the wait expires, or document deferral as faithful. The session-side arm is commented at session/mod.rs (Esc mid-wait).

title: Event VM corpus: 33 events run past the end of their bytecode (was 5)
description: The opcode work in f833e33 cut corpus stops 11381 -> 1530 but raised 'ran past end' 5 -> 33. Retail treats a read past the end as END, so these still report Done -- which hides them in the very metric that measures the work. An overrun means one of the new widths lands mid-instruction several opcodes upstream, i.e. a mis-executed scene. ~30 are an 0x01 GOTO and ~3 an 0x02 IF branching past the bytecode. Localize with a per-script trace (ffxi-event/examples/zz-event-trace.rs, zone 245 event 20076 is a known instance) or a temporary prev_op field reported by zz-event-sweep, then fix the offending width.

title: Event VM has no host input surface, so retail's input polls can only stop
description: a512f1c makes the 0x71/0xCC input polls hold ExecPointer instead of answering wrong (password window, numeric/string input buffer, Linkshell Concierge choice, search-menu zone pick). Holding is correct but terminal: the VM cannot ever be answered, so those cutscenes stop rather than proceed. Needs EventVm::submit_input plus a StepResult/DialogFrame variant carrying the text/numeric prompt, and client UI to collect it. Blocks the last of kuluu-u7r5's load-bearing opcodes.

title: mmb.rs unpacks vertex D3DCOLOR in file order while consumers read it as RGBA
description: Same defect shape as the sprite-sheet colour swap fixed in 7f2fdb0, but on the zone/model path and therefore with a much wider blast radius. Both MMB vertex readers (ffxi-dat/src/mmb.rs:307 and :626) take the 4 colour bytes in file order, while D3DCOLOR is ARGB packed little-endian, i.e. file bytes B,G,R,A (research/XIClient .../Rendering/Color/ARGBByte.h; ffxi-dat/src/d3m.rs already unpacks it correctly). If the consumers index them as (r,g,b,a) then red and blue are swapped for every MMB vertex colour. Confirm which side is wrong before changing either -- FfxiZoneMaterial's 2x overbright vertex-lit path consumes this. Found while fixing kuluu-lqz2.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (78c24f80) after adversarial review (round-1 review approve (implementer transcript lost to a stall; reviewer notes used)); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Reviewer summary: Every citation in the commit message and in the new code comment was opened and checked line by line. XIClient's ARGBByte.h really does union the u32 with a {b,g,r,a} byte struct, so little-endian file bytes are B,G,R,A. The two xim citations (ParticleMeshSection.kt:69, WeightedMeshSection.kt:157) land exactly on nextBGRA() calls, and ByteReader.kt:69-71 defines nextBGRA as (b,g,r,a)->rgba. The strongest oracle - xim's ZoneMeshSection.kt, the direct MMB zone-mesh reader - was not cited by the commit but independently confirms the same order for both the 36-byte and 48-byte strides, and mmb.rs:452 already carried that citation describing the field as BGRA while the code read it in file order. crate::d3m independently unpacks the identical 36-byte record as BGRA. The producer was unambiguously the wrong side; no consumer compensated. Nothing invented, no ungrounded retail-parity claim, no enhanced behavior introduced.
Non-blocking nits recorded by the reviewer: NIT: ffxi-dat now has three near-identical D3DCOLOR unpackers - mmb::d3dcolor_rgba (new, mmb.rs:168), sprite_sheet::rd_d3dcolor (sprite_sheet.rs:59), skel_mesh::next_bgra (skel_mesh.rs:134) - plus d3m's inline shifts. The commit's own 'so the two readers cannot drift again' rationale argues for one  | NIT: the new comment and commit message cite research/xim ParticleMeshSection.kt:69 and WeightedMeshSection.kt:157 (both verified accurate to the line), but the exact analog for the MMB zone-mesh vertex is ZoneMeshSection.kt:88/95 - which mmb.rs:452 already cites and which reads ByteColor(b,g,r,a) f | NIT/VERIFY: kuluu-render/src/zone_lights.rs:228 rejects vertices where c[2] > c[0] (warm_only, enabled by default), so this fix inverts which real-zone vertices become brazier/lamp point lights.
