Correct-er, but overbright_threshold 1.15 was tuned against swapped data; no test or branch note covers t | NIT: the smmb_one_triangle fixture uses unnamed structural offsets (HEAD + 16 for piece count, HEAD + 44 for the data offset, PIECE_OFF = 64); parse_models' SMMB_HEAD_SIZE/SMMB_HEADER_SIZE are fn-local so the fixture cannot reuse them. | NIT: all three new tests are synthetic and the 'cross-parser oracle' is our own d3m decoder. The XIClient/xim format evidence is definitive so this is acceptable, but a real-DAT assertion (e.g. a known-warm torch MMB decodes warm) would be a stronger oracle.
close_reason: Landed on main 78c24f80 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed, how it was verified, and what stays open.

title: Near-flat particle meshes still take the axial camera billboard path
description: is_solid_mesh (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs) gates the aim-at-eye axial billboard on the linked template having extent > 0 on all three axes, which correctly excludes the 98 exactly-flat templates found across zone DATs 100-500. But 'sung' (file 161, D3M, extent [9.450, 0.236, 9.432]) is a Y-thin disc authored in the XZ plane, not around X: it passes the degeneracy test and takes the aim-at-eye path, which is the most plausible surviving instance of the same failure mode in near-flat rather than exactly-flat form. Settle what retail does for a disc whose thin axis is not X. Found by the adversarial recheck of the kuluu-fjd3 remediation (7f2fdb0).

title: Valkurm Dunes renders hard-edged flat terrain polygons at the wrong shade (green cliff-top patch, sand wedges)
description:
In Valkurm Dunes (zone 103, DAT 203) several terrain polygons render as hard-edged flat patches at a shade unrelated to their neighbours: a bright green quad floating over the cliff top, and large straight-edged light/dark wedges across the sand. They read as 'unblended tiles'.

Originally suspected to be a weather-particle blend-order fault (kuluu-x2cs). Ruled out 2026-08-08: a weather A/B from a fixed camera shows the polygons identical under DUST_STORM and under weather NONE -- mean absolute difference over the artifact region is 4.2/255, versus 7.6/255 scene-wide for the dust tint itself. The dust only made them easier to notice by adding contrast.

Evidence: artifacts/verify/dust-final-b.png (DUST_STORM) vs artifacts/verify/nodust-same-spot.png (NONE), same position, night (22:20 vs 22:35 game time).
notes:
Both captures are at night, so per-vertex/time-of-day zone lighting is a prime suspect -- the green patch is lit as if it were still day. Check FfxiZoneMaterial vertex-lit path and the MZB placement/lighting seam before assuming a geometry fault; see the zone vertex-lit material and MZB placement-grid memories.

Not yet checked: whether the same polygons misbehave in daylight, and whether other zones show it.
2026-09-04 root cause found from the attached daylight F-8 recording and format audit: MMB vertex D3DCOLOR bytes are BGRA in little-endian memory (XIClient ARGBByte.h; xim ZoneMeshSection reads nextBGRA), but ffxi-dat parsed them straight into the RGBA vertex attribute. Neutral-gray tiles hid the mismatch; color-authored tiles became sharply mis-tinted at their mesh boundaries. Fixed by converting BGRA to RGBA at both MMB vertex decoders with a regression test.
Correction (2026-09-04): a later DAT measurement refuted the BGRA diagnosis for the attached F-8 artifact. Every affected ke_moa terrain vertex colour is grayscale, so exchanging red and blue cannot change these patches; that unrelated decoder change was reverted. The current candidate is insufficient transparent-terrain depth bias: retail uses D3DRS_ZBIAS 8 for these 0x8000 overlay submeshes, while Kuluu used 1. Live A/B verification is pending.
Final diagnosis (2026-09-04): the decoded retail state is indeed transparent D3D8 Z-bias layer 8, but that integer is an ordering level rather than a portable WGPU depth-unit magnitude. Kuluu translated it with a negative constant under Bevy reversed-Z, pushing the soft terrain overlay behind its coplanar base and exposing hard pale polygons. The render bridge now maps any nonzero legacy layer to the minimum forward WGPU bias (constant +1, slope +1). Literal +8 was live-tested and rejected because it pulled decals through neighboring terrain. Exact Valkurm F-8 clear west/north and Dust Storm A/B passed with no hard patches or pull-through; evidence: artifacts/verify/valkurm-f8-{clear,dust}-translated-bias-slope-*.png.
close_reason: Corrected legacy transparent-terrain Z-bias translation and passed exact Valkurm F-8 clear/Dust live verification from two headings.

title: Retail blocks walking into deep water at the shoreline; movement has no water gate (players can stand in Knightwell lake)
design:
Observed on HorizonXI (West Ronfaure): players stand *in* Knightwell lake, impossible on retail. The retail client refuses shoreline entry into deep water; our movement path (input.rs) has no water check, and LSB/HorizonXI do no server-side terrain validation of c2s 0x015 positions, so the client walks straight in and the server accepts it.

Water detection already exists — MzbCollisionGeometry::water_below / terrain_nearest / facing_water (dat_mzb.rs) — but is only wired to the fishing gate (kuluu-c4wu). Movement needs its own gate: retail behavior is a hard stop at the water's edge (no wading/swimming in field zones).

Note: verify retail's exact rule first (retail-observe) — shoreline stop vs. shallow-wading allowance, and whether it's a terrain-type flag or water-plane height test.

title: Backdrop clear color follows retail: sky horizon outdoors, record background @76 indoors
design: Retail derives no lighting from the skybox: ambient/sun/fog are independently authored channels of the 0x2F weather keyframe (XIClient XiArea.cpp:140-220 vs XiZone.cpp:149-206). The one sky->scene coupling is the clear color: outdoors DrawSky overrides BackColor with the interpolated horizon slice SkyPalette[0] (XiZone.cpp:191; xim EnvironmentManager.kt:139-140); indoors the record's own BackgroundColor (xim EnvironmentSection.kt:290, offset 76). We used fog_landscape for the backdrop and never parsed @76.
notes: Fixed: ffxi-dat WeatherRecord.background_color (@76, lerped in lerp_records); zone_clear_color picks skybox_colors[0] outdoors / background_color indoors; dump-skybox prints bg. Guard tests: outdoor_record_paints_the_sky_horizon_not_the_fog_color, indoor_record_paints_its_own_background_color.
close_reason: Landed: WeatherRecord.background_color parsed from the 0x2F record @76 (xim EnvironmentSection.kt:290 == XIClient WorldParameters.BackgroundColor), lerped in lerp_records; zone_clear_color now uses the interpolated horizon slice skybox_colors[0] outdoors (XiZone.cpp:191) and background_color indoors (xim EnvironmentManager.kt:139-140); guard tests pin both arms; dump-skybox prints bg.

title: Sub-map protocol: client never sends 0x0F2, so boundary is permanently 0
description:
LSB calls MZB sub-areas SubMap/boundary and it is a live three-way contract Kuluu implements none of:
- c2s GP_CLI_COMMAND_SUBMAPCHANGE (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x0f2_submapchange), { State, SubMapNumber }; process() does PChar->loc.boundary = SubMapNumber. STATE is General (walked into a sub-region) or Event (an event moved you between them - i.e. the chocobo rental).
- s2c GP_SERV_COMMAND_LOGIN (0x00a_login.cpp) carries SubMapNumber = PChar->loc.boundary at 0x5C. ffxi-proto/src/decode/login.rs names 0x5C only as an offset landmark in a comment and never decodes it.
- c2s 0x0EB REQSUBMAPNUM -> s2c 0x10E GP_SERV_COMMAND_REQSUBMAPNUM.

boundary IS the MZB sub-area id: transport.sql gives the four Jeuno airships boundaries 474-477, and Port Jeuno (zone 246 -> DAT 346) declares sub-areas 468-477.

HARD TESTABLE PREDICTION: CZoneEntities::TransportDepart (vendor/server/src/map/zone_entities.cpp) moves only chars whose loc.boundary == boundary. Since Kuluu never sends 0x0F2, loc.boundary is permanently 0, so boarding a Selbina/Mhaura boat or a Jeuno airship can never carry the player.

SPLIT: the decode half is standalone and can land now (decode SubMapNumber in ServerLogin, a boundary field on SessionState, accept s2c 0x10E). The EMIT half needs the sub-area latch from kuluu-vbpt.

This corrects the claim that 'LSB has no concept of sub-areas' - that came from grepping for 'subarea' and missing LSB's own vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: 0x00A SubMapNumber decoded onto SessionState; 0x0F2 emitted when the latch changes; a boat or airship carries the player.

title: Spawn morph column strands itself on the player forever
description:
The cyan light column that materialises an actor is a child entity whose id lives only inside the MorphIn component. An actor reload (mounting changes the look, which reloads) REPLACES that component, so the replacement cannot reap the old column: it freezes mid-stretch and rides the player for the session. Observed 2026-08-05 in West Ronfaure after renting a chocobo in Southern San d'Oria.

Fixed in eba9a8f: the column's lifetime is now owned by MorphIn via a Discard observer (the idiom free_skin_slot_on_remove already uses), and the effect is skipped for self because retail plays no column on your own body at zone-in (retail capture Upper Jeuno -> Rolanberry Fields, 2026-08-04). Two guard tests pin both exit paths.
acceptance_criteria: A second MorphIn insert on the same entity despawns the first column; self never spawns one.
close_reason: Fixed in eba9a8f; two guard tests pin the replace and remove paths. Not verified live.

title: Lens flare picks the wrong lf0x sheet: file order, not the active weather
description:
extract_lens_flare_sheet (ffxi-dat/src/sprite_sheet.rs) returns the FIRST 0x21 chunk with the lens_flare byte set. A zone ships several: file 201 has lf03 (26 meshes), molf (2, texture moon/kasa), lf02 (18), lf03 again (16) and lf01 (17), so the flat walk hands back lf03 no matter what the weather is.

Retail scopes the chain the same way it scopes the sun and moon billboards: the lf0x generator lives under weat/<weather>/, so the active weather selects which chain draws. celestial_particles::collect_celestial_defs already walks that subtree for the Sun/Moon-attached generators and can name the linked mesh.

Second half of the same gap: molf is the MOON's flare (the kasa halo sheet, offset 0.0 twice). Nothing draws it — lens_flare.rs only ever projects the sun.

title: AH HUD: price spinner + sell flow + sales status
description: Price Set screen per the observation record: digit-spinner gil widget (All ◀ [N] G ▶ over /cap, +/- arrows, active digit red field + orange just-edited digits; cap 999,999,999 selling / current gil bidding), 'Current Gil' panel, sell item list + fee confirm ('The total transaction fee for a set of 12 items is N gil.') + placement confirm ('Place X up on auction for N gil?') Yes/No dialogs (reuse DialogState/hud/dialog.rs), sales-status 7-slot window ('You have no items up for auction.'), chat echoes (white action lines, 3-line policy explainer, red partial-stack error, 'You were unable to buy ...'). Spinner is a reusable widget (widgets/) — gil entry elsewhere (bazaar, delivery) should converge on it later.
acceptance_criteria: Sell a stack + place a failing bid against live LSB with pixel-comparable screens vs recording frames; chat lines match retail text.
notes: 2026-09-08: code landed in 228f57e9 (+47e9e4d2 digit-spinner borrow/carry, 0122e745 catalog paging). Still in_progress solely for the live acceptance pass in the acceptance criteria; nothing is unbuilt.

title: AH HUD: browse UI (root menu, category dock, catalog, price history)
description: kuluu-render/src/hud: retail-faithful AH browse per .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/auction-house.md. Right-dock 'Auction' panel (Bid/Sell/Sales Status -> category menus -> per-item context menu Price History/Bid/Sort -> sort menu), catalog list top-left (10 rows, icon+name+bracketed stock count, scrollbar; no bracket = none listed), item detail pane reuse (hud/item_detail.rs), price-history table (date seller -> buyer price G, YY/M/D, ellipsized names), help-bar strings per row (exact text in the record), 'Downloading data ..' spinner, category tab stack with active-gold styling. Keyboard: up/down wrap, left/right page, enter/esc; mouse hover+click selection (menu_mouse_* precedent). DRY: build on hud/menu.rs DynamicMenu paging + hud/shop.rs list rendering rather than new widget infra.
acceptance_criteria: Side-by-side with recording-1 frames: root menu, catalog, price history, sort menu match layout+strings.
notes: 2026-09-08: code landed in 228f57e9 (+47e9e4d2 digit-spinner borrow/carry, 0122e745 catalog paging). Still in_progress solely for the live acceptance pass in the acceptance criteria; nothing is unbuilt.

title: AH wire surface: snapshot state across ffxi-viewer-wire
description: Extend wire::SceneSnapshot (wire_translate.rs state_to_snapshot) with the AH surface: root menu open flag, category path, catalog page (itemid + single/stack prices + counts), price-history rows, sales-status slots, pending-op spinner state ('Downloading data ..' / 'Placing bid ...'), current gil. Keep ffxi-viewer-wire transport-agnostic; both native bridge and WASM relay consume it. Prefer reusing DialogState for the Yes/No fee/placement confirms (delivery-box precedent).
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot roundtrips through postcard; native + relay builds compile.
close_reason: AuctionUi + translator landed; postcard roundtrip and translation tests green; protocol version bumped

title: Chat input: recall previously sent lines with Up/Down
description:
The chat text input has no history. Every send drops the line; retyping a command (/heal, /tell <name> ...) means typing it out again. Retail's text input keeps a rolling buffer of submitted lines and pages through them with the arrow keys while the bar is open.

Add a ChatHistory resource holding the submitted lines, and wire Up/Down in InputMode::Chat to page through it (newest first), stashing the in-progress draft so paging back down restores it.
design:
- ChatHistory lives in ffxi-viewer-core::input_mode as a Resource (VecDeque, capped) so it survives chat open/close and zone changes.
- The paging cursor + stashed draft live in ChatBuffer, which is recreated per chat-open, so each open starts at the fresh line.
- Up/Down use Action::NavUp/NavDown (already ArrowUp/ArrowDown in every preset). They are free in Chat mode: the movement/camera system early-returns on InputMode::Chat, so no conflict with CameraPitchUp.
acceptance_criteria: Open chat, send two lines, reopen: Up shows the newest, Up again the older, Down walks back and restores the partially typed draft. Unit tests cover empty history, clamping at the oldest, and draft round-trip.
close_reason: Implemented: ChatHistory resource + ChatBuffer paging cursor, Up/Down wired in InputMode::Chat. Unit tests cover the model and the key routing; not yet driven against a live session.

title: Reactor pathing ignored the mount and mis-modelled speed as speed/speed_base
description: /pathto and follow sized their per-tick step from (speed / speed_base) capped at 2x. Retail never computes that ratio: ControllableActor::StepControl reads speed*0.1 only, doubles it while mounted and clamps at 30; SpeedBase*0.1 goes to a separate field (VirtActor97) that movement never spends. Because LSB sends a LOWER speed while mounted (40 vs 50 on foot), pathing and follow were slower on a chocobo than on foot.
design: Evidence: research/XIClient .../World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp StepControl (double-if-mounted, clamp 30) and .../Game/Net/Packets/s2c/0x00D,0x00E,0x037 (Speed -> AUDIT_15C -> VirtActor95; SpeedBase -> AUDIT_09C -> VirtActor97). Mount speed cap: vendor/server/src/map/entities/battleentity.cpp CBattleEntity::UpdateSpeed.
notes: Fixed 2026-08-05 in 10375c7. The rule now lives once as state::move_speed_yps/move_speed_ratio; view_native/input.rs consumed a private copy of it before and now imports it. Reactor tests rewritten around the retail decode (BASE_PACKET_SPEED=50, the 30 y/s ceiling) instead of the old ratio model.
close_reason: Fixed in 10375c7; reactor tests pin the retail decode

title: Fishing: client-side water gate + contextual Fish action-menu entry
description:
Retail gates fishing client-side before any packet leaves: the action menu only offers Fish when the player is idle, has a fishing rod in the ranged slot, and is facing water. Kuluu has neither half — /fish always sends and the menu has no Fish entry.

Water test (research/xim Scene.canFish): sample 2..4 yalms ahead along the facing direction, take the nearest floor under each sample, and accept if its terrain type is ShallowWater or DeepWater. Terrain type is the MZB collision triangle nibble already parsed as MzbTriangleInfo::material (bit 15 of each of the four index words).

Rod test (research/xim AssetViewer.canFish): ranged-slot item skill == Fishing.
design: Terrain nibble semantics confirmed empirically, not taken from XIM (tier 6): ffxi-dat/examples/dat-fishing-terrain-probe.rs cross-checks the nibble against LSB vendor/server/sql/fishing_area.sql. Water is 0.3-4% of triangles zone-wide but 10-45% inside every radial fishing cylinder, and Snow/Sand only appear in snowy/beach zones. Independently corroborated by ffxi-dat/src/footstep.rs, whose measured terrain nibble range is 1..=10.
acceptance_criteria: Fish appears in the untargeted action menu only when idle + rod equipped + facing water; /fish refuses with the retail message when the water test fails and the zone collision is loaded (fail-open when it is not).
notes:
FIELD REPORT follow-up (live test): the fsh* poses never played at all, for self or observed players — two independent breaks, both fixed in be00b62 and pinned by kuluu-render/tests/fishing_pose_clips.rs across all 8 races:
1. The fsh0..fsh9 routines live at main_dll base_action_animation_index(race) + 1 (race 1: 38604), a DAT load_pc never read. Only the mount DAT at +5 was ever pulled from that block. The prior note in MEMORY.md claiming they sit in skel_file_id+1 was wrong.
2. fsh<n> is a ROUTINE name, not an animation id. Its first Motion stage names the real clip (fsh0 -> fh0?). The pose selector looked the routine id up among animations, matched nothing, and fell through to idle.

The same DAT carries the hits/hitl sweat routines, so kuluu-t5ru now has its playback half available.

Also fixed: zone messages naming a menu entry are no longer printed as chat. The vendored LSB's text ids sit 8-10 entries above where a May-2023 install has the fishing block (measured across 115 zones), so catch lines rendered as the 'Select Fish Type: Saltwater...' menu. Chat keeps the placeholder and warns with the numbers instead.

title: Chocobo periphery: door opening, indoor rendering, rental dialog, and the mount cutscene
description:
Reported 2026-08-04 against the retail reference capture (Screen Recording 2026-08-04 12.37.09, Upper Jeuno Chocobo Stables -> Rolanberry Fields). Three things retail does in that clip that Kuluu does not:

1. The stable door does not open / the interior does not render on the way in.
2. The rent-a-chocobo NPC dialog (Audee: 'You can rent a chocobo for N gil. I see you currently have N gil.') misbehaves.
3. The mount cutscene never plays — retail fades to black, shows the player beside the chocobo, then fades back in already mounted, still inside the stables.

Each is a distinct subsystem (zone door entity, event VM, event fade) and probably wants splitting once someone has reproduced them; filed together because they were reported as one flow.
notes:
2026-08-05 (3): RETRACTION. My 2026-08-05 (2) note claimed the cutscene item was
addressed because the VM ran zone 244 event 10003 to end_para 0. That was WRONG:
end_para 0 only proves the bytecode reached EXECEND. It says nothing about
presentation, and the capture at 13:48 (built after those commits) shows no
cutscene.

Re-diagnosed with a 13-agent fan-out against the live San d'Oria flow
(zone 230, renter Camereine, eventSucceed 599). Driving it offline now yields
AwaitMessage(6533) -> AwaitChoice(6536) -> Done at pc 325, and an instrumented
VM shows the ENTIRE scene body executing inside one synchronous step():
  0x46 DEFCAMERA, 0x42, 0x27, 0x53 'kue0', 0x2C 'sit0', 0x5D music, 0x1C,
  0x2A, 0x45 'chco', 0x45 'fdo0', 0x1C, 0x4E hide, 0x7E case1, 0x7E case2,
  0x1C, 0x2A, 0x27, 0x1C, 0x45 'fdi0', 0x2A, 0x30, GOTO, EXECEND.
Every one of those is skipped into invisibility because there is no cue channel:
StepResult (6 variants) -> DialogStep -> event_dialog::Begin/Advance ->
AgentEvent -> ViewerEvent, none of which can carry camera/fade/motion/hide.
And retail marks 0x1C/0x27/0x2A/0x53/0x7E sets_ret so the scene spends frames;
we collapse them, so EVENT_END fires on the same tick the player answers yes.

Retail ground truth for what we owe (retail capture 2026-08-04 12.37.09,
frames 22-26): a ~2s fade to black, then fade in already mounted in the same
spot. It is a screen fade, not choreography.

Re-pointed: door -> kuluu-dag, interior -> kuluu-vbpt, cutscene -> the new
cue-channel bead.

title: Mounted quick action / context menu: Dismount and Chocobo Dig
description:
Nothing in the UI can dismount or dig. ActionKind::Dismount and ActionKind::ChocoboDig already exist and are already plumbed to the encrypted wire (ffxi-client/src/state.rs, session.rs build_subpacket_action); no menu row, slash command or quick action constructs either.

Retail's mounted client actions are exactly these two (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x01a_action.h:66-67: ChocoboDig = 0x11, Dismount = 0x12). LSB handles Dismount by clearing animation + EFFECT_MOUNTED (0x01a_action.cpp:425-431) and Dig by pushing GP_SERV_COMMAND_DIG (:420-423). Engaging (Attack) also silently dismounts server-side (:236-240).

The HUD Mount ability group currently returns Vec::new() with hint 'No mounts available.' (ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/menu.rs:973,983).
close_reason: Closed

title: Mounted movement speed: client doubles server speed and caps at 30
description:
Mounting currently makes the player SLOWER, not faster.

LSB sends packet Speed = map.MOUNT_SPEED/2 = 40 while mounted (vendor/server/src/map/entities/battleentity.cpp:327-331, settings/default/map.lua:124) vs BASE_SPEED 50 unmounted. Our input.rs consumes it raw (ffxi-client/src/view_native/input.rs:846, SPEED_TO_YPS=0.1), so mounted = 4.0 y/s vs 5.0 unmounted.

Retail does the doubling client-side: speed = packetSpeed * 0.1 (research/XIClient .../Game/Net/Packets/s2c/0x00D.cpp:108, 0x037.cpp:62 — the same 0.1 our SPEED_TO_YPS encodes), then 'if (IsOnChocobo() || IsOnMount()) movementSpeed += movementSpeed;' and 'if (movementSpeed > 30.0f) movementSpeed = 30.0f' (research/XIClient .../World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp:627-637).
acceptance_criteria: Mounted forward run is 1.6x the unmounted rate for LSB defaults (40*2=80 vs 50); a unit test pins doubling + the 30.0 cap against ControllableActor.cpp:627-637.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mount/chocobo model rendering: spawn the ridden mount actor and attach the rider
notes:
2026-08-05: two parity questions raised by the fan-out, both worth one
retail-observe each (cheaper than the code):
 1. Should a mount-state change reload the entire PC model? dispatch_look_driven_models
    keys EntityModel on {look, mounted}; mounting only changes weapon-slot
    suppression and which anim DAT loads. Keeping the skeleton and swapping the
    anim set would remove the second load entirely and probably also the visible
    pop when mounting. It is also what made the spawn-column leak reachable
    (kuluu-rvif).
 2. SessionState::observe_event sets self_server_status = 0 on ZoneChanged, so
    the client briefly believes a riding player is dismounted on every zone line.
    That affects move speed, the mount actor, and the seat pose.

title: Status ribbon: countdown labels collide — derive chip pitch from the widest timer
description: Status-icon chips are packed at a 1px gap with the countdown label absolutely positioned at width=ICON_SIZE_PX (20px) and bottom=-2. Any label wider than 20px ("10:02", "1:24") overflows into the neighbouring chip, so adjacent timers read as one run-on number, and the label also overlaps the icon art it belongs to. h:mm:ss strings (food/Signet) are ~2x the icon width.
design: Derive the chip pitch from the label instead of hard-coding a gap: measure the widest timer string in the bundled monospace HUD font (ui_font::text_width_px) and set pitch = max(icon+min gap, label+margin). Row gap clears one text line so a wrapped second row is not overlapped. Ribbon countdown gets its own compact formatter (m:ss under an hour, HhMM at/over) so the worst case stays 5 chars.
acceptance_criteria: No two adjacent timers touch at any duration the decoder admits (< MAX_STATUS_TIMER_SECS); label centered under its own icon; second row not overlapped; unit test pins widest-emitted-string <= reserved width.
close_reason: Chip pitch now derives from the widest countdown via ui_font::text_width_px; verified live (min 11 device px between adjacent labels, 17px row clearance)

title: Retail-faithful /check window: icon grid, linkshell, job ribbon, message, View Wares
description:
The /check panel for PCs renders as a plain text list of 16 slot lines plus a job line (ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/check_view.rs:198-226). Retail shows the target's equipment as a 4x4 icon grid (same layout as our own Equipment window), the focused item's detail, the target's name/job/subjob, their linkshell name, their bazaar message, and a View Wares entry enabled only when the target has a bazaar.

Scope:
- rebuild check_view.rs on hud::item_grid::spawn_item_cell + hud::item_ui::focus_detail, reusing equipment_screen::EQUIP_GRID so both windows share one slot layout
- keyboard grid navigation + a focusable View Wares row (enabled from the target entity's CharFlags.bazaar bit, LSB PChar->hasBazaar())
- linkshell name/colour: decode the packed 6-bit sComLinkName already carried in 0x0C9 GENERAL (ffxi-proto/src/decode/equip_inspect.rs:47) and plumb it through CheckResult
- bazaar message: kuluu-2kr7 (0x0CA)
- View Wares opens the bazaar browse window: kuluu-egw
acceptance_criteria: Check panel renders a 4x4 icon grid matching the Equipment window layout; linkshell name shown when the target wears a pearl; View Wares row is enabled iff the target's bazaar flag is set; unit tests cover the grid layout and the button enable rule.
close_reason: Retail /check window landed in 7328407: 4x4 icon grid shared with the Equipment window, name/job ribbon, linkshell row, bazaar message, and a View Wares entry gated on the target's CharFlags.bazaar bit. Live-verified by self-check (artifacts/verify/check-window.png, check-body-slot.png, check-wrap.png).

title: Battle-message templates come from LSB source comments, not retail's mesbasic table
description: ffxi-proto::msg_basic scrapes the trailing comment off each vendor/server/src/map/enums/msg_basic.h enumerator, which makes retail's battle log only as accurate as LSB's comments: id 116 has no enumerator at all, ids 14/31/100/101/102/103/136/137/317/324 write a bare '..' where a token belongs, and the 420-427 Corsair roll family needs values the substituter cannot supply. kuluu's TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES pins the wording for the ones that matter today (kuluu-33hy), which is a hand-maintained table of exactly the kind AGENTS.md says not to keep. Retail carries the real strings in ROM/27/72.DAT, the same dmsg family ffxi-dat already parses for the emote DialogTable (ROM/27/70) and system messages (ROM/27/76). Mob TP move names have the same shape: ROM/27/80.DAT (xor 0x80 BasicStringTable, research/xim MobAbilityTable.kt:10) instead of the LSB snake_case scrape kuluu-ooki added.
acceptance_criteria: Battle lines render retail's own mesbasic strings when an install is present, and TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES is gone.

title: Mob and pet TP move completion effects never display (categories 11/13 resolve no DAT)
description: scheduler_runtime::action_dat_file_id handles only ActionCategory 3/4/6, so ActionCategory::MobSkillFinish (11) and PetSkillFinish (13) return None and a monster's TP move plays no particles, sound, or body motion — only the chat line lands. research/xim MobAbilityTable.kt resolves these through MobSkillInfoTable::getAnimationPath(animationId) -> FileTableManager.getFilePath(getFileTableOffset(animationId)), a different base from the 0x113C ability block; mob_skills.mob_anim_id is the same index the packet's animation field carries. Split out of kuluu-3gwj, which fixed the PC-side keying.
acceptance_criteria: A Goobbue's Uppercut plays its retail effect and the mob's body animates through it.

title: Nameplates must use the static authored model locator instead of mesh height
description: Nameplates use BakedActor mesh extent plus a generic offset/fallback, which differs from the original client and misplaces names for differently sized or floating models such as Damselfly. Direct inspection of the installed FFXiMain.dll and skeleton DATs establishes a static authored locator2 offset, multiplied by model scale and added to Model.Position without animated bones or facing. Earlier mesh-height, always-above-crown and shared camera/picking hypotheses were superseded by this evidence; see investigation notes and follow-ups kuluu-0hcf / kuluu-6kau.
design: Read standard locator2 from runtime skeleton DAT metadata. Match retail GetLocatorWorldPosition special case: static translation, no animated bone/facing matrix, apply model scale in the correct axes, convert to renderer axes and add Model.Position. Carry this independently of BakedActor across live, legacy skinned/CPU and equipped model load paths; hide unavailable names and refresh metadata when models replace. Preserve existing supported mount correction with root locator gating; broader mount/chair behavior is kuluu-6kau. Camera and picking policy are split to kuluu-0hcf.
acceptance_criteria: Authored locator2 metadata from installed DATs drives nameplate/overhead cursor positions with correct model scale/coordinate conversion. Tarutaru, Galka and Damselfly values differ as authored (no per-model client table); animation and facing do not move the anchor relative to Model.Position. Names with no loaded locator stay hidden and recover when metadata arrives without a new snapshot; replacement/despawn leave no stale plate. Observe Kuluu against the established retail binary/DAT reference in representative live model/pose cases before closing; do not require an always-above-silhouette result or use this locator as camera/pick policy.
notes:
2026-08-05: the mounted case of this is fixed (613da67) -- nameplate_anchor_y
now takes a `mounted` flag and adds retail's MOUNTED_ANCHOR_RISE (1.3, from
SkeletalMeshActor::GetElem's IsOnChocobo branch), fed by a MountedRider marker
scene.rs maintains. Target-ring and sub-target arrows share the function, so
they moved together.

That fix works around this bead rather than closing it, and the workaround is
the evidence for the real one: retail anchors on the AboveHead locator
(standard joint 2 -- research/xim resource/SkeletonSection.kt, StandardPosition),
which PC skeletons hang off joint 0 with a per-race offset (2.4 up for Elvaan M
vs a 2.08 baked mesh height). Anchoring on that locator instead of
BakedActor::actor_height would be both retail-exact and per-race correct, and
would make the 1.3 the only correction needed rather than one of several.
2026-09-08 investigation (checkout b14c215c): verified the name anchor against the installed retail FFXiMain.dll, not only XIM. Binary SHA256 f4f90fbd080c05448aab3f866b127d7c1675b3cc15c8beaa57bfc584064b7e7c; image base 0x10000000, decompressed .text RVA 0x1000, length 3289278. Local evidence: artifacts/retail/nameplate-2026-09-08/binary-evidence.txt and locator-data.json (reference artifacts, not committed).

Call chain: constructor at VA 0x100c5169 defaults name locator to 2; getter 0x100a3ed0 reads actor+0x8a7; name preparation 0x100cf430 calls GetElem via vtable+0x1c4 then adds actor+0x8c0 to Y before projection. GetElem 0x100d34a0 initializes output from Model.Position, calls 0x1002b980 -> 0x1002b9a0. The latter compares locator ID with 2 at 0x1002b9ac and SPECIAL-CASES it: read static locator translation (0x10029e50, record+0x0e), component-multiply by Model.Scale in x,z,y order (0x1002ba09..0x1002ba30), add to supplied model position. It bypasses the pose-evaluated gate and animated bone matrix path used for other locators. This corroborates XIClient World/Model/ModelInstance.cpp:280-324, ModelPartInstance.cpp:234-239, and World/Actor/SkeletalMeshActor.cpp:4956-4962.

Critical correction to prior notes: do NOT implement locator2 by calling the ordinary animated standard_joint_world_position helper. For the default name locator, retail uses STATIC authored translation, not animated head position, mesh bounds, or a crown-clearance test. Reference index 2 is also not necessarily skeleton bone index 2. Animation-independent is relative to Model.Position; actor movement still moves the label.

Direct installed DAT measurements at scale 1, converting retail negative Y to upward height: Damselfly model 0x01c0 -> file ID 1748 -> ROM/5/81.DAT, skeleton gaga, locator2=(0,-3.5,0), bone0; Hume M/F and Mithra 2.0; Elvaan M/F 2.4; Tarutaru M/F 1.3; Galka 2.6. All sampled locator2 references point to bone0. Damselfly model ID is corroborated by vendor/server/sql/mob_pools.sql:957. These values must be read from DATs, not copied into a client table.

Current mismatch survives latest main: kuluu-render/src/camera.rs:87 uses BakedActor.actor_height + 0.1 (2.3 fallback), nameplate_billboard.rs:303,355 adds that scalar to actor translation, and dat_vos2.rs:2333 defines height as max_mesh_y-min_mesh_y. This is structurally different even with successful model load and scale 1. For a floating model, extent also loses the bottom's offset from the entity origin. Screenshot alone cannot distinguish this from fallback on that particular runtime entity.

Implementation direction: carry the authored static locator into model metadata; compute name anchor from rendered Model.Position plus scaled/coordinate-converted locator2; keep actor-specific vertical offset and applicable mount/chair corrections. Do not automatically change pick hitbox or camera to this locator: their retail policies require separate evidence. title: Minimap/Map markers: per-entity heading, retail nameplate colours, smoother shapes
description:
Three related marker-presentation gaps (enhanced surface — retail's map shows no entity dots at all):
1. Only the self marker has a heading indicator; every entity has a heading in the snapshot.
2. Marker fill colours are a bespoke palette (minimap/overlay.rs::dot_color) that disagrees with the nameplates. The retail ncol table already loaded by nameplate_color.rs carries the real semantics — unclaimed mob yellow, claimed-by-your-party red, claimed-by-others purple, NPC green, party blue — so the dots should resolve through name_color_choice() like the plates do.
3. Markers are plain squares; target/lock state overloads the FILL colour, which collides with the semantic palette (target yellow vs unclaimed-mob yellow). Role highlight belongs on an outline, not the fill.
design: Draw each dot as a rounded/teardrop node rotated to the entity's facing; resolve fill through nameplate_color::name_color_choice with the existing per-kind palette as the pre-DAT fallback; move target/lock emphasis to a Bevy UI Outline so the fill stays semantic.
acceptance_criteria: Every marker shows facing; dot colour matches that entity's nameplate colour; target/lock reads as a ring, not a recolour.
notes: Landed in e2f0c37: fills resolve through nameplate_color::name_color_choice (retail ncol), target/lock moved to an Outline ring, dots are map pins pointing at each entity's heading, dark hairline for legibility on parchment. LIVE LEG OWED (console locked): capture a populated zone (e.g. !zone 230) and confirm each dot's colour matches that actor's nameplate.
close_reason: Fixed in e2f0c37 and verified live (artifacts/verify/minimap-*.png): map edge lands within 0.5px of the marker mapping's prediction at an overhanging window, pin tip tracks the actor's heading through all four quadrants, and fills resolve from the real retail ncol table.

title: Own character is not mouse-targetable in third person
description: Retail lets you click your own character to select yourself as target (same as the F1/party-slot-1 route we already have). In Kuluu the self entity is excluded from picking twice: scene.rs spawns it with Pickable::IGNORE and picking.rs::sync_entity_hitboxes filters Without<IsSelf>, so no transparent hitbox child is ever created for self. Everything downstream already handles a self target (TargetKindLite::SelfPc in action_model, target panel, ring, strobe) — only the click surface is missing.
design: Spawn the same EntityHitbox child for the self entity, gated on camera mode: pickable in CameraMode::Chase, Pickable::IGNORE in CameraMode::FirstPerson (the FP camera sits inside the box, which would swallow every world click).
acceptance_criteria: Clicking own character in third person sets Target to self_char_id and shows the self target panel; clicking again opens the SelfPc action menu; first-person world clicks are unaffected.
close_reason: Self entity now spawns the same EntityHitbox as every other actor, pickable in chase view and Pickable::IGNORE in first person

title: Harness config: state the .agents/-canonical rule and enforce it in checks.sh
description:
The .agents/ (canonical) + .claude/ (adapter) split is correct but neither written down as a rule nor mechanically checked, so it reads as inconsistency and drifts silently.

Evidence:
- AGENTS.md:114 points at '.claude/hooks/' for the comment-rot hooks; that directory does not exist (hooks live in .agents/hooks/ and are registered by path in .claude/settings.json).
- .agents/AGENTS.md describes the layout in prose but never states WHY .claude/hooks is absent: directory-discovered config (skills/, agents/) needs a symlink; config-registered config (hooks) needs only a path pointer.
- ffxi-agent/ carries a second, divergent harness (real .claude/hooks|agents|skills, plus opencode.json reading a .claude/ path) with nothing marking it as an intentional exception.
design:
1. Replace the .agents/AGENTS.md prose with a mechanism-to-wiring table (directory-discovered -> symlink; config-registered -> path pointer; root instruction file -> symlink; runtime state -> real + gitignored).
2. Fix AGENTS.md:114 to reference .agents/hooks/.
3. New 'harness' stage in scripts/checks.sh asserting the invariants: every tracked .claude/* symlink resolves inside .agents/; every hook command in .claude/settings.json exists and is executable; no root .claude/hooks/; no tracked doc references a root .claude/ path other than settings.json or the symlinks. Wire into .githooks/pre-push and ci.yml.
4. Carve out ffxi-agent/ explicitly in .agents/AGENTS.md as a runtime harness the checker skips.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/checks.sh harness passes on a clean tree, fails when a .claude symlink is broken / a settings.json hook path is missing / a doc cites .claude/hooks; pre-push and CI both run it; .agents/AGENTS.md carries the rule table and the ffxi-agent carve-out.
close_reason: Landed in 60f6e64: mechanism→wiring rule table in .agents/AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md:114 .claude/hooks path bug fixed, scripts/checks.sh harness stage wired into pre-push + ci.yml format job, ffxi-agent/ carve-out documented and skipped. All six invariants fault-injection tested.

title: Treasure pool state + panel UI + lot/pass input
description:
Hold the 10-slot treasure pool in SessionState (fed by 0x0D2/0x0D3), publish it over the wire snapshot, render retail's treasure pool panel (item icon/name, per-item countdown from StartTime, own lot / current winning lot + lotter name), and wire lot/pass to c2s 0x041/0x042.

Pool lifetime rules from research/XiPackets/world/server/0x00D3: JudgeFlg 0 = a lot was cast (announce roll, passes are silent), 1 = won/distributed, 2 = lost because the winner did not meet requirements, >=3 = silently clear the slot. A player's lot/pass status is only valid while they stay in the zone and party, so the pool must be dropped on zone change.
acceptance_criteria: Pool slots appear/clear per 0x0D2/0x0D3; lot and pass send the right c2s index; pool clears on zone change (see the zone-change-not-a-clean-lifecycle trap).
close_reason: Closed

title: Day-of-week and moon-phase tint only exist on the env-gated DAT celestial path
description: The moon shows no day-of-week shading because the code that applies it is not reachable by default. CelestialClock (particle_sim.rs:33) carries day_of_week and moon_phase and IS populated by track_celestial_bodies (celestial_particles.rs:215), and moon_material.rs:57-58 parses day_of_week [[f32;4];8] and moon_phase [[f32;4];12] tables. But that whole path is the DAT celestial renderer, gated behind the FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS env var (celestial_particles.rs:32) and off by default. With it off, sun_moon.rs draws the hand-authored SunDisc/MoonDisc primitives instead (dat_celestials gates their visibility at sun_moon.rs:790,822), and those apply no weekday or phase tint at all. Retail's order is documented in the cexi audit as color x colorMultiplier, then day-of-week MODULATE2X, then moon-phase MODULATE2X. Two ways forward and they are NOT equivalent: (a) fix the DAT celestial path and make it the default -- but it has two open blockers, kuluu-lqz2 (billboards render black, per-vertex colour multiplies to zero) and kuluu-fjd3 (particle-linked MMB billboards decode ~100x too large), so flipping the gate today would trade a tintless moon for a black or sky-filling one; (b) apply the weekday/phase tables to the disc primitives as an interim. Decide before implementing.
design: Do NOT flip FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS as a shortcut -- kuluu-lqz2 and kuluu-fjd3 are what put it behind the gate.
acceptance_criteria: The moon visibly shifts tint across the 8 elemental days and its phase, on whichever path is default.

title: Nameplate status icons (linkshell/GM/bazaar/away/...) prefixed to the name
description:
Nameplates render name text only. Retail prefixes status-icon glyphs to the left of the name: linkshell pearl (tinted with the linkshell's colour), GM level, bazaar, away, LFG/seeking, anonymous, linkdead, POL, job-master star, trust, mentor/new-adventurer.

The icons are font-shape glyphs 0x8E..0xB1 in group "font    fontshp " (ROM/119/51.DAT), 32x32 crops off the "menu    ustatshd" sheet drawn at 16x16 screen units. Retail builds them as a marker prefix on the name string.

Evidence:
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ActorTelemetry.cpp:347 BuildTelemetryActorName (prefix assembly), :204 GetPrimaryActorNameMarker, :296 GetSecondaryActorNameMarker, :326 GetSpecialActorNameMarker
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Rendering/Active/CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:325-376 (icon glyphs scale 0.8 / advance 0.625) and :398-418 (only glyph 0x92 keeps the linkshell tint; every other icon draws neutral)
- source bits: vendor/server/src/map/packets/char_update.cpp:61-134 flags1_t/flags2_t/flags3_t (LinkShellFlag, Flags2.r/g/b = LS colour, GmLevel, BazaarFlag, AwayFlag, LfgFlag, AnonymousFlag, LinkDeadFlag, PlayOnelineFlag, LfgMasterFlag, TrustFlag, NewCharacterFlag, MentorFlag, BallistaTeam)
- flag->telemetry mapping: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Game/Net/Packets/s2c/0x00D.cpp:127-215
design: Decode the 0x0D flag words in ffxi-proto into a named PcFlags struct, carry it on the wire Entity, and port the marker selection as a pure function returning the glyph codes. Rasterise the icon sprites into the existing nameplate billboard texture ahead of the text run.
acceptance_criteria: A PC in a linkshell shows the pearl in that linkshell's colour; GM/bazaar/away/anon/LFG/linkdead icons appear from their packet bits; icons sit left of the name at retail proportions; marker selection is unit-tested against the XIClient precedence order.
notes: Landed: kuluu-render/src/nameplate_marker.rs (marker selection) + nameplate_icons.rs (font fontshp glyph cache) + the icon compositing pass in nameplate_billboard.rs::rasterize_plate. Markers implemented: PlayOnline, LinkDead, Away, GM level, job-master star (+tail), auto-party, seeking, bazaar, linkshell pearl (tinted). Deliberately omitted for lack of a grounded source: the ballista/besieged markers 0x9E-0xA7, the Monstrosity marker 0xAB, and the pet/trust markers keyed off AUDIT_130 (which ride the 0x067 pet packet we do not decode) - so mentor / new-adventurer icons are still absent.

title: Retail nameplate name colors from the menu ncol DAT table
description:
Nameplate text colour is a hardcoded per-EntityKind guess in kuluu-render/src/nameplate_billboard.rs::nameplate_color. Retail picks from a 23-entry table loaded out of the retail menu shape group "menu    ncol    " (ROM/119/51.DAT) and selects an index per actor with ActorTelemetry::NameColorSet — so party members, mobs claimed by my party vs another party, NPCs, dead actors, LFG/anon/away PCs and GM levels all get distinct, data-driven colours. Pet colour is likewise wrong today.

Evidence:
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ActorTelemetry.cpp:1560 NameColorSet (index selection), :420 InitializeNameColors (table load, per-vertex RGBA of the ncol quads)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/UIShapeQuad.cpp:63-88 (the +1 RGB / 1.5x alpha legacy adjust applied on load)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Rendering/Active/CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:620 (D3DTOP_MODULATE2X: the 0x7F-based table values are doubled at draw)
- claim owner comes from BtTargetID (already on the wire as Entity::claim_id)
design: Read the ncol group with the existing ffxi_dat::ui_element parser (already used for the Vana'diel clock orbs), cache it in a Bevy Resource beside UiElementAtlas. Port NameColorSet's index selection into a pure function over the wire Entity + party/alliance membership so it is unit-testable without Bevy.
acceptance_criteria: Party members, own-claim mobs (red), other-claim mobs (purple), alliance-but-other-party claims (blended), NPCs (green), unclaimed mobs (yellow), dead (dark grey) and GM levels each resolve to the retail ncol index; colours come from the DAT, not literals; self-skipping test asserts the real table loads 23 entries.
notes: Verification 2026-08-03: live in-zone drive blocked - the LSB dev VM is gone (limactl: no instance; 54230/54231 held by a stale orphaned forwarder, auth dies 'tls handshake eof'). Observed live from a GUI client: nameplate_color loaded 23 entries and nameplate_icons 9 glyphs from ROM/119/51.DAT. Still unverified: packet->CharFlags->plate against a live server. Re-verify once the dev stack is rebuilt (see the lsb-dev-server-sidecar-virtiofs memory).

title: Indoor weather records and ambient beds are harvested but never selected
description: ffxi-dat harvests both halves of every zone weather set (WeatherSet::indoor 0x2F records and WeatherSet::indoor_ambient cues, ~738 cues corpus-wide), but ZoneWeather::indoor() is hardwired false because viewer-core sources no zone-indoor flag. Interiors therefore draw the outdoor environment and play the outdoor ambient bed.
design: Retail splits on XiZone::zone->PlaceCode (research/XIClient .../World/Weather/WeatherTransition.cpp:454-455). Plumb an equivalent into ZoneWeather (sample_zone_weather currently hardcodes `let indoor = false`) so WeatherSet::ambient(indoor) and select_records can reach the indo/ half.

title: Lock-on does not hold the target: Escape/Tab/party keys/mouse still re-target or clear it
description:
While lock-on is active the main target must be immovable — retail requires releasing the lock first. Today every ordinary targeting path still mutates Target while LockOn holds: ClearTarget/Escape (kuluu/src/view_native/input.rs:323), Tab cycle (:346-357), party slot F1-F6 (:376-385), and mouse click Set/Clear (kuluu-render/src/picking.rs:301-303). Since auto_lock_on_when_engaged locks on every engage, this is hit constantly in combat.

Reference: research/xim PlayerTargetSelector.kt returns early while isTargetLocked() in clearTarget (:62), targetPartyMember (:74), targetCycle (:92), tryDirectlyTarget (:225) and tryDirectlyEngage (:257), with a !subTargetMode carve-out. XIM is tier 6; XIClient has no lock-on targeting policy to cross-check (see kuluu-j03o's audit of m_TargetLock), so the rule rests on XIM plus live retail behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: With LockOn active: Escape, Tab, F1-F6 and clicking another entity or the ground leave Target unchanged; releasing the lock restores all of them. Sub-target and the engaged Switch Target flow stay exempt. Entity despawn/untargetable auto-clear and zone-change reset still clear both.
notes:
Deliberate carve-outs: (1) the engaged 'Switch Target' menu flow (SelectTargetMode) is retail's sanctioned mid-fight re-target and stays exempt; (2) clicking the locked target still opens the target action menu (that is not a de-select, and it is the mouse path to Switch Target/Disengage).

IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 (commit 16bd91d), code + unit tests, fmt/clippy clean, 706 viewer-core + 378 client unit tests pass. Policy single-sourced as kuluu-render::lock_on::suppresses_retarget(lock, sub_target_flow); call sites: input.rs:326 (target_pinned gates ClearTarget/:328, Tab+Enter-acquire/:338, party slots/:382) and picking.rs:315 via the new ClickResolution::Ignored (resolve_click_target now takes a locked flag). input.rs:~460 also releases a lock whose main target went away.

DELIBERATE HOLE: the /target, /targetnpc, /targetenemy, /targetparty1-6 text commands are NOT gated — typed commands read as explicit intent and keep an escape hatch if a lock ever traps a player. Gate them in slash_apply.rs (SlashOutcome::SetTarget) if live retail says otherwise.

REMAINING: live confirmation against the LSB stack was not run (dev stack still down per the Sidecar virtiofs path breakage). Two open questions for the retail-observe pass: (1) whether retail's Escape is a hard no-op while locked (what is implemented, XIM's shape) or releases the lock first and clears on a second press; (2) that the Switch Target flow still re-targets mid-fight.

title: Sun shadows and light intensity are physically-lit, not retail-flat
description: User observation with recordings 2026-08-03 10:12: sun rays and cast shadows are far too intense versus retail/cexi, which do not use physical lighting. Retail composes lighting as a clamped vertex-lit term with a 2x modulate and no shadow-mapped sun; we run Bevy PBR with a real DirectionalLight plus cascaded shadow maps, so contrast and shadow darkness are engine-native rather than DAT-derived. Related but distinct from the audit's clamp finding (zone_ffxi.wgsl / skinned_ffxi.wgsl do not clamp the lit term before the 2x modulate, which is its own bead). Needs a decision on how faithful to go: retail has no dynamic shadows at all outdoors, so matching it means gating or heavily attenuating the shadow pass rather than tuning it.
design: Settle whether outdoor sun shadows are Vanilla-off / Enhanced-on behind a feature flag, per the repo's vanilla-parity default, before tuning any numbers.
acceptance_criteria: A stated policy for outdoor shadows with a flag, and shadow intensity that does not read as brighter/darker than retail in A/B captures.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (f43df5d clouds/fog bit, 9009533 weat generators, cc201af vertex-colour decode + per-stage saturate); gate green, 1359 unit tests + 2 real-DAT integration tests pass. NOT yet verified in a running client.

title: [bug] Undriveable event collapses 4 distinct failures into one 'not yet supported' message
description: event_dialog::Begin::Undriveable carried only Option<u8> stopped_op, so a missing string DAT, a missing event DAT, an NPC server id with no block, and an event id absent from the block it landed in all surfaced as the identical chat line '[event] cutscene N auto-skipped (not yet supported)' with stopped_op=None. That wrongly implicates the opcode backlog (kuluu-u7r5) for failures that never reach the VM. Worked example: the outpost conquest guard event 32763. Verified it is NOT an opcode gap -- LSB uses 32763 in exactly 24 zones and the retail DATs author it in exactly those 24; in Pashhow Marshlands (zone 109) it lives in NPC block 0x0106D286 (= 0x01000000 + 109<<12 + 646, matching LSB's server-id encoding), the string DAT (file 6529) loads, and driving it end-to-end yields the real menu: 'What do you want?' / Signet / home point / Nothing. So a live auto-skip of 32763 is a lookup failure, and the message could not say which. Now carries UndriveableReason (NoStrings / NoEventDat / NoBlockForActor / NoEventEntry / StoppedOnOpcode), reported in both the chat line and the warn log, with unique_no hex-formatted so it can be compared against the DAT block actor.
acceptance_criteria: The chat line and warn log name which stage failed; opcode failures still report the opcode.
close_reason: Fixed in f89f8fe: UndriveableReason surfaced in the chat line and warn log

title: mysql_async fixtures panic instead of self-skipping when MariaDB accepts then drops the connection
description: scripts/checks.sh test fails on a machine with no LSB dev stack: ffxi-client/tests/agent_session.rs:47 panics with 'provisioning ephemeral LSB account+char: connecting to xidb at mysql://...@127.0.0.1:3306/xidb / Input-output error: connection closed'. AGENTS.md states these fixtures self-skip when the server is unreachable, and the reachability probe does pass -- something is listening on 3306 and accepts the TCP connection, then closes it during the MariaDB handshake. The probe therefore reports 'reachable' and the fixture goes on to panic. Skip on handshake/IO failure too, not just on connect-refused, so a half-up stack is treated the same as an absent one.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test with no reachable xidb skips rather than fails, whether the port is closed, refused, or accepting-then-dropping.
close_reason: Implemented in the 2026-08-19 audited bead batch; full fmt+clippy+test gate green (2672 tests incl. live integration suites against the running LSB stack); adversarially reviewed (one kzxp regression caught and fixed with a pinning test).

title: Sound ops 0x60/0x4A are dropped -- 8 spell effect DATs are fully silent
description: ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:137-168 has no 0x60 or 0x4A arm, so those stages fall to StageKind::Unknown and scheduler_runtime.rs:879 never fires. Eight files in 2800-3300 (3108-3110, 3115-3119) have zero recognised sound stages and are completely silent; their 4063/4064/4065 Sep chunks exist in-file. Corpus-wide 0x60 appears 564 times with 521/521 ids resolving locally, and 275 routines have it as their only sound stage. Both tier-5 ports carry the full family: research/xim/.../EffectRoutineParser.kt:405 maps 0x60 Global and :337 maps 0x4A PlayerOnly; cexi's effect.js:29 treats {0x0A,0x0B,0x4A,0x53,0x60} as one SoundEffect set. Operand layout (DatId, i32, far/near/unk f32) per cexi-docs/fx/effect_system.md:190. NOTE: do NOT add cexi's 4-frame same-id dedup -- it is cexi's own heuristic (effect.js:151-159), not retail; retail's only same-sound suppression is flag-driven (SoundEffectHandler.cpp:675 ExclusiveChannel).
acceptance_criteria: 0x60 and 0x4A parse to sound StageKinds and fire; the eight silent DATs produce sound stages.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (a66fc22, 203d16c, c02f435, 5080ce6, 0a0ecea); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guards

title: Event master block: ZONE_PLAYER_ACTOR is 0x7FFFFFF0, and event_entry has no 0xFFFE wildcard fallback
description: ffxi-dat/src/event_dat.rs:21 declares ZONE_PLAYER_ACTOR = 0x7FFFFFFF citing XiEvents 'Event DAT Structures.md', which is wrong on this. The bytes disagree: ROM/21/39, /52 and /54 each contain exactly one 0x7F-pattern block and it is 0x7FFFFFF0 at block 0, matching XiEvents' own local-player lookup value in 'Event VM Functions.md':463-466. zone_block() therefore returns None on every real zone; the two tests at :242-252 pass only because they synthesise blocks with our own constant. Latent today -- the only production caller (ffxi-client/src/event_dialog.rs:112) uses block_for_actor. Fix alongside: event_entry (:57-63) is an exact match and has no 0xFFFE wildcard fallback; 0xFFFE is the catch-all the engine dispatches, one or two entries per zone, sitting in the master block. 0xFFFF is a placeholder id that must NOT match.
acceptance_criteria: ZONE_PLAYER_ACTOR = 0x7FFFFFF0; zone_block() resolves on real zone DATs; event_entry falls back to a 0xFFFE entry when no exact id matches, and never matches 0xFFFF.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (a66fc22, 203d16c, c02f435, 5080ce6, 0a0ecea); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guards

title: npc_dat_id top arm is retail's formula shifted by the 307-slot registration hole
description: ffxi-viewer-core/src/look_resolver.rs:14-25 uses m<3193 -> m+0x17A8B else m+0x180F2. Arms 1-3 match retail; the top arm mistakes a registration hole for a boundary. Retail: m<3500 -> m+96907 else m+98239 (disassembly at VA 0x100C513D loads 0x18D6B=101739 and computes (m-3500)+101739, quoted at research/cexi-docs/reference/ffximain.md:288-300). Every fid for modelid 3194-3499 is VTABLE=0 and no retail mob_pools row uses them; first registered fid is 101739 = 3500+98239 (reference/model-file-ids.md:38-47). Re-resolved through VTABLE: 0/29 registered under ours, 29/29 under retail's. The dispatch gate silently continues (look_resolver.rs:639-651) so the entity spawns as a nameplate with no body. Scope: 62 npc_list rows + 3 Apex mob pools, all late-era zones; zero in classic content. Inherited honestly -- research/xim NpcTable.kt uses the same values and labels them // Speculated.
acceptance_criteria: Top arm is m<3500 -> m+96907 else m+98239; a warn! fires on an unresolved modelid instead of a silent continue.
close_reason: Implemented and committed (a66fc22, 203d16c, c02f435, 5080ce6, 0a0ecea); fmt+clippy green, all unit tests pass incl. new retail-byte guards

title: Decompose handle_sub_packet and keepalive_loop so session/ can take a domain split
description: Blocks the session/ domain split (the highest-value refactor in the repo, currently NOT EXECUTABLE). 2,781 lines -- 48% of session/mod.rs's non-test code -- live inside two function bodies: handle_sub_packet (973 lines, 45 opcode arms, 20 params, its call duplicated verbatim at two sites) and keepalive_loop (1,806 lines, 55 command arms, 22 params, 35 let-mut locals). You cannot split a function across files.
design: Four blockers, strict order. (1) Two parameter objects. (2) Eleven arms escape via continue/break -- converting those to a returned control-flow enum is a REWRITE, not a refactor, and a single missed one silently swallows Disconnect or kills link-down detection. (3) 38 .await sites hold &mut MapClient while event_tx / dialog_session / local_menu / dbox are live, so expect split borrows, not a god-struct. (4) The tick branch batches multiple subpackets into one payload and computes datagram_header_id(sub_seq) AFTER the last increment -- that is the c2s seq-window invariant, where drift means the server silently ignores every client packet while the session still looks healthy. Move it LAST, if ever. Target vocabulary once unblocked: entity, battle, event, chat, inventory, movement, mog_house, status, emote, shop, widescan, plus a shared msg_render. party (48 lines, 2 of 50 commits) fails boundary criterion 6 and folds into entity.

title: Split slash_commands.rs by command family, paired with slash_apply.rs
description: kuluu/src/view_native/slash_commands.rs is 4,999 lines and is the highest-value executable refactor in the repo under the refactoring-economics rubric: technique #1 (per-domain split on the axis questions arrive on), applied to a file the domain already partitions, with no god-function residue of the kind that blocks session/mod.rs.
design: Precondition already established by kuluu-5725: text_input/slash_apply.rs (1,159 lines) holds the APPLY side per family. kuluu-5725 REJECTED the per-family sub-split of slash_apply.rs on boundary criterion 5 (near-disjoint) precisely because the PARSE side still lives here -- so 'what does /minimap do' opens two files, before and after. Moving the parse side to matching family files closes that leak and makes both splits buyable at once, with a uniform skeleton across the pair. PRE-FLIGHT GATE before any edit: a writable public surface on one page, a grep-proven closed blast radius, a named repetition with a count, and the target file list written down BEFORE any helper extraction -- Phase 1 without a named Phase 2 target list is forbidden. Do NOT extract shared parse helpers first. Measure a representative change's read set before and after, or state plainly that the justification is design quality rather than tokens.
notes: Blocked-adjacent work, do NOT fold in: the mouse_nav_dispatch_system dissolution (design change, not relocation -- and a file for it would be the mechanism-axis shape that measured zero) and the SlashWriters narrowing (a post-split sealing commit).

title: Finish the subpacket_header_word contract: cite it, const fn it, mask it, and convert SubPacketWalker
description: d9e1384 moved the subpacket header-word bit contract to its emitter but only half-installed it. Four gaps: (1) NO vendor/server citation, despite the commit's whole purpose being to make ffxi-proto::framing the canonical home -- LSB counterparts are vendor/server/src/map/packets/basic.h:91-119 and map_networking.cpp:422-423. (2) It is 'pub fn', not 'pub const fn', though the body is fully const-evaluable over u16, so any const context must re-type the bit math the helper exists to own. (3) It omits both defensive steps LSB performs: LSB masks the id (basic.h:110, 'ref<uint16>(0) |= id & 0x1FF;') and rounds size up to a 4-byte multiple (basic.h:118). Unreachable today -- max size_words is 38 -- but this is pub in a library crate, and a size_words >= 128 would emit a zero-size header, terminating LSB's subpacket walk at map_networking.cpp:419-420 and silently dropping every batched subpacket after it. (4) SubPacketWalker::next, 90 lines below in the same file, still decomposes the identical contract byte-wise with four unnamed literals that the new guard test does not cover.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (d8eb58a6, f06851f1) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Review follow-up commit dbdabf3b lands on wt/kuluu-0rem. Final shape of the framing subpacket contract: SUBPACKET_{OPCODE_MASK, SIZE_WORDS_SHIFT, SIZE_WORDS_MASK, WORD_BYTES, HEADER_SIZE} consts; MIN_FRAME_SIZE derives from SUBPACKET_HEADER_SIZE; `subpacket_header_word`/`subpacket_opcode`/`subpacket_size_bytes`/`subpacket_size_words` are all `pub const fn` and are the single emitter/matcher pair that SubPacketWalker and map_client both go through. `subpacket_size_words` saturates at 0x7F words (508 bytes) rather than casting; this is an intentional, documented divergence from LSB setSize's modulo-256 wrap at an unreachable input, and is pinned by subpacket_size_words_saturates_at_the_header_field_width. Citations verified against vendor/server: basic.h:91-99, 106-111, 113-119 (118 = round-up line), map_networking.cpp:419-423. Nothing pushed.
Unknowns left open: The worktree already contained uncommitted edits matching all three findings when I arrived (likely an earlier interrupted pass on this same task). I reviewed them line by line, re-verified the vendor/server citations and the saturation bound myself, re-ran fmt/clippy/tests, and committed them as my | Saturating deliberately diverges from LSB's setSize, which would wrap modulo 256 for an oversized body. The divergence is unreachable in practice (max FFXI subpacket body is well under 508 bytes) and was chosen for the defensive posture the finding asked for; if strict LSB byte-for-byte emulation at | Did not run the full scripts/checks.sh workspace gate (build/style stages) in the shared target dir; only the two crates touched by the change were checked.
close_reason: Landed on main d8eb58a6, f06851f1 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Narrow session/codec.rs visibility and give the new wave modules real import lists
description: 62e5acd's message claims 'nothing widened past pub(crate)', but pub(crate) is one level wider than the compiler demands. Proven by experiment: rewriting all 16 pub(crate) items in codec.rs to pub(super) compiles; making mod.rs:15 'pub(crate) use codec::*' private compiles; making build_subpacket_header (:359), CHAT_NAME_UNKNOWN00 (:431) and ITEM_MOVE_AUTO_SLOT (:542) fully private compiles. Only ZMRQ_LE needs to escape. Separately, all seven modules this wave created open with a bare 'use super::*;' and the parent answers with a glob back, so the glob runs both directions and a reader of codec.rs still cannot resolve a name without the 7,966-line parent -- which defeats the point of the split. codec.rs's real dependency surface is five use lines.
design: Rubric technique #4: visibility narrowing is what seals a split from a convention into a compiler-checked boundary. 7facf48 did exactly this for decode/ and it worked. Do the same here. The bidirectional glob is the more important half.

description: Bevy 0.19 shipped perf work (GPU task offloading, skinned-mesh-aware culling, renderer optimizations per release notes). Audit which 0.19 perf improvements are automatic vs opt-in, whether our custom pipelines actually participate (culling, batching, GPU-driven paths), and whether 0.19.x point releases contain perf fixes the vendored pins block. Apply the confirmed-applicable ones. Triggered by alternativeto.net Bevy 0.19 coverage; authoritative source is bevy.org release notes + migration guide.

title: delivery_box_against_live_lsb: fresh fixture char never gets a self 0x00A LOGIN, so DeliOpen never opens the outbox
description:
Surfaced 2026-08-01 once the kuluu-d2ec 1062 duplicate-charid blocker was cleared — this failure was previously MASKED by the fixture dying during provisioning, so it is newly visible, not newly introduced.

The fixture char now provisions and logs in fine (lobby 0xA1 char-list, 0x07 select, 0x02 ack, 0xA2 handoff, lpkt_next_login all clean, map UDP bound), but the session never sees itself:

  WARN zone-in flood ended without a self-position seed (no 0x00A LOGIN for self before deadline)
       — outbound POS suppressed until a CHAR_PC for self lands, iteration=1 current_zone_id=0
  zone-in flood drained iteration=1 total_subs=0 server_last_seq=0 self_pos_seeded=false
  tally: BoxTally { in_zone: true, pc_entity_seen: false, opened: None, ... }

then ffxi-client/tests/delivery_box_live.rs:204 asserts DeliOpen opened the outbox and gets None.

Note total_subs=0 and current_zone_id=0: the flood drained with nothing in it. This is the fresh-char zone-in path, where two prior bugs were already found and fixed (the c2s datagram header must carry the LAST subpacket's sync — see MEMORY c2s-seq-window-invariant; and the intro cutscene rides the 0x00A LOGIN packet and must be 0x05B-ended — see MEMORY zone-in-cutscene-rides-0x00a). Check whether this is a third symptom in the same area or a regression in one of those two fixes.

Unknown whether the other three live-LSB tests (play_lifecycle, zone_change, agent_session) also fail — cargo aborted after this target. Re-run with --no-fail-fast to find out.

NOT caused by commit 1bc4bbf, which touched only mzb/d3m/particle_gen/ui_element/particle_sim/nameplate_billboard/scheduler_runtime/zone_clouds/event-VM — none on the delivery-box or zone-in path.

title: Agent socket: focus-free screenshot (Bevy GPU readback) so verification never steals the human's focus
description:
Capture is the last piece of GUI verification that needs the window frontmost. /verify's drive-gui.md currently shells out to `screencapture -l <window_id>`, which reads the macOS window-server backing store — for an occluded window that returns a stale cached frame (documented gotcha, drive-gui.md:135), so every capture has to raise the window and interrupt whatever the human is doing.

The client already has the right mechanism and just cannot reach it from the socket. ffxi-client/src/view_native/screenshot.rs uses Bevy `Screenshot::primary_window()`, which in bevy_render-0.19 is a GPU readback of the render target (copy_texture_to_buffer at screenshot.rs:598, map_async at :653) — NOT a window-server grab. It cannot return a stale frame, needs no Screen Recording permission, and does not care whether the window is visible. Today ScreenshotRequest is only written by the /screenshot slash command (text_input.rs:1539) and a keybind (input.rs:269), both of which need typed input.

Bevy keeps rendering while unfocused (bevy_winit-0.19 winit_config.rs:21, unfocused_mode = reactive_low_power 1/60s), so a background window still produces live frames.

Add AgentCommand::Screenshot{path} on the kuluu-0pof bridge pattern: intercept in agent_codec (do not forward to session), bump a seq + carry the path on the shared Arc<Mutex<DebugControl>>, and add a Bevy system that fires the existing ScreenshotRequest on seq change. Expose it as an ffxi-mcp tool alongside walk/debug_heights. Then make drive-gui.md focus-free-by-default.
acceptance_criteria: A socket screenshot command writes a correct, current PNG while the ffxi-client window is fully occluded by another app and was never raised. drive-gui.md leads with the focus-free path.
notes: Follows kuluu-0pof (closed): debug_drive/debug_heights already bridge socket->Bevy via DebugControl. Session commands (chat/action/snapshot) were already confirmed focus-free in live use.
close_reason: Built + verified live + committed (21a6fbb). AgentCommand::Screenshot{path} bridges socket->Bevy via DebugControl; ffxi-mcp screenshot tool added. play --unfocused / --mute added. scripts/launch.sh + capture.sh in the verify skill; drive-gui.md rewritten focus-free-first. Two limits found and handled rather than assumed away: macOS app-level activation is not suppressed by winit focused:false (launch.sh restores the prior frontmost app), and a fully occluded window renders nothing so the GPU readback is black (capture.sh asserts lit and auto-recovers with a logged focus blip). Follow-up kuluu-jiiv covers menu nav, the last keystroke-only surface.

title: macOS QoS: promote frame-critical Bevy threads to P-core-eligible classes
description: Activity Monitor during crowd play shows E-cores pegged while P-cores idle: Bevy's render thread and task-pool workers spawn at default macOS QoS, so the scheduler parks frame-blocking work on efficiency cores. No pinning API exists on macOS; the sanctioned lever is pthread_set_qos_class_self_np. Fix: init Compute/AsyncCompute/Io pools before TaskPoolPlugin with on_thread_spawn self-promotion (UserInteractive / UserInitiated / Utility), mirroring TaskPoolOptions default sizing; render thread self-promotes to UserInteractive via a once-guarded Render-schedule system (guaranteed to execute on the render thread). Session tokio threads stay default (E-core fine). Evidence: user Activity Monitor captures 2026-07-31.
notes: Landed: ThreadClass role abstraction (qos.rs) — macOS pthread QoS (FrameCritical=UserInteractive on compute pool + render thread via once-guarded Render system; AsyncCompute=UserInitiated; Background/IO=Utility), Windows SetThreadPriority (above/below normal), Linux background nice +5 via gettid/setpriority. Pools pre-initialized before DefaultPlugins, sizes formula-pinned to bevy_app defaults by tests. VERIFY: (1) live A/B — Activity Monitor core distribution + fps in crowd with/without (env-flag if needed); (2) Windows EcoQoS (SetThreadInformation/THREAD_POWER_THROTTLING) refinement needs real hybrid-Windows hardware; (3) Deck cross-build links gettid (needs glibc>=2.30 in the docker image — the deck-build gate will catch it).
close_reason: Re-verified 2026-09-09 by an adversarial done-check: Confirmed done. Commit 86469b92 implements every acceptance criterion in kuluu/src/view_native/qos.rs (moved intact under the kuluu-* rename in 3f2e5f03) and its 5-line wiring in kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs: a ThreadClass role abstraction with macOS pthread QoS self-promotion, Windows SetThreadPriority, and Linux background-nice; Compute/AsyncCompute/Io task pools pre-initialized before DefaultPlugins with per-role on_thread_spawn promotion and bevy_app-formula-pinned sizing (tested); and a once-guarded Render-schedule system that self-promotes the render thread. Session tokio threads are correctly left untouched. `cargo test -p kuluu --features native-window qos::` passes all 3 unit tests. The bead's NOTES field itself records this as "Landed" and lists three residual items explicitly as VERIFY/follow-up (live A/B measurement, Windows EcoQoS hardware-gated refinement, Deck glibc gettid check) rather than as unmet acceptance criteria — closing as done, with those three trackable as a separate follow-up if still wanted.

title: Vanilla sun flare costs a full depth prepass (~2ms encode) whenever the sun is up
description: apply_camera_prepass_system (ffxi-viewer-core/src/graphics/settings.rs:1302) inserts DepthPrepass when sky_style==Vanilla && sun_altitude>0 so the lens flare can occlude behind terrain — that re-encodes ALL zone+actor geometry into a prepass every frame (~1.8-2.0ms avg measured in populated Jeuno, 2026-07-31 differential run), on every preset including Low, daytime only. Cheaper faithful alternative: raycast camera->sun against the MZB zone collision BVH (already resident for player movement) to decide flare occlusion, dropping the prepass requirement for the flare entirely (keep it for DoF/TAA).

Live checks pending next session: archway fade-out, Mog House interior (BVH coverage), camera_skip surfaces. Accepted behavior change: PCs/NPCs covering the sun no longer dim the flare (BVH is zone-only).

title: Skinned material instancing: shared/bindless FfxiSkinnedMaterial instead of per-submesh instances
description: Every actor submesh gets its own FfxiSkinnedMaterial with per-instance tint/flags baked in (ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs, FfxiSkinnedFlags spawn path), so no two crowd draws batch — bind-group churn per draw. Upstream bevy#24448 (the 0.18->0.19 Apple-integrated-GPU regression, bisected to bevy#23481) closed with exactly this app-side fix: one shared bindless material restored 0.18 parity on 0.19. Move tint/flags to per-instance data (mesh attribute or bindless uniform array) and share the material. Payoffs: (1) rgraph encode + rprep shrink on the current CPU path, (2) precondition for re-testing FFXI_GPU_PREPROCESS=1 on macOS (view_native/mod.rs force-disables the GPU path after measuring 12.8 vs 34.3fps — that measurement predates this refactor). bevy#23662 (MeshUniform GPU allocation, merged to main 2026-07-07, unreleased) may help further in 0.20; not worth cherry-picking onto 0.19.
notes: Attributed trace 2026-07-31 (trace-1785546703711757, 2112 frames): wgpu command translation is the dominant render cost — RenderContextState::apply 7.2ms/frame + CommandEncoder::finish 7.2ms/frame ≈ 14.4ms of the 21.4ms render wall. Device::create_bind_group ~29/frame (first trace). upload_ffxi_material_buffers costs 1.4ms/frame from ~200 small write_uniform calls (joints+lighting per skin, ~17us wgpu overhead each) — consolidate into one buffer with per-skin dynamic offsets as part of this refactor (2 writes/frame total).
close_reason: Phases 1a/1b/2 landed on main (commits 62f66d8, 268ee1a): per-actor joints/lighting/flags moved from ~800 per-submesh material assets into two shared storage buffers (FfxiSkin 9056B/actor + FfxiInstance 48B/submesh) indexed via MeshTag; one ExtractSchedule uploader = 2 write_buffer/frame (was ~200); materials deduped by texture via FfxiSkinnedMaterialCache; strobe/lighting/pose mutators moved off material assets (unblocks tick par_iter, kuluu-ye8e). Guard tests: WGSL mirrors, encase sizes, slot allocator, growth generation bump, despawn slot-free observers, cache dedupe — 613/613 lib tests + full gate green. Live Jeuno counter capture (write_buffer ~200->2, create_bind_group ~29->~0, fps) pending next user session. Follow-ups: kuluu-ddkn (mesh dedupe), kuluu-fwom (bindless textures), kuluu-d2v7 (motion-vector prev-frame skins).

title: Camera FOV is an uncited 50 degrees; retail's is 2*atan(192/350) = 57.4
description:
GraphicsSettings::fov_deg defaults to a bare 50.0 in ffxi-viewer-core/src/graphics/settings.rs (four preset sites: 498, 528, 558, 592), fed to Bevy's PerspectiveProjection.fov, which is the VERTICAL fov. No citation, so it is a magic number by the AGENTS.md rule.

Retail computes its vertical fov from a focal-length parameter:
  research/XIClient/.../World/Generator/Effects/CMoElem.cpp:274
    float fovy = 2 * atan2f(192.0f, GameManager::instance->ProjectionFocalLength);
  research/XIClient/.../World/Camera/CameraManager.cpp:318
    SetProjectionFocalLength(350.0f)          <- the default
=> fovy = 2 * atan(192/350) = 57.43 degrees.

The 192 is half of 384, i.e. retail's internal projection half-height; the focal
length is what cutscenes and zoom effects animate (CameraResource.cpp:125 sets it
from a keyframe's FovCalculationParameter, ControllableActor.cpp:424 drops it to
280.0 = 68.6 degrees for some state, CameraManager.cpp:684-732 eases it back
toward 350 at 6 units/tick).
design:
Express it the way retail does rather than hard-coding 57.43: a named PROJECTION_HALF_HEIGHT = 192.0 and DEFAULT_FOCAL_LENGTH = 350.0, with fov_deg derived. That keeps the door open for the focal-length animation above (cutscene FOV pulls), which we do not model at all today and which is the real reason retail parameterises it this way.

Deliberately NOT bundled into e48bb7f: changing the default FOV moves every frame the user sees, and fov_deg is a user-facing graphics setting with its own FOV_SLOTS cycle, so it wants its own before/after look rather than riding along with a camera-collision fix.
acceptance_criteria: fov_deg default derives from the two cited retail constants; a test pins the derived value at 57.4 +/- 0.1; FOV_SLOTS still contains the default.
close_reason: Implemented in the 2026-08-19 audited bead batch; full fmt+clippy+test gate green (2672 tests incl. live integration suites against the running LSB stack); adversarially reviewed (one kzxp regression caught and fixed with a pinning test).
