title: Locomotion clips are never time-scaled — retail scales playback rate, causing foot-slide when hasted/slowed/mounted
notes:
REVERSED RULE (2026-09-09), all from research/XIClient (tier 2, no retail observation).

SkeletalMeshActor::SelectMotionResId takes one scalar r (the move-vector ratio) and returns BOTH a clip id and a playback speed:

  r <= 0.0001        -> idle clip, speed 1.0
  0.0001 < r <= 0.5  -> wlk clip,  speed 3r   (1.0 at r=1/3, 1.5 at r=0.5)
  r > 0.5            -> run clip,  speed r    (0.5 at the threshold, 1.0 at full)

The source spells this as 'r > 1/3 then 3r <= 1.5', which reduces to a single threshold at r = 0.5. Deliberate discontinuity there: wlk at 1.5x hands off to run at 0.5x, crossfaded over the 16-frame fade DefaultMove passes to SetSystemMotion. The clip table field_7C8 is seeded from Constants::Strings::SkeletonAnimations = "idl?wlk?run?btl?" and refilled per status by ActorTelemetry::MotionSetChg (slot 0 idle, 1 wlk, 2 run, 3 btl, 4 currently-playing).

So the 'between run and walk' gait a player sees is NOT a third clip -- it is the run clip at a fractional rate. We cannot express it at all: ffxi-actor/src/actor_state.rs movement_animation returns a clip id only, and kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs advance_actor_pose leaves loop_duration None for every locomotion clip, so ffxi-actor/src/animation.rs computes scaling_factor == 1.0 always.

WHERE r COMES FROM -- SkeletalMeshActor::GetMoveVectorRatio has two paths, and they disagree:

Path A, local player under direct stick/key control (not autorun, GetMoveMode() != 1, not EVT):
  r = field_594 * (VirtActor94 / VirtActor96)
field_594 is the QUANTIZED stick magnitude from ControllableActor::AdjustAnalogKeyLength (|stick| <= 0.05 -> 0, <= 0.9 -> 1/3, else 1), capped to 1/3 under IsWalkLock. VirtActor94/VirtActor96 is current speed over base speed. So retail's self gait DOES respond to a server slow: at 70% base the run clip plays at 0.7x, below 50% it demotes to wlk.

Path B, all remote actors, plus the local player while auto-running / in an event / GetMoveMode()==1:
  expected = CheckTick() * VirtActor96() * (1/60)   [1/37.5 when riding]
  r_inst   = |displacement_xz| / expected
  r        = 0.75 * r_prev + 0.25 * r_inst          (field_824)
Measured, not commanded, with a 75% carry. Clamped to 1.0 when VirtActor73(), else 3.0. Final speed is then scaled by field_7E0.

TWO DIVERGENCES BEYOND THE MISSING RATE SCALE:

1. Threshold shape. Retail's threshold is on the NORMALIZED ratio (0.5 of the actor's own base speed), so it is scale-free. Ours is an absolute WALK_RUN_BOUNDARY = 3.0 y/s (kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs infers_walk_gait) applied identically to a 5 y/s PC (ratio 0.6) and a 10 y/s mount (ratio 0.3).

2. Self gait is a pure toggle for us. kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs tick_live_ffxi_actors reads WalkMode.walking for self and only calls infers_walk_gait for remotes. Nothing in kuluu-render reads the snapshot's entity speed/speed_base for pose purposes at all -- the 0x0D/0x37 speed fields reach only self movement stepping, reactor stepping, and debug_chat. So a bound or Gravity'd self keeps playing run at 1x.

ADJACENT PREDICTION worth checking against retail (relates to kuluu-b091): under manual input the self takes Path A, where r never sees actual displacement -- so when ControllableActor::CheckContactActor withholds the tick's move, retail keeps the run cycle at full rate and the player runs in place. Under auto-run the identical block routes through Path B and the animation winds down to a jog and toward idle over a few frames. Same situation, different animation, decided only by input path.

title: Actor contact (CheckContactActor): withhold the move, do not depenetrate
description:
Retail blocks movement against other actors within 8 yalms. The per-actor radius is 0.8 x the XZ magnitude of skeleton element 44, and the block expires after a 30-tick window so you eventually push through rather than jamming.

We have no per-actor collision radius anywhere in the tree.

EVIDENCE: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp:308, :786-791, :921-1000 (tier 2).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION: actor-actor collision was NOT missing. It shipped in the walker rebuild - kuluu/src/view_native/walker/obstacles.rs (MobObstacle circles, MobBlockRadius from the mesh AABB) and walker/step.rs. What was wrong was the RESPONSE MODEL, reported from live play: it was hard collision (depenetration to the circle boundary) where retail is a withheld move that persistent input overcomes.

RETAIL RULE (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp ControllableActor::CheckContactActor, called from ControllableActor::HandleThirdPersonControl):

  movementDirection *= RawTimeDeltaScale;
  if (CheckContactActor(&movementDirection) == false)
      newPosition += movementDirection;

1. Contact WITHHOLDS the whole tick's movement. There is no push-out, no slide, no velocity scale anywhere in the path. Actors may overlap, and a standing player is never shoved by an actor walking into them.
2. Only the SINGLE nearest eligible actor is considered, measured from the PROJECTED position (ControlResolvedPosition + movementDirection), with the scan seeded at squared distance 64 = 8 yalms. A farther actor the move also overlaps does not block.
3. Contact predicate: dist - myCollisionSize - theirCollisionSize < 0.
4. The block expires. First tick of contact with an actor arms a 30-tick budget; each later tick decrements it by GameManager::CheckTick, and once it goes negative the actor stops blocking until you separate.
5. CheckTick returns SmoothedTimeDeltaScale = 60 / EffectiveFramerate (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Game/GameManager.cpp GameManager::CheckTick), so the tick unit is a sixtieth of a second and the window is ~0.5 s at any framerate - NOT 1.0 s. Our old PUSH_THROUGH_SECS = 0.8 was a tuning knob, not this value.
6. A change of nearest actor re-arms the budget. That is what produces the 'resistance' feel in a crowd: repeated short stalls rather than one clean pass.

The user-reported 'resistance/slowdown overcome by persistent movement' is emergent from (1) + (4) + (6), not a separate speed-scaling mechanism.

LANDED: walker/consts.rs CONTACT_SEARCH_RADIUS + CONTACT_BLOCK_TICKS + CONTACT_TICKS_PER_SEC (imported from input.rs RETAIL_MOVE_TICKS_PER_SEC, not re-typed); walker/mod.rs PushThrough replaced by ActorContact porting retail's three fields; walker/step.rs contact_blocks() replacing the per-mob depenetration loop.

TESTS: 74 walker tests pass. New pins - contact_budget_expires_after_retail_window (same ~0.5 s at 60 and 30 Hz), contact_budget_rearms_on_target_change_and_clear, contact_takes_the_nearest_actor_only, contact_never_depenetrates, mob_circle_blocks_then_walks_through (asserts the path crosses the mob's CENTER, so a regression to sliding around fails), mob_circle_does_not_shove_an_idle_player.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE: source inspection plus headless walker tests only. No retail observation and no live LSB session was run for this change.

REMAINING (split out): kuluu-53tn radius from model locator 44 instead of the mesh AABB; kuluu-wazp the eligibility predicates we still skip (dead actors, fading, mounted, GM).

title: Chase camera passes through Lower Jeuno roof: MZB ceiling gap, unknown if faithful
description:
At Oldman's spot in Lower Jeuno (zone 245, ffxi 18.06/40.93/-1.00) the zoomed-out chase camera passes through the roof overhead.

Ruled out (all measured, see kuluu-0nnl probes):
- Roof missing from the collision set: no. MZB models ceilings here.
- BVH traversal missing hits: no. zone_bvh_ray_cast_agrees_with_brute_force (ffxi-client collision_bvh.rs) sweeps 720 orbit rays against real zone-245 geometry and passes.
- Systems unregistered/misordered: no. build_zone_collision_bvh_system runs before clamp_chase_camera_to_collision, which runs after chase_camera_system and writes the transform last.
- MMB not being collided: NOT the fix. Both XIM (Collider.nearestLocalCollision over zoneCollisionMap) and XIClient (CollisionManager over ZoneCollisionData, MzbVersion) show retail's camera casts against MZB collision geometry only, never MMB model meshes. Enabling MMB zone-wide would diverge from retail.

Actual finding: the MZB ceiling genuinely does not cover that column. Highest surface above head height, 2-unit grid (bevy_y, '.' = open):

  ffxi_y\x    13.1    15.1    17.1    19.1    21.1    23.1
     35.9    9.20    9.20    9.20    9.32       .       .
     37.9    9.20    9.20    9.20       .    8.60    8.20
     39.9    9.20    9.20       .       .       .       .
     41.9    6.43       .       .       .       .       .   <- player at (18.06, 40.93)

The ~9.2 ceiling covers x 13-19 / y 35.9-39.9 with a ragged edge stopping just short of the player.

Open question, and the reason this is not yet actionable: is that gap faithful (retail's camera also clips there) or is our MZB parse dropping a placement? Indistinguishable from the DAT alone. Next step is the retail-observe skill — stand at the same coordinates in HorizonXI and zoom out.

Related: retail's grid broadphase uses 4.0-unit cells ((HalfWorldWidth + x) * 0.25, CollisionQuery.hpp GetGridRange) and anchors the search at the RAY START within +/-1..2 cells, re-anchoring every ~4 units for long rays (SomeCollisionCheck segments the ray). Our global BVH is a superset of that, so it is not a candidate cause — but it does mean retail deliberately limits camera-ray reach, worth knowing before 'fixing' any gap.
acceptance_criteria: Retail comparison at ffxi 18.06/40.93 in zone 245 recorded (screenshot or note): either confirmed faithful and this closes as not-a-bug, or confirmed divergent and the MZB parse gap is identified.
notes:
CLOSED — the open question ("does retail clip there too?") is answered, and the
answer produced a second, larger fix than the zoom clamp.

Retail observation (retail-observe, HorizonXI, Lower Jeuno I-6, artifacts/retail):
`,`/`.` are zoom out/in; at the zoom stop a ~2-yalm character fills ~37% of
viewport height, which at retail's own vertical FOV puts the eye 4.5-6 yalms
out. DIST_MAX = 6 confirmed independently of the three references that set it.
Six more seconds of held `,` moved nothing, so that IS the stop.

That sent me back to XIClient for the rest, where the real cause was:

1. Retail's camera has no pitch. CameraManager.cpp:527-529 adds to the eye's
   world Y (`CurrentEyePosition.y += offset`) and leaves the horizontal offset
   alone; :822 then eases the grown eye->target distance back toward 6.
2. What bounds the tilt is a pair of standoffs on an unobstructed camera
   (v269 == true): :830-836 pushes the 3D distance out to 3, and :837-846
   independently pushes the HORIZONTAL separation out to 3.

Our eye is polar, so horizontal = radius * cos(pitch), and that standoff is the
pitch ceiling: acos(3/6) = 60 degrees, against the 80 an uncited PITCH_MAX =
1.40 allowed. At 80 degrees the eye sat 1.0 yalm horizontally from the anchor —
the anchor-to-eye segment was short and near-vertical, so it threaded the gap
instead of hitting the ceiling's underside. At 60 it can never come nearer than
3 horizontally.

Measured at the reported spot ffxi(17.71, 40.54, -1.00), anchor bevy_y 2.265,
via zz-mzb-tri-probe KULUU_CAMSWEEP (which now drives ChaseCamera itself rather
than a hand-rolled copy of the clamp):
  max eye height  8.18 -> 7.461
  horizontal reach 1.02 -> 3.000
  at the three yaw bands where a ceiling IS authored (0/15/30 and 270/285/300)
  the ray now hits it, n.y ~ -0.9 to -1.0
The remaining "free flight" directions are NOT a bug: the authored ceiling over
those columns is at 8.5-9.2 (x=15.7 -> 8.511), so an eye topping out at 7.461 is
legitimately inside the hall, under it.

Also fixed: camera_collision.rs placed the eye a second time from
`chase.distance`, which is now short of where chase_camera_system actually puts
it — the far end of the eye's travel went unswept. Both sites take
orbit_radius(); `collision_sweeps_the_distance_the_camera_actually_travels`
names the coupling.

DIST_MIN was likewise an uncited 2.0; :830 says 3.

Live verify (Verilamp, local LSB, teleported to exactly 17.71/40.54/-1.00):
held pitch to the stop and orbited a full circle in four 90-degree steps —
every frame interior floor/pillars/NPC, no sky, no rooftops, no exterior.
artifacts/verify/cam-01-default.png, cam-02-maxpitch.png,
cam-04-maxpitch-orbit.png.

Shipped in e48bb7f. Follow-ups filed separately: retail's FOV, and the
motion-model divergence (we match the reachable envelope, not the path).
close_reason: Root cause was PITCH_MAX, not the geometry: retail bounds tilt with a horizontal standoff (CameraManager.cpp:837-846), which for a polar eye is acos(3/6)=60deg, not the uncited 80. Fixed in e48bb7f; verified offline (camsweep) and live (max-pitch orbit stays inside).

title: Camera collision ignores retail's skip policy (mesh Flags != 0 && tri VertexIndex3 & 0x4000)
description:
Retail runs every MZB ray query through one templated CollisionQuery specialised by policy (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/include/World/Zone/Terrain/CollisionQuery.hpp). The chase camera uses DoubleSidedSkipPolicy, whose SkipTriangle is:

    return (header->Flags != 0 && (triangle->VertexIndex3 & 0x4000) != 0);

We parse that exact bit already — ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:350 `is_barrier = (v2_raw & 0x4000) != 0` — and never use it anywhere. So our chase camera collides with triangles retail's camera passes through. Zone 245 has 1092 such triangles.

Note the gate on `header->Flags`, which is our MzbSubMesh.flags (the doesnt_block_los field). The skip only applies where the mesh header flags are nonzero, so this is NOT a plain per-triangle mask.

XIM describes this loosely as a hitWall material bit (type & 0x40, research/xim/.../ZoneDefParser.kt:18, Collider.kt:287) and gets the predicate wrong; XIClient is the authority here. See research/README.md tier 2 vs tier 6.

Fix: carry is_barrier through MzbSubMesh into the camera BVH (alongside tri_normals, added in ab7258d) and skip those triangles in the camera raycast only — movement/grounding must keep them, since retail's movement query (FastCheck1, BacksideCullingPolicy) does not skip.
acceptance_criteria: Camera BVH skips triangles where the source submesh flags != 0 and the triangle's is_barrier bit is set; grounding unaffected; guard test over real zone-245 geometry showing the skipped-triangle count is nonzero and that ground_step results are unchanged.
notes:
Corroborated independently by research/cexi-docs/zone/collision.md:201-209, which states the same predicate and cites CollisionQuery.hpp DoubleSidedSkipPolicy: the camera radius pull-in and client LoS ray skip a triangle only when its mesh's CollisionMeshHeader.Flags != 0 AND the triangle's THIRD index word has bit 0x4000. Two independent sources (tier 2 + tier 4) now agree, so this is settled.

Same doc, two further divergences found while confirming, both meaning we currently collide with MORE than retail:

1. Per-object Y-cull is unimplemented. Each 0xC0 collision-object record stores a world-space Y AABB at +0xB4/+0xB8 and retail skips the whole object unless the player's Y overlaps it (CollisionManager.cpp: obj->minY <= playerMaxY && obj->maxY >= playerMinY; visible in XIClient CollisionQuery.hpp as 'objectData->minY <= maxY && objectData->maxY >= minY'). We do not parse or apply it. cexi notes xim has no such cull either, which is why structurally-valid blockers can pass xim-based tooling yet not block in retail.

2. cexi claims player movement keys off the SECOND index word's 0x4000 bit — our MzbTriangleInfo.is_invalid (ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:349). UNVERIFIED and suspicious: our probe measured is_invalid == 0 across zones 245, 246, 230 and 100, so if it gated movement blocking nothing in those zones would block. Treat as hypothesis (cexi-docs is tier 4) and check against XIClient before acting.

Also confirms ab7258d's grounding fix is retail-faithful: 'Collision is one-sided... the winding is normalized to the normal, so the normal alone decides' and 'Floors keep a single up-facing (negative-FFXI-Y) normal'. That matches the measurement that drove the fix (authored normal antiparallel to winding for 70-98% of triangles, never anything between) and matches XIClient's BacksideCullingPolicy reading NormalArray[triangle->GetNormalIndex()].
close_reason: Fixed in ee38ed7: camera BVH built from camera_triangles(), which applies retail's DoubleSidedSkipPolicy (mesh flags != 0 && triangle third-index-word 0x4000). Grounding untouched by construction and proven bit-identical over 1681 columns. Measured first: skip set is 0.17-2.26% of placed triangles, almost all walls.

title: Launcher footer: build stamp + Discord/GitHub/Patreon links
description:
The launcher has no version display and no path to the project's community or funding. A player who hits a bug can't say which build they're on, and a would-be contributor has no visible link to Discord, the repo, or Patreon.

Add a persistent footer bar across every AppPhase::Launcher sub-state: build stamp (version, debug/release, target triple) on the left, three icon+label external links (Discord, GitHub, Patreon) in full brand colors on the right. Spawned OnEnter(AppPhase::Launcher) / despawned OnExit, same lifecycle template as the update banner. Gone once in-game.

Enhanced, not vanilla parity - retail has no such footer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Footer visible on all 18 LauncherState sub-states, absent in AppPhase::InGame
- Version stamp reads vX.Y.Z, profile, target triple
- All three links open the correct URL and visibly react to hover
- BrandIcons resource removed on OnExit (no Image handle leak across logout)
close_reason: Footer shipped and runtime-verified: renders on the login screen (v0.4.0 · debug · aarch64-apple-darwin left, three brand links right), absent in-game, respawns on disconnect back to Launcher. Commit ddc25b4.

title: Silent degradation: missing DAT data produces a healthy-looking client with no log line
description:
Apply these corrections (everything else in the bead verified true as of 2026-07-31 — no listed path has gained a log line; scheduler_runtime.rs contains zero logging macros and particle_sim.rs has only the two success-path debug! calls at :195/:280):

2. mzb.rs — CAUTION: this file has ~575 UNCOMMITTED insertions from a concurrent session, so line numbers are a moving target; re-locate by symbol before editing. At HEAD: grid_cells_x :111, parse_placements :428, the gw/gh guard :449, the empty-placements test :949. In the current worktree: grid_cells_x :189-192, parse_placements :565, the guard :581-583, the test :1234, and the MZB_SUB_BLOCK_SIZE comment at :135-139 ('Most zones ship 40-unit blocks (10 sub-blocks); Port Jeuno ships 80 (20)'). 3. scheduler.rs — StageKind::from_stage is at :137-168 with `_ => Self::Unknown` at :166, plus a SECOND silent StageKind::Unknown at :246 for id-less stages. title: Real-DAT and live-server tests skip green on CI, hiding the range's most valuable assertions
description:
Systematic coverage gap found in the v0.4.0 review: the highest-value assertions live in tests that PASS when they do not run.

14 real-DAT tests (7 in ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs, 7 in kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs) carry the ONLY coverage of control-flow branch ordering, damage-callback reachability, and the three-tier hit-spark chain. They self-skip on any machine without a retail install, i.e. CI, and report PASS. archive.rs:130 open_test_install prints 'SKIP (real-DAT guard): ...' (:145, :154), which is the right pattern, but eprintln! is not loud enough — output is captured without --nocapture, and no CI job sets FFXI_DAT_PATH (grep over .github/ and scripts/ is empty).

Remaining holes in the guard itself:
- ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:712 bypasses the loud helper entirely — DatRoot::from_env_or_default() with three consecutive fully-silent bail-outs (:714, :717, :720). It is the only test asserting joint-21 target attachment against real data.
- ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:494, :568 and the :968 schedulers_in_file helper also bypass it with silent from_env_or_default()/`?` — scheduler.rs never calls open_test_install at all.
- In scheduler_runtime.rs only the FIRST guard of each test prints; the resolve() and fs::read() failures below return bare (:1742, :1745, :1928, :1931, :1987, :1990), and the helpers read_dat (:2018), routines_in_file (:2365), global_effect_dir (:2372) swallow with ?.

Same shape for live-server tests (play_lifecycle.rs:38, zone_change.rs:28, agent_session.rs:21, delivery_box_live.rs:64, disconnect_recovery.rs:19/:34/:39) — so zone change, logout, reconnect/backoff and death/homepoint have no integration coverage on CI, which is exactly the session-stranding class the LSB-boundary rule cares most about.

Proposal: REQUIRE_REAL_DAT=1 / REQUIRE_LIVE_SERVER=1 turning the skip into a panic, set in whichever job has the install/server (neither env var exists today). Route every guard through the loud helper.

Highest-value missing fixtures, in order:
1. BATTLE2 with trg_sum > 1 and result_sum > 1 AND has_proc/has_react set. Every existing fixture (session.rs:7369-7500) leaves those bits clear, so the asymmetric proc 17/10 vs react 14/10 block widths — confirmed at vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x028_battle2.cpp:170-173 and :188-191, mirrored at session.rs:3953-3954/:3963-3964 — are dead in tests. A desync there garbles every subsequent battle line.
2. A synthetic 0x49 chunk pinning CAST_UNIT_MS. parse_spell_table (ffxi-dat/src/spell_info.rs:102) has ZERO tests; decode_block_round_trips_fields (:204) checks the raw bytes but never the * 250 ms conversion (:17). Change the constant and every spell silently loses its cast time with a green suite.
3. Unclosed / nested 0x3D random block: scheduler.rs:218-220 clears open_group only on an explicit 0x3E, and :281-282 gates running_frame on open_group.is_none(), so an unclosed opener stops the clock for the whole rest of the routine. No test covers it.
4. ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs palettised decode — the 5 tests at :498/:510/:524/:533/:543 cover name extraction only; swapping the FLG_PALETTE/FLG_PALETTE_EXT offset arms (:159-166, feeding decode_palettized at :217) decodes every 0x91/0xB1 texture to garbage, green.
5. AgentEvent::SelfServerStatus — no test at any layer, while its sibling weather (reset three lines above, state.rs:990 vs :993) has one. Dropping the reset re-enters the rest stance after a zone change.
6. kuluu-snapshot PROTOCOL_VERSION (now 9, lib.rs:15) has no guard test — lib.rs:1401 only round-trips the constant against itself, so a schema change without a bump still passes.

DONE since this bead was filed (do not re-do): the corrupt-markers.json tests (marker_store.rs:344 and :358, commit 9ebf75e, kuluu-hdco) and the argless/control-flow synthetic fixtures (scheduler.rs:868/:894/:912/:930, commit 1918365 — which also lands the >= STAGE_HEADER_LEN gate at scheduler.rs:222 and the open_group clear at :218, i.e. every acceptance criterion of the kuluu-bvwz dependency; verify and close it). wire_translate.rs:570/:587 now assert both surviving ActionStarted fields (the third, resolution/animation, was merged into `result` when PROTOCOL_VERSION went 8 -> 9).

Test-quality issues worth fixing in the same pass: session.rs:8512 `server_extract_result` is a LOCAL re-implementation of LSB's HandleCustomMenu (real source vendor/server/src/map/lua/luautils.cpp:5323) that session.rs:8520 round-trips the builder against, so the mirror and the builder can stay wrong together; session.rs:7383/:7429 pad fixtures with w.write(0,32) purely to satisfy the reader's 64-bit over-read, which MASKS it (only the :7484-7485 fixture uses a 0xFFFF_FFFF tail — make that the default); marker_store.rs:269 default_path_uses_player_facing_dir asserts a hardcoded path suffix against the real user config dir.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
A CI job with the retail install fails rather than skips; every real-DAT guard routes through the loud helper; the three highest-value fixtures (BATTLE2 proc/react, CAST_UNIT_MS, unclosed 0x3D) land.
acceptance_criteria: A CI job with the retail install fails rather than skips; the three highest-value fixtures land.

title: Sweep: ~20 vendor/XIM citation line anchors are wrong (values correct, lines drifted)
description:

title: is_door cites a Monstrosity-only LSB guard as a general door gate; range/status gates not mirrored
description:
TITLE: is_door cites a Monstrosity-only LSB guard as a general door gate; status gate not mirrored

kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:226-234. The doc comment on `is_door` states 'LSB gates doors on look.size == 0x02 (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x01a_action.cpp:212)'.

The cited line is the MONSTROSITY-ONLY guard, not a general door gate:
  // MONs are allowed to use doors, but nothing else            (:211)
  if (PChar->m_PMonstrosity != nullptr &&                       (:212)
      PNpc->look.size != 0x02 && ...                            (:213)

LSB's GENERAL trigger path (:222) applies no look.size filter at all — any NPC within 6.0f with IsSpawned() && status == STATUS_TYPE::NORMAL (or the player inside a Mog House) is triggerable. The citation therefore supports 'look.size == 0x02 identifies a door' but NOT 'LSB gates interaction on it'. Restricting EntityKind::Other to doors (lib.rs:244) is our own heuristic wearing an LSB citation.

Fix: reword the comment to say what :211-213 actually supports, and cite :222 for the real trigger preconditions.

CORRECTION (2026-07-31 re-audit) — the RANGE half of this bead is wrong and was wrong at authoring; do not re-file it. The 6.0-yalm gate shipped in the very commit that added door targeting: 9c2d1f4 (2026-07-13, kuluu-dag) added both TargetActionId::Open and `| TargetActionId::Open` to `needs_range`. Today: kuluu-render/src/hud/action_model.rs:3 `NPC_INTERACT_YALMS = 6.0`; :239 computes in_range for the door target; :152-155 lists Open among needs_range so :205 sets `enabled: !out_of_range` with hint 'Target out of range.'; and kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:1019 refuses a disabled entry before the only Open dispatch (:1121-1133, ActionKind::Talk). A door beyond 6 yalms is already non-actionable. It remains *selectable* (is_targetable, lib.rs:239-247, carries no range test), but selectable != actionable and no source in this tree establishes that retail range-gates target selection.

The real residual gap is the STATUS gate: kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:203-224 uses a fail-open blacklist (DISAPPEAR/INVISIBLE/STATUS_4/CUTSCENE_ONLY/STATUS_18/SHUTDOWN), so a door with status UPDATE (=1, vendor/server/src/map/entities/baseentity.h:50) is presented as targetable and actionable even though LSB :222 requires exactly NORMAL and will silently drop the Talk. (Whether LSB ever sends UPDATE for a door entity in practice is not established here — worth confirming against a live server before treating this as user-visible.)

Side note, unconfirmed: kuluu-render/src/picking.rs:54 `require_markers: true` (deliberate, kuluu-k929) means zone geometry never blocks the pick ray, so entity hitboxes behind a closed door are clickable. Whether retail occludes world clicks is NOT established — research/XIClient exposes only terrain-collision ray policies (World/Zone/Terrain/CollisionQuery.hpp:9,15,21) and no cursor-picking path. Needs a retail observation before it is treated as a defect.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (rewritten — the old 'door outside 6.0 yalms is not actionable' is already satisfied): comment states the real LSB behaviour (Monstrosity guard vs general trigger, citing :222 for the preconditions); a door whose status != NORMAL is not presented as actionable.
acceptance_criteria: Comment states the real LSB behaviour; a door outside 6.0 yalms is not presented as actionable.

title: Map-screen zoom is unreachable with default keybinds
description:
text_input.rs:3680-3688 gates map zoom on bindings.matches_logical(Action::CameraZoomIn/Out, key).

Those actions default to Period and Comma (keybinds/presets.rs:64-65), and nav_keycode_for deliberately returns None for non-letter printables — so the logical-key path never produces a match. zoom_radius stays None (fit-to-zone) forever and the feature is dead with stock binds.

The adjacent comment claiming the zoom works this way is rotted.

Fix: gate zoom on ev.key_code rather than the logical path (or extend nav_keycode_for), and correct the comment.
acceptance_criteria: Period/Comma zoom the full-screen map on a default-bind profile.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Audit 2026-07-31: confirmed live. title: zone_point_lights: is_character skip was deleted (field now write-only), plus per-actor per-frame heap allocs
description:
Two issues in ffxi-viewer-core/src/zone_point_lights.rs — one live perf bug, one dead field mis-framed as a regression.

1. `is_character` is now dead state. It is written at :93 (decl), :148, :163, :259, :394 and read NOWHERE (`rg -n 'is_character' -g '*.rs'` returns only those five writes). The skip DID exist and WAS deleted inside the v0.4.0 range (git show 4c403ad:zone_point_lights.rs:285-287 had `if l.is_character { continue; }`; 267a95c removes it, `git tag --contains 267a95c` -> v0.4.0), but the removal was deliberate: 267a95c's message reads 'All zone lights (incl c*) now spawn as PointLights so clustering sees them; glow billboards stay non-character-only', and the rationale survives as a comment at :290-291. fd1228e then dropped the billboard, taking the last read of the field with it. Note the skip never covered the per-actor feed anyway — 4c403ad:90-97 already pushed c* lights into ActiveSceneLights at their raw base_position — so 'restore the skip' would not by itself stop a c* light lighting actors from a fixed world position. Action: delete the field and the `c*` name test at :259 unless live observation shows a c* light at base_position is visibly wrong, in which case the exclusion belongs on the clustered feed at :148 as well as on entity spawn.

2. LIVE: per-actor, per-frame heap traffic in the light-selection path. zone_point_lights.rs:195 `nearest_point_light_arrays` allocates two Vecs and runs a comparison sort (:200-204 collect, :205 sort_by, :206-210 collect). ffxi_actor_render.rs:2465-2470 calls it once per actor inside `for (actor, gt) in &q_actors`, and lib.rs:311-316 schedules that system in `Update`. The v0.3.0 version was a fixed `[(f32, usize); 4]` insertion sort that still collected one <=4-element Vec (`git show v0.3.0:ffxi-viewer-core/src/zone_point_lights.rs`) — so the correct statement is 'bounded allocation' not 'zero heap traffic', and the regression is that the alloc now scales with the in-range light count (267a95c: 'zones have up to ~250 lights'). Fix: bounded insertion into a `[(f32, usize); MAX_POINT_LIGHTS]` scratch, or a reused `Local<Vec<_>>` with clear().

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
No per-actor allocation in the light-selection path; `is_character` is either read by something or removed. (The old criterion 'no character-attached Generator light renders at a fixed world position' is not satisfiable by restoring the entity-spawn skip alone — the clustered feed at :148 carries them too.)
acceptance_criteria: No character-attached Generator light renders at a fixed world position; no per-actor allocation in the light-selection path.

description:

title: markers.json is rewritten on every menu keypress
description:

title: SpellTable::open blocks a Tokio worker on a multi-MB disk read once per zone change
description:
TITLE should also change: 'SpellTable::open blocks a Tokio worker re-reading ROM/118/114.DAT on every zone change' (drop 'multi-MB').

session.rs:470-472:
  cfg.dat_root.as_ref()
    .map(|r| ffxi_dat::spell_info::SpellTable::open(r.root())),

`SpellTable::open` is a synchronous `std::fs::read` of ROM/118/114.DAT (ffxi-dat/src/spell_info.rs:143-146; path const at :10) followed by a per-block `to_vec()` + `decode_block` over every 0x64-byte block (:111-113). It is evaluated as an argument to `keepalive_loop` (session.rs:448) inside `async fn run_map_session` (session.rs:297), which `run()` (:150) re-enters from its loop (:239-241) on every zone change (`MapOutcome::Reconnect`, :3526). So a Tokio worker does blocking file I/O plus a full table decode on the zone-in path, where the keepalive/sync deadline lives.

Size correction: the file is ~394 KB (403,280 bytes in the reference install), not multi-MB. The cost is the blocking syscall plus the decode loop on a runtime worker, not I/O volume. The table is zone-invariant and re-read on every zone change for no reason.

Fix: hoist above the loop, load once via `spawn_blocking`, pass an `Arc<SpellTable>`.

NOTE: the GUI process opens the same DAT independently from `SpellSuffixCache` (ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:2237), held as a `Local` in two systems (ffxi_actor_render.rs:2252, scheduler_runtime.rs:853). 'Once per process' is achievable, but needs a shared `Arc<SpellTable>`/Resource across all three sites, not the session fix alone.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
ROM/118/114.DAT is read at most once per process and never on a Tokio runtime worker; the session path takes an Arc<SpellTable> loaded before the zone loop.
acceptance_criteria: ROM/118/114.DAT is read once per process, off the async runtime.

title: ActionAssets is inserted per action and never removed; stale ActionTarget mis-sites the next routine's particles
description:
scheduler_runtime.rs:806-810.

ActiveScheduler self-removes after POST_FINISH_TTL_SECS, but ActionAssets (holding decoded RGBA textures, MMB meshes and D3Ms) and ActionTarget are try_insert'ed alongside it and there is no remove::<ActionAssets> anywhere in the workspace (grep-confirmed). Every actor that has ever cast retains one action DAT's decoded texture set until despawn.

Second, related defect: ActionTarget's doc comment at scheduler_runtime.rs:20-21 claims it is 'written in the same commands chain as ActiveScheduler by every routine dispatcher, so it can never outlive the routine that set it'. That is false. It is inserted at 810, 919, 1032, 1162, 1325 and never removed, and at :1160-1163 the insert is CONDITIONAL:
  entity.try_insert(active);
  if let Some(target) = flipped_target { entity.try_insert(ActionTarget(Some(target))); }
When flipped_target is None, a new ActiveScheduler is written while the entity keeps the PREVIOUS routine's ActionTarget — which particle_origin_entity/sound_origin_entity then use as the emit position.

Fix: strip ActionAssets and ActionTarget in the same branch that removes ActiveScheduler, and insert ActionTarget(None) unconditionally so the stated invariant is enforced rather than asserted.
acceptance_criteria: ActionAssets/ActionTarget are removed with ActiveScheduler; the doc-comment invariant is either enforced or deleted.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Re-verified 2026-07-31. Both defects still present. One anchor refresh after commit f07b668 (2026-07-30): the melee-dispatcher ActionTarget insert is scheduler_runtime.rs:1034, not :1032; the other four sites (810, 919, 1162, 1325) and the :20-21 / :806-810 / :1160-1163 anchors are exact. The reachability of the false invariant is pinned at :1095-1099 — target_link_context returns (actor, None) for any self-aimed or untracked target, so run_routine_on's conditional insert is a live path, not a theoretical one. Label note: the second half (stale ActionTarget mis-siting particle/sound emit positions via particle_origin_entity at :28-40 and sound_origin_entity at :45-51) is a correctness bug, not perf — consider adding a combat-action/rendering area label alongside `perf`.

title: Gamepad buttons dispatch the wrong action after any keybind rebind
description:
ffxi-client/src/view_native/gamepad_input.rs:215-231:
  fn logical_key_for(key_code: KeyCode) -> Key {
      match key_code { KeyCode::Escape => Key::Escape, /* fixed set */ _ => Key::Enter }
  }

A hand-copied partial inverse of the private keybinds::nav_keycode_for (ffxi-viewer-core/src/keybinds/mod.rs:252) with a silent catch-all `_ => Key::Enter` (:229). It omits nav_keycode_for's `Key::Character` arm (mod.rs:272-283: single ASCII letters -> KeyA..KeyZ, '+' -> NumpadAdd) — exactly where the two tables disagree. Consumers resolve via Bindings::matches_logical (mod.rs:230-237), which compares `nav_keycode_for(key) == Some(b.key)` and never looks at the synthesized `key_code` field.

Concrete failure: rebind OpenChat from Space to KeyT via keybinds.json overrides (ffxi-client/src/keybinds_store.rs:21). The gamepad right-trigger path (gamepad_input.rs:366-368 -> synth_bound_key :259 -> synth_nav_key :233) emits KeyboardInput { key_code: KeyT, logical_key: Key::Enter }, which does NOT match OpenChat (text_input.rs:716) and DOES match whatever is bound to Enter, i.e. ConfirmAction (text_input.rs:719; presets.rs:59). The gamepad button talks to an NPC instead of opening chat.

Scope: no shipped preset binds a synthesized action outside logical_key_for's table (presets.rs:56,59,78-83; standard() at :133 overrides none of them), and /keybinds only switches presets (slash_commands.rs:2976-2996; KeybindUpdate is Preset|Reset|List, :1161-1167). So today the bug needs a hand-edited keybinds.json; it becomes user-reachable the moment a rebind UI lands.

Direct AGENTS.md violation: a contract between modules re-typed in the consumer instead of exported by the emitter — the doc comment at gamepad_input.rs:213 admits it mirrors a private function.

Fix: export keybinds::logical_key_for(KeyCode) -> Option<Key> sharing ONE table with nav_keycode_for; skip synthesis on None rather than defaulting to Enter.

Related, same file (locator corrected — the original ':113' pointed at gamepad_launcher_nav_system, fn at :94): the only GamepadAxisHeld drain is gamepad_input.rs:158-160, the no-gamepad early return inside gamepad_movement_camera_system (fn at :152), which is registered `run_if(in_state(AppPhase::InGame))` (ffxi-client/src/view_native/mod.rs:563-568). Leaving AppPhase::InGame with the stick pushed strands synthetic W presses in ButtonInput<KeyCode>; the two OnExit(AppPhase::InGame) blocks (mod.rs:426-429, :485-495) drain other resources but not this one.

Also: 369 lines with zero tests (no #[cfg(test)] module). bound_key, sync_axis_key and logical_key_for are pure functions that would test trivially, and the axis dead-zone/edge logic is the classic source of stuck-key bugs.
acceptance_criteria: Roundtrip guard test asserts nav_keycode_for and logical_key_for agree for every navigable action; gamepad actions still work after rebinding OpenChat.
close_reason: Fixed by the direct-dispatch refactor in kuluu-uos3.5's first increment: keybinds::logical_key_for is now exported sharing one table with nav_keycode_for (roundtrip guard test logical_key_for_roundtrips_the_nav_table), pad synthesis skips unmappable binds instead of defaulting to Enter, pad->keyboard ButtonInput synthesis is gone entirely (PadPressed dispatches Actions directly; PadKeyEvent rides its own message channel so keyboard_input_system never sees it), and OnExit(InGame) drains pad state (drain_pad_state).

title: LSB enums hand-copied with no build-time scrape and no drift guard (melee/magic/chat_kind)
description:
Direct violation of the AGENTS.md 'never hand-copy vendor values, scrape at build time' rule, in the one crate whose build.rs already scrapes packet_s2c.h, packet_c2s.h, emote.h, msg_basic.h and (new this range) zone_entities.cpp.

1. ffxi-proto/src/melee.rs:1-49 — CATEGORY_BASIC_ATTACK=1, ActionResolution 0..4, AttackAnimation 0..4. All match vendor/server/src/map/enums/action/resolution.h:30-34 and attack.h:52-59 today. An LSB renumber silently maps every Parry to a Block.
2. ffxi-proto/src/magic.rs:3-13 — eleven SKILL_* ids (32..44) hand-copied from battleentity.h with no citation at all.
3. ffxi-proto/src/map.rs:317-334 — chat_kind is a hand-typed mirror of chat_message_type.h and is MISSING MESSAGE_NS_LINKSHELL3 = 31 (chat_message_type.h:56). A kind-31 line therefore renders WITH a speaker prefix. This is exactly the failure mode the scrape rule exists to prevent.
4. MESSAGE_GMPROMPT: u8 = 12 is defined locally at session.rs:4849 while ffxi-proto::map::chat_kind is the module that already mirrors that enum — a duplicated contract across a crate boundary.

The same v0.4.0 diff added a scraper PLUS a vendor-drift test for ENTITY_RENDER_DISTANCE (ffxi-proto/src/entity_stream.rs:17-46, build.rs:441-478). That is the model: rerun-if-changed, a plausibility band that fails the build on a bad parse, a duplicate-declaration guard, and a runtime test that re-parses the LSB source.

Also melee.rs:58 — the test named wire_values_match_lsb_enums never opens LSB; it asserts Rust against Rust.
acceptance_criteria: melee/magic/chat_kind values are generated by build.rs from vendor/server, or pinned by a test that re-parses the vendor header; NS_LINKSHELL3 handled.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Re-verified 2026-07-31 against vendor/server @ c39004ce. All five claims stand. Two anchors drifted after commit f07b668 (2026-07-30): the Rust-vs-Rust test is now ffxi-proto/src/melee.rs:112 (was cited :58), and MESSAGE_GMPROMPT is now kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:4852 (was cited :4849). The chat_kind consumer that makes NS_LINKSHELL3 a live rendering bug is the speaker-suppression match at session.rs:4841. Two additions to scope: chat_kind also omits MESSAGE_LINKSHELL3 = 30 (chat_message_type.h:55) — harmless today since it is a speaker kind, but the same scrape should pick it up — and the LSB enum continues past 31 (MESSAGE_UNITY = 33, MESSAGE_JP_ASSIST = 34, MESSAGE_NA_ASSIST = 35 at chat_message_type.h:58-60), so a scrape is strictly better than patching 31 by hand.

title: /tell truncates recipient names to 14 of the 15 available sName bytes
description:
session.rs:4921 — let r_len = r_bytes.len().min(14);

sName is 15 bytes (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x0b6_chat_name.h:31 — note the bead's original :33 anchor is the closing `);`; independently confirmed by research/XiPackets/world/client/0x00B6/README.md:28) and LSB reads it with asStringFromUntrustedSource(this->sName, sizeof(this->sName)) (0x0b6_chat_name.cpp:76), whose strnlen(str, max_size) form (vendor/server/src/common/logging.h:81, strnlen at :89) tolerates a fully-populated, unterminated 15-byte field. FFXI names are max 15 chars (vendor/server/src/common/utils.h:71, PacketNameLength = 16 // 15 + null terminator; vendor/server/sql/chars.sql:10 charname varchar(15)).

The packet already reserves the full field — session.rs:4925 sizes the body as 1 + 1 + 15 + t_len + 1 and the message starts at buf[21] — so byte 20 is simply left zero. A /tell to a 15-character character name goes on the wire with its last character chopped and LSB's name lookup then fails. The custom-menu path is unaffected (_CUSTOM_MENU is 12 bytes), but build_subpacket_tell (session.rs:4919) is shared with real tells (:2171). Retail's own emit-side policy is not checkable here — research/XIClient carries no GP_CLI_COMMAND_CHAT_NAME reference — so the justification rests on LSB's read side, which is the authority for whether the server resolves the recipient.

Related low-severity edge in the same area: lobby_client.rs:695 nul = ...unwrap_or(CHR_INFO2_SLOT_NAME_LEN) (const = 16 at :633) yields a 16-byte name if the server ever sent an unterminated slot, which build_view_select (:481, VIEW_SELECT_NAME_LEN = 15 at :467) then truncates to 15 -> name mismatch -> LSB closes the socket. Not reachable with LSB.

Citation drift to fix while here (corrected 2026-07-31 — the earlier note in this bead was wrong; vendor/server has been pinned at c39004ce since 2026-04-27, so no upstream drift is possible):
- session.rs:4850 names HandleCustomMenu but cites 0x0b6_chat_name.cpp:79. Line :79 is the `strcmp(recipientName.c_str(), "_CUSTOM_MENU")` guard, :80 is HasCustomMenuContext, and HandleCustomMenu is :82. Retarget to :79-:82.
- session.rs:4849 and :4854 cite luautils.cpp SetCustomMenuContext / 'NA' with no line numbers — they are luautils.cpp:5288 and :5369.
- session.rs:4848 cites lua_baseentity.cpp:621 for customMenu; CLuaBaseEntity::customMenu is at :615.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
A /tell to a 15-character name arrives; test asserts the built subpacket carries all 15 bytes. Note this requires REWRITING the existing test session.rs:6834 tell_packet_truncates_oversize_inputs, which asserts &buf[6..20] == [b'a'; 14] and buf[20] == 0 — after the fix a 15-char name leaves sName unterminated, which is exactly what LSB's strnlen read tolerates.
acceptance_criteria: A /tell to a 15-character name arrives; test asserts the built subpacket carries all 15 bytes.

title: TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES id 565 silently shadows the build-scraped LSB msg_basic value
description:
session.rs:4191-4194:
  const TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES: &[(u16, &str)] = &[
      (116, "<player> uses <ability>."),
      (565, "<target> obtains <amount> gil."),

The override is NOT an accident, and the citation it needs is in LSB's C++, not just its lua. Every use of 565 in vendor/server is a gil payout:
  - vendor/server/src/map/utils/charutils.cpp:4756 — pushPacket<GP_SERV_COMMAND_BATTLE_MESSAGE>(…, gilPerPerson, 0, MsgBasic::Obtains) (party split, gilPerPerson at :4751)

  - vendor/server/scripts/globals/regimes.lua:1478-1480 — `-- gil` / addGil(reward) / messageBasic(xi.msg.basic.FOV_OBTAINS_GIL, reward)
Those are the only three; msg.lua:330 names the enum FOV_OBTAINS_GIL and renders the placeholder as <gil>.

It is also already pinned by a green test: session.rs:7269-7281 `battle_message_565_obtains_gil_override_appends_unit` asserts 'Mithy obtains 4 gil.'. Removing the entry regresses that test — the bead does not mention it.

STILL UNSETTLED (needs retail, not LSB): whether retail's own mesbasic 565 string literally contains ' gil' or whether retail formats the numeric argument with a gil unit at render time. title: ChunkWalker::next() never advances past a truncated header — walk().flatten() spins forever
description:
ffxi-dat/src/chunk.rs:47-55: when the remaining tail is shorter than the 16-byte chunk header, next() returns Some(Err(DatError::TruncatedChunk)) but leaves self.cursor where it is, so the iterator yields that same Err forever. Any consumer that discards errors with .flatten() therefore hangs at 100% CPU instead of stopping.

Reproduced before the example fix: 'cargo run -p ffxi-dat --example dat-d3m-texture -- 5820' never terminated; vendor/game-files/.../ROM3/0/66.DAT is 4 zero bytes. The two examples now use .map_while(Result::ok), but that is a workaround at the call site, not a fix.

Live .flatten() call sites that would hang on such a DAT:
- ffxi-dat/src/zone_interaction.rs:189
- ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:724
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:142 (collect_sound_assets, runs on the actor-load path)

Fix: set self.cursor = self.bytes.len() on the truncated-header branch (the same terminal treatment the total_bytes < 16 branch already gets one branch later), so the error is yielded exactly once and the iterator then ends. Add a unit test walking a buffer whose tail is < 16 bytes and asserting the iterator terminates.

Found by the adversarial review of the StaticMesh particle-texture lane.
close_reason: Fixed in faf0171: ChunkWalker::next() now sets cursor to the buffer end on the truncated-header branch, so the error is yielded once and the iterator terminates. Tests: a_tail_shorter_than_a_header_yields_one_error_then_ends and a_buffer_that_is_only_a_short_tail_terminates_under_flatten (both bounded with .take(8) so a regression fails rather than hangs). Verified the previously-hanging example now exits: dat-scan-generators over ROM3/0/66.DAT returns immediately.

title: MZB header: offset 0x08 is CollisionDataOffset and is legally 0 for the 15 vehicle zones; the probe loop misreads it
description:
SETTLED (retail reversing, 2026-07-31). Root cause is neither a decrypt failure nor a format-version difference.

The dword at MZB+0x08 is `CollisionDataOffset`, and for exactly 15 zone DATs it is legitimately **0** — those zones ship no static collision section at all. They are the moving-vehicle zones (boats/airships), which have no fixed terrain grid.

`MzbHeader::parse` (ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:137-152) probes for the first non-zero dword starting at 0x08. When 0x08 is zero it slides to 0x0C and reinterprets the four terrain bytes (zone_blocks_x / zone_blocks_z / block_width / block_length) as a dword — which is where 0xA0A02850 / 0x50505050 / 0x28284C30 come from.

Retail wraps the entire collision path in `if (CollisionDataOffset != 0)`. **Zero is a legal state, not an error.**

EVIDENCE
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/include/Resource/Derived/ZoneBlockFormat.h:20-67 — packed 0x20 header, `CollisionDataOffset` at 0x08 (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Rendering/ZoneRenderer.cpp:574 — `if (zoneBlockHeader->CollisionDataOffset != 0)` (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Zone/Terrain/CollisionManager.cpp:225-263 — 128-vs-192 stride at version <= 0x19; `GridData` present only when `ZoneType == 1` (tier 2)
- TIER 1: all 574 retail MZBs re-measured. Versions {23:1, 26:14, 27:559}. `coll_off == 0` <=> `SubstructureType == 2` <=> exactly ids {101,103,146,147,158,159,160,320,321,323-328}. The three garbage values above reproduce byte-for-byte.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL BEAD
- "these zones fall back to unplaced (identity-transform) geometry" is **wrong**. `parse_placements` returns `Err(MzbError::MeshTableOutOfRange)` first, and the MMB visual path (ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mzb.rs:791-877) is unaffected — models do place today. Real impact is a spurious hard error plus no collision, and no collision is what retail does here too.
- "likely cause is MZB decrypt" — ruled out. Decrypt is fine.
- The proposed grid-formula reorder to `(scale * units) / 4` is **moot**: zero of 574 retail files has a non-multiple-of-4 `TerrainUnits`. Do it for fidelity if you like, but it is not the bug.

- Delete the probe loop (ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:137-152); read 0x08 as a named `COLLISION_DATA_OFFSET` const.
- Add named consts for every header offset; add the version gates (18 / 21 / 27 / 0x19) rather than assuming one layout.
- `parse_meshes` (:428-445) and `parse_placements` (:243-251) return `Ok(vec![])` when the offset is zero, not an error.

- ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mzb.rs:608-620 must distinguish "no collision section in this zone" (normal) from "grid parse produced nothing" (a bug) — MEMORY: silent-degradation rule, log the former once.
- Update examples dat-mzb-gridprobe.rs and dat-mzb-maplist.rs.

title: Melee SFX are non-positional, non-attenuated and not deduped across an attack round
description:
dispatch_sound_stages emits crate::audio::SfxEvent::new(se_id), which hardcodes volume 1.0 and carries no world position (kuluu-render/src/audio.rs). Now that every tracked actor's swing dispatches sound routines, a distant mob's swings play at full volume in the player's ear.

Related: decode_battle2_header exposes only the FIRST result of the FIRST target, but LSB packs one result per swing for a whole attack round (vendor/server/src/map/entities/battleentity.cpp:2999-3006 loops addResult() setting actionResult.animation per swing) — so multi-hit rounds are under-represented, and if that is later fixed the sound path must dedupe rather than fire per swing-result.

FIX: give SfxEvent an optional emitter position + distance attenuation, and decide the retail rule for how many impact sounds an attack round plays.
notes:
--- 2026-07-31 retail reversing ---
"Non-attenuated" is our bug, not retail's absence. Retail's Calc3D DOES ship a curve: y scaled x3, LINEAR
falloff from near 3.0 to far 30.0, x0.65 in the back hemisphere, stereo pan by screen X, with per-SEP
near/far overrides. See research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Resource/Derived/CYySepRes.cpp:16-96 and
CYySoundElem.cpp:33-38 (tier 2). Our kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:513-541 invents 1/r with an 8-yalm dry
radius and carries a comment asserting retail has no curve — that comment is wrong. Tracked separately as
the Calc3D bead; this bead keeps the dedup-across-attack-round half.

title: ROUTINE_FPS 60 also doubles zone auto-run particle rate (braziers/campfires)
description:
The ROUTINE_FPS 30->60 correction (kuluu-k6tz) is right for effect routines and their particle generators, but tick_particle_simulator advances EVERY generator on that clock — including the zone auto-run generators spawned by zone_particles.rs (braziers, campfires, torches, hearths).

Consequence: ambient zone particles now emit at double rate and live half the wall-clock time. No test pins this and it was outside the melee/effect scope the commit verified.

Needs a live look at a zone with visible ambient fire (Bastok braziers, any campfire) to judge whether retail's ambient rate now matches or whether zone generators need the 30fps clock. research/xim MainTool.kt:118 feeds ALL of EffectManager (zone included) the raw 60fps elapsed, which suggests 60 is correct everywhere and the ambient effects were simply half-speed before too — but that is inference, not observation.
close_reason: Works-as-designed: xim (MainTool.kt:118, Scene.kt:125-126) feeds one 60fps clock to every generator incl. zone autoRun; ambient fire was half-speed before kuluu-k6tz, not correct-then-doubled. Pinned by zone_auto_run_generators_share_the_routine_clock.

title: [bug] Particle generators ignore attach_joint_target — hit sparks spawn at the victim's root, not the strike joint
description: ParticleGeneratorDef carries attach_joint_source/attach_joint_target (research/xim ParticleGeneratorAttachment.kt:64-111) but particle_sim::spawn_particle_generators only uses the origin entity's Transform plus base_position. Every melee hit generator in ROM/0/0.DAT (hit1: g010-g013, hi10/hi12/hi13/hi14 ...) has base_position [0,0,0] and attach_joint_target=49, so the sparks currently render at the victim's feet instead of the struck joint. Needs the target actor's posed joint world matrix (FfxiJointMatrices / pose_world) exposed to the sim. Affects spell/JA effects the same way, not just melee.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Re-verified 2026-07-31 against the tree and the retail install. Still unfixed: ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:127-128 parses attach_joint_source/target (masks at :80-83, read at :171-174) and nothing in kuluu-render reads them — spawn_particle_generators positions on the origin entity's root alone (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:214, `origin: origin_xf.translation + Vec3::Y * def.base_position[1]`). Retail DAT dump of ROM/0/0.DAT confirms the numbers: g010 (attach 0xC402), g011, g013 = TargetActor j1=49 base [0,0,0]; g012 = 0xC404 TargetActorSourceFacing j1=49; 108 generators in that file carry j1=49. Two corrections to the description's parenthetical: (1) hit1/hi10/hi12/hi13/hi14 are particle MESH chunks (kind 0x1F), not generators — the generators that use mesh hi10 (po00/po01) are attach type SourceActor with j0=48, not TargetActor j1=49; (2) 'every melee hit generator has base_position [0,0,0]' holds for the hit-spark set but not universally — g082 is j1=50, and g274/gs00/gs02/nul0/wa00/cri0 are j1=49 with a non-zero base X (0.2 / -0.3 / -0.5). Prerequisites already exist: FfxiJointMatrices (kuluu-render/src/skinned_ffxi_material.rs:97) and pose_world (ffxi-actor/src/skeleton_instance.rs:66).

title: [bug] Melee hit particle effects never spawn: wrong reaction branch (ranged daml/ldam) + missing 0x09 context flip
description:
A landed melee swing produces no hit sparks.

Two defects:

1. hit_reaction_routine maps ActionResolution::Hit -> 'ldam'. Retail 'ldam' is the RANGED hit reaction: global 'ldad' (ranged) -> 'daml' -> ldam/sway/gurd/pary, and 'ldam' links 'lhit' -> eflg/selg, which exist in no melee weapon DAT. The MELEE dispatcher is 'dada' -> 'dam0', whose hitTypeFlag (var 0x28) switch is, byte-for-byte in ROM/0/0.DAT chunk dam0 @0x4C0-0x700: case 0 -> (var 0x3B==1 ? damh : damg), 1 -> sway, 2 -> gurd, 3 -> pary, 4 -> gur1. That also settles ActionResolution::Block = 'gur1'. research/xim leaves var 0x3B unhandled (EffectRoutineInstance.kt:689-701 defaults to 0), so a normal hit is 'damg'.

2. The 0x09 (LinkedEffectRoutine useTarget) context flip is not implemented. research/xim EffectRoutineInstance.kt:387-394 createChild does cloneWithOverrideTarget(actor.id) - the child runs on the target with the PARENT as its target. run_routine_on inserts ActiveScheduler without touching ActionTarget, so the chain stalls: attacker -> damg on victim -> 0x09 chit needs to flip BACK to the attacker so 'ef h' resolves in the attacker's equipped-weapon DAT (findResource searchAssociatedDir, :580-604).

Chain that must work: ati0 -> dada -> 0x2B DamageCallback -> damg on victim (target=attacker) -> 0x09 chit on attacker (target=victim) -> 0x57 'ef h' (weapon DAT) -> 0x03 'hit1' (global) -> Particle g010..g013, all AttachType::TargetActor -> sparks land on the victim.
close_reason: Closed

title: Melee attack / hit sound effects never dispatch (no BasicAttack routine path, 0x57/0x09 unparsed, actor SEPs unloaded, fixed 64-byte scheduler header)
description: Four stacked defects mute every melee swing: (1) no dispatcher inserts an ActiveScheduler for ActionCategory::BasicAttack (only dispatch_action_overlay pulls the first Motion clip out of ati0); (2) opcodes 0x57 / 0x09 (LinkedEffectRoutine, research/xim EffectRoutineParser.kt:136-140,371-375) parse as Unknown and are dropped, so ati0's skaz whoosh and atk0's vatk grunt never link; (3) PC ActionAssets (face-DAT voice SEPs, weapon-DAT skaz/shit) are never collected nor inserted as a component, so dispatch_sound_stages cannot resolve them; (4) Scheduler::parse hardcodes a 64-byte header instead of reading the 3-section offset table at body +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 (EffectRoutineParser.kt:34-57), so daml/dam0/crtl/atpr yield ZERO stages.
close_reason: All four stacked defects the bead names are fixed in the tree, each with a test: BasicAttack now has a dispatcher (dispatch_melee_action_started), 0x57/0x09 decode as sub-routine links, PC face/weapon SEPs are collected and offered to dispatch_sound_stages as a tier, and Scheduler::parse reads the section-2 offset at body+0x14 instead of a fixed 64-byte header. The fixes landed 2026-07-24 19:45-21:15 PDT, i.e. within ~1.5h of the bead being filed (2026-07-24 19:39 PDT), and the bead was simply never closed.

title: Action/cast timing drift: effect-routine clock is 30fps, retail authors at 60
description: Effect routines and particle generators run 2x too slow: FFXI_FPS=30 drives ActiveScheduler::current_frame and tick_particle_simulator, but retail authors routine delays at 60 fps (research/xim util/Fps.kt:9 internalFps=60; ActorManager.kt:59-62 halves ONLY the skeleton domain to 30). Our own half_frames() bridge in ffxi_actor_render already assumes the 60fps source. Also: the self cast bar is armed optimistically at send (RTT of lead) instead of on the server's BATTLE2 MagicStart; scheduler tick is unordered vs the stage dispatchers; opcodes 0x2B (DamageCallback) and 0x3B/0x3C (blocking sub-routine) are not distinguished.
close_reason: Closed

title: Singleton particle generators emit nothing when their spawn frame exceeds the emit window
description:
ffxi-viewer-core/src/particle_sim.rs advance_generator now gates the singleton branch on `emitting`
(!stopped && (auto_run || age_frames <= emit_window.max(1.0))). The pre-change code deliberately did NOT gate it —
the singleton branch fired on the first tick regardless of the emit window.

is_singleton() is max_life_frames == 0.0, the default when the generator's init stream carries no life opcode,
and real routines contain dur=0 Particle stages (ner1: gn1s dur=0; eis3: ge3s dur=0, ge31 dur=0), giving
emit_window.max(1.0) == 1.0. Since age_frames == frames on the first tick, any singleton generator on a
short-duration stage silently emits NOTHING whenever the frame that spawns it is longer than 1/30 s.

That is not hypothetical here: dispatch_action_started does a blocking std::fs::read + parse_action_bytes on the
render thread, so the frame right before these generators spawn is exactly the long one.

FIX: restore the unconditional first-tick emission for singletons, or gate on `stopped` alone.
close_reason: Already fixed in 104d3ea2: particle_sim.rs:427-433 gates the singleton branch on !stopped + empty/first-tick only, exactly as this bead asked. Regression test particle_sim.rs:1008 singleton_emits_on_a_first_frame_longer_than_its_emit_window (LONG_FRAME=9.0 vs a zero-duration window) plus stopped_singleton_never_emits pin it. Bead was filed 16 min before the fix landed and never closed.

title: Cast aura stopped on frame 1 for cast routines with no Motion stage (caso/calg/cage)
description:
ffxi-viewer-core/src/scheduler_runtime.rs stop_cast_effects_when_cast_ends uses FfxiRenderActor::cast_posing()
as its liveness proxy, but dispatch_action_overlay only sets ActionPlayback.cast_pose when routine_motion_clip()
finds a Motion stage (ffxi_actor_render.rs:2235 continues otherwise).

Verified against the retail DAT: `cargo run -p ffxi-dat --example dat-routine-stages 7072 caso` (also calg, cage)
shows routines whose stages are only Unknown op=0x76 + SubRoutine — ZERO Motion stages, unlike cabk/cawh/cafa.

So for a summoner/ranged/geomancy cast: dispatch_cast_routine_started inserts ActiveScheduler(effects_only) +
CastRoutine, but cast_posing() is false immediately, the aura is stopped on the very first frame it exists, and
the CastRoutine marker is removed — so any generator the routine spawns on a LATER frame is never stopped by
this path either.

FIX: track cast liveness on the CastRoutine marker itself (or on the session's self_casting / the actor's
action state) rather than inferring it from whether a Motion clip happened to resolve.
close_reason: The bead's DAT premise is confirmed against the retail install (caso/calg/cage really have zero Motion stages), but the defect it describes was fixed by commit 104d3ea — landed 16 minutes after the bead was filed — which added exactly the fix the bead proposes: a `posed` latch on the CastRoutine marker so the teardown no longer reads 'not posing' as 'cast over'.

title: Real-DAT guard tests silently skip under scripts/checks.sh (no FFXI_DAT_PATH)
description:
Six real-DAT guard tests added by 49e5ed3/929fd71 vacuously no-op under the project's own gate, so the commits' claim that they "pin retail bytes" is false for CI and for any dev who has not exported FFXI_DAT_PATH:
  real_dat_global_dir_holds_cast_aura_and_its_stop, cast_routine_flattens_across_actor_and_global_dirs,
  real_dat_poison_sheet_name_indexes_its_backing_img, cast_overlay_still_owns_the_looping_pose,
  real_dat_poison_generators_attach_to_target, real_dat_spell_main_links_caster_finish_routine

Cause: scripts/checks.sh test runs cargo test --workspace and never sets FFXI_DAT_PATH. Cargo sets each test
binary's cwd to its own package root, and DatRoot::from_env_or_default (ffxi-dat/src/archive.rs:78-87) falls back
to the RELATIVE path vendor/game-files/SquareEnix/FINAL FANTASY XI, which does not exist under ffxi-dat/ or
ffxi-viewer-core/. So the guard resolves nothing and the test returns early.

Blocked on a second problem: exporting FFXI_DAT_PATH to make them run turns the suite red via a pre-existing
unrelated failure, audio::tests::bgm_pipeline_end_to_end_with_real_install (missing add_message::<ToastEvent>()
in its test App; then slots.active is None). That needs fixing first or the workaround is unusable.

FIX: resolve the default DAT root against CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/workspace root rather than cwd, or have checks.sh
export FFXI_DAT_PATH when a local install is present and make the skip LOUD (print a skip line) so a silent
no-op is never mistaken for a pass.
close_reason: Residual done in c5e6f1b. The bead's filed root cause (DatRoot resolving its default install relative to cwd) was already fixed in 104d3ea2. Remaining work landed: archive::open_test_install is the single gate for real-DAT tests and prints why it skips, so a vacuous no-op can no longer read as a pass; EventLog::push now owns the cursor protocol (EVENT_LOG_CAP pop_front / push_back / pushed_total) that was re-typed at six call sites. The audio bgm_pipeline_end_to_end_with_real_install test runs green. Not done: a hard-fail FFXI_REQUIRE_DAT env gate — libtest captures stderr for passing tests, so the skip reason shows under --nocapture only.

title: Particle colour: retail stage gains are a per-element-type table (D3m: rgb 4x, alpha 8x) plus vertex alpha
description:
SETTLED (retail reversing, 2026-07-31). The bead's plan survives but its stated arithmetic was wrong.

There is no single universal 4x gain — retail uses a per-element-type TSS table. For the element type we actually render (D3m textured default, `NonZeroTwoTSS`):

  rgb   = 4 * D * T * F
  alpha = 8 * D.a * T.a * F.a

(D = diffuse/vertex, T = texture, F = TEXTUREFACTOR.)

In our normalized units (vertex colour already divided by 128) the three missing pieces are: the TFACTOR operand's 2x, an extra 2x on alpha, and **vertex alpha entirely** — `SpriteTemplate` has no vertex-alpha field.

CORRECTION: the bead previously recorded "XIM stage-1 gains (2x RGB, 4x alpha)". XIM's stage 0 is a vec4 multiply and agrees with retail **exactly** — the alpha gain is **8x**, not 4x. The transcription was wrong, not XIM.

EVIDENCE
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Resource/Derived/CMoD3m.cpp:16-104 — the six numeric TSS tables; :333-411 `Draw` with TEXTUREFACTOR set at :351 (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Generator/Effects/CMoD3aElem.cpp:15-55 — the same table spelled symbolically, validating the numeric decode (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Generator/Effects/CMoElem.cpp:381-458 — blend-byte enum; ALPHAREF 0x60 discard (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Rendering/ZoneRenderer.cpp:1361-1460 (`DoD3mDraw`) — the MMB-mesh particle branch we also have (particle_sim.rs:337-338, 742-752); totals coincide (tier 2)
- CMoD3m.cpp:345-349 — at blend byte 0x44 (our default Blend path) a TFACTOR alpha >= 0x7F is promoted to 0xFF.
design:
- ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:221-241 — parse `renderStateFlags & 0x1000` (bit 28) so the element type is known.
- kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:491, 570-584, 611, 663, 725, 742-752 — TFACTOR 2x on rgb, 4x stage gain on alpha, and add vert_alpha to SpriteTemplate.
- Name every gain as a const citing CMoD3m.cpp; do not inline the literals.
notes:
2026-07-31: implemented in 1bc4bbf (per-element table, D3m/Mmb split, 0x64 override, 0x44 promotion, per-stage saturate). Runtime-UNVERIFIED: the gain math was only glanced at through one particle effect with no before/after or numeric comparison. Needs a zone comparison or a debug overlay reading computed RGB/alpha before closing.
2026-08-01: Implementation landed in 1bc4bbf. Still runtime-UNVERIFIED after a second attempt: no active particle effect was captured on camera (both lanterns photographed read as static emissive geometry; two self-cast attempts were rejected server-side). The ~4%% brightness swing measured is plausibly AA noise - compare against the ~20%% structured oscillation that DID confirm the nameplate pulse. Needs a numeric before/after RGB/alpha comparison on a real flame or spell effect.
2026-09-09 adversarial done-check (triage flagged it as landed): NOT fully done. Evidence: Implementation of the per-element-type TSS gain table did land in commit 1bc4bbf8 ("Five retail-verified parity fixes from the research/ reversing sweep", Fri Jul 31 17:20:18 2026): kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs has the D3M_STAGE1_RGB_GAIN=2.0 / D3M_STAGE1_ALPHA_GAIN=4.0 consts (lines ~136-141), the D3M_VERTEX_BAKED_GAIN=2.0 note for the folded stage-0 MODULATE2X (line ~140), D3mDrawPath::{D3m,Mmb} split with ignores_texture_alpha() and D3M_MMB_FORCE_IGNORE_TEXTURE_ALPHA_BLEND_BYTE=0x64 (lines ~157-160,163-165), tfactor_alpha()'s 0x44 promotion (D3M_TFACTOR_PROMOTE_BLEND_BYTE/MIN/PROMOTED, lines ~166-183), the d3m_stage_chain() function applying the 2x/4x gains with per-stage clamp (lines ~189-207), and SpriteTemplate.colors: Vec<Vec4> (not a separate vert_alpha field, but the design's four-component vertex colour subsumes it) populated in sprite_template()/mmb_sprite_template()/sprit
Remaining: The bead's own acceptance bar (stated in its notes, not just a headline "implement the gain table") is a live, numeric before/after comparison of computed particle RGB/alpha against retail on an actual moving particle effect (flame or spell effect), via either a zone screenshot comparison or a debug overlay printing computed RGB/alpha values -- not just eyeballing a static/emissive-looking lantern. Two prior attempts (2026-07-31, 2026-08-01) failed to capture a genuinely active particle effect on camera and could not confirm the ~4% brightness swing they did observe was signal rather than AA noise. This verification pass has not been repeated since, and no code/commit exists that performs or records it.

title: Cast routine drops every non-Motion stage — no casting aura particles on the caster
description:
While casting, the caster plays the right body motion but shows none of retail's casting aura/particles.

Cause: kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:1254 routine_motion_clip() reduces the whole cast routine to its FIRST Motion stage and throws the rest away; dispatch_action_overlay (~:2215) then plays that clip and nothing else.

Evidence (examples/dat-routine-stages.rs, Hume M skeleton file 7072) — the black-magic cast routine has three stages, only the middle one survives:
  routine cabk
    frame 0 kind=SubRoutine id=hwmg
    frame 0 kind=Motion     id=mb0?  dur=33 loops=63   <- the only one we play
    frame 0 kind=SubRoutine id=ner1                    <- the cast aura
  routine shbk   (cast-complete)
    frame 0 SubRoutine hwmg / SubRoutine stbk / SubRoutine eis3 / frame 1 SubRoutine ssbk + Unknown wash
The ca<suffix> routines exist for every magic type in the race skeleton DAT: cabk cabl cafa cage cait calg canj casm caso cast cawh.

research/xim Actor.kt:263-266 startCasting() calls enqueueModelRoutine(DatId.castId(spellInfo)) — it runs the FULL model routine (particles, sound, subroutines), not a bare motion clip.

FIX: run the cast routine through the scheduler (dispatch_*_stages) the same way completion effect routines are run, instead of extracting one clip; resolve the SubRoutine ids (hwmg/ner1) against the actor's own resource dirs. Depends on the actor-side generator/particle plumbing.
notes:
REVIEW OUTCOME: the dispatch plumbing landed (929fd71) but is INERT against real packets — see kuluu-f1ew (P0): BATTLE2 cmd_arg for category 8 is the routine FourCC ('cabk'), not a spell id, so the suffix lookup always misses and the generic 'cast' routine resolves instead of 'cabk'. ky8c cannot be closed until f1ew lands. Also open from review: cast-aura-stopped-on-frame-1 for Motion-less routines (caso/calg/cage), and the singleton emit-window regression in particle_sim.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: AUDIT 2026-07-31 (read-only): the blocker cleared and the citations drifted.

- kuluu-f1ew is CLOSED (fixed and shipped in v0.4.0, 104d3ea/a867f9b). cmd_arg is now read as the routine FourCC at kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:880-890 and ffxi_actor_render.rs:2275-2285, with 'sp*' interrupts tearing the cast down. The 'IMPLEMENTED but INERT against real packets' note above no longer holds.
- Line drift: routine_motion_clip is now ffxi_actor_render.rs:1303-1310 (cited :1254); dispatch_action_overlay is now :2248 (cited ~:2215).
- The scheduler path landed at 9952d39: dispatch_cast_routine_started (scheduler_runtime.rs:845-923) flattens the entire routine via ActiveScheduler::effects_only (:142-144, MotionStages::Suppress) and is registered at :1386, so non-Motion stages are no longer discarded; routine_motion_clip now supplies only the body pose.
- Of the two residual review items, only ONE is still open: kuluu-vxv8 (cast aura stopped on frame 1 for Motion-less caso/calg/cage) — dep-link that one. kuluu-vgps (singleton generators emitting nothing past the emit window) is already CLOSED, fixed in 104d3ea2 with regression tests at particle_sim.rs:1008.
- Close this on a live cast observation (the ner1 aura appearing on a BLM cast), not on the code read.
- Not re-verified here: the cabk/shbk stage dump, which needs `cargo run -p ffxi-dat --example dat-routine-stages`.

title: Tie dynamic point-light glow to its lamp fixture geometry (keep combined)
description: Faithful point lights sit at authored ~1.8m sconce height, but hanging lamp MODELS are higher (Lower Jeuno zone 245: light pl07 bevyY -4.2 vs player feet -6.0, model hangs above), so the glow billboard reads below the fixture. User wants the light+lamp kept combined, robust to edge cases (raycast-up to lamp mesh, or move light to fixture). Needs live visual iteration to tune. Evidence: zone_point_lights.rs glow billboard; dat-scan-lightpos zone 345.
close_reason: Resolved by removal: the DAT has no light->fixture association (Port Windurst DAT 340 lights 4-7 sit ~1.3m from their lanterns; most Lower Jeuno lights have no fixture placement at all), so no snap heuristic can keep a separate glow tied to its lamp in general. Dropped the glow billboard in fea2bba; lamps are now lit solely by their clustered PointLight, as retail does. Follow-up for lamp-fixture brightness at distance tracked separately.

title: Configurable dynamic-light count (expand 4-slot point-light uniform)
description: Zone + actor FFXI materials share FfxiLightingUniform with point_pos/color/atten [Vec4;4] (skinned_ffxi_material.rs:58); both WGSL shaders loop over 4 nearest-to-viewer lights. So only the 4 nearest lamps illuminate zone geometry — distant lamps show the glow billboard but cast no ground light until near. User wants this cap configurable. Plan: bump the shared array to MAX_POINT_LIGHTS=16 (Rust uniform + both .wgsl, guard-tested contract), fill nearest-N via the pickers, add a Dynamic Light Count graphics setting (<=MAX). Shader already skips empty slots (range<=0). Evidence: ffxi_zone_material.rs:542, skinned_ffxi.wgsl:140.
notes: SUPERSEDED APPROACH: raising the nearest-N cap can't fix pop-in — zones have up to 251 point lights (file 233/289), so feed-all is infeasible and nearest-to-viewer inherently pops. HOLY-GRAIL PLAN: Bevy clustered forward lighting in zone_ffxi.wgsl + skinned_ffxi.wgsl, looping the fragment's cluster point lights with FFXI 2x-overbright falloff (not Bevy PBR). Efficient (spatial bins), no pop-in, scales to 250, keeps flicker, works with shared/instanced meshes. title: Render server customMenu (GMPROMPT/_CUSTOM_MENU) as interactive dialog, not chat
description: Server sends customMenu prompts (home point Set/Yes/No, etc.) via GP_SERV_COMMAND_CHAT_STD with type MESSAGE_GMPROMPT(12) and sender name _CUSTOM_MENU, message = quoted-concat "Title""Opt1""Opt2" (vendor/server/src/map/lua/lua_baseentity.cpp:621, luautils.cpp SetCustomMenuContext).
