title: Poison completion particles render white (wrong color/effect)
description: After the spell-DAT cast-motion fix, Poison casts with the correct (black-magic) motion but its COMPLETION particles show as plain white instead of the poison effect. The completion effect DAT + particle color/texture selection (dispatch_action_started -> spell_file_id, particle_sim spawn) is picking a wrong/untinted effect. Likely related to spell_file_id (0xAF0 + animation index) resolving the wrong effect DAT, or the particle def's color/texture not applied. Cross-check research/xim EffectDisplayer.displaySkill. Needs live verify + DAT dump.
notes:
LANDED (49e5ed3) — Part A, the texture-resolution fix, is complete and green.

Root cause confirmed exactly as noted: resolve_mesh looked the backing Img up under the sheet's NAMESPACE token (images_by_name.get(&ss.category) = get("venom1")) while ActionAssets indexed Imgs under the LOCAL token ("fir"), so it always missed and d3m_material(blend, None) drew an untextured quad.

CORRECTION to the bead's stated fix. The notes proposed 'match the full 16-byte texture name on both sides (XIM-faithful)'. That is NOT what XIM does and it would have broken four other consumers. research/xim DatResource.kt:312-315,483-493 SPLITS the qualified 16-char name into (namespace, localName) and matches the qualified PAIR first, then falls back to localName only. And MMB models physically only carry 8 bytes (ffxi-dat/src/mmb.rs:505-517 reads decrypted[off+8..off+16]), so retail itself matches MMB textures on the local token alone — a full-16-byte key would have broken dat_mmb.rs:236, dat_vos2.rs:162, zone_clouds.rs:258 and the MMB fallback at particle_sim.rs:273 to fix one particle.

What landed:
  - ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs: new split_qualified_name + extract_texture_tokens; extract_texture_name is now extract_texture_tokens(..).map(|(_,id)| id), so its four existing callers are unchanged.
  - ffxi-dat/src/sprite_sheet.rs: texture_tokens now calls the shared splitter. The drift between that local copy and texture.rs's was the bug; the split now has one home.
  - kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs: added ActionAssets::images_by_qualified_name; the Img arm populates both tiers. images_by_name is untouched.
  - kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs: the SpriteSheet arm does qualified-then-local lookup. THE one-line fix.

Guard tests (all run, all pass):
  - scheduler_runtime::real_dat_poison_sheet_name_indexes_its_backing_img — REAL DAT (file 3020). Asserts the sheet is ('venom1','fir'), that images_by_qualified_name has that pair, that images_by_name has 'fir', and that images_by_name does NOT have 'venom1' (the original miss). Confirmed to actually execute, not skip: the retail install is present and dat-sheet-texture 3020 reproduces the same tokens.
  - sprite_sheet::sheet_and_img_split_the_same_qualified_name — synthetic emitter/matcher coupling guard.
  - texture::extract_texture_name_is_the_local_token / split_qualified_name_trims_both_tokens.
  - particle_sim::sheet_texture::{resolves_by_qualified_name, falls_back_to_local_name, does_not_resolve_by_namespace_alone}.

Gate: scripts/checks.sh fmt clippy clean; ffxi-dat 236 passed; kuluu-render 558 passed.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE. No GUI session was run. What is proven is that the Img handle now resolves; that the venom cloud actually LOOKS right on screen is unobserved. Note kuluu-nefy is still open, so the effect renders on the CASTER, not the target.

PART B (colour normalisation) SPLIT OUT to kuluu-ilan, deliberately not landed. The arithmetic is now proven against primary sources (XimParticleShader.kt:247,249 + ParticleDrawer.kt:126 + Color.kt:70 + MeshBuffers.kt:41): we are exactly 2x dark in RGB and discard vertex alpha entirely, with no compensating gain downstream (d3m_material is unlit/WHITE). But it is a global brightness change to every particle in the game, additive compounds it to as much as 8x, and — decisively — you cannot calibrate a 2x brightness change against a quad that was untextured until this commit. Part B has to be A/B'd live AFTER Part A is seen. zone-render-headless does not wire particles, so no headless capture is possible.

Also filed kuluu-0itr: the StaticMesh arm still resolves its texture by 4-byte DatId, a third naming convention — same class of latent bug.

Leaving OPEN pending live verification of the venom cloud.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Append to NOTES:

AUDIT 2026-07-31 (read-only). Part A re-verified in the tree; three citations corrected.

- COMMIT HASH: the landed commit is 6031f66, not 49e5ed3 (49e5ed3 is unreachable from any branch — the worktree commit was rebased on the way to main).
- Everything else in the Part A account checks out: ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs:53,60-64,70-71 (split_qualified_name / extract_texture_tokens / extract_texture_name delegating to it), ffxi-dat/src/sprite_sheet.rs:191-192 (texture_tokens calls the shared splitter), kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:277,281,493-495 (both index tiers), kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:694-706 (the one-line qualified-then-local fix). All six named guard tests exist: scheduler_runtime.rs:1981, sprite_sheet.rs:358, texture.rs:498/543, particle_sim.rs:1247/1252/1259.
- The CORRECTION is itself correct. research/xim DatResource.kt:312-316 splits the 16-char name at 8 (TextureName.fromFullyQualified) and :488-492 matches the qualified pair first, then localName only — it is not a full-16-byte match. Corroborated by format: ffxi-dat/src/mmb.rs:505-517 reads only decrypted[off+8..off+16], so an MMB physically cannot carry a namespace.
- MMB fallback line ref drifted: particle_sim.rs:273 -> particle_sim.rs:337-343.
- kuluu-0itr is now CLOSED (abe671f). particle_sim.rs:675-691 tiers qualified -> local -> DatId, so "the StaticMesh arm still resolves its texture by 4-byte DatId" no longer holds.
- Part B: kuluu-ilan has since SETTLED against XIClient (tier 2) and supersedes the XIM-derived arithmetic quoted here — the alpha gain is 8x, not the 4x transcribed, and the gains are a per-element-type TSS table rather than one universal factor. Read kuluu-ilan, not this note, for the numbers.
- STILL OPEN and unchanged: the only remaining scope is live visual confirmation that the venom cloud renders as poison rather than white. Not doable statically (zone-render-headless does not wire particles).
2026-09-08 live GUI verification (LSB dev stack, verilight/Verilamp, release build target/release/kuluu). Confirmed the Part-A texture-resolution fix renders on screen for the first time (previously proven only by unit tests against static DAT bytes). Cast pipeline round-trips cleanly: self_cast_started -> self_cast_ended{interrupted:false} -> action_started{action_kind:4} -> 'Verilamp casts Poison. <target> is Poison.' A precisely-timed screenshot burst (started at the instant the completion action fired on the agent socket, 120ms cadence, 16 frames) caught the completion particle growing on Snipper (Valkurm Dunes, zone 103) from t=0.99s to a clear bloom at t=1.62s post-completion, then fading by t=1.87s -- it is NOT visible in the surrounding frames (t=0 to 0.87s), confirming it is a short-lived transient effect roughly 0.6-1s long that is easy to miss without instrumented capture. Sampled pixel color at the bloom core is RGB(96,13,92) -- magenta/purple, with R and B channels far exceeding G -- decisively not the pre-fix uniform white/gray. A same-region pre-cast baseline (flat tan sand, RGB~165,160,145) rules out a terrain/shadow artifact. char_jobs.blm=50 (>=6) confirmed live via docker exec against server-database-1 before casting, ruling out a server-side spell-rejection false negative. The cloud renders at the TARGET's base (not the caster), confirming kuluu-nefy's target-attach fix also landed, though its own known joint-21-offset gap (cloud at base vs. correct joint) remains open and separate. Artifacts: artifacts/verify/kuluu-7jpq/{pre_cast.png, pburst_f00..f15.png, events.jsonl, client.log}. The clearest single frame is pburst_f14.png. Exact hue-vs-retail colorimetric match is explicitly out of this bead's scope (kuluu-ilan). title: Cast motion + cast-bar duration must come from retail spell DAT (ROM/118/114.DAT), not LSB
description:
Root cause of two reported bugs: (1) Poison plays the wrong cast animation, (2) Water's cast-bar duration is wrong.

Today ffxi-proto::magic::cast_suffix derives the cast motion from the LSB *skill* (Enfeebling->white 'cawh'), and the cast bar uses the scraped LSB spell_list.castTime (ms). Both are wrong vs the real client, which reads its OWN spell-list DAT:

Authoritative source: research/xim SpellListSection.kt + DatResource.kt::castSuffix.
- File: ROM/118/114.DAT, DAT section type 0x49 (S49_SpellList), 0x64-byte blocks, decoded via XIM BlockDecoder (popcount of bytes 0x02/0x0B/0x0C -> rotate amount).
- Per-spell fields: index(u16)=spellId, magicType(u16), element(u16), targetFlags(u16), skillType(u16), mpCost(u16), castTime(u8), recastDelay(u8). castTime/recast are in units of 0.25s (XIM SpellInfo.toFrames: time/4).
- Cast motion clip = 'ca'+suffix where suffix keys on magicType: White=wh, Black=bk, Summon=sm, Ninjutsu=nj, Song=so, Blue=bl, Geomancy=ge, Trust=fa. Poison's magicType is Black -> 'cabk' (NOT white). This split is exactly why the skill heuristic is wrong.
- Interrupt/stop-cast clip = 'sp'+suffix (spwh/spbk/...).

Plan: add ffxi-dat spell_info parser (model on item_dat.rs + chunk::walk, port SpellListSection layout + BlockDecoder), expose spell_id -> {magic_type, cast_time_ms}. Use magic_type in action_routine kind-8 suffix + the interrupt clip; use cast_time for SelfCasting.total_ms/cast bar. Add unit tests pinning Poison=Black, Cure=White, and a couple cast times. Requires FFXI_DAT_PATH retail files to run tests + live cast to verify visually.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (commit 8b8ac56), pending visual verification. Added ffxi-dat::spell_info (SpellTable+MagicType, XIM-ported), wired magicType->kind-8 cast suffix (render, LSB skill fallback) + castTime->cast_bar/action_lock_ms (session). Round-trip + suffix unit tests pass; fmt+clippy green. STILL NEEDS: live cast of Poison (expect cabk motion, not cawh) + Water (expect cast bar to match server) against the LSB stack, since the DAT offsets/values can only be confirmed against the user's retail ROM/118/114.DAT at runtime.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: OFFLINE VERIFICATION (adversarial re-audit, 2026-07-31): the parser was re-run against the user's own retail ROM/118/114.DAT, independently of the auditor.
- CONFIRMED: walking the file with our 7-bit-kind/19-bit-size rule (ffxi-dat/src/chunk.rs:60-64) yields a kind-0x49 chunk named 'mgc_' at 0x28720, 102416 bytes -> 1024 blocks of 0x64; every block's u16@0x00 equals its position.
- CONFIRMED: poison(220) decodes to magicType 2 = BlackMagic -> 'cabk', mp 5, castTime 4 units (1000 ms), recast 20 units (5000 ms) — an exact match to vendor/server/sql/spell_list.sql:302. cure(1) matches too (8 mp / 2000 / 5000). Bug (1)'s premise is confirmed at the data level; only the on-screen clip is left to look at.
- CONFIRMED: our key choice. XIM's readElement calls u16@0x00 `index` and reads a DIFFERENT `spellId` u16 at 0x3E (SpellListSection.kt:155-180); the two disagree for 1011 of 1024 blocks. Keying by index@0x00 (spell_info.rs OFF_SPELL_ID) reproduces LSB mpCost for 791 of 891 spells; keying by id@0x3E reproduces only 182. OFF_SPELL_ID = 0x00 is right.
- NOT fully confirmed, contrary to an earlier note: the field layout is corroborated but not proven. mpCost disagrees with LSB for 100 of 891 spells, systematically across the elemental family (fire DAT 24 vs LSB 7, water 13 vs 5, aero 18 vs 6, stone 9 vs 4), where LSB's ascending 4/5/6/7 series is the familiar retail one. And castTime disagrees for 20 of the 110 spells with id<=111 — the exact range where spell_list.sql:49 asserts 'Value = .dat value * 250' (banish 4000 vs 2000, blindna 3000 vs 1000, cure_vi 3250 vs 2000, stoneskin 8000 vs 7000). Either our castTime offset/decode is not universally right, or LSB's audit is. That is unsettled from these sources alone.

CAVEAT ON THE LIVE CHECK: DAT and LSB disagree on castTime for 133 of 891 spells and water(169) is one of them — DAT 8 units = 2000 ms vs spell_list.sql:251 castTime 500 ms, which is what LSB enforces (vendor/server/src/map/spell.cpp:490 setCastTime). Against a stock LSB dev stack the new bar will deliberately NOT match the server's completion, so 'cast bar matches the server' is the wrong pass condition. Verify Water on an era-locked server, or assert only that the bar reads 2.0s and that Poison plays cabk — and treat the 20 in-audited-range castTime disagreements above as an open question worth a retail-observation pass.

title: Cast interrupt must cancel the looping cast animation pose
description: Interrupting a spell (movement/paralyze/silence) clears the cast bar + self_casting, but the self actor's looping cast pose (action_routine kind 8, ActionPlayback looping, remaining=CAST_TIMEOUT_FRAMES 60s) is only cleared by a later ActionStarted event. An interrupt is a battle-message, not an ActionStarted, so the caster keeps playing the cast loop for 60s. Fix render-side: tag the spell cast-loop ActionPlayback as cast_pose and cancel it on the self actor in tick_live_ffxi_actors when self_casting is None/interrupted.

title: Home Point crystal body strobes to fully transparent (continuous track-less particle fade)
description: The Home Point crystal renders as a generic NPC actor whose visible geometry is built from embedded particle generators. The crystal BODY is a 'continuous' generator (GEN_FLAG_CONTINUOUS) that holds exactly one particle, re-emitted each time it expires. In particle_sim.rs rebuild_mesh, a generator with no alpha keyframe track defaults its per-frame alpha to 1.0-progress (particle_sim.rs:479), so each re-emit cycle fades the single body particle to nothing -> the whole crystal strobes to fully transparent. The aura shell carries a real alpha track and is unaffected. Fix: a continuous track-less generator holds its init opacity (init_color[3]) instead of fading; transient sprays keep the 1.0-progress fade.
notes: CORRECTED understanding: per-generator dump of DAT 1351 shows depthMask (bb & 0x1000)=0 on ALL generators — retail NEVER depth-writes/occludes the crystal. The gem is a large closed 192-tri additive shard (sil, texture nami ~0.5 alpha) drawn 2x (sil0+sil1); it reads dense purely from additive brightness, not opacity. wa/naka=additive halos, bind=alpha-blend ring, pou=additive billboard sparkle. The 'solid body' direction was a misread; making it opaque (static Mask lit material) produced white slabs + black backfaces. Real keepers: strobe fix (continuous track-less additive shards hold constant brightness, no fade) + blip fix (gapless continuous re-emit). Faithful default = translucent additive. Any hard-occluding/denser gem is an ENHANCEMENT (no generator flag supports isolating sil generically; would need mesh hardcode).
close_reason: Fixed strobe (continuous additive shards hold constant brightness) + blip (gapless continuous re-emit). Crystal confirmed faithfully translucent-additive per DAT 1351 (depthMask=0 on all generators — retail never occludes it); a denser/opaque gem would be an Enhanced feature. User accepts the faithful look.

title: Cloud canopy occludes zone geometry: CLOUD_MIN_RIM=4000 is 1500u inside sky dome
description: weat/<type> cld1/cld2 canopy (zone_clouds.rs) is AlphaMode::Blend and camera-following. Its rim is pushed only to CLOUD_MIN_RIM=4000, but the comment (and the depth-occlusion invariant it relies on) require it just inside SKYBOX_RADIUS=5500. Any terrain past 4000 (Jeuno, wide fields) is farther than the canopy, so the translucent canopy draws over it -> dome-shaped foggy band overlaying zone mesh. Fix: derive the min rim from SKYBOX_RADIUS so the const can't drift from its own comment.
close_reason: Derived CLOUD_MIN_RIM from SKYBOX_RADIUS (5400, was 4000); canopy now depth-occluded by all in-dome terrain instead of draping over it

title: Textured top-down minimap bake (lit + re-bake on light change)
description:
Replace the grey synthetic-collision-mesh top-down minimap bake with a render of the real textured zone geometry (MMB meshes via FfxiZoneMaterial), viewed top-down from the ceiling-clamped ortho bake camera.

Current: ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/topdown.rs bakes a synthetic unlit mesh rebuilt from MzbCollisionGeometry. Camera sits at ceiling_y = max_y - top_cull_yalms looking down; near plane clips the roof.

Target: point the same offscreen ortho bake camera at the real textured static zone meshes instead.
- Tag static zone meshes (dat_mmb.rs MMB geometry) onto MINIMAP_BAKE_LAYER (RenderLayers::from_layers(&[0, BAKE_LAYER])) so the bake camera sees walls/floors but NOT actors/sky/weather/particles/water.
- Keep the ceiling-clamp camera placement so the near plane still slices the roof.
- Lighting: LIT bake (FfxiZoneMaterial vertex lighting + point lights + time-of-day). Lights must be on the bake render layer. Re-bake when zone lighting/time-of-day changes materially so the map stays current (do not leave a night-baked map frozen).
- One-shot per (zone, lighting-state); dispose bake mesh path since synthetic mesh no longer used.

Faithfulness: Enhanced fallback only (retail uses hand-drawn static map art = Retail backend). Applies where no retail map art exists (Mog House interiors etc.).

title: Chase camera clips through Mog House door (non-collision zone geometry ignored)
description: In the Mog House the chase camera passes through the closed exit-door panel and escapes the room into the void. Root cause (confirmed via camera_collision debug probe): the door panel is visible MZB geometry flagged doesnt-block-LOS, so it lands in the non-collision set and is excluded from the camera's zone BVH (which is built only from block-LOS/collision triangles). Per-cast probe in SdO MH (zone 0x00E6): rays toward the door return bvh_hit=false AND brute_hit=false while rays toward real walls/ceiling hit. Fix: include the non-collision (camera_only) MZB geometry in the camera-collision BVH (ZoneCollisionBvh) while keeping grounding/nav on collision-only geometry. Matches XIM PolarCamera (Collider.getObjectDistance casts against all visible geometry, skipping only hitWall material tris).

Retail pages vertical list menus with Left/Right (one screenful per press, clamped at the ends) while Up/Down step one row.

IMPLEMENTED in commit fbf7272: kuluu-render/src/hud/menu.rs:332-348 (list_page_rows + page_cursor, unit-tested at menu.rs:1432-1461), driving the Items branch at kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:3531-3549 and a generic is_dynamic branch at :3585-3606 (Graphics value-cycles and the Equipment grid still consume Left/Right in their own blocks at :3553-3583). Up/Down still wrap one row at a time (text_input.rs:3607-3621).

REMAINING: live GUI keypress confirmation — open the ring Items list and a Magic/Abilities list, press Left/Right, confirm the cursor jumps ~one page. Not agent-socket drivable. Note the main Items list already paged before the fix (the fbf7272 pre-image had the jump inline); the gap was UsableItems and the other dynamic lists, so confirm which menu the original report was about.

UPSTREAM CAVEAT: XIClient implements no in-game menu-list cursor navigation (its only menu cursor is the lobby button index, CIwLobbyMenu.cpp:48/223-239; UI/Elements/Menu.cpp:552-568 is scrollbar geometry), so the only upstream corroboration is research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/game/UiState.kt:790-798 (tier 7). XIM scrolls the viewport a page and holds the cursor's within-page offset; page_cursor moves the absolute cursor by `rows`. Those agree at the ends but differ mid-list (absolute cursor 20 with viewport start 8 and a 13-row page: XIM -> 12, ours -> 7). Settle that against retail during the live check.
notes: IMPLEMENTED (commit fbf7272): generic Left/Right paging for all is_dynamic list menus via menu::list_page_rows + menu::page_cursor (both unit-tested, 27 hud::menu tests ok); client compiles. PENDING: live GUI keypress confirmation (not agent-socket drivable) — open ring Items list + a Magic/Abilities list, press Left/Right, confirm cursor jumps ~one page. If retail's Items menu ALSO felt non-paging to the user, note the main Items menu already paged pre-fix — the gap was UsableItems/other lists; may need to confirm which menu the user tested.

title: Bastok Markets (zone 0xEB): character falls through floor into water between two positions
description: Walking between two specific positions in Bastok Markets (zone id 0xEB=235) causes the player to fall through the floor and appear in the water. Likely a ground-height / collision raycast gap that falls back to water_height or Y=0. Reported with screen recording.
notes:
LIVE REPRO via the new focus-less tooling (kuluu-0pof). Drove char forward from point A; it fell into the canal water (visually confirmed, screenshot). /debug heights readings:
- At A (walkway): server_z=1.80, mzb_floor_bevy=-2.0, nav_bevy=-1.8 (all agree, on walkway).
- At the drop (x=-200.6, y=-128 / y=-126): server_z fell 1.8 -> -3.3 -> -3.9; mzb_floor_bevy=-8.0 AND nav_bevy=-7.8 — BOTH drop to the canal/water floor (~6 yalms below the walkway).
So mzb (visual) and nav AGREE at the fall spot too — the floor genuinely drops off to water level here; the char walks off the walkway edge and is grounded onto the low canal floor. Still TBD: whether the drop is a smooth descent or a cliff/hole (trace debug_heights at closely-spaced points from y=-157 to y=-126 along x~-200.6), which decides the fix (edge/rail collision vs accept). Tooling now makes this a quick trace.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: RE-MEASURE BEFORE ACTING — the 2026-07-21 readings predate the collision fix.

The NOTES conclude "mzb (visual) and nav AGREE at the fall spot too — the floor genuinely drops off to water level here". Two problems. First, the mzb_floor readout was never the visual mesh: debug_heights reads `Res<MzbCollisionGeometry>` (and did at the time — git show be8d8f9:kuluu/src/view_native/debug_heights.rs:36,71). Second, that collision geometry then EXCLUDED every submesh with mesh flag bit 0 set — `let is_collision = sub.flags & 1 == 0;` routed them into a separate non-collision buffer (git show ab7258d~1:kuluu-render/src/dat_mzb.rs:1467). kuluu-0nnl (ab7258d, 2026-07-30) proved that filter wrong: bit 0 is `doesnt_block_los`, a line-of-sight property ordinary walkable street tiles set, and gating on it left 13% of the Lower Jeuno street columns with no floor to ground against (kuluu-render/src/dat_mzb.rs:363-369). A missing walkway column is exactly what produces mzb_floor_bevy=-8.0 (the canal floor beneath), so the measurement basis is invalid. nav_bevy=-7.8 is not independent corroboration: the LSB Recast mesh is coarse mob-pathing geometry and is not the authority for player floors (AGENTS.md).

Also changed since the reading: collision now uses the authored per-triangle MZB normals rather than winding-derived ones (so undersides are no longer landing surfaces), and player movement goes through `ground_step` — nearest up-facing floor within MAX_GROUND_STEP_UP=1.0, unbounded downwards (dat_mzb.rs:219, :262-283). kuluu/src/view_native/input.rs:920-925 now names this very case as handled: "a stacked column (Bastok Markets' walkway over its canal) resolves to the level we're on rather than teleporting to another layer".

The TBD (smooth descent vs cliff) no longer needs a live session: `cargo run -p kuluu-render --example zz-ground-walk 235 <x0> <y0> <z0> <x1> <y1> [step]` replays the client's per-frame grounding along the walked segment from the DATs and reports every height change. Run it from y=-157 to y=-126 along x~-200.6 first. If the walkway column is now solid this closes; if it is a genuine ledge, the fix is horizontal wall/rail collision, which is kuluu-q5sn's scope (input.rs:935-937 — horizontal movement is deliberately unconstrained until then), not a separate fix here.

title: Retail-faithful sky/lighting/atmosphere: fix zone-geom distance fog, sun disc visibility, warm ToD tone
description: Comparison vs retail (Sarutabaruta, dawn) shows our rendering diverges: (1) zone terrain/water ignores DistanceFog (zone_ffxi.wgsl never imports/samples bevy_pbr::fog) -> distant horizon falls to dark ClearColor 'black void' instead of retail's hazy fade; (2) no visible sun disc/bloom at times the sun is up; (3) cooler/greener overall tone + flat sky vs retail warm golden-hour gradient. Infra exists (skybox.rs gradient, sun_moon.rs disc+lens flare, weather.rs DAT fog/ambient, atmosphere.rs) but the play-path result is wrong. Fix the confirmed fog gap first, then diagnose sun-disc + tone at runtime via verify/retail-observe loop.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-07-20 (both main gaps):
(1) DISTANCE FOG — zone_ffxi.wgsl + skinned_ffxi.wgsl now apply_distance_fog() under #ifdef DISTANCE_FOG (consume the DistanceFog weather.rs already sets). Deterministic proof artifacts/verify/fog-fix-BEFORE/AFTER-saruta-dawn.png: distant terrain fades to warm horizon vs black void.
(2) SUN GLOW / retail sky — ROOT CAUSE: default sky_style was Enhanced (all 4 presets), which DISABLES the retail painterly lens flare (lens_flare_system gates on !sky_embellishments); Enhanced's sun is a flat glowless disc (bloom 0.08 ~no-op). Vanilla style = retail-faithful painterly sun (bright core + soft halo + horizontal streak + ghosts). Fix: flipped all presets sky_style Enhanced->Vanilla (settings.rs for_preset Low/Med/High/Ultra), aligning with AGENTS.md vanilla-parity-default. Updated 5 settings tests; 35 pass. A/B artifacts/verify/sun-ENHANCED-default-flat-h7.png vs sun-VANILLA-retail-faithful-h7.png vs sun-DEFAULT-now-vanilla-retail-h7.png.
SKY GRADITENT: confirmed FINE (skybox.wgsl 8-color DAT gradient) — user's flat green sky was overcast weather + low sun, not a gradient bug; at clear dawn it renders navy zenith->warm amber horizon.
HARNESS: examples/zone-render-headless.rs gained --sky/--vanilla-sky/--enhanced-sky flags reusing the REAL SkyboxPlugin+MoonMaterialPlugin+LensFlarePlugin+spawn_sun_and_moon+sun_moon_system (no reimplementation) — deterministic daytime sky/sun tuning at fixed --hour.
CAVEAT: our LSB dev weather != retail HorizonXI weather (independent); matched structure not exact pixels. NOTE: working tree had many unrelated pre-existing uncommitted files (not mine).

title: Launcher/char-select UI click leaks into world targeting, opens no-target action menu on zone-in
description:
click_to_target_system (picking.rs) ran unconditionally in every AppPhase, gated only on InputMode::World (the startup default). During Launcher/character-select, clicking a UI button resolves to hit_id=None with current_target=None -> ClickResolution::OpenContextMenu, setting InputMode::TargetAction with an empty (no-target) context. That state persisted into InGame; once the HUD spawned on zone-in the leaked Magic/Abilities/Items target-action menu became visible.

Fix: added WorldPickingEnabled(bool) resource in ffxi-viewer-core::picking (default true for the launcher-less wasm viewer). click_to_target_system early-returns + drains the click queue when false. Native client (view_native/mod.rs) overrides default to false and toggles true on OnEnter(AppPhase::InGame) / false on OnExit(AppPhase::InGame), stopping the leak at its source.
close_reason: Fixed: WorldPickingEnabled gate blocks world-click targeting outside AppPhase::InGame

Fix: pivot_steer feeds resolved.steer into advance_heading_turn (same path as first-person arrow-turn) at HEADING_TURN_RATE when forward==0; steer_in_chase now requires forward!=0 so steer only becomes a camera-relative run direction combined with W/S. moving=false while pivoting, so no run animation.

title: Self player never plays directional locomotion anims (mvl/mvr/mvb): backpedal moonwalks with the forward run clip
description: ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:2055-2059 hardcodes forward_vel/strafe_vel to (0.0,0.0) unless engaged && !is_self, so the self character always plays run?/wlk? while moving — S-key backpedal (BACKPEDAL_SCALE 0.5, input.rs:721) slides backward under a forward-run animation (observed live 2026-07-19, artifacts/verify/mvcam-06-s-hold-b.png). Selection logic already supports the directional clips (ffxi-actor/src/actor_state.rs:185-198 movement_direction thresholds at 161-183); it's only the self input wiring that zeroes them. Retail shows directional gait when moving backward/sideways (locked-on strafe/backpedal). Fix: feed real forward/strafe velocity for self; retest backpedal + locked-on strafe visuals.
notes: Do NOT fix naively by feeding real forward/strafe velocities unconditionally: retail plays directional clips (mvl/mvr/mvb) ONLY when locked on — unlocked movement is always velocity-parallel-to-facing (tank controls), so unlocked run/walk is the only correct clip. Under Kuluu's current camera-relative steer (kuluu-ltns), W+A has a heading-lerp lag window (HEADING_LERP_RATE 5.0/s, input.rs:697-698) where velocity and facing disagree; unconditional velocity feed would flicker mvl/mvr there — a NEW divergence retail cannot express. Correct shape: resolve kuluu-ltns first (movement model), then gate directional anims on lock-on; unlocked stays run?/wlk?. Also the blend-lag foot-slide itself (diagonal translation under forward-run clip) is an artifact only the tank-control model eliminates.
close_reason: SelfMoveIntent now carries forward/strafe character-frame components; ffxi_actor_render feeds them for self (was hardcoded 0,0). Directional clips (mvl/mvr/mvb) can only trigger while locked on because the tank model makes unlocked velocity always facing-parallel (S about-faces instead of backpedaling) — matching retail's lock-on-only directional gait. Moonwalk gone by construction; visual confirmation of mvl/mvr/mvb clips during locked strafe still worth a human-eyes pass.

title: Keyboard movement model diverges from retail: camera-relative W + steer-blend A/D vs retail character-relative tank controls; S backpedals instead of turn-and-run
description:
Retail observation (HorizonXI, char Oldman, Mog House + plaza, artifacts/retail/20260719-14*.png session): keyboard movement is CHARACTER-relative. 'A'/left-arrow rotate the character in place (tank turn, camera trails behind); W+A carves a curved arc; S turns the character 180 and runs toward the camera (no unlocked backpedal); after orbiting the camera with numpad4, W continues along the character's OWN facing (camera swings back), not camera-forward.

Kuluu today (ffxi-client/src/view_native/input.rs): W snaps heading to camera yaw (input.rs:659-662, heading_for_yaw(chase.yaw)) — camera-relative; A/D do a camera-relative steer-blend (turn_in_chase, input.rs:668-708, HEADING_LERP_RATE 5.0/s); S backpedals facing away at BACKPEDAL_SCALE 0.5 (input.rs:50,721). Fast auto-recenter (camera_polish_system input.rs:979-1027, rate 3.0) masks the difference in casual play — live drive 2026-07-19 (artifacts/verify/mvcam-08-*.png) observationally matched retail only because the camera had already recentered before W was pressed.

Decide: vanilla-faithful tank-control mode (at least as the default or an option) vs keeping the modern scheme as an enhanced-flagged alternative. Retail evidence: first driver log in session artifacts; remake evidence artifacts/verify/mvcam-*.png.
close_reason: Implemented retail tank controls in dispatch_movement_system (input.rs): unlocked A/D rotate the character in place at TURN_KEY_RATE_RAD_PER_SEC 5.0 (fast, per user feedback — Q/E keep the slow HEADING_TURN_RATE 0.86; exact retail A/D rate still unmeasured, retest in a future retail session); W moves along the character's own heading (camera-relative snap removed); unlocked S = about-face (+128) + full-speed forward run, no unlocked backpedal; locked-on A/D strafe and S backpedals with heading pinned to target; steer-blend (HEADING_LERP/CHASE_TRACK) removed; autorun now steerable (turn keys no longer cancel it). FP keeps view=facing (rigid yaw coupling). Live-verified with probes+screenshots (artifacts/verify/tankmove-*), unit tests resolve_tank_inputs in input.rs.

title: Intermittent slab_allocator use-after-free corrupts renderer: all zone geometry renders pure black after first zone-in until relaunch
description: Found during kuluu-042y verification (2026-07-19): bevy_render::slab_allocator logged 'Use-after-free: attempted to copy element data for an unallocated key' repeatedly right after first outdoor zone-in; from then on ALL zone geometry (walls/floor/ceiling/lamps) rendered pure black in every dynamic-lights mode while skinned character models stayed lit. Clean relaunch of the identical character rendered normally. Intermittent Bevy renderer corruption independent of the lights feature but fully masks it when it occurs. Suspect mesh-allocator interaction with zone mesh despawn/respawn on zone-in; possibly related to bevy 0.18 slab allocator + our zone rebuild path.
notes:
LIVE VERIFY 2026-07-21 (GUI, Verilamp): fixed build, login -> zone 231 (San d'Oria) -> !zone 234 (Bastok Mines), ~90s runtime. 7 auto-run particle generators spawned and ran (nak0/nak1/sil0/sil1/bnd0/wa00/wa01 — each meshes.add(empty_mesh()) + per-frame rebuild, the exact zero-vertex path). Result: 0 'unallocated key'/Use-after-free lines, 0 slab_allocator lines all session (grep on artifacts/verify/particle-empty-mesh-run.log). Evidence recorded .verify/latest.json. REMAINING: the all-black zone-geometry symptom was NOT visually re-checked this run (macOS console was locked -> screencapture/System Events blind, gotcha drive-gui.md:110). Reopen a GUI session on an unlocked console to confirm zone geometry stays lit across repeated zone-ins; if black-out ever recurs with 0 slab errors, it is a separate bug from this (now-fixed) empty-mesh spam.
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: AUDIT 2026-07-31 (static): the slab_allocator half of this bead is fixed and pinned. b5b21b0 makes empty generators upload one zero-area, fully-transparent triangle (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:626-645 push_hidden_primitive, used by empty_mesh() at :754-767 and by rebuild_mesh's empty branch at :616-618), with regression test mesh_is_never_zero_length at :866-882. The error text matches bevy_render 0.19.0 slab_allocator.rs:937 verbatim.

Correction to the DESCRIPTION: this is not a Bevy 0.18 issue. bevy_render 0.18.1 ships no slab_allocator module at all and contains no 'Use-after-free'/'unallocated key' string; the module is new in 0.19, and the tree was already on 0.19 (e67662b, 2026-07-14; Cargo.toml:95) when the bead was filed on 2026-07-19. The 'mesh-allocator interaction with zone mesh despawn/respawn on zone-in' suspicion was also off — the source was zero-live-particle generators rebuilding an empty mesh every frame.

REMAINING (unchanged, runtime-only, cannot be settled statically): re-check on an unlocked console that zone geometry stays lit across repeated zone-ins. If black-out recurs with 0 slab lines, file it as a separate bug; this bead should then close as the empty-mesh fix it became.

title: Dynamic-lighting settings incompatible with retail: heuristic emitters double-light Generator zones; knobs scale the faithful path
description: Two point-light systems run at once: zone_point_lights.rs (faithful DAT Generator lights) and zone_lights.rs (heuristic overbright-vertex emitters tuned by LightThreshold/Intensity/Range). The knobs also scale the faithful path (light_reach_scale on ZONE_LIGHT_REACH_SCALE, zone_point_lights.rs:133,379), so retail-faithful lighting can be silently distorted, and Generator zones get double-lit. Fix: DynamicLights becomes Off|Vanilla|Enhanced (serde aliases Few/Many->Vanilla). Vanilla (default): Generator lights only, DAT-driven consts, no user scaling. title: Home Point crystal (and glowing lamp fixtures) render as dark slabs: skinned-actor path drops mesh render state; model-embedded particle generators never auto-run
description: Retail (2026-07-19 capture): Home Point crystal is a glowing translucent blue crystal with an animated electric aura; our client renders a dark flat slab (Upper Jeuno HomePoint#2). Diagnosis (file:line): (1) The crystal is a skinned NPC actor (npc_list.sql:292 look modelid 51 -> DAT 1351 via look_resolver.rs:14-25). ffxi-dat DOES parse per-mesh RenderProperties (display_type_flag, t_factor - skel_mesh.rs:10-24,433-455) but build_actor_children discards them (ffxi_actor_render.rs:924-953) and FfxiSkinnedMaterial hardcodes AlphaMode::Mask(0.271) (skinned_ffxi_material.rs:285-286); skinned_ffxi.wgsl has no additive/translucent/emissive branch. XIM builds a per-mesh RenderState with additive blend + depth-write-off for blended meshes (SkeletonMeshSection.kt:35,210-217,364-384; GLDrawer.kt:198-201) - our zone/MMB path honors this, the skinned path does not. title: Honor DAT indoors flag: static indoor diffuse, no sun/cascade shadows, MH weather load, lamps lit + flicker
description: Retail reference (2026-07-19 recordings): MH + indoor zones are point-light dominant, warm, no sun through walls, lamps flicker. Root causes found: (1) load_zone_weather early-returns when snapshot.myroom.is_some(), so Mog House DAT 356 weather records (indoors=true, black sun diffuse, dark warm ambient) never load -> synthetic full-daylight sun + cascade shadows inside MH. (2) WeatherRecord.indoors is parsed (ffxi-dat weather.rs:78) and copied into ZoneDirectionalLighting (sun_moon.rs:672) but never consumed: sun/moon arc + cascade shadows stay on indoors. XIM EnvironmentSection.kt:139-149: indoors uses a single static DiffuseLight (direction from signed moonLightColor bytes /128, negated; color = sun diffuse) + zone ambient, no sun/moon. (3) zone point lights are gated by lamp_night_factor even indoors (zone_point_lights.rs:85,317) so indoor lamps are dark by day; and no flicker exists (retail lamps/braziers visibly flicker).
notes: Implemented: (1) ffxi-dat weather.rs parses indoor_light_dir_entity/landscape from signed moonLightColor bytes (XIM EnvironmentSection.kt:251-256) + indoor_light_direction() helper + tests. (2) load_zone_weather no longer skips myroom -> MH DAT 356 records (indoors=1, black sun, warm dark ambient) now load. (3) sun_moon_system: indoors -> single static diffuse on the sun DirectionalLight (entity block color, indoor dir, shadow_maps_enabled=false), moon off, ZoneDirectionalLighting publishes static indoor dirs for zone+actor materials ungated by sun/moon altitude. (4) zone_point_lights: lamp_lit_factor (indoors OR black daytime sun diffuse -> lamps always lit; Upper Jeuno retail capture 08:14) + lamp_flicker two-sine (gated by GraphicsSettings.light_flicker). (5) weather_fx apply_weather_to_sun_system no longer compounds sun.illuminance *= mul across frames (sun_moon's write-cache made the in-place multiply decay the sun exponentially under any weather with mul != 1) - tracks pre-multiplied base in a Local.
close_reason: Implemented + runtime-verified: MH now loads DAT 356 weather (indoors=1) -> warm dark interior, no sun/cascade shadows (artifacts/verify/moghouse.png); lamp flicker numeric 76->98->77 across 0.5s frames; Upper Jeuno dark with no sun patches (jeuno-day.png); lamps-lit gate covers indoors + black-daytime-sun zones; weather sun-multiplier compounding fixed

title: Headless CharSelection::Id sends empty charname in 0x07 view select — LSB rejects ('mismatched character name'), agent_session test cannot pass
description: ffxi-client/src/session.rs:183 lobby.handshake(&auth_session, *cid, "", 0, key3) sends an empty charname for the CharSelection::Id path. Current LSB validates SELECT accid FROM chars WHERE charid=? AND charname=? (vendor/server/src/login/view_session.cpp:72) and closes the socket, logging 'tried to select a character id with a mismatched character name'. Only ffxi-mcp hits this path (it prefers FFXI_CHAR_ID over FFXI_CHAR, ffxi-mcp/src/main.rs:1029, and enters session::run with initial_state None); play/GUI do a named pre-select and dodge it. close_reason: Behaviour fixed in 3861258; made unrepresentable in 2417899. LobbyClient::handshake no longer accepts a name at all — select_by_id resolves it from the account's own chr_info2 slots, so no caller can put a name on the wire that LSB rejects (view_session.cpp:62-75 WHERE charid=? AND charname=?). Pinned by a loopback fixture asserting the name bytes leaving the client for the (char_id, "") input session.rs used to pass; the pre-3861258 form fails it. View-select and chr_info2 field offsets are now named after the LSB reader that consumes them.

title: FFXI client: top menu bar + item tooltip behavior during menuing (retail reference)

ITEM TOOLTIP / DESCRIPTION WINDOW (bottom-left):

title: ui_kit Phase 0: retail window frame is a 10-part additive Msb menu shape in ROM/0/14..21, not a nine-slice off the icon sheet
description:
SPIKE RESOLVED (retail reversing, 2026-07-31). The spike's premise was wrong on two counts, and the answer rules out the planned implementation.

WHERE THE ART IS
The window frame is a 10-part "menu shape" (Msb, `ResourceType::Msb == 49`) named `menu    win00`. It lives in the eight **window-style** DATs `ROM/0/14.DAT` .. `ROM/0/21.DAT` — style s selects file id `14 + s`.

It is **not** in the `menu frames` icon sheet: `ROM/119/51.DAT` holds `menu    framesus`, 208 groups over nodes with no `corner` / `vfr1` texture; and `ROM/0/13.DAT`'s only Msb is `menu    magicon`.

WHY A BEVY NINE-SLICE CANNOT DO IT
Parts pull from three separate textures (`newtex` 128^2, and `corner` / `hfr1` / `vfr1` at 32^2). Borders **tile** under WRAP addressing. Parts 1-8 composite **additively** (SRCALPHA/ONE) over an alpha-blended background quad. A single `NodeImageMode::Sliced` reproduces none of that.

GEOMETRY CONSTANTS (retail)
cornerSize 24, borderThickness 5, side borders drawn only when `m_h > 0x30`, corners drawn last.

EVIDENCE
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/BorderedFrame.cpp:5-8, 22-86 — part order, source rects, the 24/5/48 constants, the `m_h > 0x30` gate, borders using an empty BlendFactorPacked (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/include/UI/MenuShapeFormat.h:24-45 — 61-byte packed `QuadData`; `SourceBlendFactor` at **+42** (tier 2)
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/UIManager.cpp:944-955 — `GetMenuShapeByIndex(style + 14)`; :985-991 — COLOROP/ALPHAOP = MODULATE2X (tier 2)
- TIER 1: all eight of ROM/0/14.DAT..21.DAT re-parsed independently — 10 groups, identical src rects, blend triples (0,1,1) background / (0,2,1) borders.

SPLIT THIS OUT FIRST (small, independent correctness fix)
ffxi-dat/src/ui_element.rs currently labels the byte at +42 `UNK7`. It is `SourceBlendFactor`. That mislabel is tier-6-derived and is live today, affecting 163 of 2,433 quads in the icon sheet. Land the rename (plus parsing +41/+43/+44, and deleting the bogus `draw_enabled`) as its own commit before the frame work.
design:
- ffxi-dat/src/ui_element.rs: rename UNK7@+42 -> source_blend_factor; parse +41/+43/+44; remove draw_enabled.
- New menu-shape / window-frame accessor in ffxi-dat/src/.
- kuluu-render/src/ui_element_atlas.rs:18-23 — win0 style DAT path + cache keyed by style id.
- New kuluu-render/src/hud/frame.rs implementing the 10-part composite (additive parts over an alpha-blended bg), not NodeImageMode::Sliced.
- MEMORY dat-root-resources-dual-wiring: insert the DatRoot in BOTH kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs:399 AND kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/settings.rs:386, or it silently no-ops on the play path.
notes: 2026-07-31: the +42 SourceBlendFactor split-out landed in 1bc4bbf (also +41/+43/+44, draw_enabled removed). Parse-only - repo-wide grep confirms ZERO runtime consumers of source_blend_factor/dest_blend_factor/blend_operation outside ui_element.rs itself. The 10-part additive win0 frame work is still the open body of this bead.

title: Moogle Mog Menu (0x02E OPENMOGMENU) + job change (0x100 MYROOM_JOB main/support)
description:
Retail: triggering the resident Moogle (or a Nomad Moogle in towns) opens the Mog House menu, whose Job Change entry lets you set main + support job. Kuluu has zero job-change support of any kind — this is the single biggest missing vanilla mechanic in the Mog House cluster.

LSB (authoritative):
- Moogle onTrigger -> xi.moghouse.moogleTrigger: prints Mog Locker expiry, then player:sendMenu(xi.menuType.MOOGLE) — the ONLY action (vendor/server/scripts/globals/moghouse.lua:366-380; thin NPC wrapper e.g. scripts/zones/Southern_San_dOria/npcs/Moogle.lua:8-22).
- sendMenu(MOOGLE=1) pushes s2c 0x02E GP_SERV_COMMAND_OPENMOGMENU (src/map/lua/lua_baseentity.cpp:2570-2584; header-only packet src/map/packets/s2c/0x02e_openmogmenu.h). Everything the menu offers is then driven by dedicated c2s packets, NOT moogle events.
- Job change is c2s 0x100 GP_CLI_COMMAND_MYROOM_JOB {MainJobIndex, SupportJobIndex} (src/map/packets/c2s/0x100_myroom_job.h:27-31), validated to require being in the MH or a MISC_MOGMENU zone (0x100_myroom_job.cpp:48; MISC_MOGMENU=0x0020 src/map/zone.h:483).
- Nomad-moogle availability is advertised in 0x00A MogZoneFlag = CanUseMisc(MISC_MOGMENU) (src/map/packets/s2c/0x00a_login.cpp:212) — that byte is the "Mog Menu allowed here" flag, not an in-house flag.
- Moogle visibility is a per-player conditional NPC: name "Moogle", shown when inMogHouse && !on2F (src/map/zone_entities.cpp:1206-1210).

XIM (client-side reference): routes any NPC named Moogle to ChangeJobInteraction — opens the native job menus (menu jobchang / jobcselu) and plays the moogle's job0 animation routine (research/xim src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/game/configuration/assetviewer/ChangeJobInteraction.kt:15-45).

Current state (grounded 2026-07-09): nothing. No 0x02E decode, no Mog Menu UI, no AgentCommand or 0x100 encode, no slash command (sweep found only unrelated 0x1000 equip-model and 0x110 fishing hits). The event VM handles generic NPC menus (session.rs:2045-2113; event_dialog.rs:92-142) but the Mog Menu is a dedicated packet-opened menu, not event bytecode, so it needs its own UI surface.

Scope: decode 0x02E and open a Mog Menu; Job Change flow (job list from char state, main+support selection, AgentCommand + 0x100 encode, state refresh on the server's follow-up packets); honor 0x00A MogZoneFlag for nomad moogles; storage/locker entries can defer to kuluu-6a0. Optional /jobchange slash command for the agent path.
notes: Research (2026-07-10): 0x02E is header-only (presence = open menu), pushed by sendMenu(MOOGLE=1) from moogleTrigger — no event bytecode, intercept in recv loop beside the 0x032 intercept. Job menu data source is s2c 0x01B JOB_INFO (undecoded before this work): unlocked u32@0x08 (bit 0 = subjob-feature flag, not a job), job_lev2 [u8;24]@0x44 (NOT legacy i8 @0x0C), mjob@0x04 sjob@0x07. c2s 0x100: buf[4]=main buf[5]=sub, 0=keep-current (no way to unset sub); validation failures are silent server drops — never update job state optimistically; refresh rides the follow-up burst 0x01B/0x037/0x061/0x062/0x119/0x0AC/0x063/0x067/0x0DF (equipment strip included). CliStatus 0x061 mjob/mjob_lv/sjob/sjob_lv at body 8/9/10/11 were previously skipped.
close_reason: Mog Menu (0x02E intercept) + job change (0x01B JOB_INFO decode, c2s 0x100 main/support, no optimistic update) landed; real Moogle NPC now spawns via SendResRdy (7dac9be)

title: Mog House entry: residence-door 0x05E (zmr/zms) trigger + 0x00A MYROOM decode + interior rendering
description:
Retail: walking into a Residence door sends the same 0x05E maprect used for zone lines, with a zmr*/zms* RectID fourcc. The server keeps you in the SAME town zone (no zone change), isolates you per-player, and the 0x00A zone-in tells the client to draw the room interior instead of the town.

LSB (authoritative):
- Entry detected by fourcc prefix: vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x05e_maprect.cpp:74-75 ("zmr" classic cities, "zms" WoTG/Adoulin); sets m_moghouseID=char id and destination=current zone (:234-242). MH is NOT a separate zone/instance — isolation is m_moghouseID equality (src/map/entities/charentity.h:540; src/map/zone_entities.cpp:172-175, 1022-1073); resident Moogle is a per-viewer conditional NPC (zone_entities.cpp:1162-1218).
- Client is told to render the room purely via 0x00A: LoginState=SAVE_LOGIN_STATE_MYROOM + MyroomMapNumber=GetMogHouseModelID (src/map/packets/s2c/0x00a_login.cpp:195-206, model table :35-72; struct fields 0x00a_login.h:115-127 incl. MyRoomExitBit :126 and MyroomSubMapNumber :122 for 2F).
- Zone-in lua forces pos (0,0,0,192), strips effects, may fire the 2F-unlock cutscene: scripts/globals/moghouse.lua:281-332.

XIM (client-side reference): entry is a walk-into zone line special-cased by DAT id — MogHouseConfig maps each city to entry ids + room-model file indices (research/xim src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/tools/ZoneChanger.kt:18-28, matcher :182-184); room model picked by rentalIndex / 2F fileIndex (xim/resource/table/ZoneTables.kt:14-20); zone name "Mog House 1F/2F" (ZoneTables.kt:74-77); music forced to 126 (ZoneSettingsTable.kt:42-44); town NPCs suppressed (NpcTable.kt:197-200); zmr_/zms_ ids special-cased in DAT id parsing (DatResource.kt:243-261).

Current state (grounded 2026-07-09):
- No entry path: residence-door rects are absent from the scraped LSB zoneline table (ffxi-nav/src/zonelines.rs:16-26 — they live in zone DATs, not LSB SQL), so the reactor proximity trigger (ffxi-client/src/reactor.rs:651-695) can never fire for a Residence door; no UI/interaction targets one either.
- Exit direction already works: /mhexit -> AgentCommand::MogHouseExit -> 0x05E "zmrq" (session.rs:1759-1804, builder :3501-3521).
- in_mog_house is decoded only from party packets (moghouse_flg: ffxi-proto/src/decode.rs:952,984,1007) and drives only MH BGM slot 6 (ffxi-viewer-core/src/audio.rs:170,243-246) + a chat notice (session.rs:3432-3456). The 0x00A MYROOM fields (LoginState/MyroomMapNumber/MyRoomExitBit/MyroomSubMapNumber) are NOT decoded, and nothing ever loads an MH room model — zone geometry is always the town MZB.

Scope: parse residence entry rects from the zone DAT interaction section (zmr*/zms* ids) and send 0x05E on walk-in; decode the 0x00A MYROOM fields; load and render the per-city MH interior model (1F + 2F variants) instead of town geometry; zone-name banner; keep the existing BGM behavior.
notes: Research correction (2026-07-10 session): residence-door rects are NOT absent — all 21 zmr*/zms* lines are in vendor/server/sql/zonelines.sql as same-zone rows and already scraped into ffxi-nav ZONE_LINES; the reactor trigger already fires them. MH entry IS a full same-zone 0x00B/0x00A reconnect handshake. Real gaps: (1) 0x00A MYROOM decode — LoginState u32@0x7C, MyroomSubMapNumber u8@0xA4, MyroomMapNumber u16@0xA6 (MODEL id, 0x01FF sentinel), MyRoomExitBit u8@0xAA, MogZoneFlag u8@0xAB; (2) apply_zoneline_spawn_fallback would clobber the legitimate (0,0,0,192) MH spawn — must be suppressed when LoginState==MYROOM (both call sites); (3) model→DAT-file table (16 XIM-verified pairs, e.g. 256→356 Jeuno, 615-618→8380x 2F; Feretory 729 excluded/unverified); (4) renderer re-key on resolved file id, not zone_id (zone_id unchanged in MH; transient zone_id=None is watch-coalescible); (5) reactor zonelines must go inert inside MH (town OBBs vs near-origin coords misfire); (6) scraped trigger box is paper-thin (1.0x4.0) vs faithful DAT RID OBB (12x8x2) — RID chunk kind 0x36 parser layout verified on retail DATs.
close_reason: MH entry landed: 0x05E zmr/zms trigger, 0x00A MYROOM decode, interior DAT render via effective_zone_dat_file_id, XIM door offsets; live-test fixes in 7dac9be (navmesh off in MH, camera min distance, SendResRdy Moogle spawn)

TIER CAVEAT: that the retail *client* gates confirm on the DAT flag byte @0x02 has **no tier-2 support** —
`grep -rni 'buffcancel|BuffNo|0x00F1' research/XIClient/src` returns zero hits and KaMenuBuff overrides no
confirm handler. Support is circumstantial: the byte correlates with the canonical cancelable set (tier 1),
and vendor/server/.../status_effect.h:69 comments "CAN NOT CLICK IT OFF IN CLIENT". The **data layer is
CONFIRMED at tier 1** and is a real delta — ship it, but do not describe the mechanism as verified.

title: Chat input: persistent send-channel rotation + missing channels (Linkshell 2, Yell, Unity, Assist)
description:
Retail rotates the chat input's persistent send channel with one key; the chosen channel persists across messages until rotated again.

Retail's chat-mode SET is confirmed at tier 2 by XIClient's chatModeTable (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/Windows/InGame/CTkSubWindow.cpp:18-36): say=1, shout=2, yell=3, tell=4, party=5, linkshell=6, linkshell2=7, unity=8, with retail aliases /s /sh /yl /t /p /l /l2 /u. The rotation ORDER and the F-key/Y-pad binding are still sourced only to "FFXI User Interface Guide Pt1 - Vanilla Interface" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rL2lL_dnIBQ&t=159 (2:39-3:10) — confirm against retail before pinning either; XIClient's table carries no assist entry and no key binding, and the draft order in the original description omitted yell. NOTE the key collision: F is already Action::SelectActiveWindow in Kuluu's keyboard preset (kuluu-render/src/keybinds/presets.rs:71), so the binding needs a decision, not just a lookup.

Current state (regrounded 2026-07-31):
- Channel rotation exists ONLY inside the target-action context menu Chat entry: kuluu-render/src/hud/action_model.rs:167 (modes = Say/Tell/Party/Linkshell/Unity/Shout, mode_idx at :168), rotated on NavRight at kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:841-847.
- chat_buffer_for_mode (text_input.rs:1225-1239) wires only Tell / /p / /l / /sh; Unity is mode_idx 4 and falls through to `_ => ChatBuffer::empty()` at :1237.
- Plain chat open is an empty buffer with NO persistent send channel: Action::OpenChat at text_input.rs:716-717, Action::OpenChatCommand at view_native/input.rs:314-315.
- Slash commands cover only /s /p /sh /l /t: view_native/slash_commands.rs:483-512. No /yell (/yl), /l2, /unity (/u) exist; the /assist at slash_commands.rs:213 is the ActionKind::Assist targeting command, not the assist chat channel. Those handlers also pass bare kind literals (0/4/1/5) instead of ffxi_proto::map::chat_kind consts — fold that cleanup in (only /em at :528 uses chat_kind::EMOTION).
- CORRECTION to the earlier draft: proto chat kinds are HAND-WRITTEN, not scraped — ffxi-proto/build.rs has no reference to chat_message_type. ffxi-proto/src/map.rs:317-334 has YELL = 26 (:330) and LINKSHELL2 = 27 (:331), matching LSB (vendor/server/src/map/enums/chat_message_type.h:51-52). The NS_* constants are NOT assist channels: LSB documents NS = "No speaker object displayed, otherwise same as MESSAGE_*" (chat_message_type.h:38-41, :53). The kinds this bead needs are MISSING from ffxi-proto and must be added: MESSAGE_UNITY = 33, MESSAGE_JP_ASSIST = 34, MESSAGE_NA_ASSIST = 35 (chat_message_type.h:58-60).

title: Retail chat log: two independent windows (per-channel routing, H/V split, per-window lines/width, timestamps, window style)
description:
Retail vanilla FFXI has TWO independent chat log windows. Config > Windows chooses horizontal or vertical split, timestamps (off / 12h / military), and window style; per-window settings control max lines, width, and resize speed; Config > Log routes each message category to window 1 or window 2 (typical retail setup: chat/social channels left, battle log right).

Source: "FFXI User Interface Guide Pt1 - Vanilla Interface" (Sakura Destros) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rL2lL_dnIBQ — chapters: The Chat Bar (t=84), Windows split (t=2351), window sizing (t=2403), Log routing (t=2447).

Retail behavior (video):
- Two windows, user-routable per channel category (window 1 vs window 2 checkbox lists at t=2447).
- Split horizontally or vertically; timestamps optional (military or 12h); window style selectable (t=2351).
- Per-window: line count (e.g. keep 5 visible lines so chat is never fully hidden), width, resize speed (t=2403).

Current state (grounded 2026-07-05):
- kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs:58-63 — ONE chat window with 3 hardcoded tabs (Social/Battle/Debug), shown one at a time.
- kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs:125-136 — routing hardcoded via ChatKind::accepts, not user-configurable.
- kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs:11-16 — fixed VISIBLE_ROWS=12; height animates 60-220px via idle fade, not configurable.
- No timestamps anywhere (grep clean); no split; no window-style options.
- Wire channel vocabulary already exists: kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:235-248 (Say/Shout/Tell/Party/Linkshell/Yell/System/Other/Battle/Debug).
notes:
--- 2026-07-31 retail reversing ---
Retail's chat-log auto-size is a PER-LINE decay, not a panel fade. An accumulator moves by +/- LineVisibleTime;
VisibleLineCount = timer / LineVisibleTime, clamped to 4..24. See
research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/Windows/InGame/CTkDrawMessageWindow.cpp:30-34, 176-195, 341-370, 799-839
(tier 2). Ours fades the WHOLE PANEL 60->220px over 10s (kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs:11-23), which
is a different mechanic with a different feel. Fold the per-line model into this bead's scope.

title: Actor model DAT loads run synchronously on the render main thread: 110-160ms frame freeze per newly-visible NPC/PC
description: Repro: drive the character around Port Bastok (agent socket patrol, run11 /tmp/ffxi-perf-run11.log 03:02:49-03:07:11Z). Every few seconds a frame spikes 110-160ms with cpu~130ms, model+1, churn img+~7 (~1.8MB) mesh+~40 — process_load_actor_requests (ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:1475) calls load_npc/load_pc (full DAT read+parse+DXT decode) inline in an Update system. fps drops to 37-55 while moving. Fix: kick/poll AsyncComputeTaskPool pattern already used by dat_mzb.rs (kick_load_mzb_tasks/poll_load_mzb_tasks) and char_preview.rs:208. Secondary observations from same run (not this bead): constant skin+~1000-1600/s FfxiSkinnedMaterial churn bursts and std+~120/s StandardMaterial churn keep baseline elevated (see kuluu-zh5); one unexplained 116ms spike with zero churn/model at 03:03:43Z.
close_reason: Fixed & verified via agent-socket patrol A/B runs. (1) load_npc/load_pc moved to AsyncComputeTaskPool (kick_load_actor_tasks/poll_load_actor_tasks, mirrors dat_mzb pattern); (2) clip/scheduler parse moved into loader (derive_animation_sets, Arc-shared); (3) mesh build + mip gen + bind pose moved into task (prepare_actor_parts); (4) subject+quality-keyed LRU cache (48) of Arc<PreparedActor> so radius-flapping NPCs respawn cheap; (5) spawns capped at 2/frame. Drive-window comparison (240s Port Bastok patrol): sync run11 19 spikes >=100ms (max 290ms) fps min 37 -> run16 zero actor-attributable spikes >=50ms, median 5s-max frame 147ms->21.7ms, fps ~60. Residual non-actor classes tracked in kuluu-zh5.

title: Default xiloader version (2.0.0) rejected by current LSB testing image (needs 2.1.x); breaks agent_session test + provision
description: LSB landsandboat/server:testing now enforces xiloader >= 2.1.x; our default version string reports 2.0.0, so LOGIN_CREATE fails ('Your xiloader is too old') unless --xiloader-version 2.1.0 is passed. This makes agent_session_drives_mcp_end_to_end fail whenever the login server is reachable (it no longer self-skips into a pass), and breaks provision/create-char defaults. Fix: bump the default (or scrape the accepted version from vendor/server at build time per the vendor-scrape convention) and keep the CLI override.
notes: Second env failure mode found 2026-07-12 (behind the xiloader gate): with FFXI_XILOADER_VERSION=2.1.0 the fixture then fails 'accid mismatch: requested 12339320 but got accid=17276929' — the dev DB accounts AUTO_INCREMENT (~17.2M) has outrun the fixture's 1M-range sentinel scheme. Fix should bump the version pin AND make the fixture tolerate high AUTO_INCREMENT (or self-skip on version mismatch instead of failing).
close_reason: Default xiloader version now scraped at build time from vendor/server/src/login/auth_session.h (SupportedXiloaderVersion, currently 2.1.0) via ffxi-proto build.rs -> ffxi_proto::login::SUPPORTED_XILOADER_VERSION; auth_client default uses it (CLI --xiloader-version and FFXI_XILOADER_VERSION overrides unchanged, now unit-tested via pure resolve_client_version_from). Second sub-item: EphemeralChar fixture no longer hard-fails on accid mismatch when accounts AUTO_INCREMENT outran the 1M sentinel range; it warns and proceeds with the server-assigned accid. Verified: 5 new unit tests pass (cargo test -p ffxi-client auth_client --features native-window), scripts/checks.sh fmt clippy green. Live end-to-end against the LSB testing image pending a reachable server.

title: Third periodic render hitch: ~80ms every ~0.9s in uninstrumented render residual
description: Live perf logs show a ~80ms-over-16.6ms spike at steady ~0.9s cadence. Rules out snapshot clone (rebuild 10-22us) and camera-collision brute-force (probe 0us). All instrumented buckets ~0; cost is in perf_hud residual render_us = frame_period - cpu_us (cpu only brackets First->PostUpdate). vsync ruled out; no periodic pipeline-specialization logs. Remaining candidates: late-PostUpdate/Last main-thread system, render extract/prepare/queue, RenderDiagnosticsPlugin GPU-timestamp readback. Step 1: add a Last-schedule mark to split main-thread-late vs render-thread/present.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (pending visual confirm). The ~60ms-every-~0.9s hitch was update_zone_material_lighting (ffxi_zone_material.rs): LIGHTING_EPSILON=1.5e-3 change gate vs Vana sun angular rate 2pi/3456s=1.8e-3/s -> epsilon crossed every ~0.85s -> Assets::iter_mut() over ALL ~673 per-submesh FfxiZoneMaterials -> every one flagged Modified -> render prep rebuilt 673 uniform buffers+bind groups in one frame (~45ms rprep + ~14ms rgraph). Proven live via new perf instrumentation: rprep/rgraph/rtotal render-app fences + AssetChurn per-type Modified counters (spike lines showed churn zone+673 exactly on each spike). FIX: adopted the skinned-material persistent-buffer pattern — zone lighting now lives in ONE shared GPU buffer (ZoneMaterialBuffers.lighting) written via write_buffer in ExtractSchedule from new ZoneGlobalLighting resource; FfxiZoneMaterial got manual AsBindGroup (same WGSL bindings, shaders untouched) with per-instance persistent flags/tint/uv buffers; cloud tint/uv anim switched to get_mut_untracked; star dome StandardMaterial write gated to 1/255 steps. AFTER: steady 60.0fps, churn zone+0, max rprep 3-4ms (was 45ms). Remaining separate blip: ~28ms exactly every 10.00s, cpu-heavy, correlates with periodic img+1MB (512x512 minimap?) — follow-up bead.
close_reason: User confirmed: rhythmic ~0.9s stutter gone after shared-lighting-buffer fix (commit 'fix(render): ~60ms hitch every ~0.9s'). Residuals tracked: kuluu-zh5 (10s blip), kuluu-p09 (snapshot clone).

title: Self character model doesn't update on equipment change (ensure_self_lookcomp clobbers server look)
description:
User: character model should update when equipment changes; does it support other players?

Findings: the look->model pipeline (LookComp Changed -> dispatch_look_driven_models -> respawn skinned mesh) already routes EVERY entity's look. Other PCs update on gear change because the server broadcasts their CHAR_PC (0x0D) look and sync_entity_looks_system applies it to LookComp. The SELF player did NOT update because ensure_self_lookcomp_system runs after sync_entity_looks_system and every frame forces the self LookComp back to the launcher-time SelfAppearance (never updated post-launcher), clobbering the server-driven look. session.rs:670-736 already decodes+upserts the self look (incl. on equip). 

Fix: ensure_self_lookcomp_system now SEEDS the self look only when absent (before the server CHAR_PC for self arrives); once present, the server-driven sync owns it. Strictly better: identical when server look is None (falls back to launcher look), correct when present (gear changes re-render). NEEDS visual verification in GUI (can't run headless).
close_reason: Self equipment changes update LookComp via sync_entity_looks_system; self merged into tracked entities at zone-in

title: Equipment screen polish: icon alpha, cell layout, races off-by-one, MON->MNK job code
description:
Follow-up fixes after item DAT lookups landed (kuluu-2he), from user testing:
1. Item icons rendered opaque black background: icons are 8bpp flag-0x91 bitmaps whose palette carries FFXI half-range alpha (index 0 = A0 transparent bg, art = A128). parse_graphic forced 0xFF for 0x91. Added map_image::parse_graphic_icon (PaletteAlpha::HalfScaled) used by item_dat::decode_icon; general bitmaps unchanged.
2. Grid icon offset + label overlapping icon: cell laid icon+label side-by-side (row flex) and label was always shown. CellLabel now hidden when the slot has an item, so the icon centers alone.
3. Races off-by-one: item DAT races field is 1-indexed by race id (Mithra=bit7 0x0080, Galka=bit8 0x0100, all=0x01FE). Table was 0-indexed so Mithran Gaiters read 'Galka'. Fixed + verified vs retail DATs.
4. 'MON6' -> 'MNK6': status_panel::job_abbrev truncated the full name ('Monk'->'MON'). Scrape canonical 3-letter codes from LSB job_name.lua first element into ffxi_proto::job_names::abbrev (JOB_ABBREVS table); status_panel + item_detail::format_jobs now use it (unified, dropped hardcoded table).
Tests: job abbrev canonical, races 1-indexed, icon alpha verified vs real DATs. fmt+clippy clean.
close_reason: Fixed and verified vs retail DATs: icon alpha (transparent bg), grid cell layout (label hides when item present, icon centers), races 1-indexed (Mithran Gaiters -> Mithra), canonical job codes (MNK not MON) scraped from LSB.

title: Launcher graphics settings menu: compact rows + responsive scroll so it fits any window size
description: The graphics settings menu (ffxi-client/src/view_native/launcher_ui/graphics.rs) renders ~22 fixed-height rows in a non-scrolling panel; on smaller windows the list overflows and is clipped at top and bottom (screenshot). Rows are tall because labels wrap to 2 lines at the 160px label width with the theme default font. Fix: (1) explicit compact row font + no-wrap label sizing + tighter gaps/widths; (2) cap the panel at a fraction of viewport height and move the settings list into a scroll_y region (ScrollPosition + mouse-wheel system) so the title/hint/footer stay pinned and the list scrolls at any window size.
notes: Follow-up: added a visible scrollbar. Wrapped the list + a 6px scrollbar track in a horizontal Row (align stretch). Uses bevy_ui_widgets Scrollbar{target=list, Vertical, min_thumb 28} + CoreScrollbarThumb (ScrollbarPlugin already active via feathers UiWidgetsPlugins) — plugin sizes/positions the thumb from the list's ScrollPosition and makes it drag-scrollable. Rounded track (subtle) + lighter thumb; new GraphicsScrollbar marker + update_scrollbar_visibility system hides the track (Display::None) when content fits so a full-height thumb never implies scroll on a non-scrolling list. BorderRadius is a Node field in Bevy 0.18 (not a standalone component). Build + clippy clean.
close_reason: Graphics settings menu made compact + responsive: smaller row font, no-wrap labels, viewport-capped panel with a scrollable settings list (pinned title/footer). Builds + clippy clean.

title: Resolve {Choice:N}[a/b] dialog alternatives instead of leaking the raw marker
description: dmsg decodes control code 0x0C to a {Choice:N} marker and passes the following literal [opt0/opt1] bracket through; clean_display leaves the marker unresolved, so NPC speech renders 'Good luck, {Choice:0}[citizen/comrade].' instead of 'Good luck, citizen.'. Resolve {Choice:N}[a/b/..] to a single alternative in the render layer. Message parameter array isn't wired from the VM yet, so default the selector to alternative 0 (correct for the common single-param case).

title: Item DAT lookups: correct per-type ROM files + O(1) id-base indexing; fix unequip showing Gil
description:
Follow-up to kuluu-051. Item icons/details never rendered because ITEM_DAT_FILE_ID (0x0DA9-0x0DAC) resolved to tiny wrong DATs and the loader indexed by raw item_id*stride. Reworked to the real model (verified vs XIM InventoryItemParser + empirically against retail DATs):
- Item DATs are per-type, id-ranged, gap-free 0xC00-block files: ROM/118/106-109.DAT (item/usable/weapon/armor), ROM/174/48.DAT (currency), ROM/286/73.DAT + ROM/301/115.DAT (expansions). block index = item_id - base_id (base = block 0's id). New ffxi_dat::item_dat::ItemTable (open/lookup/icon), O(1), on-demand 3KB block reads.
- Client item DAT jobs field is 0-INDEXED (bit==job; White Belt=0x04=MNK), unlike LSB item_equipment.jobs (1-indexed). Fixed item_detail::format_jobs to consume DAT-native 0-indexed.
- Gil bug: unequip showed 'Gil' because the server reports an empty equip slot as inventory index 0 (charutils.cpp:2268), which resolve_equipment joined to Gil. EquipUpdated now clears the slot when container_index==0.
Tests: ItemTable verified against real DATs (White Belt/Bronze Dagger/Breastplate/Gil all resolve name+icon+desc); equip_updated_index_zero_clears_slot; format_jobs 0-indexed. fmt+clippy clean.
close_reason: Implemented and verified against real retail DATs + XIM reference. Icons/details/descriptions resolve; unequip no longer shows Gil.

title: Head-look (facetarget) not sent or applied: bidirectional gap vs LSB
description:
FFXI head-turn-to-look is driven by the entity 'facetarget' field (the targid a char has selected), relayed by the server in both directions. We handle neither.

OUTBOUND (retail can't see our head): build_subpacket_pos (ffxi-client/src/session.rs:3354) builds the 0x015 client position packet but never writes facetarget. LSB GP_CLI_COMMAND_POS (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x015_pos.h) places uint16 facetarget at body offset +22 (after dir@+20 and the TargetMode/RunMode/GroundMode bitfield@+21). We leave buf[22..24]=0, so the server broadcasts facetarget=0 for us and retail clients never turn our head. Fix: thread the player's current target targid (act_index) into build_subpacket_pos and write it at +22.

INBOUND (we don't turn other players' heads): PosHead decodes flags0 (ffxi-proto/src/decode.rs:113) but never extracts facetarget = (flags0>>17)&0x7FFF. Both 0x0D (char_update.cpp:271 Flags0.facetarget=m_TargID) and 0x0E (entity_update.cpp:321 ref<uint16>(0x1A)=m_TargID<<1) pack it into flags0 bits 17-31. The renderer (ffxi_actor_render.rs:1847) instead aims non-self head-look at bt_target_id (the combat claim UniqueNo, set only during combat, wrong id-space), so other players only head-track in combat. Fix: add PosHead::facetarget(); plumb face_target:u16 onto state Entity -> wire Entity -> snapshot; resolve it by act_index/targid in the renderer and use it as the non-self look target.
notes:
LANDED (verified), pending merge to main. Split across two places due to the shared-tree churn:
1. ffxi-proto/src/decode.rs (PosHead::facetarget() + 2 tests) is ALREADY in main HEAD (1f90540) — another session committed the whole file, sweeping in my hunk alongside their CliStatus work. Confirmed present.
2. The other 13 files are on branch 'facetarget-headlook' commit b0a7fe3 (worktree /Users/jon/src/ffxi-facetarget), based on e7af8b4.

FULL GATE PASSED in the isolated worktree (vendor symlinked, reused target cache): ffxi-proto pos_head tests (incl. facetarget) pass; ffxi-viewer-core + ffxi-client(native-window) build clean; cargo fmt --check clean; 245 ffxi-client lib tests pass; clippy clean on all 4 crates. git merge-tree shows facetarget-headlook merges into current main with no conflicts.

title: Vana'diel clock: elemental day-of-week orb sprite (menu frames 106–113)
description:
Retail draws an elemental orb sprite immediately before the clock time, indicating the Vana'diel day-of-week's element (the colored circle in the reference screenshot). We compute the weekday today but only surface it as a one-shot toast on day change — no icon is drawn. This bead renders the authentic DAT sprite (full-sprite approach chosen over a tinted-glyph placeholder).

The orb is UI element 'menu    frames  ' at index 106 + element. Depends on the menu UI-element DAT sprite loader (roadmap:hud:menu-ui-element-dat-sprite-loader) to load that group.

Day-of-week → sprite-index mapping: our VANA_WEEKDAYS is indexed in DAY order (0=Firesday); the 'menu frames' sub-index is in ELEMENT order (Fire=0,Ice=1,Wind=2,Earth=3,Lightning=4,Water=5,Light=6,Dark=7). So the per-weekday sprite offset table, indexed by (total_vana_days % 8), is [0,3,5,2,1,4,6,7] (Firesday→Fire/0, Earthsday→Earth/3, Watersday→Water/5, Windsday→Wind/2, Iceday→Ice/1, Lightningday→Lightning/4, Lightsday→Light/6, Darksday→Dark/7); final sprite index = 106 + offset.

Evidence (ours):
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:48-57 — VANA_WEEKDAYS (day order, 0=Firesday)
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:77-88 — weekday computed (total_vana_days % 8) but emitted only as a toast; no icon
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:23-46 — clock widget spawn; orb sprite node goes here, left of VanaClockLabel

- research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/UiResourceManager.kt:21-26 — the four UI DATs that contain the 'menu frames' group

DAY_TO_ELEMENT_OFFSET = [0,3,5,2,1,4,6,7]. Fallback (loader miss): hide the orb (or a neutral placeholder) rather than a wrong-element sprite. Keep the magic indices as named consts citing Compass.kt.

title: Vana'diel clock: retail HH:MM time + (col-row) map-grid position
description:
Our HUD clock renders one label as 'V {year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02} {hour:02}:{minute:02}' (e.g. 'V 0886-01-15 13:55'). Retail shows only 'HH:MM   (col-row)' — clock time then the player's map-grid cell, e.g. '13:55   (I-7)'. This bead drops the V/date prefix and adds the map-grid coordinate. (The elemental day-of-week orb that precedes the time is its own bead: roadmap:hud:vanadiel-clock-elemental-day-orb.)

Two sub-changes:
1. Time format — reformat format_vana to emit 'H:MM' (retail uses no leading-zero hour, 2-digit minute). v_hour/v_minute are already computed; this is a format-string + test change.
2. Map grid (col-row) — compute the player's lettered/numbered cell from world position + the current zone's ZoneMapRecord (size, x/y offset). We already parse that record from FFXiMain.dll and use it to calibrate the minimap; reuse it here. Player position is the IsSelf entity Transform.

Evidence (ours):
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:106-122 — format_vana currently emits 'V {year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}'
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:113-114 — v_hour/v_minute already computed; only the format! string changes
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs:128-162 — existing format_vana unit tests to update for the new format
- ffxi-dat/src/main_dll.rs:21-28,61-84 — ZoneMapRecord {size, x_offset, y_offset} parsed from FFXiMain.dll
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/retail.rs:223-237 — current calibration via MainDll::zone_map(zone_id, 0); zone_map_to_aabb at :19-29, MENUMAP_TEX=512.0 at :17
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/components.rs:12 — IsSelf marker; player world pos read pattern at ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/mod.rs:264-267 (Transform.translation.x/.z)

Evidence (retail, re-express — do NOT copy):
- research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/ui/Compass.kt:56-62 — clock string is 'H:MM   (col-row)' (no date, no V prefix)
- research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/ui/MapDrawer.kt:54-63,139-140 — grid formula (below)
- research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/resource/table/ZoneMapTable.kt — ZoneMap {size, offset} layout matching our ZoneMapRecord
design:
Map-grid formula (re-express MapDrawer.kt:54-63,139-140; 16x16 grid, columns A.., rows 1..):
  mapPos.x = 0.5 + worldPos.x / size * 512
  mapPos.y = -0.5 + (-worldPos.z) / size * 512
  mapPos.x -= x_offset ; mapPos.y -= y_offset      // zoneMap.offset * -1
  col = ('A' as u8 + floor(15 * mapPos.x / 512)) as char
  row = 1 + floor(15 * mapPos.y / 512)
Clamp col/row into [A..P]/[1..16]; render '?-?' when no ZoneMapRecord for the current zone/subzone (mirrors XIM's mostRecentMap == null). Use subzone 0 as the minimap does today. LSB/DAT-boundary: cite the XIM file and add lsb-invariant-prober tests pinning the grid math against known zone fixtures.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-30. Clock label now renders 'H:MM   (col-row)' (e.g. '13:55   (I-7)'), dropping the V/date prefix.
- format_vana -> format_vana_time (time-only, no leading-zero hour, 2-digit minute); reuses vana_minutes_since_epoch. ffxi-viewer-core/src/hud/vana_clock.rs.
- Map grid: MinimapAabb::world_to_grid (ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/mod.rs) computes the 16x16 cell via floor(15*uv); reuses the minimap's calibrated world_to_uv, which reproduces XIM MapDrawer.kt:54-63,139-140 exactly because our Bevy world flips Z vs FFXI-native (transcribing XIM's raw formula would invert the row axis).
- PlayerMapGrid resource + update_player_map_grid system in minimap/retail.rs: image-independent calibration from FFXiMain.dll ZoneMapRecord (subzone 0) on zone change; '(?-?)' when no record/player. ensure_dll dedups the DLL load.

title: Diagnose + fix periodic ~70ms GPU frame spikes (render-thread bound, shadow cascades suspected)
description: Frame spikes to ~70ms (baseline ~13ms) every 1-2s, worse with camera pitched up. perf split: cpu~2ms, render~67ms — render-thread/GPU bound, NOT the snapshot clone (kuluu-p09, since CLOSED) or the camera_collision probe (kuluu-5lc, since CLOSED; probe 0us on these). Named peak render passes are the sun's 4 shadow cascades (4096^2; max_distance on High is now 700, not the 600 this bead was written against — kuluu-render/src/graphics/settings.rs:546-550, changed by d8e7088 on 2026-06-30) but their CPU encode is <7ms, so the 67ms is unattributed GPU/render-world. Two leading hypotheses: (1) directional shadow cascade GPU cost ballooning when the frustum sweeps skyward (cascade fit), (2) on-demand wgpu pipeline specialization as new geometry/shadow-casters enter view. MEASUREMENT IS STALE (2026-06-30/07-06, pre-Bevy-0.19): re-measure before diagnosing further — 144145f (2026-07-16) stopped the per-frame celestial light/material writes that its own commit message says were re-specializing every shadow cascade view each frame, and kuluu-a7cs (P0, in progress) found 4096 shadow rendering ~6x more expensive on 0.19 (constant, not periodic). FFXI_GPU_TIMING=1 now yields real ~gpu spans (kuluu-fgs CLOSED; gate at kuluu/src/view_native/perf_hud.rs:256), then pick the lever — clamp cascade maximum_distance/count, or warm pipelines. Citation drift: the sun's shadow-emitting DirectionalLight moved from sun_moon.rs:145 to kuluu-render/src/sun_moon.rs:178-183 and the field was renamed shadows_enabled -> shadow_maps_enabled; the moon (:195-199) remains shadow_maps_enabled: false. graphics/settings.rs:1024 cascade_config_from_settings still holds the knobs.
