title: First-person self nameplate dips/jitters vertically (stutter-amplified near-camera overhead projection)
description: In first-person with camera pitched up, the self nameplate billboard visibly dips vertically, and the dips coincide with frame spikes. Root: nameplate world Y = self.y + actor_height + 0.1 sits ~0.28u directly above the camera eye (self.y + actor_height*0.92), a near-degenerate overhead projection. Camera eye is set unsmoothed and the nameplate system reads self-position at a different schedule point, so a 1-frame skew (tiny at 75fps) becomes a visible swing on a 70ms stutter frame. Fix: remove the camera/nameplate skew (shared finalized self transform, deterministic ordering) and/or don't render the self nameplate overhead (vanilla-faithful: own name isn't shown).
close_reason: Suppressed the self nameplate billboard (vanilla-faithful: retail never draws the local player's own overhead name), removing the near-degenerate overhead projection that dipped/jittered in first-person on stutter frames. scene.rs no longer spawns a plate for is_self (self char_name fallback removed with it); update_nameplate_billboards_system despawns any plate matching self_char_id via new is_self_billboard() predicate, covering plates spawned before self id was known; spawn_nameplate_billboard's is_self param + Pickable::IGNORE branch removed (dead). Verified: 4 new unit tests on is_self_billboard (known-self suppressed, others kept, None/0 self id unresolved => no suppression); cargo test -p ffxi-viewer-core all 416+ green; scripts/checks.sh fmt clippy green. Live visual confirm pending.

title: Equip filter: fits_job off-by-one hides job-restricted gear (White Belt unequippable by MNK)
description: The Equipment menu's equippable-item filter uses the wrong job-bit convention. ffxi-proto::equip_info::fits_job tests `jobs_mask & (1 << job_id)`, but LSB's item_equipment jobs bitfield is 1-indexed: a job occupies bit (job-1). Confirmed in vendor/server/src/map/utils/charutils.cpp:2313,3377 and lua_baseentity.cpp:5082 — all use `getJobs() & (1 << (PChar->GetMJob() - 1))`. Example: White Belt (item 13184) has jobs=2 (bit 1 = MNK), but a MNK (main_job=2) tests bit 2 and misses, so the Waist Equip submenu shows '(no equippable items for this slot)'. Fix fits_job to use (1 << (job_id - 1)) with a job_id==0 guard; add a regression test for White Belt + MNK.
notes: Fixed: fits_job now uses 1<<(job-1) (LSB charutils.cpp:2313). Also fixed item_detail::format_jobs same off-by-one (bit+1) + added jobs 17-22. Tests: white_belt_fits_mnk_not_war (proto), jobs_all_when_unrestricted updated. White Belt (13184, jobs=2=bit1=MNK) now equippable by MNK.
close_reason: fits_job + format_jobs off-by-one fixed; regression tests added and passing

title: PC face/hair off-by-one: resolve_face is 1-based, retail face slot is 0-based
description: resolve_face() in ffxi-viewer-core/src/look_resolver.rs computes FACE_BASE[race-1] + face - 1 (with a face==0 -> 1 special case), making every face index >= 1 render the model one slot too low. The retail face byte is a 0-based index into the per-race Face sub-table: LSB validates creation faces 0..15 ('Face 8B' = 15, vendor/server/src/login/login_helpers.cpp:240) and xim EquipmentModelTable.getItemModelPath indexes the Face slot directly (offset + itemModelId, no -1). Symptom: PC hair color+style wrong (e.g. a red non-pigtail Mithra renders as the adjacent blonde-pigtail face). Affects live look dispatch, DAT preview, launcher char preview, and model viewer (all route through resolve_face). Fix: 0-based index derived from PC_MODEL_IDS slot-0 breakpoints; drop the duplicated FACE_BASE table; tighten bound to face<32.
close_reason: Fixed resolve_face off-by-one: now 0-based direct index (file=base+face) matching XIM EquipmentModelTable + LSB face range 0..15. title: Zone water spills onto dry paths: per-height AABB union instead of actual footprint

title: Faithful fishing: network + animation (observe + /fish minigame)
description:
Re-implement FFXI fishing faithfully. Two phases per the LSB/XIM references:

PHASE 1 (observe other players): render the fsh0-fsh6 macro-state animations from the wire entity animation byte (server_status). LSB ANIMATIONTYPE 56-62 (+pre-overhaul 38-43,50) -> XIM Actor.kt fsh0..fsh6. animation byte already decoded into wire::Entity.animation and persisted across pos-only updates; renderer only consumed it for ATTACK.

PHASE 2 (/fish + minigame for our player): full client protocol state machine.
- start: action packet 0x1A id 0x0E (ActionKind::Fish exists).
- 0x037 SERVERSTATUS carries server_status(animation)+fishing_timer(hookDelay); not yet decoded.
- after hookDelay: send 0x110 mode2 RequestCheckHook.
- server: 0x115 GP_SERV_COMMAND_FISH (stamina/arrow_delay/regen/move_frequency/arrow_damage/arrow_regen/time/angler_sense/intuition) + animation FISHING_FISH; run minigame client-side.
- minigame end: 0x110 mode3 RequestEndMiniGame (para=300 fail/200 force/0 caught/else stamina; para2=special).
- resolution anim (CAUGHT/BREAK/STOP) -> after finish, 0x110 mode4 RequestRelease. mode5 RequestPotentialTimeout near timeout.

Refs: research/XiPackets/world/{client/0x0110,client/0x0066,server/0x0115,server/0x0037,server/0x000D}; vendor/server/src/map/utils/fishingutils.cpp; research/xim FishingAnimationState.kt, ActorSubStates.kt(FishingState), FishingAttemptInstance.kt, FishHppUi.kt, Actor.kt:361.
notes: Phase 1 (observe others) DONE: ffxi-proto animation fishing consts + fishing_phase(); ffxi-actor fishing_clip()+ActorAnimInputs.fishing_phase; ffxi-viewer-core drives fsh0-fsh6 pose from the wire animation byte for observed players. Phase 2 (self /fish + minigame) DONE (network+animation+state machine): 0x115 FishPacket decode, 0x037 server_status+fishing_timer decode, 0x110 build_subpacket_fishing encode, fishing.rs FishingMachine (10 tests), reactor wiring (auto-play + FishingInput), /fish + /hook + /rl + /rr + /reelstop slash cmds, self pose via wire::SceneSnapshot.self_fishing. protocol-conformance-reviewer: PASS, no wire divergences. Remaining: native HUD + keybinds (see dependent bead). All tests green; clippy clean.

title: Zone water rendered as opaque cutout + fake blue plane, not translucent textured surface (XIM parity)
description:
Zone water is not faithful. XIM (research/xim) renders water as part of the normal textured zone mesh, with the 0x8000 material flag enabling real alpha blending (BlendFunc Src_InvSrc_Add, zBias High); ShallowWater/DeepWater TerrainType is only a collision/fishing classifier, not a render path, and there is NO separate water plane and NO UV scroll/animation.

Our client diverges in two ways:

(1) The real water surface geometry IS rendered (it lives in the MMB visual zone models, ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mmb.rs), but the 0x8000 translucency flag is approximated as AlphaMode::Mask(0.5) — an alpha-test CUTOUT — see submesh_alpha_mode() at ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mmb.rs:695-705. The reason is FfxiZoneMaterial's WGSL hardcodes output alpha = 1.0 (ffxi-viewer-core/src/zone_ffxi.wgsl:153), so it physically cannot blend. Result: water renders opaque/holey, not translucent.

(2) A separate non-faithful hack in ffxi-viewer-core/src/dat_mzb.rs:1208-1264 parses a water_height field from the MZB material chunk (ffxi-dat/src/mzb.rs:457-473) and spawns flat semi-transparent blue StandardMaterial quads sized to the placement bounding box ('N water planes spawned' in logs). XIM has no equivalent; this double-covers the real water geometry.

Faithful fix:
- Thread the 0x8000 blend flag into FfxiZoneMaterial.material_flags (flags.y is currently unused: dat_mmb.rs sets Vec4::new(has_texture,0,0,discard_threshold)).
- In zone_ffxi.wgsl fragment, emit alpha = texel.a * in.color.a when blend-mode, else 1.0 (keep opaque ground/wall fully opaque to preserve the no-holes guard documented at dat_mmb.rs:687-694).
- Set alpha_mode = AlphaMode::Blend for 0x8000 subs (XIM zBias High → likely depth_write off + transparent sort).
- Remove or debug-gate the MZB water_height blue-quad hack once translucent water geometry works.

Evidence cited inline. Area: zone-render. Vanilla parity.
notes:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (my first pass was wrong): water 'not rendering at all' was NOT a material problem — the MZB water_height plane was tagged MzbNonCollisionMesh, which apply_zone_geom_visibility + compute_init_visibility keep Hidden in every zone_geom_mode except the 'All' debug mode (default mode is Off). So the water plane was invisible in normal play. There is NO water surface in the MMB visual geometry for outdoor ponds — outdoor water in our pipeline comes solely from the MZB water_height plane (XIM doesn't render outdoor water specially, which is why the Explore agent found 'no separate plane'). My initial deletion of the plane made it strictly worse (no water object at all).

Fix shipped:
- dat_mzb.rs: restored the water_height plane spawn; retagged it MzbOverlay + Visibility::Inherited and DROPPED MzbNonCollisionMesh, so it is governed only by cull_mzb_by_distance (real scene content), never the debug toggle. Material tuned toward water (translucent blue-green, roughness 0.06, reflectance 0.55) so it catches sun/sky specular instead of flat blue.
- dat_mmb.rs + zone_ffxi.wgsl (committed f607dd3): 0x8000 MMB subs -> AlphaMode::Blend with real shader alpha. This is still a valid XIM-parity improvement for genuine translucent MMB props (glass/windows) but is orthogonal to outdoor water.

Remaining (not yet done, follow-up): the plane is a bounding-box rectangle per height (crude shape, relies on terrain occlusion to clip) and is static (no ripple/scroll/reflection). A dedicated animated FfxiWaterMaterial would be the next faithfulness step.
close_reason: Submesh 0x8000 alpha blend applied, zone_ffxi.wgsl outputs proper alpha, water entities use AlphaMode::Blend

title: beads -> GitHub Issues publisher (create/update/close lifecycle)
description: Single one-way publisher: each bead -> one GitHub issue, keyed by an HTML-comment marker <!-- beads-id: <id> --> in the issue body. title: Periodic ~1Hz +20ms frame spike: camera_collision brute-force validation probe runs every 1s on main thread regardless of log level
description: clamp_chase_camera_to_collision (ffxi-client/src/view_native/camera_collision.rs:111-152) runs a BVH-vs-brute-force VALIDATION raycast over ALL zone+MMB collision triangles every >=1.0s. title: Network health HUD widget (retail S/R baud + connection % + animated arrows)
description:
Faithful reproduction of retail FFXI's top-right network indicator: two animated send/receive arrows that tint green->red, a connection-health percentage, and 'S <n>'/'R <n>' baud-rate readouts.

Research (this session):
- S=send rate, R=receive rate = BAUD RATE (data throughput), not ping/seq counts. Game engineered for ~3000 baud duplex (v.90 dial-up); crowded-zone 'R3000' = saturated receive pipe. Source: bg-wiki Draft:Network + corroborating community.
- Percentage = separate connection-health metric; 100% solid, falls on packet loss/no server response, 0% => client self-declares disconnect -> title/POL.
- LSB sends NOTHING for this: confirmed no baud/percentage field in vendor/server (preparePacket/finalizePacket, zero grep). Datagram header carries seq/ack only (MapSession.client_packet_id/server_packet_id, retransmit-on-ack-mismatch). Widget is 100% client telemetry. LSB disconnect ladder: 5s->isLinkDead, MAX_TIME_LASTUPDATE(~30-60s)->hard delete.

Decisions (agreed):
- Placement: VANILLA always-on HUD element (ffxi-viewer-core/hud/), top-right like retail, with a /netstat slash toggle to hide.
- Scope: full widget end-to-end (byte-rate plumbing + S/R + % + animated green->red arrows).
- % model: ACK-GAP based. recv_health from contiguity of inbound server seq (gaps=recv loss); send_health from server's echoed ack of our bundle_seq vs sent (lag=send loss). Overall % = min(send,recv); up-arrow color<-send_health, down-arrow color<-recv_health.

Plumbing: add on-wire byte counters at map_client.rs send/recv boundaries -> bytes/sec rolling 1s window (S/R). Add fields to state.rs Diagnostics -> wire_translate diagnostics_to_wire -> ffxi-viewer-wire Diagnostics -> read in new view widget. Reuse existing sync_in/sync_out/last_server_packet_age_ms.

Evidence: map_client.rs send_encrypted/recv_decrypted (byte boundaries known at blowfish/zlib); framing.rs Header{sync_in,sync_out}; state.rs Diagnostics; session.rs recv loop reads header.id_and_size(server seq)+sync_in(server ack of us); wire_translate.rs diagnostics_to_wire; hud/mod.rs HudPlugin+add_hud_spawners+palette+DevHud; perf_hud.rs/vana_clock.rs widget pattern.
notes:
FOLLOW-UPS since initial impl:
- b8912dc: S/R baud now refreshes on a 3s window (retail ticks ~3s, not sub-second).
- 3d50d79: widget is fixed-width (% in 36px right-justified box, S/R values in 38px boxes after static S/R prefixes) so digit-count changes don't reflow neighbors.
- 7781663: FIX — keepalive send failure no longer breaks the map loop. Previously a failed send (link down, remote server) tore the session down immediately, freezing the widget so % never decayed. Now we swallow send failures (log once on rising edge), keep ticking, and let last_recv aging drive S/R->0 (after ~3s) and %->0 (linear 3s..MAP_SILENCE_TIMEOUT=60s); silence timeout remains the single disconnect trigger. Matches retail 'decay to 0 then disconnect'. Reported by user: remote server + wifi-off showed no S/R/% change (loop had broken).
close_reason: Network status widget top-right, arrows/% updated from net_stats, /netstat toggle wired, keepalive-decay fix applied

title: Move MMB zone-prop parse onto AsyncComputeTaskPool
description: process_load_mmb_requests parses MMB props synchronously on the main thread (load_mmb: fs::read + decrypt + parse_models + decode_texture), throttled by a work budget that is really a frame-hitch guard. title: Event-dialog ending is not uniform across exit paths (Esc advances instead of cancels; walk-away/range and server force-close not handled)
description:
The four ways an event-dialog can end behave inconsistently; some leave the player desynced server-side.

Paths (ffxi-client/src/view_native/text_input.rs + session.rs):
1. Option select (Enter/click): EndEventChoice -> EVENT_END sent. (EndPara value is the separate bug kuluu-jbq.)
2. Esc / NavCancel (text_input.rs:2442): view *immediately* clears snapshot.dialog + returns to World, then sends AgentCommand::EndEvent. In session.rs:1259 EndEvent calls dialog_session.advance(None). For a MESSAGE frame, None just dismisses and yields the NEXT frame (ffxi-event runner.rs:62) -> session re-emits EventDialog -> dialog_mode_sync_system (text_input.rs:283) re-opens it. So Esc on a multi-frame VM event ADVANCES instead of cancelling (dialog visibly closes then reappears). Only a menu (QUERYWAIT) frame cancels via work_zone[0]=254.
3. Esc legacy path with empty pending_event_end: session.rs:1279 else-branch only fires when pending is non-empty; if empty, NOTHING is sent. Local dialog closed but server may still consider player in-event, and the watchdog (session.rs:1708) won't fire because it keys on non-empty pending.
4. Walk away / out of range: no handler ends the event on movement. Only backstop is the 10s PENDING_EVENT_END_GRACE watchdog (session.rs:1723-1744) that force-flushes EVENT_END(option=0) and emits an Error toast (user-driven mode only; agent mode flushes every tick).
5. Server force-close: incoming 0x052 EVENTUCOFF is not decoded to clear the UI; a server-initiated event close can leave a stale local dialog.

Fix scope:
- Esc must cancel the whole event reliably (route a real cancel into the VM that ends it, not advance), and clear the UI only once the EVENT_END is actually queued.
- Decode incoming 0x052 (and/or a new event start) to clear snapshot.dialog when the server closes the event.
- Make cancel always resolve server-side (send EVENT_END for the active event id even when pending list is empty), or document why a no-op is safe.
- Consider ending the dialog cleanly on confirmed out-of-range / NPC despawn rather than relying solely on the 10s watchdog.
notes:
RETAIL OBSERVED 2026-07-19 (HorizonXI, Atti, Bastok MH + Markets; artifacts/retail/20260719-14*.png):
- Esc on TOP-LEVEL choice frame (Mog Menu, cursor on Storage): whole dialog + help bar close instantly, no cursor-to-cancel step (142556 -> 142622).
- Esc on NESTED frame (Delivery Box grid): backs out ONE level to the Receive/Send submenu, help bar stays (142809 -> 142835). Unifying rule: Esc sends the frame's CANCEL result; the SERVER script decides parent-menu vs end (matches both observations).
- Esc on plain MESSAGE frame: NOT OBSERVED (no multi-frame text NPC reachable in crowded night plaza) — remains open; implement per LSB-accepted cancel semantics and re-verify when VM free.
- Movement during open menu: W with Receive/Send open rotated view/char while menu stayed open (142835 -> 142856) — ambiguous (camera auto-rotate?), open question.
close_reason: Landed (merge of 6cf9018): Esc now cancels via DialogRunner::cancel() -> 0x05B Mode=End EndPara=1<<30 (= LSB utils.EVENT_CANCELLED_OPTION, utils.lua:8); EVENTUCOFF handler generalized (CANCEL_EVENT clears dialog+pending, mode-1 ack inert per 0x05b_eventend.cpp:71); empty-pending stays local-only (LSB validation would drop a fabricated 0x05B). Retail-observed Esc semantics recorded in notes (choice-frame close, nested back-one-level — both = 'client sends cancel result, server script decides'). title: Distance-prioritized + view-distance-gated MMB zone-prop streaming
description:
The MMB zone-placement load queue (dat_mmb.rs process_load_mmb_requests) drains FIFO at 48 work-units/frame regardless of where the player is, and nothing visibility-culls loaded MmbOverlay props (cull_mzb_by_distance is defined but unregistered; only cull_entities_by_distance runs). Result: zone-in loads props in arbitrary order and far props render until zone change.

Add: (1) sort MmbLoadQueue.pending nearest-player-first each frame (entity/look-driven spawns keep priority, zone-spawns sorted by XZ-dist2); (2) defer zone-spawn loads beyond draw.world*margin (re-checked as player moves, never dropped); (3) cull_mmb_props_by_distance visibility system at draw.world so far loaded props stop rendering, with load margin>cull radius for hysteresis. Despawn-unload intentionally skipped: mesh/texture/material handles persist in MmbParseCache/MmbHandleCache/MmbTexPools for the whole zone, so despawn frees little while adding reload thrash.
notes: v2 after playtest: load gate now driven by GraphicsSettings.view_distance (was DrawDistance.world=80, far too low and not the setting users control). Removed cull_mmb_props_by_distance entirely — the camera far plane (= view_distance, settings.rs:1068) already frustum-culls props beyond the visible range, so the extra distance-cull was redundant and was the source of the pop-in/pop-out at 80 units. Net: load nearest-first within view_distance*1.25 (lead ring), render bounded by far plane, no visibility toggling.
close_reason: Shipped v2: MMB zone-prop queue sorts nearest-player-first and defers loads beyond GraphicsSettings.view_distance*1.25 (re-checked as player moves). Rendering bounds left to the camera far plane; redundant distance-cull removed. fmt/clippy/tests green.

title: Death/resurrect music+combat lifecycle (dead-slot, self-death disengage)
description: Reported: dying did not play death music; after resurrect the character stayed engaged (stance + now battle music) until /disengage. Root causes found and two fixed: (1) audio dead detection used icons.contains(EFFECT_KO=0) which is wrong — KO is not a status-effect icon; fixed to self_entity.is_dead() (hp_pct==0, wire Entity helper). (2) reactor Goal::Engaged only disengaged when the TARGET died (reactor.rs:597), never on self death; added self_is_dead() check so death forces Goal::Idle (+test self_death_disengages_even_if_target_alive). REMAINING/OPEN: (a) Dead music slot 5 is never populated — zone-in 0x0A only carries slots 0-4 and LSB only sets slot 5 via scripted Lua changeMusic, so a normal field death has no track; faithful behavior is battle-music-stops→zone-music. Decision needed: vanilla (server-driven only) vs enhanced hardcoded death jingle. (b) Bevy ECS WARN 'Entity despawned generation N' double-despawn around homepoint warp (InGameEntity zone-cleanup vs AudioFade despawn) — separate lifecycle hardening.
notes: Self-death state now reliable. ROOT: self KO is signaled only via 0x037 CHAR_STATUS (hpp==0) -> death_homepoint_secs; the self entity hp_pct and (when solo) the party row never reach 0, so the renderer's self_dead (party-row) + audio dead (entity) never fired. FIX: DeathTimerUpdated now carries Option<u32> (Some=KO w/ homepoint secs, None=alive) so CHAR_STATUS both sets AND clears death (fixes raise-in-place stuck-dead; zone-change already cleared). Renderer self_dead (ffxi_actor_render.rs:1654) and audio dead now read death_homepoint_secs.is_some() (||existing party-row/entity). Reactor disengage gated to Some(_) so an alive CHAR_STATUS doesn't disengage (test revive_event_does_not_disengage). Diagnostic log now prints dead + death_homepoint_secs. NOTE: vanilla has no field death MUSIC (slot 5 empty) — battle->zone on death is correct; this fix is about the death ANIMATION + correct dead flag.
close_reason: Self-death disengage (reactor.rs:369-382); dead-detection audio fix (audio.rs:250); double-despawn hardening (audio.rs:938-940); all three sub-fixes present on main.

title: Battle music doesn't trigger on engage (zone 116, slot 2/3)
description: Engaging solo in zone 116 (East Sarutabaruta) does not switch to battle music, despite zone_settings defining battlesolo=101/battlemulti=103. The full slot infrastructure (BgmSlots, resolve_audible_slot, 0x0A MusicNum[5], 0x5F) is already built and retail-faithful. The suspect is derive_bgm_playback_state (ffxi-viewer-core/src/audio.rs:221): engagement is gated solely on self_entity.bt_target_id != 0, which depends on the LSB server echoing the self CHAR_PC update with a battle target. The self status byte is hardcoded to 0 (session.rs:688), so it can't be a fallback. The reactor already tracks engagement authoritatively as current_goal == Engaged (carried in the snapshot, wire/lib.rs:325) but the audio system ignores it. Step 1: add change-detected debug logging to derive_bgm_playback_state exposing bt_target_id, current_goal, and self status, then engage in zone 116 to confirm which signal is live. Step 2: drive battle music from the reliable signal (likely current_goal primary, bt_target_id fallback).
notes: FIXED engage trigger: derive_bgm_playback_state now drives engaged from reactor current_goal==Engaged (||bt_target), since LSB never echoes the self bt_target (confirmed via live log: engaged_signal=false self_bt_target_id=0 reactor_goal_engaged=true). Extracted self_engaged() helper + regression test reactor_goal_drives_engaged_without_server_bt_target. Awaiting live re-test in a zone with distinct battle music (116 = East Sarutabaruta, battlesolo=101).

title: In-app self-update download+replace+restart behind a self-update feature
description: Behind feature `self-update`, implement apply_update() against the assets dist actually publishes. VERIFIED scheme (dist 0.32.0 `dist plan` with this repo's [workspace.metadata.dist], Cargo.toml:113-138): `kuluu-<triple>.tar.xz` on unix and `kuluu-<triple>.zip` on Windows — the tag appears only in the release URL directory, NOT in the filename, and unix archives default to .tar.xz (not .tar.gz) since no `unix-archive` override is set. Checksums: dist emits one `<asset>.sha256` per artifact plus an aggregate `sha256.sum`; it does NOT emit `SHA256SUMS`. That is a live break, not a detail — the landed verifier fetches `{DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL}/{tag}/SHA256SUMS` (kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/updater.rs:112-141), and that file exists only because the hand-rolled release.yml:221-223 generates it; kuluu-0kz deleting release.yml silently breaks kuluu-va7's integrity contract unless the updater is repointed at `<asset>.sha256`. Current state: updater.rs is check-only — version poll, banner, "Open release page" (updater.rs:143-256); `fetch_and_verify_sha256` and `UpdateStatus.sha256_verified` are present but `#[allow(dead_code)]` (updater.rs:30, :111); no `self-update` feature in kuluu/Cargo.toml:24-44 and no self_update/axoupdater dependency. Implement: download-to-temp, verify checksum, atomic replace, prompt restart. macOS: do NOT strip/re-sign client-side — the released artifact's signature must survive or the binary is killed:9 (release.yml:126-128). Disable for package-manager installs. Before hand-rolling, weigh dist's built-in `install-updater` (axoupdater) — a supported [workspace.metadata.dist] key in 0.32.0 that ships an `kuluu-update` binary with the shell/powershell installers. Depends on signed artifacts existing so updates are trustworthy.
notes: 2026-08-20: v0.5.1 adds aarch64-linux and aarch64-windows release assets. When this self-update flow constructs the artifact filename, it MUST select by std::env::consts::ARCH as well as OS — an OS-only match on a Snapdragon/ARM machine downloads the x86_64 asset. Asset name contract (emitter: .github/workflows/release.yml): kuluu-<tag>-<arch>-<os>.<tar.gz|zip> with arch in {x86_64, aarch64}.

title: Windows Authenticode signing via Azure Trusted Signing owned by dist
description: User chose Azure's managed CI code-signing service (~$10/mo Basic SKU, no HSM, signs in CI). Upstream renamed it: Trusted Signing is now **Artifact Signing** — docs at learn.microsoft.com/azure/artifact-signing/ (the /azure/trusted-signing/quickstart URL now canonicalises there), CLI extension `az artifact-signing`, resource provider `Microsoft.CodeSigning`. The action's README documents `uses: azure/artifact-signing-action@v2` with inputs `endpoint`, `signing-account-name`, `certificate-profile-name`, `files-folder`, `file-digest`, `timestamp-rfc3161`, `timestamp-digest`. NOTE: `trusted-signing-account-name` still exists in action.yml as a retained (required: false) legacy alias for `signing-account-name` — prefer the new name, but it is not a removed input. Credentials reach the action as `azure-tenant-id`/`azure-client-id`/`azure-client-secret` (env AZURE_TENANT_ID/AZURE_CLIENT_ID/AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET); AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID is NOT consumed by the signing action — only add it if an `azure/login` step is used. Pinning `timestamp-rfc3161: http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com` is belt-and-braces, not a hard requirement: it is already the action's declared default. MECHANISM MUST BE CHOSEN BEFORE STARTING — "owned by dist" is not a config knob: dist 0.32.0 ships exactly one Windows signing backend, SSL.com eSigner (`ssldotcom-windows-sign`, sign/ssldotcom.rs, SSLDOTCOM_* env) and no Azure backend; `github-build-setup` steps run BEFORE `dist build` (.github/build-setup.yml:1-11) so they cannot sign a built exe, and the `*-jobs` hooks only run after dist has archived it. Options: (a) a dist custom job that unpacks, signs and re-packs the Windows archive and regenerates its `.sha256` (see kuluu-fwz), (b) contribute an azure/artifact-signing backend upstream to dist, or (c) switch to SSL.com eSigner, which dist already drives end-to-end. Requires completed identity validation — portal-only, 1 to 20 business days per the Microsoft quickstart, so start early. BLOCKED on user.

title: macOS Developer ID sign + notarize + staple as a dist post-strip custom job
description:
dist 0.32.0 CAN codesign but has NO macOS notarization. Verified against the pinned binary (/Users/jon/.cargo/bin/dist, cargo-dist 0.32.0, matching Cargo.toml:114): its DistMetadata config schema carries a `macos-sign` key (workspace-level only), and the binary ships the whole keychain-import + codesign pipeline — /usr/bin/security create-keychain / import -k -P -t -f pkcs12 / set-key-partition-list, /usr/bin/codesign with --sign/--options/--keychain, driven by CODESIGN_IDENTITY / CODESIGN_CERTIFICATE / CODESIGN_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD / CODESIGN_OPTIONS, plus a CI template fragment gated on `{%- if macos_sign %}`. There is NO notarytool, stapler, xcrun or App Store Connect code path anywhere in the binary.

So split the work per the epic's 'signing DELEGATED to dist' rule:
1. DELEGATE codesigning: set `macos-sign` in [workspace.metadata.dist] (Cargo.toml:113-138) and supply the Developer ID Application cert + CODESIGN_OPTIONS via repo secrets. Do NOT hand-roll the keychain import — the original plan step above did, and that is the part to drop.
2. CUSTOM JOB (what dist genuinely cannot do): after dist's local-artifacts build, ditto the signed binary into a .zip, `xcrun notarytool submit --wait` with an App Store Connect API key, `xcrun stapler staple`, and switch the macOS artifact to the stapled .zip.

MANDATORY ORDERING: signing must happen after any strip — strip invalidates the arm64 signature and the binary dies with 'killed: 9' (.github/workflows/release.yml:125-128). CONFIRM BEFORE WIRING where dist strips: [profile.dist] (Cargo.toml:142-144) sets no `strip` key and there is no [profile.release] in this workspace, so this repo does not currently pin it — read dist's own strip behaviour rather than assuming it matches the hand-rolled leg.

BLOCKED on Apple Developer Program ($99/yr) + App Store Connect API key secrets.

title: Re-wire auto-release-on-main to dist's tag-triggered release
description: auto-release-on-main.yml:52 calls the hand-rolled release.yml as a reusable workflow with a tag input; dist's release.yml is tag-triggered (push tags v*), breaking the contract. Keep version-bump detection but push the tag with GH_RELEASE_PAT so the tag event fires (GITHUB_TOKEN-pushed tags don't trigger workflows — auto-release-on-main.yml:46). Drop the old release: reusable-call job; re-add the ci.yml fmt/clippy/test gate before the tag push. BLOCKED on user secret GH_RELEASE_PAT.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Verified 2026-07-31 against dist itself. `dist plan` in this repo emits the generate-check diff for the file dist 0.32.0 would own: its trigger block is `on: pull_request` + `push: tags: ['**[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*']` with NO `workflow_call`, so auto-release-on-main.yml:52's `uses: ./.github/workflows/release.yml` breaks exactly as described (v-prefixed tags do match that glob — the `**` prefix admits them). The generated file also carries no CI gate, confirming the "re-add the ci.yml gate" item; ci.yml:7 already declares `workflow_call`, so auto-release-on-main can call it before tagging with no change to ci.yml. GitHub docs confirm the PAT requirement: "events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN will not create a new workflow run, with the following exceptions: workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch events always create workflow runs." That exception is the cheaper alternative worth weighing before provisioning GH_RELEASE_PAT: dist's `dispatch-releases = true` config key replaces the tag trigger with `workflow_dispatch` (input `tag`, description "Release Tag"), which auto-release-on-main can fire with `gh workflow run` using the default GITHUB_TOKEN — no user secret, no blocked bead. Trade-off: with dispatch-releases the tag no longer drives the release, so a hand-pushed tag would need the same dispatch.

title: [bug] Minimap blank after zone-in: image-source change-detection edge consumed before MinimapImage node exists
description:
Symptom: minimap renders dots but no map texture right after zone-in / game load; re-issuing '/minimap cull 6' (forces a top-down re-bake) reliably makes the map appear.

Root cause: update_minimap_image_source (ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/mod.rs:406) is gated on '!state.is_changed() && !mode.is_changed()'. The retail/top-down image becomes available via a single MinimapState change, but on that frame the system early-returns at a LATER guard (q.single_mut() Err because the MinimapImage node from OnEnter(InGame) isn't present yet, or retail_image is momentarily None during the zone-change clear). That consumes the change edge; the gate then short-circuits forever and the ImageNode.image handle is never assigned until the next bake mutates MinimapState. The overlay (dots) and crop systems run unconditionally so they stay correct — only the image handle is stuck on the transparent placeholder, showing the dark BACKGROUND.

Fix: drop the is_changed() early-return in update_minimap_image_source so it idempotently re-evaluates and assigns the resolved handle every frame (the existing 'image_node.image != h' check keeps it cheap and churn-free). update_minimap_crop_rect already runs unconditionally on the same query, so this is consistent.
close_reason: Dropped the is_changed() early-return in update_minimap_image_source (ffxi-viewer-core/src/minimap/mod.rs) so the resolved minimap handle is re-evaluated/assigned every frame (idempotent via image_node.image != h). Fixes blank map after zone-in where the single MinimapState change edge was consumed before the MinimapImage node existed. Build + 20 minimap tests pass, clippy/fmt clean.

title: [bug] Dead entities (hp_pct==0) remain tab-cyclable and click-targetable
description: Dead targets should not be cyclable via Tab nor selectable via click. build_tab_candidates (ffxi-client/src/view_native/input.rs) and click_to_target_system (ffxi-viewer-core/src/picking.rs) do not filter dead entities; auto_clear_target_system already drops a target on death (hp_pct==Some(0)) but selection still lands on corpses first. Fix: centralize an Entity::is_targetable() predicate in ffxi-viewer-wire and apply it to tab-cycle candidates, click picking, and should_clear_target. Open question: which other states (cutscene/event NPCs, despawning) should also be excluded.
notes: Implemented. Centralized Entity::{is_dead,is_targetable,is_cycle_candidate} in ffxi-viewer-wire. Decisions (user): (1) dead PCs stay click-targetable for Raise, but no corpse cycles via Tab; dead mobs/NPCs fully blocked. (2) Also exclude LSB STATUS_TYPE hide states {2,3,4,6,18,20} (verified vs vendor/server/.../baseentity.h; CUTSCENE_ONLY=6 not 4). Fixed a latent bug found by protocol-conformance-reviewer: Entity.status was only decoded under UPDATE_HP(0x04), but LSB writes status every tick (UPDATE_STATUS=0x02 changes never set 0x04), so status went stale. Split status into a top-level session Entity field decoded every tick (NpcState::decode_char_npc_status); npc_state still carries UPDATE_HP-gated animation/animationsub. Call sites: build_tab_candidates uses is_cycle_candidate; click_to_target_system + should_clear_target use is_targetable. Tests added in ffxi-viewer-wire, input.rs, scene.rs, decode.rs, state.rs.

title: Tab-target list empty at normal camera pitch in hilly zones (W. Ronfaure): vertical transform sign flip
description: Repro: in W. Ronfaure (trees + height differentials) the Tab target list is empty until the camera is pitched top-down. Root cause: build_tab_candidates (ffxi-client/src/view_native/input.rs:821) computed the projection point as Vec3::new(e.pos.x, e.pos.z, -e.pos.y) — the vertical (Bevy-up) component had the WRONG SIGN vs the canonical ffxi_to_bevy (ffxi-viewer-core/src/scene.rs:14 = Vec3::new(p.x, -p.z, -p.y)). Every entity was projected at a mirrored height; at normal pitch the bad ndc.y fell outside CYCLE_NDC_Y_LIMIT(1.6) so all entities were culled, but top-down the vertical barely affects screen xy so they reappeared. Existing cycle tests all used z:0.0 so the sign was never exercised. Fix: use ffxi_viewer_core::ffxi_to_bevy(e.pos); added regression test candidate_projects_at_canonical_grounded_height pinning the vertical transform. Follow-up for fuller retail parity: cycle uses screen-space NDC culling, which still drops valid nearby targets at extreme camera pitch and requires on-screen framing; retail selects by world-space range + forward arc (heading-relative), pitch-independent and no LOS/occlusion requirement.
close_reason: Tab-target vertical sign-flip fix + regression test verified already present in main (input.rs:822); bead was stale-open

title: Enhanced sky over-reddens at dusk (atmosphere multiplied by saturated sun-light color)
description:
In Enhanced sky mode the whole sky dome turns deep maroon near sunset (~V17:00), not just the horizon. Root cause: graphics_settings::apply_physical_sky_system inserts Bevy Atmosphere::earthlike + AtmosphereSettings::default on the camera (ffxi-viewer-core/src/graphics_settings.rs:1196-1204). Bevy's atmosphere uses the sun DirectionalLight's color*illuminance as incident sun radiance, so it multiplies in-scattered sky light by the light color. sun_moon::sun_moon_system sets that light to sun_color_for_hour() (sun_moon.rs:392-398), which at dusk is heavily saturated (~rgb(1.0,0.41,0.30) at hour 17 — sun_color_for_hour, sun_moon.rs:207-229). That red tint is applied on TOP of the atmosphere's own wavelength-dependent reddening => maroon everywhere.

Fix direction: in physical/Enhanced mode feed the atmosphere a near-white (physical) sun light color and let the scattering produce the sunset gradient; leave the Vanilla gradient path (driven by weather-DAT keyframes) untouched since it looks correct. Likely needs a small live tuning pass on the whiten amount and possibly AtmosphereSettings (scene_units_to_m).
notes: Implemented in 47cce4b. sun_moon_system now whitens the sun DirectionalLight color toward white (lerp 0.85) when settings.sky_style.physical() (Enhanced), so Bevy's atmosphere isn't fed a saturated dusk tint. Vanilla gradient path untouched. PENDING: visual verification — confirm dusk sky is no longer uniformly maroon; the 0.85 whiten factor is a one-number tune in sun_moon.rs if it needs more/less warmth.
close_reason: No bevy_atmosphere dependency; sky dome uses retail-faithful gradient, sun/light don't tint dome; red moon disc only

title: Lens-flare sun glare drifts off the sun disc (overscan vs screen-UV mismatch)
description:
In Vanilla sky mode the sun's god-rays (halo/streak/ghosts) render vertically offset from the sun disc, most visibly near sunrise/sunset when the sun sits away from screen centre.

Root cause: the lens-flare quad is intentionally oversized by FLARE_OVERSCAN=1.15 (ffxi-viewer-core/src/lens_flare.rs:53,132) so it always covers the frustum. But the shader used the quad's in.uv as the screen coordinate (ffxi-viewer-core/src/lens_flare.wgsl:109) while comparing against 'sun', a TRUE screen UV from the projection (lens_flare.wgsl:75-77). A quad 15% larger than the frustum maps in.uv to screen [-0.075,1.075], so every flare element drew at 0.5+(sun-0.5)*1.15 -> offset 0.15*(sun-0.5). Sun above centre (sun.y<0.5) pushes the glare up by ~0.03 of screen height (~33px), vanishing only when the sun is dead-centre.

Not a sun_dir/look_at issue: disc and flare share the identical sun_dir and radius 4000, and OperatorCamera is unparented so view.world_position==cam_pos; the world point is the same.

Fix: derive screen UV from the fragment framebuffer coord instead of the overscanned quad UV: uv = (in.position.xy - view.viewport.xy)/max(view.viewport.zw,1). Keeps the overscan coverage margin while landing the flare exactly on the projected sun. Reuses the same view.viewport convention the occlusion taps already use (lens_flare.wgsl:85).
close_reason: Fixed in lens_flare.wgsl: screen UV now derived from framebuffer coord, so the overscanned flare quad no longer drifts the glare off the sun disc.

title: /logout should return to character select, not the launcher front (retail parity); differentiate /logout vs /shutdown destinations
description:
Retail: /logout returns to the CHARACTER SELECT screen (account session retained, you can pick another character); /shutdown returns to the title/POL/server-select screen.

LANDED SINCE THIS BEAD WAS FILED — a clean logout already resumes the character list:
- classify_disconnect_reason maps a reason starting "server logout state=" to DisconnectKind::Clean, everything else to Forced (kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs:689-707; the emitter of that string is kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:3203).
- return_to_launcher_on_disconnect writes the error toast only on Forced and inserts ResumeCharListAfterLogout on Clean before AppPhase::Launcher (mod.rs:828-858; unit tests at mod.rs:861-888).
- resume_char_list_after_logout consumes the marker and bounces through LauncherState::AuthInFlight with the stored credentials, landing on CharList (kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/mod.rs:977-994; registered OnEnter(AppPhase::Launcher) at :606-613).
So the acceptance criterion's third clause (a Forced disconnect returns to launcher with the error toast) already passes, and the old bullet "CharList is never the destination" is obsolete.

WHAT REMAINS:
1. /shutdown is not differentiated: both /logout and /shutdown end as DisconnectKind::Clean, so both resume CharList, where retail's /shutdown must return to login/server select. LSB cannot tell them apart on the wire — the only two GP_GAME_LOGOUT_STATE push sites in the whole server are ZONECHANGE (charutils::SendToZone, vendor/server/src/map/utils/charutils.cpp:7284) and LOGOUT (charutils::SendDisconnect, :7312, with ForceLogout an alias at :7316-7320); the richer states MYROOM/CANCELL/POLEXIT/JOBEXIT/TIMEOUT/GMLOGOUT in the enum (vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x00b_logout.h:29-42) are never sent. The distinction must therefore come from the ReqLogout the client itself sent: ReqLogoutKind::Logout* vs Shutdown* (kuluu-session/src/state.rs:2341-2367; kind::LOGOUT=0x01 / kind::SHUTDOWN=0x03 at ffxi-proto/src/map.rs:250-254), remembered across the disconnect and read by the disconnect watcher.
2. The resume re-authenticates. OpenedLobbyInner's LobbyHandle + AuthSession are take()n by spawn_connect_task (kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/async_work.rs:244-246) and are gone by the time the map session ends — resume_char_list_after_logout's own doc comment says so. Faithful behavior is a return to CharList WITHOUT re-authenticating: retain the AuthSession and re-open the lobby/view connection (the map server hands the client back to the lobby).
3. There is still no character-select AppPhase: AppPhase is {Launcher, Connecting, InGame} (kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs:164-172) and CharList is a LauncherState SubState of Launcher (launcher_ui/mod.rs:71-110, CharList at :96); re-entering Launcher runs decide_initial_screen (launcher_ui/mod.rs:997) unless the resume marker short-circuits it.

Also note: classify_disconnect_reason treats state=2 (ZONECHANGE) as Clean too (mod.rs:871-873), so if a zone-change LOGOUT ever reaches the disconnect watcher it would also resume CharList — worth pinning when the /shutdown split lands.

Still depends on disentangling the /exit-vs-disconnect race (kuluu-2oq).
acceptance_criteria: /logout (LeaveGame) returns to the character-select list with the account session intact; /shutdown returns to login/server select; a Forced disconnect still returns to launcher with the error toast.

title: Periodic render hitch: full SceneSnapshot deep-clone on render thread per snapshot change
description: Symptom: ~1-2s periodic frame hitch even at max FPS. Root cause (code-evidenced, not yet profiler-confirmed): ffxi-client/src/session.rs:2028 run_event_folder calls state_tx.send_modify() on EVERY AgentEvent; the render thread's poll_snapshot (ffxi-client/src/view_native/bridge.rs:25) responds to any watch change by deep-cloning the ENTIRE SessionState into a SceneSnapshot via state_to_snapshot (ffxi-client/src/wire_translate.rs:9): entities/party/chat/status_icons/recasts/spell+ability lists/inventory/equipment, then Box-allocates it. Amplified by the state.dirty O(n) fan-out (ffxi-viewer-core/src/snapshot.rs ingest + scene.rs sync_* systems). Server traffic (keepalive + nearby-entity position/HP updates) clusters ~1Hz, riding the beat. Tab-targeting ruled OUT (picking.rs is event-driven; no timed target rebuild). Fix direction: drive the render side off incremental SceneDelta (drain_deltas already exists at bridge.rs:34 but returns empty) instead of a full clone-and-rebuild per change; or hash/coalesce to skip no-op rebuilds. Confirmation instrument added to /devhud (snap us / rebuilds-per-sec / frame-max ms in target-list panel).
notes: Live /devhud data refined the diagnosis: snap rebuild is only ~6us at n=7 (cheap) and rebuilds/s exceeds 60 -> the watch channel reports changed EVERY frame (send_modify per AgentEvent on the Tokio side), so the render thread does a full clone + state.dirty O(n) fan-out every frame = continuous baseline waste, but NOT the periodic 1-2s spike (frame max ~24ms observed on non-rebuild-cost frames). Added a frame-spike detector + correlation counters (ffxi-viewer-core/src/perf_probe.rs: model_loads, nameplate_rasters) bumped at load_pc/load_npc and the nameplate rasterize site; /devhud panel now shows spike magnitude, ~interval, and on-spike model/nameplate/rebuild correlation to pinpoint the periodic culprit. Two problems: (1) per-frame full rebuild [delta path], (2) the still-unidentified ~1-2s spike [pending live correlation read].
close_reason: Made SessionState::apply_event return bool ('actually mutated') with cheap equality/dedupe checks for high-frequency no-op events (identical EntityUpserted, self position, weather/time ticks), and switched session.rs to watch::Sender::send_if_modified gated on that bool so the watch channel only signals real state changes. This eliminates the per-frame wakeup + full snapshot/rebuild fan-out in NativeSource without touching the (empty) SceneDelta path at bridge.rs:50.

title: Player ↔ player trade window
description:
Player ↔ player trade window — 4×2 grid + gil selector + quantity + OK/Cancel

Re-grounded 2026-07-31: still [~]. The trade window UI exists and is wired into the Bevy app (4×2 grid, gil selector, stack/quantity selector, OK/Cancel, focus nav, spawn+update systems registered) and opens from the target menu, but nothing is dispatched: item-into-slot placement is an explicit stub, the gil max is hardcoded 0, and the TradeIntent message has NO consumer anywhere — it is written but never read and never becomes an outbound packet.

Correction to the original grounding: the outbound packet is NOT 0x036. Per LSB, c2s 0x036 GP_CLI_COMMAND_ITEM_TRANSFER is 'sent by the client when completing a trade with an NPC' and its handler resolves the counterparty as TYPE_NPC|TYPE_MOB within 6.0' (vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x036_item_transfer.h:26-27, .cpp:73-79). Player↔player trade is c2s 0x032 TRADE_REQ (request a trade with another player), 0x034 TRADE_LIST (set an item inside the trade window: ItemNum/ItemNo/ItemIndex/TradeIndex), 0x033 TRADE_RES (Kind Start/Cancell/Make/MakeCancell, handler resolves TYPE_PC via TradePending), answered by s2c 0x021 ITEM_TRADE_REQ / 0x022 ITEM_TRADE_RES / 0x023 ITEM_TRADE_LIST / 0x025 ITEM_TRADE_MYLIST. None of those six opcodes exist in ffxi-proto today.
Evidence (line numbers in kuluu-render/src/hud/mod.rs drift — that file is under active edit):
- kuluu-render/src/hud/trade.rs:302 — spawn_trade_window builds the 4x2 grid (TRADE_COLS=4/TRADE_ROWS=2 at :12-13), Gil cell, OK/Cancel; update_trade_window at :388; registered in hud/mod.rs:200 (init_resource), :206 (add_message), :288 (update), :416 (spawn)
- kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:1107-1109 — TargetActionId::Trade opens the window via TradeState::open(e.id)
- kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:972 — selecting a grid slot is a stub: '[trade] Item placement not wired yet — gil-only for now'
- kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:965 — gil max is hardcoded `let snapshot_gil = 0;`
- kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/mod.rs:977-982 — OK writes TradeIntent::Confirm and prints '[trade] Trade sent (gil only; outbound 0x036 pending consumer)'; that chat string names the wrong opcode and should say 0x032/0x034/0x033
- kuluu-render/src/hud/trade.rs:131 — TradeIntent has only MessageWriters (text_input.rs:84,796,887,977,988,994) plus the add_message registration; zero MessageReader in the repo
- ffxi-proto/src/map.rs:386-388 — the crate's 0x032/0x033/0x034 are s2c EVENT/EVENTSTR/EVENTNUM; no trade c2s constants and no 0x021/0x022/0x023/0x025 s2c constants
- vendor/server/src/map/enums/packet_c2s.h:48-51 and packet_s2c.h:48-51 — authoritative opcode assignment
- vendor/server/src/map/packets/c2s/0x032_trade_req.h:26-31, 0x033_trade_res.cpp:48-77, 0x034_trade_list.h:26-32, 0x036_item_transfer.cpp:73-79 — NPC vs PC counterparty resolution

title: Nameplate billboards
description:
Nameplate billboards. Retail sizing settled by reversing (2026-07-31); the previously recorded curve was wrong in both model and arithmetic.

RETAIL MODEL
Nameplates are **screen-space pre-transformed quads (RHW = 1) at constant pixel size** — never world-space quads. Glyph size is `XRes * 0.0023437501 * nameScale`.

`nameScale` ramps linearly over **fixed-point NDC depth**, not world distance:
  Distance = trunc(z_ndc * 4096)
  Distance <  0xFB4  ->  scale = 1.0
  Distance >= 0xFB4  ->  scale = (0x1004 - Distance) / 80      (quantized in 1/80 steps)

With retail's projection (near 0.1, far 65535) that is `clamp(0.049922 + 5.120008/d, floor, 1.0)`: flat out to ~5.46 yalms, then falling. The `> 0x1004` cull is unreachable in practice.

The floor is **0.0625**, not 0.05 — CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:261-263 rejects `z >= 1.0`, so the largest drawable Distance is 4095.

EVIDENCE
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Rendering/Active/CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:31 (`ActorNameScreenScale`), :47-81 (FixedPointScale 4096, NDC store), :90-100 (the 0xFB4/0x1004 ramp), :276-277 and :391-394 (screen-pixel quads, RHW=1) — tier 2
- research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Game/GameManager.cpp:789-801, 2234-2239 — near 0.1 / far 65535, the only assignments in the tree — tier 2

CORRECTION: the previously recorded "0.104x at 50 yalms" divergence ignored our own MIN clamp. The real ratio is **0.189x**.

ALSO IN SCOPE (same file, tier 2, small)
Target-name alpha **pulse**: `sin(frame * 16deg) * 32 + 96`, plus the depth-cull / margin pass — CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:100-113, 614-628. We have no pulse anywhere in nameplate*.rs.
design:
- ffxi-viewer-core/src/nameplate_billboard.rs: rewrite distance_to_scale (:258); delete QUAD_BASE / MIN_QUAD_WIDTH_YALMS / MAX_QUAD_WIDTH_YALMS (:18-21); switch sizing at :213-216 to a screen fraction; add &Projection to the query at :154.
- BAKE retail's near=0.1 / far=65535 as named consts. Do NOT read our own camera projection — the graphics view-distance preset (ffxi-viewer-core/src/graphics/settings.rs:496-590) would otherwise move the ramp with the user's setting, which retail never does.
notes:
Self nameplate implemented + runtime-verified (round2/self-nameplate.png: 'Verilamp' plate in chase cam, PC styling; hidden in first person). Remaining bead scope: retail distance-to-scale curve tuning.
Nameplate alpha pulse folded in: sin(frame*16deg)*32+96 on the target name, plus the depth-cull/margin pass. research/XIClient/.../CXiActorNameDraw.cpp:100-113, 614-628 (tier 2). No pulse exists in our nameplate*.rs today.
2026-07-31: sizing half implemented in 1bc4bbf (NDC-depth ramp, baked near/far, pulse added). Depth ramp runtime-VERIFIED (own plate constant px, distant plate shrinks). The target-lock alpha pulse is UNVERIFIED - Tab kept selecting an off-screen NPC, so no pulsing plate was ever on screen. Keep open for the pulse.

title: Weaponskill chain UI
description:
Weaponskill chain UI — WS dispatch and the WS-finish animation are wired; the skillchain *message* never renders because the scraped msg-id table has no 288-303 entries

Re-grounded 2026-07-31: two claims from the 2026-06-14 grounding are wrong today.
1. The weaponskill animation IS wired — not through ffxi_actor_render::action_routine (which maps only the *start* categories and is the cast-pose path), but through the effect-DAT path: scheduler_runtime::action_dat_file_id maps category 3 (weaponskill finish) to weapon_skill_file_id = FFXiMain.dll per-race base + the skill's animation index, and dispatch_motion_stages drives the routine's Motion stage into FfxiRenderActor::begin_completion_motion.
2. A skillchain proc message does NOT 'render generically' — nothing renders. LSB encodes the element in the message id itself (recordSkillchain: addEffectMessage = 287 + effect, 384 + effect when absorbed), so ids 288-303 are the sixteen skillchain lines, and msg_basic.h contains no entries in 288-305. MSG_BASIC is scraped only from that header, so template_for_id misses and build_battle2_line drops the line. The discarded 6-bit proc_kind is redundant for the text; it is the element hint retail uses for the skillchain burst VFX/colour.

Remaining work: source the missing battle-message text (a retail DAT message table, or an explicit TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES block for 288-303/384-399), then decide whether proc_kind is needed for the burst effect.

- kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:3947-3955 — proc block decode: has_proc(1), `let _proc_kind = br.read(6);`, proc_info(4), proc_value(17), proc_message(10); layout matches vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x028_battle2.cpp:167-174

title: Write a viewer-compatible patch.ver after a native update
description: ffxi-install's updater leaves patch.ver absent (it sends a zero version block, which the server labels 'empty', so updates still work). PlayOnline Viewer stores its version string encrypted in patch.ver: polcore.dll (1.18.15e, sha 73b1864b) FUN_1004a0e0 decode / FUN_10049e00 encode, 0x120-byte buffer, 64-bit block cipher FUN_10007bc0 (key schedule) + FUN_10008000/FUN_100080c0 (rounds, sbox .data 100715e4), key = FUN_1004a090 byte-sum hash of the registry SOFTWARE\PlayOnline(US)\Interface\%04d string (FUN_10049f80) plus the title index (FUN_10049f60). Implement encode (and decode for reading an existing viewer-written patch.ver) so an install updated by Kuluu is also accepted by the official viewer, and so the version block sent in the type-7 frame matches what the viewer would send. Decompiled C is in artifacts/polre/decomp/polcore/ (gitignored).

design: Reuse the cited-path extraction in run_comments; capture the next whitespace-separated token; skip tokens that are English words (reuse the KEYWORDS idea from the /tmp resolver); grep -F in the resolved file.

title: Skinned models do not receive point-light shadows (per-model uniform has no clusterable id)
description: zone_ffxi.wgsl receives Enhanced point shadows through the clustered loop (light_id -> shadows::fetch_point_shadow). skinned_ffxi.wgsl lights actors from FfxiLightingUniform's nearest-N point slots (retail's per-model D3D light binding), which carry position/colour/attenuation but no clusterable index, so a lantern's shadow falls on the deck and walls but not across a character standing in it. Option: walk the fragment's cluster list in the skinned shader and match each uniform light by position (within epsilon) to recover the id for fetch_point_shadow; or carry the id in the uniform by resolving entity -> GPU index (bevy_light prepare_lights order).
notes:
Landed: kuluu-render/src/point_shadow.wgsl (kuluu_render::point_shadow::point_shadow_factor) walks the fragment's cluster point-light list, matches the per-model slot to its clustered light by world position (both packed from the same ZonePointLight.world_pos, pinned by zone_point_lights test packed_slot_position_is_the_spawned_light_s_translation), and samples fetch_point_shadow when the light carries POINT_LIGHT_FLAGS_SHADOWS_ENABLED_BIT. skinned_ffxi.wgsl applies it per slot inside scene_irradiance, gated by the Model Shadow Receiving flag (flags.z), no floor (matches zone_ffxi.wgsl). Registered via load_shader_library in FfxiMaterialPlugin.

Evidence: (1) zz-character-shadow-repro modes point / point-off / point-unshadowed: skinned plate band behind the blocker 87 vs lit 164-168; receive off or shadow map off -> 168 (no change). (2) zone-render-headless --pc placement in Selbina (file 348, hour 22, --enhanced-lights 2): two Humes in line from the counter lamp; enh vs enh --no-receive differs only on the far character (14.8k px, max 150) where vanilla vs vanilla --no-receive differs by 488 px (moon). Crop: far character's back goes dark behind the near one with receive on.

Harness flags added: zone-render-headless --npc <file> x y z yaw, --pc <race> x y z yaw (needs --sky; grounds on MZB, prints nearest lamps), --no-receive. Not done: the realistic (flags.y) branch shares the same path so also shadows; no perf read taken on a crowd (per in-range slot: one cluster walk + PCF fetch).
close_reason: Landed in 0818919e: point_shadow.wgsl resolves the per-model slot to its clustered light by position and samples the cube map; skinned_ffxi.wgsl applies it per slot under Model Shadow Receiving. Verified by the synthetic repro (band 87 vs lit 168) and a Selbina two-character A/B (receive-only diff on the far character).

title: Actor-local screen billboards leave the DAT template unflipped — verify against an asymmetric actor sprite
description: After the world-space fix, the two billboard paths disagree on the template's vertical sense: world-space folds (x,-y,-z) into the template before the view rotation; actor-local computes rot = parent_rot.inverse() * cam_rot so the parent's basis cancels and the raw DAT template reaches the screen with +y up. One of them is mirrored relative to retail. Pick an asymmetric actor-attached sprite (a rising fire spell flame, or the hi12 ribbon used by an action routine) and compare with retail/xim (research/xim Particle.kt computeParticleSpaceOrientationTransform, Matrix4f.axisBillboardInPlace; xim's Vector3f.UP is (0,-1,0)). Fix whichever side is wrong and pin it.

title: Sub-area interior DATs: their auto-run particle generators are never spawned (unverified)
description: zone_particles.rs reads only the main zone DAT (effective_zone_file_id). sub_area_activation.rs swaps interior blocks in from other DAT files via LoadMzbRequest, and research/xim Scene.kt SubAreaManager.update calls registerEffects() on the activated sub-area, i.e. retail/XIM run the interior's own auto-run generators (hearths, lamps) while it is active. Unverified here: whether the shipped sub-area files carry auto-run generators at all, and whether their base positions are in the same zone frame. Survey first, then extend the spawner to the active sub-area block and despawn on retire.

title: Zone-static life==0 auto-run generators outside weat/ are drawn by nobody (wind sheets, distant lamp glows)
description: zone_particles.rs takes only timed (max_life_frames > 0) auto-run generators; dat_mzb.rs takes uv-scrolling model-spawn singletons (sea/river sheets); zone_clouds.rs takes weat/ canopies. The remaining life==0 auto-run singletons outside weat/ are 18,866 corpus-wide (survey 2026-09-09, 298 zone DATs) and no module draws them. Selbina (file 348) examples: t_se/effe/wind/wi01..wi35 (static 'wind' MMB sheets, additive), t_se/effe/ligh/lt15..lt17 (far harbour/lighthouse lamp glows, D3m ltcu). Retail runs them like every other auto-run generator (XIClient XiZone.cpp InitWeather / CYyGenerator flags & 0x1000). Related: kuluu-zi3t covers the weat/ side of the same split.
acceptance_criteria: Selbina wind sheets and lt15-17 glows render; sea1/sea2/scol are not double-drawn with dat_mzb's water; canopies stay with zone_clouds.

title: Remaining per-frame render costs after the Selbina pass: skins upload, clustering, per-material specialization scans
description: From the post-fix Selbina idle sample (20s): upload_ffxi_shared_buffers 107 (re-encodes every skin and instance buffer each frame; dirty ranges would cut it), prepare_clusters_for_gpu_clustering 132 + upload_view_gpu_clustering_buffers 34 + bind groups ~40 (7 point lights; consider a smaller ClusterConfig, and confirm the minimap bake camera is inactive between bakes so it does not add a view), check_entities_needing_specialization<M> for 7 material types ~350 total (par_iter task fan-out per material type per frame — mostly thread wake overhead), update_actor_mesh_aabbs 36-67, upload_zone_material_buffers' remaining ~60 samples are the unconditional per-frame lighting write_uniform. None is a regression; listed so the next perf pass starts from numbers.

title: bevy_ui per-frame O(nodes) systems over ~1300 pre-spawned chat spans
description: Selbina idle sample (20s): ui_layout_system 253-287, ui_stack 63-81, update_clipping 56-79, prepare_uinodes 58-73, ui_picking 66, measure_text 39-60, ui_focus 36, extract borders/bg ~70 — together ~0.5ms/frame, now the largest single-system cost after the shadow fix. The chat log pre-spawns 3 panels x EXPANDED_ROWS(24) x (1 Text + SPANS_PER_ROW(16) TextSpan) = ~1200 text entities that bevy_ui walks every frame whether or not the panel is shown (kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs spawn_chat_panels). Options: spawn rows for the visible panel only, size SPANS_PER_ROW to what segment_line actually emits, or despawn rows past the compact window until expand.

title: Self walk-toggle moves at 1/4 base speed; retail's walk is 1/3
description:
kuluu-render/src/combat_stance.rs WalkMode::WALK_SCALE is 0.25 and is uncited. Retail says one third in two independent places: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp ControllableActor::AdjustAnalogKeyLength quantizes the analog magnitude to 0.33333334 for the walk band (and that same factor scales the movement vector, so it is the speed, not just the gait flag), and research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/BaseActor.cpp BaseActor::GetWalkSpeed returns field_98 / 3.0f.

kuluu/src/view_native/input.rs already carries the correct constant as WALK_SPEED_DIVISOR = 3.0 with that BaseActor::GetWalkSpeed citation, but applies it only to the locked-on backpedal in move_step_speed_yps; the forward case multiplies by walk_scale (0.25) instead. Two walk speeds in the same function, one cited and one not.

Beyond the raw speed being wrong, 1/4 breaks the animation contract in kuluu-di0c: retail plays the wlk clip at 3r, so r = 1/3 is exactly where the clip runs at its authored 1.0x. Walking at 1/4 base speed guarantees foot-slide by construction even once rate scaling lands.
acceptance_criteria: WALK_SCALE removed in favour of the existing WALK_SPEED_DIVISOR (or a single shared const), so self walk speed is base/3 on both the forward and backpedal paths. Guard test pins the two paths to the same walk speed.

title: Hoist consts that the literal-naming pass had to define one layer up into their domain crates
design: From kuluu-9qzz: kuluu-mcp SEND_FLAG_NAME and kuluu-session's bare 0x08 -> make ffxi-proto decode/entity.rs SEND_NAME pub; kuluu-render look_resolver EQUIP_SLOT_ID_MODEL_MASK and kuluu-session lobby_client's repeat -> ffxi-proto GRAP_ID_MODEL_MASK pub; ffxi-event runner DMSG_MAGIC_BASE/DMSG_OFFSET_XOR -> ffxi-dat dmsg.rs MAGIC_BASE/OFFSET_XOR pub; kuluu-render CIB_MOTION_INDEX_NONE -> ffxi-dat cib.rs; kuluu-render NGX_FAIL_PLATFORM_ERROR -> kuluu-dlss-nr FAIL_PLATFORM_ERROR pub; kuluu-snapshot NAMEVIS_HIDE_NAME ideally ffxi-proto (kuluu-snapshot has no ffxi-proto dep, so decide the dependency direction first). Each is a contract between modules and should have one emitter per AGENTS.md.

title: Actor contact eligibility predicates (dead, mounted, fading, GM)
description:
Retail's CheckContactActor filters the candidate list before picking the nearest actor (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ControllableActor.cpp ControllableActor::CheckContactActor). We implement the nearest-actor scan and the block/expire rule but only two of the filters (EntityKind::Other is skipped, and an actor with no drawn mesh is skipped).

Retail additionally skips:
- self at GM level >= 3 - no actor collision at all
- ActorType DOOR / LIFT / MODEL (we approximate with EntityKind::Other)
- actors whose GameStatus is N_DEAD or B_DEAD - corpses do not block
- actors with face-slot equip id in 50..=59
- actors with FadeAlpha < 1.0 - still fading in
- actors flagged by the chocobo/mount virtuals (VirtActor201 / VirtActor204)
- a Telemetry/ServerID high-byte condition

The dead-actor case is the most player-visible: a corpse blocks in Kuluu and does not in retail. WorldEntity (kuluu-render/src/components.rs) carries no status today, so this needs death state plumbed into the obstacle rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: A dead mob does not block movement; a fading-in actor does not block.

title: Generator::parse masks its size byte with 0x0F while every other DAT section walker uses 0x1F
design: Surfaced by the kuluu-9qzz literal-naming pass: ffxi-dat/src/generator.rs Generator::parse uses SETUP_SIZE_NIBBLE_MASK (0x0F) on the setup record size byte; generator.rs section walkers and particle_gen.rs use SIZE_WORDS_MASK (0x1F). Either the setup record genuinely has a 4-bit size (then document via research/XIClient CYyGenerator citation) or it is a latent truncation for setups >= 16 dwords. Check research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Generator/CYyGenerator.cpp and a DAT survey before changing.

title: Directory-scoped resource resolution residuals: mmbs/seps/keyframes/images still last-writer-wins; zone/weather generators collect defs without their directory
description: kuluu-ua36 added d3ms_by_dir / sprite_sheets_by_dir to ActionAssets (resolve order effect dir -> root -> global per research/xim ParticleLinkedDataProviders.kt:171-215, link resolved against the DEF's own localDir per ParticleInitializers.kt:145). Still flat, last-writer-wins: mmbs, seps, keyframes (particle_sim.rs keyframe()), and images/images_by_name/images_by_qualified_name. zone_particles.rs::zone_static_defs and weather_particles.rs still collect defs by chunk name without directory, so resolve_mesh cannot use the dir tier for them. Extend the (dir, name) keying to those maps and thread the def directory through the zone/weather collectors.

title: audio.rs Now-playing BGM line is client telemetry emitted on the system channel
description: kuluu-render/src/audio.rs (~:505) emits 'Now playing: <track> by <composer> [track #N, slot=...]' via ToastEvent::system, so it prints in the player chat log. Retail has no now-playing chat line. Same class as the seven emitters kuluu-ka0m routed to ToastEvent::debug (dev-HUD only). Decide: debug channel, or gate as enhanced. hud/auction.rs:1013 and kuluu/src/view_native/screenshot.rs:55 also use ::system but read as deliberate player feedback; leave them.

title: decode_palettized ignores ColorFormat/BitDepth and the trailing DXT fourcc
description: Found while widening extract_texture_tokens for kuluu-tm7m. ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs decode_palettized always reads 8-bit indices behind a 1024-byte BGRA palette at PALETTE_OFF. research/XIClient (pinned aba6c816) GameTexture.cpp:249-285 branches on ColorFormat and, inside Indexed4Bit/Indexed8Bit, on BitDepth: Indexed8Bit skips 512/768/1024 palette bytes for BitDepth 16/24/32 (:266-270), Indexed4Bit 32/48/64 (:254-258), Direct16/24/32 carry no palette (:274-282); GameTexture.cpp:291-300 re-points PixelData past a trailing DXT fourcc. Now that 0x81 Imgs are accepted, the ~269 Indexed8Bit 0x81 Imgs with a trailing DXT3 marker (install census on vendor/game-files) hit this gap. Mirror the XIClient branches and pin with a real-DAT test.

title: No client log line for a successful outbound c2s 0x01A action send (opcode/action_id/target)
description: Observed 2026-09-08 during kuluu-x2vk live verification: the only evidence that /ra sent the right packet was the server's reply text. Add a tracing line (debug level, target e.g. c2s_action) at the 0x01A send site in kuluu-session recording action kind, action_id and target, so log-only verification can confirm the packet went out.

title: scene_summary reports HP/MP 24% while the HUD shows 100%
description: Observed 2026-09-08 during kuluu-x2vk live verification: the agent-socket snapshot's scene_summary text repeatedly reported 'HP 24%, MP 24%' for Verilamp while the on-screen HP bar was full. Likely a stale or mis-sourced field in the scene_summary builder (kuluu-session or kuluu-mcp). Check which SessionState fields feed it versus the HUD's self panel.

title: Casting reconcile follow-ups: paralyze mid-cast misclassified (a), recast-down gear not modeled (b), non-magic categories on optimistic timer (c)
description: Carried out of kuluu-iy4y (closed after live verification 2026-09-08). (a) vendor/server/src/map/action/interrupts.cpp:289-325 MagicParalyzed pushes MagicFinish (SkillInterrupt anim, IsParalyzed2) before the sp* MagicStart; our handler ends the cast on the MagicFinish and reports SelfCastEnded{interrupted:false}. Needs decode_battle2_header to surface ActionAnimation::SkillInterrupt / the battle message for magic categories; confirm against a live paralyze first (no GM command found to apply Paralyze locally). (b) base recastTime gate over-blocks a hasted caster because recast-down gear is not modeled (session.rs spell_recast_until). (c) SkillFinish 3 / AbilityFinish 6 / RangedFinish 2 still fall back to the optimistic lock timer; fine while the bar is spell-only.

title: Pin retail's item-name green for drop/obtain chat lines via retail-observe
description: Follow-up carried out of the closed treasure-pool epic kuluu-k3gm. kuluu-render/src/hud/chat_panel.rs:561 hard-codes the item-name green as sampled from the user's 2026-08-03 drop screenshots (a JPEG/scaled sample). Pin the exact RGB from a lossless retail capture via the retail-observe skill (and, if the retail Font Colors config page exposes it, from that page's default), then replace the sampled constant and record the observation under .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/.

title: Event VM: 0x12/0x13 rand opcodes unimplemented (deferred from the arithmetic family for sweep reproducibility)
description:
0x12 stores rand(), 0x13 stores rand() %% (operand+1) (research/XiEvents/OpCodes/0x0012.md, 0x0013.md). Both are work-slot writes like the rest of the arithmetic family implemented in kuluu-cjct, and were deliberately left out of that pass for one reason: ffxi-event has no RNG dependency, and adding real randomness makes zz-event-sweep non-reproducible, which would destroy the corpus baseline that is kuluu-u7r5 acceptance oracle.

Corpus frequency is negligible today (0x13 appears once in the spin tally, 0x12 not at all), so this is not blocking coverage -- but the ops are real and events that branch on them currently take a fixed path.
design: Take a seed on EventVm::start rather than calling a global RNG, so the host supplies session randomness while the sweep pins a constant. A small LCG in-crate avoids a new dependency; faithfulness here is about the distribution being non-degenerate, not about matching MSVC rand() bit for bit -- retail seeds from the clock, so no observable sequence exists to match.
acceptance_criteria: 0x12/0x13 apply their retail semantics; zz-event-sweep remains bit-reproducible run to run (seed fixed or injected by the harness).

title: Overlay search path in the launcher settings UI (Discord request)
description: Sir Youda (Discord, 2026-08-25) asked for 'an easier way to configure the overlays (like xipivot) in ui'. The machinery exists (kuluu-gp3s: pivot.ini auto-discovery, /overlay list|add|remove|clear|reset, persisted dat_overlays.json), but the only surface is the slash command. Add an overlay list panel to the launcher settings screen: show active overlays + source (discovered vs override), reorder/add/remove/reset. Wire through the same overlay_store + set_overlays path /overlay uses; remember the dual-wiring gotcha (apply at both DatRoot construction points).

title: TarutaruF face band overruns the real face block: faces 24-31 resolve to ranged-motion DATs (0 meshes, headless)
description: PC_MODEL_IDS (kuluu-render/src/look_resolver.rs) gives every race a 32-entry face band, but on a full retail install TarutaruF face ids 24-31 (fids 22984-22991) resolve to DATs containing bow/poi/lau/wee/kne ranged-motion clips, not face models - collect_skel_meshes()==0, so a TaruF with a stylist face >=24 renders decapitated. Retail's FTABLE also aliases TaruF face ids 16-23 onto the same physical files as 0-7 (e.g. fid 22960 and 22976 both -> ROM/51/63.DAT; face 22 was later patched to ROM/143/33.DAT), so TaruF effectively has 16 real faces + 8 aliases. Repro: cargo run -p ffxi-dat --example dat-face-survey. All other 7 races pass 32/32.
notes: Before clamping the band to 24 (or 16), verify against the authoritative source: PC_MODEL_IDS derives from xim EquipmentModelTable / FFXiMain.dll equipment lookup (cexi-docs reference/ffximain.md VA 0x100C513D area). If retail's own table says 32 for TaruF, retail is headless for those values too and matching it is the faithful behavior - in that case just keep the (now loud) unrendered warn and close. LSB caps creation faces at 15 so only stylist/GM values can hit this. Related: kuluu-39fi (Discord decapitation report; this is probably NOT that user's cause).
close_reason: Not a table bug: retail's own dll table gives TaruF a 32-entry face band and retail loads the same ranged-motion DATs for faces 24-31 (headless on retail too, verified via XIClient SkeletalMeshActor.cpp model-load loop + DAT survey). Parity says keep 32. Values are unreachable from LSB anyway (creation caps face at 15); kuluu now warns when such a file yields no meshes. Sweep evidence recorded on kuluu-39fi.

title: kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist ships a committed 58MB .wasm build artifact
description: git push warns: 'File kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist/kuluu-viewer-wasm-8f9ac8b0616aa839_bg.wasm is 58.46 MB; larger than GitHub's recommended 50MB'. trunk's dist/ output appears to be tracked in git; build artifacts should not be committed (and this one still carries the pre-rename kuluu-viewer-wasm name). Decide: gitignore kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist and remove from tracking (plain rm from index going forward — do NOT rewrite history), or justify why it is vendored. Check nothing (release.yml packaging, wasm relay docs) depends on the committed copy.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (e910d79b, dfea500d) after adversarial review (round-1 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Resolved on branch wt/kuluu-pjy0 (commits c46eff85, 50adab56). The three files under kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist/ are out of the index via `git rm --cached` — no history rewrite, files left on disk. Decision: not vendored, removed. Investigating turned up the actual root cause the bead did not name: the .gitignore rule intended to cover this was still on the pre-rename path `ffxi-viewer-wasm/dist/`, so after the crate rename `git check-ignore kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist/index.html` matched nothing and the directory was tracked with no guard. Repointed to `kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist/`.

Verified nothing depends on the committed copy. release.yml:281-290 and release-wasm.yml:50-58 both run `trunk build --release` in kuluu-viewer-wasm and only then zip the directory trunk just produced, and the committed dist is provably stale output rather than input: dist/index.html titles the app "ffxi-viewer" and preloads /ffxi-viewer-wasm-8f9ac8b0616aa839{.js,_bg.wasm}, while the trunk template kuluu-viewer-wasm/index.html titles it "kuluu-viewer" and contains no script tag (trunk injects the hashed names per build). A repo-wide grep for 8f9ac8b0616aa839 finds no other tracked reference; no wasm-relay doc points at the committed bundle.

Added a durable guard as rule 6 of scripts/checks.sh run_harness (the pure-shell stage pre-push and CI already run first): fail on any tracked path under a dist/ directory, and fail on any tracked blob over 50MB (GitHub's push-warning size; hard reject at 100MB), with sizes read from the index via `git ls-files -s | git cat-file --batch-check` filtered to blob modes so gitlinks for deinitialized submodules do not break it. Verified as a real oracle, not a name check: `git add -f kuluu-viewer-wasm/dist/` makes the stage exit 1 reporting all three paths plus the 61301583-byte blob, and it returns to exit 0 once untracked; running the stage with the threshold lowered to 1MB reports exactly .beads/issues.jsonl and vendor/bevy_pbr's stbn.ktx2, proving the size rule scans the whole index on its own. Largest remaining tracked blob is now 1.5MB. Also ran `bash -n scripts/checks.sh` and `cargo fmt --all --check` (both pass; no Rust changed). Not done: a local end-to-end `trunk build --release` to regenerate the zip, skipped because the Bevy wasm release build would hold the shared target dir for a long time — the CI-independence argument above is static.
Unknowns left open: No full `trunk build --release` was run locally to produce a fresh zip end-to-end (trunk 0.21.14 is installed, but a Bevy wasm release build would occupy the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR for a long time and contend with other agents). The CI-independence argument is static but decisive: both workflows bu | shellcheck is not installed on this host, so scripts/checks.sh was only syntax-checked with `bash -n` plus the live runs above. | No clippy/test run for any crate: the change touches no Rust (only .gitignore, scripts/checks.sh, and the git index).
close_reason: Landed on main e910d79b, dfea500d after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: kuluu-render wasm build broken: skybox/zone_texture not gated for wasm32 (8 E0433 errors)
description: cargo check -p kuluu-viewer-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown fails with 8 E0433s: camera.rs (crate::skybox::camera_far), graphics/settings.rs, nameplate_billboard.rs (crate::skybox::SKYBOX_RADIUS, crate::zone_texture::image_with_mips/TextureQuality), lib.rs:295. skybox/zone_texture appear to be native-gated modules referenced from un-gated code. Pre-existing before the widescan compass-pointer work (whose compass additions are cfg-gated correctly).
close_reason: Re-verified 2026-09-09 by an adversarial done-check: Fixed in commit 4f03d0b76873a510d56d43051dec215ae7846724 ("wasm: un-gate skybox/zone_texture, native-gate mount dispatch (fix the v0.5.0 wasm leg)"), landed the same day the bug was filed (2026-08-20). The blanket `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` gates were removed from the `skybox` and `zone_texture` module declarations in kuluu-render/src/lib.rs and from the `#![cfg(...)]` inner attribute in zone_texture.rs, since both modules compile cleanly on wasm32 (ffxi-dat is an unconditional dependency). The one genuinely native-only consumer, `look_resolver::dispatch_mount_models` (feeds the dat_mmb mesh loader, which wasm doesn't carry), was moved out of the shared systems tuple into its own `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`-gated registration. `ffxi-skin-probe.rs` got a wasm stub `main` for target-wide checks. Re-ran `cargo check -p kuluu-viewer-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` against the current probe checkout of main and it finished clean (exit 0, only unrelated dead-code warnings, no E0433s). Closing as already done.

title: Player-facing surfaces expose dev/agent verbs: Debug+Graphics root-menu entries, ~20 ungated dev slash commands
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. kuluu-render/src/hud/menu.rs:41-42 puts Graphics and Debug in the retail-styled root Command menu (retail has neither; Config is the retail home for options). kuluu-client/src/view_native/slash_commands.rs:823-953 registers ~20 dev/diagnostic commands in release builds (/load_mmb, /zonegeom, /weather override, /renderscale, ...) while only /wscan is #[cfg(debug_assertions)] (:676-682) - apply the same cfg consistently.
