TextureFiltering::Vanilla already exists (:462,491, used by Low/Medium). Add QualityPreset::Vanilla (retail-equivalent pipeline: no bloom/MSAA/aniso/CSM, retail draw distance) and make it the default; High stays one click away. DynamicLights (:88-117) is the model.

title: Persistent weather emoji glyph + vana clock default-visible are non-retail
description: Vanilla-parity audit 2026-08-19. kuluu-render/src/hud/weather_icon.rs:13-29 (spawned hud/mod.rs:126) draws a persistent modern-emoji weather glyph - retail's classic HUD has no persistent weather indicator and the glyphs are not retail art. hud/vana_clock.rs:18-22 VanaClockVisible defaults true (retail shows Vana time via Menu > Current Time only; /clock toggle exists). Default both hidden behind the Enhanced runtime toggle.

title: Agent socket snapshot command exposes no entity/widescan state — protocol-level verification of scene data is impossible headlessly
description: Found during kuluu-iw58 verification: AgentCommand::Snapshot (kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs) only re-emits Connected/StageChanged/PositionChanged/Diagnostics. The agent socket is a typed-event forwarder, and widescan (plus the full entity table) lives only on SceneSnapshot, which reaches the Bevy renderer or the opt-in --relay-listen websocket — never the JSON socket or kuluu-mcp resources. A verification that needs 'which entities/widescan entries does the session hold right now' has no headless readout and must fall back to screenshots. Options: extend Snapshot to dump SessionState (or add a scene_query command), or add an kuluu-mcp resource over the relay. Additive-only: AgentCommand/AgentEvent are extension surfaces.
notes: Evidence: artifacts/verify/snapshot_pre.json vs snapshot_widescan.json identical in shape while the map screen visibly held 16 widescan entries.

title: Audit launcher_ui despawn_ui loops for the recursive double-despawn WARN
description: launcher_backdrop's bare .despawn() loop flooded bevy_ecs WARNs at login (fixed with try_despawn, matching despawn_ingame_entities). ~12 launcher_ui screens (char_list.rs:171,305, graphics.rs:371, account_create.rs:179,274, server_edit.rs:291, change_password.rs:170, mod.rs:958, footer.rs:226, login.rs:446,551, server_select.rs:250) use the same for-e-in-query bare .despawn() shape. They are only buggy if the marker component sits on NESTED nodes (parent recursion frees children first); root-only markers are fine. Audit each screen's spawn site: marker on root only -> leave; marker on descendants -> try_despawn. Do not blanket-change without checking.

title: sub_area_activation retires interior collision a frame before the load is in flight
description: drive_sub_area_activation (kuluu-render/src/sub_area_activation.rs:167-183) retires ZONE_SLOT_SUB_AREA and then only WRITES a LoadMzbRequest message; the Task is not spawned until start_mzb_loads consumes it, so LoadMzbInFlight::any_pending() is false for up to a frame with the interior collision already gone. Not exploitable today -- that window is far below UNDER_FLOOR_RECOVERY_SECS and the first gated tick zeroes the debounce -- but nothing pins the retire->request->task ordering, and a future change that delays the spawn past 0.5s reopens the kuluu-0nnl roof snap through kuluu-mo4q's recovery system. Pin the ordering with a test that drives drive_sub_area_activation rather than fabricating a populated LoadMzbInFlight.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (9d0b64b0) after adversarial review (round-1 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Landed on wt/kuluu-oubj as 67caa73cb48b2fff778e7946ba4363c0637629c8. No production behavior change: the request-to-task segment DatOverlayPlugin already registered inline (drive_sub_area_activation -> dispatch_look_driven_models -> kick_load_mzb_tasks, inside an already-.chain()ed Update tuple) is now a named `dat_mmb::zone_load_dispatch_systems()` returning the same three systems .chain()ed, so the test can drive the one declaration production registers instead of re-typing the order. The new `sub_area_activation::doorway_tests::the_interior_load_is_in_flight_the_frame_the_shell_stops_colliding` builds a `Doorway::streaming()` app whose main collision block is the interior's shell placeholder (tri_sub_area = the interior id, the field is_suppressed_placeholder keys on), walks the player into the doorway rect, and asserts that in that single update the placeholder has stopped flooring the interior column AND LoadMzbInFlight::any_pending() is true - no fabricated in-flight map, and no frame with the floor gone and nothing streaming for ground_recovery_candidate (kuluu/src/view_native/input.rs:1416) to act on. The harness runs Update with ScheduleBuildSettings::ambiguity_detection = Error, so the declaration must order the segment rather than merely contain it. Verified as an oracle by two reverted mutations: moving kick_load_mzb_tasks ahead of the driver fails the any_pending() assert (and nothing else), and swapping .chain() for .into_configs() fails on the schedule ambiguity panic (that second mutation did not fail before the ambiguity gate was added, which is why it is there). cargo fmt --check, clippy -p kuluu-render --all-targets -D warnings, and the full kuluu-render suite (lib 1035 passed, integration targets green with FFXI_DAT_PATH set) all pass. Caveat for whoever re-runs: the shared /tmp/kuluu-wt-target repeatedly served lib test binaries built from other worktrees, so results were only accepted from runs whose test inventory matched this tree.
Unknowns left open: The shared build dir /tmp/kuluu-wt-target is being clobbered between concurrent worktrees: cargo repeatedly served a kuluu_render lib test binary built from a *different* worktree's source (test counts 1037/1039 vs this tree's 1035, and this tree's new test missing from --list). Every result above w | The new test pins the ordering as declared in one ECS schedule run; it does not pin the FixedUpdate-vs-Update relationship, i.e. it cannot catch a future change that moves grounding into a schedule that interleaves differently with Update. | Retail grounding: none needed or claimed - this is an internal ECS scheduling invariant, matching the triage entry's retail_grounding: not_applicable.
close_reason: Landed on main 9d0b64b0 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Particle billboard bits 13/14 (planar/cylindrical/spherical) are not modelled
description: research/XIClient CMoElem.cpp:742-770 GetProcOrCModMatrix shows retail selects the planar/cylindrical/spherical billboard view matrix from bits 13 and 14 of the billboard word; ffxi-dat's ParticleBillboard::Xz is retail's cylindrical case. Every Camera generator in zone DATs 100-500 has both bits clear, so this does not affect the kuluu-fjd3 fix -- but the modelling gap is real and should be closed by anyone touching billboard modes again. Found during the kuluu-fjd3 remediation census.

title: Particle meshes sort in the transparent pass from the world origin, not the particles
description:
Every particle generator's mesh entity is spawned with Transform::IDENTITY and its vertices baked in world space (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs spawn_zone_particle_generator / rebuild_mesh). Bevy's Transparent3d phase sorts by the entity's world translation, so every particle mesh in a zone sorts as if it sat at (0,0,0) -- all of them at the same wrong depth, and wrong relative to any other alpha-blended geometry.

This is a real latent defect in the sort key, but it is NOT the cause of the Valkurm 'unblended tiles' it was filed for. Verified 2026-08-08 in Valkurm Dunes (zone 103, DAT 203) with a weather A/B from a fixed camera: the hard-edged polygons (green cliff-top patch, sand wedges) are present identically under DUST_STORM and under weather NONE -- mean absolute difference over the artifact region is 4.2/255 versus 7.6/255 scene-wide for the dust tint alone. Artifacts: artifacts/verify/dust-final-b.png, artifacts/verify/nodust-same-spot.png. The terrain artifact is tracked separately.
notes:
Candidate fix: put the generator origin in the entity Transform and emit vertices relative to it, so the sort key tracks the emission. Camera-relative generators rewrite that origin per frame already.

No user-visible symptom is currently attributed to this -- it needs a scene with two overlapping particle populations at different depths to demonstrate. Do not fix speculatively without one.

title: Celestial 0x4E/0x4F tint tables come from the first generator in the file, not the active weather's moon
description:
sprite_sheet::extract_celestial_color_tables walks the whole DAT and takes the day-of-week (0x4E) and moon-phase (0x4F) tables off the first generator that carries each. In file 201 that is weat/fine/moon/kasa (the lunar halo), whose tables differ from the moon sprite's own:

  kasa  dow[1] = (0.50,0.50,0.20,a0.16)   phase alpha 0 except frames 5/6/7
  moon  dow[1] = (0.50,0.46,0.27,a0.50)   phase alpha 0.42, 0.50 at frame 6

so the hand-authored moon disc is tinted with the halo's table. Both are also per-weather. Scope the scrape to the active weather's Moon-attached SpriteSheet generator (the one with moon_phase_sprite set), the way celestial_particles::collect_celestial_defs already scopes the billboards.

The halo's phase-alpha column is itself a retail detail worth keeping: kasa only appears around the full moon (frames 5-7).

title: [bug] Lens-flare texture (kasa) still carries the DXT3 alpha dither
description:
kuluu-u5mm resolved FFXI's stored 4-bit alpha dither for the cloud canopy, star dome and moon sheet. The lens-flare texture was measured as affected but NOT fixed: weat/<tag>/kasa is 128x128 DXT3 whose alpha is 100% the nibble 7/8 dithered-opaque pair (dat-sky-alpha-histogram on zone file 331). Unlike the canopy it loads through particle_sim.rs -> dat_d3m::decoded_texture_to_image, which applies apply_ffxi_alpha_remap directly and has no undither hook.

Whether it is actually visible depends on how large the flare is drawn — it is a camera-facing billboard, so at full bloom it magnifies like the canopy does. Confirm visually before spending effort.
design: ffxi_dat::texture::resolve_dxt3_alpha_dither already exists, is public, and self-validates its precondition (declines non-nibble alpha), so this is a call-site addition in dat_d3m::decoded_texture_to_image or a sky-specific variant of it — the same shape as zone_texture::decoded_sky_texture_to_image. Note dat_d3m's converter is shared with all D3M particle textures, so a blanket application there is wider than the sky.
acceptance_criteria: Either the flare renders with no per-texel stipple at its largest on-screen size, or the bead is closed with a screenshot showing the dither is not visible at the sizes the flare is actually drawn.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (57820042, 164af15f, f8c8d334) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
CLOSURE RATIONALE + RE-SCOPE (needs writing into the bead by whoever updates beads; I did not run any bd command).

What the bead asked for vs what is true:
- The bead names the LENS FLARE and its `kasa` texture. Two corrections from the retail DATs. (a) `kasa` is the LUNAR HALO sheet, not the lens flare; the lens flare proper is the screen-space lf0x chain owned by lens_flare.rs. (b) The lens flare cannot carry this defect at all: on files 210/331/201 lf01/lf02/lf03 are 128x256 Bgra32 with distinct_alpha=1, a=255 everywhere (verified with `cargo run -p ffxi-dat --example dat-sky-alpha-histogram -- 210 331 201`). There is no DXT3 nibble dither in the flare sheets to resolve - the bead's premise does not apply to the flare.
- The sheets that ARE dithered under weat/<type>/ are `kasa` (128x128 Dxt3, 100% the nibble 7/8 pair) and `moonshap` (256x256 Dxt3 nibble ramp). What shipped routes the celestial (Sun/Moon-attached) generator set through a sky-specific D3M converter so those sheets are undithered before `apply_ffxi_alpha_remap`, mirroring zone_texture.rs and moon_material.rs:131 (kuluu-u5mm).
- `kasa` still binds no texture today: on file 210 the `kasa` generator is mesh_kind=StaticMesh mesh_id=`moon`, the MMB `moon` carries an empty texture name, and the sheet that actually holds `kasa` (chunk `molf`, cat="moon" id="kasa") is referenced by no generator. The lunar halo therefore draws untextured, and the bead's named sheet remains unfixed by construction. FOLLOW-UP BEAD suggested: "Lunar halo (`kasa`) binds no texture - wire the molf sprite sheet to the weat/<type>/kasa generator", area sky/celestial, enhanced=no (vanilla parity), evidence: kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs resolve_zone_mesh (MMB path uses mmb.texture_name, which is empty for `moon`).

Acceptance criterion, second path, now satisfied with evidence: rendered f_ro (file 210) headless through the real sky pipeline (`kuluu-render/examples/zone-render-headless --file 210 --sky --hour 3 --cam 0 250 0 --tgt -636 886 0 --cap 120`, FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS=1, 1280x1280) twice, once with the undither and once with `spawn_celestial_set` reverted to `ZoneGeneratorOptions::default()`. The DAT moon draws ~90 px across from a 256x256 sheet (minified ~3:1) and the two frames are indistinguishable - mean |dI/dx| inside the lit crescent 9.139 vs 9.142. Conclusion to record: at the size the celestial billboards are drawn today, the DXT3 alpha dither is NOT visible; this change is a correctness alignment (the D3M path now agrees with the moon-material and zone-texture policy on the same sheets, and is armed if the halo is ever wired up or drawn magnified), not a user-visible fix. Screenshots at /tmp/celestial_fix.png and /tmp/celestial_plain.png (6x crops alongside); note they live in /tmp, not the repo.

Scope caveat to record with it: the whole changed path is behind the opt-in FFXI_DAT_CELESTIALS gate (celestial_particles.rs:33-37), so a default build is unchanged. Also, our celestial billboard scale is itself an open question (memory note 'celestial-are-dat-particles': MMB billboard scale is the open blocker), so the "not visible" measurement is conditional on that scale.

Review findings 1, 4, 5 fixed in f845e91e (end-to-end test through spawn_celestial_set with both links mutation-checked, DXT3_ALPHA_DITHER_STEP exported from ffxi-dat and imported, unverified "at or below 1:1" doc claim removed). Finding 2 refuted: dat-sky-alpha-histogram does report lf01/lf02/lf03 (they sit under weat/<type>/); the original commit's attribution stands and the reproduction is recorded in f845e91e's message.

Incidental fix included: `zone-render-headless --sky` panicked before drawing a frame because `sync_weather_particles` now takes `Res<HudPanels>`, which the example never inserted; the example now inits it. Anyone using that harness on main today hits the same panic.

Tooling hazard worth a bead of its own: the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/kuluu-wt-target served a stale kuluu-render lib-test binary across several `cargo test` invocations - 1037 tests reported green while newly added tests were not in the binary at all (confirmed with `--list` and `strings` on the test executable). CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 forced a correct rebuild. Any agent verifying with that shared target dir can get a false green.
Unknowns left open: The visual check used our client's celestial billboard scale, which memory ('celestial-are-dat-particles') records as an open blocker (MMB billboard scale). If that scale is wrong and retail draws the halo/moon much larger, the 'dither not visible' conclusion would need re-taking at the corrected si | The bead's named texture `kasa` still binds nothing: on file 210 the `kasa` generator is mesh_kind=StaticMesh mesh_id=moon, MMB `moon` carries an empty texture name, and the sprite sheet holding `kasa` (chunk `molf`, cat=moon id=kasa) is referenced by no generator. So the lunar halo's own sheet neve | Whether any non-celestial D3M particle sheet is ever drawn magnified enough to show its stipple is still unsurveyed; the doc now says so rather than claiming otherwise. | Why the reviewer's run of dat-sky-alpha-histogram on 210 emitted only three lines with no lf rows is unexplained (different DAT install or truncated output); my run on the vendored retail install emits them.
close_reason: Re-scoped and closed 2026-09-09: the lens-flare lf0x sheets carry no DXT3 dither (a=255 everywhere, dat-sky-alpha-histogram on files 210/331/201) and 'kasa' is the lunar-halo sheet, so the bead's premise was wrong; the undither call-site wiring for celestial sheets landed and is pinned end-to-end. See notes.

title: /check: print the target's title in chat (<Name>'s title: <Title>)
description:
Retail prints the checked PC's title as a chat line on /check — 'Zanon's title: Royal Cavalier' (retail capture 2026-08-04, HorizonXI). We already decode the id: s2c 0x0CA INSPECT_MESSAGE DesignationNo lands in ffxi_proto::decode::InspectMessage::title, but nothing consumes it because no title-name table exists.

Needs: a title-name source. LSB ships no title strings (they are client-side DAT text), so this likely means locating the title DialogTable in the retail install and reading it with ffxi_dat::dmsg, then plumbing title -> AgentEvent::CheckMessageReceived -> a chat line.
acceptance_criteria: Checking a PC with a title prints "<Name>'s title: <Title>" in chat with the resolved title text; a target with no title prints nothing.
notes:
Audit 2026-08-19 (ready to implement): Bead is current: s2c 0x0CA is decoded (ffxi-proto/src/decode/inspect_message.rs:44 fills `title` from DesignationNo) but the session handler at kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:1336-1344 drops it — AgentEvent::CheckMessageReceived carries only name+message, and no title-name table exists anywhere in the tree. One bead assumption is WRONG and the audit corrects it: the titles DAT is NOT the DialogTable format ffxi_dat::dmsg parses. It is file id 55704 (POLUtils ROMFileMappings.xml, Menu:StringTables > Menu:English > Menu:Titles, line 3087), resolving to ROM/180/78.DAT in the local install, in the d_msg fixed-block format (POLUtils DMSGStringTable3.cs + Things/DMSGStringBlock.cs): "d_msg" magic, 0x40 header, u32 bytes-per-entry at 0x20 (256 here), u32 entry count at 0x28 (1149); per block an i32 string count (bit-flipped when negative), (offset,flag) u32 pairs, strings at block offset 28+off, XOR 0xFF when bit-flipped. Verified end-to-end against the install: entry 230 = "Royal Cavalier", matching both the bead's retail capture ("Zanon's title: Royal Cavalier") and LSB vendor/server/scripts/enum/title.lua:231 ROYAL_CAVALIER=230; entry 0 = "N/A" (the no-title sentinel). Fix: (1) new ffxi-dat module (e.g. src/dmsg_table.rs) parsing the d_msg fixed-block table, re-expressed from vendor/POLUtils/PlayOnline.FFXI/FileTypes/DMSGStringTable3.cs and Things/DMSGStringBlock.cs (cite both), exporting a TitleDat::open(&DatRoot) + name(title_id) API; export from src/lib.rs. (2) ffxi-dat/build.rs: extend the existing ROMFileMappings scrape (pattern at build.rs:224 parse_string_dat_table) to emit a TITLES_FILE_ID const from the Menu:StringTables/Menu:English/Menu:Titles rom-file id — no hand-copied 55704. (3) kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs: add a lazy TitleResolver cloned from cfg.dat_root, exactly following the EmoteTextResolver pattern (mod.rs:64-80, constructed at mod.rs:355, threaded into handle_sub_packet like the resolver params at mod.rs:596-600); in the s2c::INSPECT_MESSAGE arm (mod.rs:1336) resolve m.title and, when title != 0 and the lookup succeeds, additionally send AgentEvent::ChatLine with text format "{name}'s title: {title}." on ChatChannel::System (same channel as the examine line built at mod.rs:4750-4780); title 0 / unresolvable / no DAT root prints nothing. Keep CheckMessageReceived, state.rs, and the wire snapshot untouched — the ChatLine event reaches both the native HUD chat log and the headless JSON stream, satisfying acceptance with minimal surface.

VERIFY: Unit tests: (a) in the new ffxi-dat module, synthetic-block tests for both the plain and bit-flipped (XOR 0xFF) encodings, plus a truncated-header rejection; (b) an install-gated guard test using the existing ffxi_dat::open_test_install() self-skip pattern asserting TitleDat entry 230 == "Royal Cavalier" and entry 0 == "N/A" (pins the LSB title-id <-> DAT-index correspondence, citing vendor/server/scripts/enum/title.lua:231); (c) a session-side test on the extracted title-line formatter asserting the exact "<Name>'s title: <Title>." text and that title 0 yields None. Runtime evidence (optional but cheap via the verify skill): on the local LSB stack set a test char's title (LSB !addtitle/charvar or direct chars.title in MariaDB), /check them from a headless session and observe the ChatLine event in the JSON stream; /check a fresh title-0 char and confirm no line.

title: Change Map floor list counts POLUtils maps, not the zone's DLL records
description:
change_map_targets (hud/map_screen.rs) still builds the floor list from ffxi_dat::map_image::map_count_for_zone, while load_viewed_map now resolves the chosen ordinal against MainDll::zone_maps. The two counts agree for 178 of the 195 zones present in both tables; where POLUtils lists more (e.g. zone 238 lists 3, the DLL has 2), the extra Change Map row previews blank instead of being absent.

Fixing it means threading a MainDll (or a precomputed per-zone count) into change_map_targets, which is a pure fn also called from the client's key handler (kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/map_screen.rs) — hence deferred out of kuluu-bqm5, which fixed the live-map defect.
acceptance_criteria: The Change Map list shows exactly the maps the zone's DLL records describe; no row previews blank.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (357e249a, fc8f5e73, 425521df) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Roster source settled: the Change Map list is now built entirely from FFXiMain.dll's zone-map table (MainDll::zone_map_counts), with negative keys skipped because the field is signed (research/xim ZoneMapTable.kt, next16Simgned -> next16Signed). Measured on the local retail install: 384 keys total, 231 non-negative (max 291), 153 negative (0xFF07..0xFFFF); POLUtils names 197 zones, misses 36 that ship maps, and names 2 (14, 77) the DLL has no record for. Every record under a non-negative key resolves through VTABLE/FTABLE, so no offered row can preview blank.

ffxi_dat::map_image::zones_with_maps was deleted (last caller gone) so the wrong roster cannot be reintroduced; map_count_for_zone remains and its doc now names all four ways POLUtils disagrees with the DLL.

Latch fixed rather than documented away: MapCalibration is now re-armed in view_native::insert_dat_roots alongside SpellSuffixCache, so a settings DAT-path change reloads the DLL and rebuilds the catalog (previously it would have rebuilt from the previous install's DLL). Anyone adding another latched DAT cache should add it in that one function.

Residual gap worth a follow-up if anyone cares: retail's own Change Map roster was never observed on the real client (no retail-observe session), so the acceptance oracle used is "every row resolves the way load_viewed_map resolves it", not "matches what retail displays". Also unexplored: what the ~153 negative-key rows are for.
Unknowns left open: Roster facts were measured against the one retail install at vendor/game-files (HorizonXI-era client). Zone counts asserted in the real-DAT tests (238 -> 2, 50 -> 2, 157 -> 6, 77 -> 0) are era-specific; a different client build could shift them, though those tests self-skip without an install rather | Not observed on the retail client itself: whether retail's own Change Map list offers exactly the 231 non-negative DLL keys. The grounding used here is internal-consistency (the list must offer only rows load_viewed_map can resolve) plus the DLL table + xim's reader, not a retail screenshot. | Zones 14 (Hall of Transference) and 77 (Nyzul Isle) have POLUtils map DATs but no DLL zone-map record, so they are no longer listed. Why the DLL omits them (instanced/dynamic maps?) is unverified; a POLUtils-built row for them previewed blank, so dropping them is at worst neutral. | The negative-key band was only checked for 'is not a zone id the server sends'. What the client actually uses those ~153 rows for (their file ids mostly do not resolve on this install) is unexplored.
close_reason: Landed on main 357e249a, fc8f5e73, 425521df after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Item drop lines show the display name, not retail's lowercase log name
description:
Retail's chat log uses an item's LOG name, which is lowercase for common nouns: XiPackets quotes 'You find a fire crystal on <name>.' and the 2026-08-03 screenshots show 'a lizard tail' / 'a pair of bounding boots'. Kuluu renders ffxi_proto::item_names (LSB item_basic, prettified to 'Fire Crystal'), so the line reads 'You find a Fire Crystal on the Rock Lizard.' — right content, wrong case.

Simple lowercasing is wrong: proper nouns keep their case ('an Emperor's Ring'). The log name is its own string. ffxi-dat's item_dat string-table probe returns a single string per block on this install, so where the singular/plural log names live is unresolved — POLUtils exposes LogNameSingular/LogNamePlural, which is also what the 0x25/0x27/0x2A inline tag kinds select between.
acceptance_criteria: A drop line reads 'You find a fire crystal on the Rock Lizard.' with retail's casing, sourced from the DAT rather than case-folded.
close_reason: Implemented in the 2026-08-19 audited bead batch; full fmt+clippy+test gate green (2672 tests incl. live integration suites against the running LSB stack); adversarially reviewed (one kzxp regression caught and fixed with a pinning test).

title: weat/ cloud canopy variants beyond cld1/cld2 are drawn by nobody
description: zone_clouds::build_cloud_layers renders only CLOUD_CANOPY_GENERATOR_NAMES = [cld1, cld2]. weather_particles::is_precipitation excludes the same two plus every life==0 sheet, so per-weather canopy variants such as La Theine weat/rain's ~4cl overcast sheet are excluded from both modules and never reach the screen. The follow-up note in zone_clouds.rs pointed at kuluu-nfrp, which is closed.

title: weather_opacity covers 4 of 20 weather tags; the rest fall to a flat default
description: zone_clouds.rs weather_opacity matches fine/suny (0.35), clod/mist (0.70), rain/thdr (0.90) and defaults everything else to 0.50. Now that all 20 ids resolve to distinct tags, 14 of them land on that default -- including the storm family (squl, stom, bliz, bolt) where the function's own comment says the tuning should be 'clear sparse, storm dense'. Deliberately NOT invented as part of the table fix: the comment notes cloud generators ship no 0x63 alpha keyframe, so coverage cannot be read from the DAT and every value here is a hand tuning. Needs a retail-observe pass to set them from what retail actually looks like per weather rather than by guess.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 20 tags has a value justified by an observation record, or the default is documented as deliberate for the remainder.

title: Live fixtures should skip on an unhealthy DB, not just an unreachable port
description: Live-server fixtures self-skip on TCP reachability only, so a reachable-but-saturated MariaDB (ERROR 1040 Too many connections) FAILS instead of skipping. This is not theoretical: five of six kuluu-5725 slice reports asserted the gate was red on this basis when it was in fact green, and the executors spent verification effort proving a phantom pre-existing failure. Skip on a successful handshake, not on a successful connect.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (170ed21a, 5b07dc09) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Review finding on the ERR-packet citation resolved in f2aab94a. Half of it was right and half was not, which is worth recording so it is not re-litigated:

- The mariadb.com /kb/en/ protocol namespace was reorganized, but the old URLs 301-redirect to the new /docs/server/reference/clientserver-protocol/... pages. They resolve; they are not 404s. Verified with curl for /kb/en/0-packet/, /kb/en/err_packet/ and /kb/en/mariadb-error-code-reference/.
- The genuine defect was that /kb/en/0-packet/ (i.e. the packet-header page) was cited for the ERR-packet layout it does not describe. That page covers only the 4-byte header; the 0xFF tag, u16 error code and conditional SQL-state field live on the separate ERR_Packet page.
- The no-SQL-state-before-handshake rule that err_packet() actually relies on is not stated by either MariaDB page - the ERR_Packet page only says SQL state is present "if next byte = '#'". The rule is stated by mysql_async 0.37 src/conn/mod.rs:894-898, which is also the code the test drives, so that is now cited alongside the two spec pages.

Rule of thumb this suggests: when a citation covers a multi-claim comment, check that the cited page carries every claim, not just the first one. A resolving URL is not evidence that it says what the comment says.

No behavior change; the xidb_conn() self-skip classification and its four tests are untouched and still pass.
Unknowns left open: The first full `cargo test -p kuluu-session` run hit `error: extern location for rustls does not exist: /tmp/kuluu-wt-target/debug/deps/librustls-*.rlib` during doctests. This is a shared-target-dir race with the other agents using /tmp/kuluu-wt-target, not a code defect - rerunning `--doc` alone re
close_reason: Landed on main 170ed21a, 5b07dc09 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Make the decode/ const narrowing principled where it sizes a public field
description: 7facf48's rule was purely compiler-driven, which produced an arbitrary public surface for one shape: two narrowed consts still size PUBLIC array fields -- 'pub num: [i32; Self::NUM_COUNT]' (messages.rs:32/41) and 'pub linkshell_name_raw: [u8; Self::LS_NAME_LEN]' (equip_inspect.rs:47/59). It compiles and no out-of-crate consumer breaks, but an external reader cannot name the length of a field they can see. Four siblings in the same shape stayed pub only because kuluu happened to name them. Pick a rule -- either a const that sizes a pub field stays pub, or the field stops being pub -- and apply it uniformly.

title: Delete PosHead::decode_char_npc and re-baseline the decode test-name invariant
description: After 962643c the function reads in full: 'let head = Self::decode(body)?; Ok((head, head.bt_target_id))'. It adds no name a reader lacks -- bt_target_id is already a public field of the returned struct -- and rg proves zero production callers workspace-wide (definition plus two tests). Correct diagnosis, deliberately wrong wave: deleting it removes decode_char_npc_extracts_claim_id and decode_char_npc_unclaimed_yields_zero_claim, which trips the exact test-name invariant every p52e slice was gated on, and it is a public-API deletion. Do it as its own commit with an explicit re-baseline.

title: PosHead::try_extract_name has no branch for LSB's 0x44 dynamic-entity name write
description: LSB writes the CHAR_NPC name at three offsets: packet 0x34 (vendor/server/src/map/packets/entity_update.cpp:371 and :429), packet 0x35 when targid < 1024, and packet 0x44 on dynamic-entity first spawn (targid >= 0x700). try_extract_name covers only the first two. Fails safe today -- LSB's 0x44 branch writes UpdateFlags = 0x57, clearing UPDATE_NAME, so our flag guard returns None first -- but trusts, fellows and dynamic NPCs therefore render nameless until a later update takes the isRenamed branch. Found by protocol-conformance-reviewer while auditing 962643c; pre-existing, not introduced by the wave.
close_reason: Re-verified 2026-09-09 by an adversarial done-check: Already fixed. This bead (filed 2026-08-01) describes the same defect as kuluu-g0z3 (filed 2026-08-04), which landed in commit 32a9c3a874a336f8b5a301b45a6046ee87de1e39. `PosHead::try_extract_name` (ffxi-proto/src/decode/entity.rs:175) now branches on all three LSB name-write offsets -- 0x34, 0x35 (targid < 1024 rename), and 0x44 (dynamic-entity first spawn, targid >= 0x700, mask 0x57 with UPDATE_NAME clear) -- with the 0x18 spawn marker guarded against its `loc.p.moving` offset collision. Five unit tests exercise the new branch and its edge cases (`try_extract_name_reads_the_dynamic_entity_spawn_slot`, `_dynamic_slot_needs_the_name2_flag`, `_falls_back_when_the_long_name_marker_is_moving_data`, `_ignores_look_bytes_on_a_plain_equipped_spawn`, `_char_npc_renamed_low_targid_shift`), all passing. Closing as a duplicate/already-resolved by kuluu-g0z3.</close_reason>

title: Agent socket: focus-free menu navigation (the last piece needing real keystrokes)
description:
After kuluu-0pof (movement) and kuluu-wwwv (capture), menu navigation is the only GUI verification surface still requiring the client window frontmost. The agent socket carries session-level AgentCommands, not key events, so the target-action menu, main menu, chat bar, and Tab-targeting can only be driven via osascript System Events — which steals the human's focus mid-session and is fire-and-forget (no confirmation a key landed).

Observed cost during kuluu-wwwv verification: Tab-targeting and Enter had to raise the window, and a keystroke intended to open the contextual menu instead re-targeted a different NPC, with no way to tell from the socket that it had gone wrong.

Proposal: extend the DebugControl bridge with menu/target intents — something like AgentCommand::DebugInput{ MenuUp/Down/Left/Right/Confirm/Back/TabTarget } feeding the same InputMode state machine real keys drive, so a driver can walk the menu stack focus-free and read the resulting InputMode back in the snapshot. Wider surface than debug_drive (touches hud/menu.rs, target_action_menu.rs, text_input.rs dispatch), so it wants its own design pass rather than being folded into a capture change.

Alternative worth weighing first: whether exposing the resulting InputMode + focused row in the wire snapshot is enough on its own — a driver that can SEE menu state may not need to drive it blind.
acceptance_criteria: A driver can open the target-action menu, move the cursor, confirm, and back out entirely over the socket, with the window unfocused, and read back which row is focused at each step.
notes: Follows kuluu-0pof (movement bridge, closed) and kuluu-wwwv (capture). /verify drive-gui.md documents the current keystroke fallback under 'What still needs focus'.

title: EphemeralChar fixture: reachable-but-broken DB fails tests instead of self-skipping
description: agent_session_drives_mcp_end_to_end fails with 'connection closed' when something accepts on 127.0.0.1:3306 but drops mid-handshake (half-up colima/lima LSB stack) — the self-skip only covers connection-refused. Treat early connection-closed/timeout during fixture provisioning as skip (server-unavailable), keeping real assertion failures fatal. Bit us 2026-07-31 during the perf-wave integration gate.
close_reason: Re-verified 2026-09-09 by an adversarial done-check: Already fixed — this bead is a duplicate of kuluu-yn60, which was implemented and closed on 2026-08-20 (commit 1bb78c4d, "tests: self-skip live fixtures when MariaDB accepts then drops"). EphemeralChar::create's xidb_conn helper now wraps the connect in a 5s timeout and maps both the accept-then-drop mysql_async::Error::Io class and a timed-out handshake to Ok(None) (self-skip), matching the existing connection-refused skip path, while other errors still propagate as fatal. All five live integration test entrypoints (agent_session, play_lifecycle, disconnect_recovery, zone_change, delivery_box_live) already destructure the Some/None and self-skip on None. Two unit tests (accept_then_drop_self_skips, refused_port_self_skips) pin both classes and pass locally. No further work is needed; close as duplicate/already-done.

title: CollisionBvh::from_world_triangles panics on empty triangle list
description: Found during kuluu-6ef7: from_world_triangles(vec![]) hits index-0-of-empty in patch_leaf_offsets (kuluu/src/view_native/collision_bvh.rs). Never hit in production because callers gate on non-empty geometry, but it is a landmine for tests and future callers — return an empty BVH instead.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (8fd04b82, c6527bc4) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Review findings addressed on branch wt/kuluu-u639 in commit 52ded482 (on top of the fix commit 8c58b21a).

Finding 1 was correct and is fixed: build_collision_bvh_system returns early both when mesh.indices() is None and when tri_count == 0, so an empty triangle list from a CameraOccluder mesh can never reach build_bvh_with_leaf_offsets. The only reachable empty-list caller is the zone path where camera_triangles() is emptied by the skip filter. Doc comment corrected.

Finding 2 was correct and is verified by mutation, not just by reading: stubbing out `patch_leaf_offsets(&mut bvh.nodes, 0, &mut offset)` leaves single_triangle_bvh_hits_at_the_brute_force_distance green, because build_recursive emits one leaf with left = 0 and the patch writes offset = 0 back. That test's claim is now weakened to "traversal agrees with brute force on the smallest non-empty build". The real oracle is the new multi_leaf_bvh_traversal_agrees_with_brute_force: 64 triangles on an 8x8 grid at z = 5 + gx + gy, asserted to exceed LEAF_THRESHOLD and to produce more than one node, with one +Z ray per cell compared against both the expected distance and ray_cast_brute_force (which indexes the reordered triangle array directly and so is independent of leaf offsets), plus an off-grid miss. Under the stubbed patch it fails 48 of 64 rays. This is the first multi-leaf offset coverage that does not require FFXI_DAT_PATH.

No production behavior changed by this commit; it is doc-comment accuracy plus test coverage. Full kuluu test suite (419 tests) and clippy -D warnings both clean with the retail DAT path exported.
close_reason: Landed on main 8fd04b82, c6527bc4 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

Faithful-preserving alternative: static per-generator quad mesh, per-particle motion evaluated in the vertex shader from a small per-generator uniform (time, seed, emitter params) — eliminates CPU rebuild + upload entirely. Follows Bevy 0.19's GPU-direction; keep the vanilla look pixel-close (compare against retail-observe references for fire/smoke).

title: Launcher decide_initial_screen blocks ~4.8s on the main thread
description: Attributed trace 2026-07-31: ffxi_client::view_native::launcher_ui::decide_initial_screen ran 2x totalling 4.78s wall inside OnEnter(Login) — a multi-second synchronous stall on the Bevy main thread at launcher entry (likely blocking I/O: keychain/network/DAT probe). Compile-verified; runtime observation next launcher run: password appears ~2s after screen instead of a 4.8s freeze.

title: Chase camera matches retail's reachable envelope but not its motion model
description:
After e48bb7f our camera reaches the same set of eye positions retail does, but it gets there differently, so the FEEL differs even though the geometry agrees.

Ours (kuluu-render/src/camera.rs chase_camera_system): a polar orbit. yaw + pitch + radius, eye = anchor + yaw_dir*(r*cos p) + Y*(r*sin p). Pitch is a first-class input.

Retail (research/XIClient/.../World/Camera/CameraManager.cpp):
- yaw is an orbit — RotateEyeAroundTarget(angle), :518, and the rate is
  normalised by distance so the on-screen swing rate is constant: :506
  angle = 6.0f / eyeToTargetDistance * angle.
- 'pitch' is not an angle at all — :527-529 does CurrentEyePosition.y += offset,
  a pure vertical translate at 0.10666667 per tick per analog unit. The
  horizontal offset is untouched, so the eye->target distance GROWS as you tilt.
- the distance is then a SOFT SPRING, not a clamp: :822 pulls in by
  (d - 6) * 0.012 per tick when past 6, :815 by (d - 100) * 0.5 past 100, and
  :830-846 push back out to 3 (3D) / 3 (XZ). So the camera can transiently sit
  well past 6 while you hold the tilt and then drift back in.
- there is also a vertical eye standoff we do not implement: :960-975 clamps the
  eye to 0.17 below any ceiling within 10 up (VCalibrate2) and 0.17 above any
  floor within 10 down (VCalibrateUpsideDown). These are penetration standoffs,
  not containment — they will not rescue a camera that has already left a room —
  but they are what stops the eye rendering from inside a ceiling slab.

Observable difference today: hold tilt-up while zoomed in. Ours snaps the radius
out via orbit_radius(); retail eases out and then springs back toward 6.
design: Worth doing as one change, since the spring and the Y-translate are the same loop. Keep orbit_radius()'s envelope as the acceptance floor — whatever replaces it must not reintroduce a horizontal approach nearer than MIN_XZ_STANDOFF (that regression is what kuluu-64fh was).
acceptance_criteria: Tilt is a vertical eye translate, not a pitch angle; distance is a spring toward DIST_MAX rather than a hard clamp; orbit_never_trades_retails_horizontal_standoff_for_height still passes.

title: Retail BGM selection: battle music on party-claim proximity, day/night by Vana'diel hour
description:
Retail triggers battle music when **any party-claimed** actor is within 45.0 yalms — not just when you personally are engaged. The day/night music slot is chosen by `gamehour < 6 || gamehour >= 18`, not by sun altitude.

kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:225-236 uses self-engagement only, and :269 uses `sun_altitude < 0.0` even though vana_time.rs already exposes the clock.

EVIDENCE: research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/World/Actor/ActorTelemetry.cpp:37, :1717-1723; Game/GameManager.cpp:1611-1618 (tier 2).
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (38f10ba5, 3f3b71be, 8dc68f52) after adversarial review (rounds: needs_fix, needs_fix, approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
2026-09-09 round-2 review fixes, worktree /tmp/kuluu-wt/kuluu-cq2w, commit f26a688d "Model NormalMusicPlay's fishing early return and name its BGM slots (kuluu-cq2w)".

Landed:
- audio.rs `resolve_audible_slot` now models GameManager.cpp:1597-1599. Retail's fishing branch does `if (MusicBuff[7] == 0) { return; }` - it holds the currently playing track instead of descending to the battle/day-night slots. Our loop fell through, a divergence that only became reachable when commit 4293491d promoted fishing above battle. It now returns `slots.active` when FISHING_SLOT is eligible and its track is unset or 0; `bgm_swap_needed` compares track ids, so this is a genuine no-op transition. Test `fishing_without_slot_track_holds_current_track` covers unset slot, explicit 0, and active==None.
- audio.rs play_index values are named consts: ZONE_DAY_SLOT 0, ZONE_NIGHT_SLOT 1, BATTLE_SOLO_SLOT 2, BATTLE_PARTY_SLOT 3, RIDING_SLOT 4, DEAD_SLOT 5, MOG_HOUSE_SLOT 6, FISHING_SLOT 7. Grounding read first-hand this round: GameManager.cpp:1584-1619 for the branch order, 0x00a_login.cpp:177-181 for MusicNum[0..4] (day/night/GetSoloBattleMusic/GetPartyBattleMusic/mount), zone.h:500-501 for m_bSongS/m_bSongM. The candidate-table comment now also records that the battle branch itself is XICLIENT_CODE_MISSING at GameManager.cpp:1603, so party-over-solo is an LSB reconstruction, not an XIClient reading.
- nameplate_color.rs comment rot fixed at the three sites that asserted the GM lookup runs after the allegiance block (fn doc ~:276, inline ~:292, BELLIGERENT_* const doc ~:64). The GM rows were hoisted into `pre_claim_color` (:391-395) and now run before it; retail tests them at ActorTelemetry.cpp:1663-1668, between the allegiance write (:1638) and the claim branch (:1678). Same colour either way for a GM, so no behaviour change. The claim that "every later check overwrites that white" was additionally narrowed: it holds for the belligerent *player* (base allegiance is always PLAYER, charentity.cpp:127), but an unclaimed belligerent *mob* keeps kuluu's mob row where retail leaves white - already pinned by `belligerent_allegiances_fall_through_to_the_kind_colour`, now stated honestly in the comments.

Not coded, unverified inference to carry forward: ActorTelemetry.cpp:1562 returns from NameColorSet when AUDIT_120.BIT_9 == 0, so a plate-suppressed actor never raises SomeMusicByte. kuluu-snapshot::Entity::name_hidden() (lib.rs:394, VIS_HIDE_NAME 0x08) exists and `is_party_claimed` ignores it. BIT_9 is not confirmed to be that flag; if someone confirms it, `is_party_claimed` should gate on name_hidden too.

Verification: cargo test -p kuluu-render 1050 unit + 15 integration passing (recompile confirmed from this worktree's path), clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean, scripts/checks.sh style clean. No live-server run this round.
Unknowns left open: ActorTelemetry.cpp:1562 `AUDIT_120.BIT_9` is not confirmed to be VIS_HIDE_NAME (0x08). If it is, `is_party_claimed` should also return false for `entity.name_hidden()`, since retail's early return means a name-suppressed actor never raises SomeMusicByte. Left uncoded as an unverified inference. | Shared-target-dir hazard hit here: the first clippy run failed with `cannot find function extract_lens_flare_sheet` pointing at an ffxi-dat/src/sprite_sheet.rs:322 that does not exist in this worktree (ours is :262) - kuluu-render compiled from this worktree but linked a stale ffxi-dat rmeta left by | The fishing hold-current path is unit-tested but not runtime-verified against the live LSB stack (no server session was driven for this round).

title: Litigate: numeric KO homepoint countdown is Vanilla or Enhanced (+ 0x00A DeadCounter)
description:
hud/death_prompt.rs renders a `Home Point in M:SS` line driven by the 0x037 char_status decode (dead_counter1 @0x38, gated on hpp==0; SessionState.death_homepoint_secs -> wire snapshot). Retail shows the **homepoint menu**, not a visible numeric clock — so this may be an Enhanced addition wearing Vanilla clothes.

Decide and label it: either confirm retail surfaces a countdown somewhere (keep as vanilla) or flag it `enhanced` and gate it behind the feature flag per the AGENTS.md parity rule.

Second, smaller item in the same area: the `0x00A LOGIN` `DeadCounter` (body offset 0xA0, same encoding as 0x037) is not decoded. It only matters when zoning in while still KO'd — without it the countdown starts blank until the next 0x037.

title: Death corpse pose loops instead of playing the collapse once and holding
description:
Retail plays the death collapse motion ONCE and holds the final corpse frame. Kuluu resolves the corpse pose to `cor?` (ffxi-actor/src/actor_state.rs:151, `dead && owner_is_none`) and registers it as a *looping idle*, so if `cor?` is a collapse motion it will replay forever instead of holding.

Unknown until a live run: whether `cor?` is a collapse motion (needs one-shot-hold) or already a static pose (no change needed). Retail reference: .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/death-ko-behavior.md

The faithful server signal is `animation == ANIMATION_DEATH (3)`. PC animation state IS now decoded (decode::NpcState::decode_char_pc, kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:848), so the trigger no longer has to lean on party-row hp alone.

title: MH-only MMB camera collision may now be redundant and diverges from retail's source
description:
camera_collides_with_mmb (ffxi-client/src/view_native/camera_collision.rs:20) forces MMB CameraOccluder BVHs on inside a Mog House. It came from 23c56cf / kuluu-da4e, which fixed the camera punching through the closed MH exit door.

Two reasons to revisit:

1. kuluu-da4e's own root-cause analysis prescribed a DIFFERENT fix from the one that shipped. The bead says the door is 'visible MZB geometry flagged doesnt-block-LOS, so it lands in the non-collision set and is excluded from the camera's zone BVH', and prescribes 'include the non-collision (camera_only) MZB geometry in the camera-collision BVH while keeping grounding/nav on collision-only geometry'. The commit instead special-cased MMB furniture in Mog Houses.

2. ab7258d (kuluu-0nnl) has since made MzbCollisionGeometry include every submesh regardless of the doesnt_block_los bit, and ZoneCollisionBvh is built from it. Zone 245's camera BVH went 42469 -> 48305 triangles, exactly the 5836 flag-0 submeshes. That IS the fix kuluu-da4e prescribed, arrived at from the grounding side.

So the MH door may now collide via MZB alone, making the MMB special-case dead weight. Retail's camera casts against the MZB collision grid only (XIClient CollisionManager over ZoneCollisionData; XIM Collider over zoneCollisionMap), so MMB as a camera source is a divergence either way.

Caveat before deleting anything: retail's KO_LineCollision DOES have a Mog House branch — research/XIClient/.../CollisionManager.cpp:884 carries an unimplemented 'if (Placeholder::g_pYkMyroom)' stub. So Mog Houses are genuinely special in retail collision; we just don't know how yet. Do not assume the special-case is wrong, only that its current MMB implementation is not what retail does.

Task: re-test the MH door with MMB collision forced off now that camera_only MZB geometry is in the BVH. If it holds, remove camera_collides_with_mmb and the MMB BVH build gate; if it does not, document why and leave it.
notes:
RESOLVED — premise was wrong; the special case is justified, not redundant.

The claim was that ab7258d (kuluu-0nnl) had already brought the MH exit door into ZoneCollisionBvh by putting every MZB submesh into the collision set. It did not: build_collision_geometry consumes only MzbSubMesh/MzbInstance, and MMB static placements are a separate set — parsed from geom.mmb_spawns, spawned with entity_id: None, which is exactly what earns them CameraOccluder (dat_mzb.rs -> dat_mmb.rs). Nothing in the kuluu-0nnl change touches them.

Proven offline rather than argued: ffxi-viewer-core/tests/mh_collision_grounding.rs::mh_391_doorway_is_a_gap_in_mzb_collision sweeps 24 horizontal headings from the MH spawn anchor at head height against MZB-only collision for DAT 391. Result: walls on 23 of 24 headings (6.5-11.1 units, all vertical normals), and NOTHING on the 24th (yaw 0). That gap is the doorway. It reproduces commit 23c56cf's live finding ('rays toward the door found no hit, confirmed false even brute-force') without a running client, and it now fails loudly if the door ever does become MZB geometry.

Corroborating: research/XIClient CollisionManager.cpp KO_LineCollision carries an unimplemented 'if (Placeholder::g_pYkMyroom)' stub, so retail genuinely special-cases Mog Houses in collision — we just don't know how yet.

Also measured while here: Mog House DATs 391 and 356 contain zero camera-transparent triangles, so kuluu-eg5g's DoubleSidedSkipPolicy filter is inert inside a Mog House and cannot have changed this either way.

Left in place: camera_collides_with_mmb and its guard test. camera_collision.rs now documents that the gap is still open and that the MZB and MMB camera sources differ in policy (MZB filtered by double_sided_skip; MMB models carry no CollisionMeshHeader.Flags and are raycast whole).
close_reason: Premise disproved. The MH door is an MMB placement, absent from MZB collision — pinned by mh_391_doorway_is_a_gap_in_mzb_collision (walls on 23/24 headings, gap at yaw 0). The special case is justified; no code removed.

title: SFX stereo panning: place world emitters left/right from the camera
description:
kuluu-y00a gave world SFX distance attenuation but deliberately no stereo placement. audio.rs::sfx_attenuation is the sole loudness authority and PlaybackSettings::with_spatial(true) is intentionally NOT set, because rodio's Spatial (rodio-0.22.2 src/source/spatial.rs:56-67) applies its own per-ear (1/dist_sq).min(1) gain, which would stack a second distance law on top of ours.

Panning, if wanted, has to come from rodio's pan term ALONE — i.e. express the emitter relative to the CAMERA (the correct ear for left/right, unlike distance which is measured from the player) and neutralise the spatial distance gain, or hand-write a two-channel pan.

Also note SE entities get a static Transform and do not follow a moving emitter; fine for short swing SE, wrong for any long looping SE ever routed through this path.
notes:
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31 [proposed supersede]: Close as superseded by kuluu-96ev (P2, labels audio/roadmap/vanilla), which subsumes ebv4's entire scope with higher-authority evidence. research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Resource/Derived/CYySepRes.cpp:37-90 shows retail's Calc3D takes the vector from the CAMERA EYE to the emitter (CachedEyePosition - pos) with y scaled x3 in the default mode (mode 2 zeroes y, mode 1 leaves it unscaled), attenuates LINEARLY between near and far ((1.0 - (v10 - near)/(far - near)) * vol), multiplies by back_sound_rate in the back hemisphere, then transforms the emitter into view space and pans by projected screen X: ProjectionFocalLength / z * x / sound_width, clamped to +/-1, scaled by the caller's pan-width argument and offset to centre 64, finally clamped to 0..127. Constants at CYySoundElem.cpp:35-38: sound_near 3.0, sound_far 30.0, back_sound_rate 0.65, sound_width 512.0.

Before closing, carry two still-valid implementation notes into kuluu-96ev:
(1) rodio's Spatial applies a per-ear (1/dist_sq).min(1) distance gain (rodio-0.22.2 src/source/spatial.rs:63-64, applied at :66/:68) multiplied by its pan term, so PlaybackSettings::with_spatial(true) would stack a second distance law on whatever Calc3D-faithful curve we implement — panning must come from the pan term alone with the distance gain neutralised, or from a hand-written two-channel pan.
(2) An SE entity today carries NO Transform at all — kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:656-659 spawns only InGameEntity + AudioPlayer + PlaybackSettings::DESPAWN, and bevy_audio-0.19.0/src/audio.rs:250 requires just PlaybackSettings (the only #[require(Transform)] there is on SpatialListener at :171). Its gain is baked once at spawn from the emitter position (audio.rs:629), so it cannot follow a moving emitter; enabling with_spatial without also adding a Transform would trip the bevy_audio-0.19.0/src/audio_output.rs:131 warning 'Spatial AudioPlayer with no GlobalTransform component. Using zero.'. ebv4's wording 'SE entities get a static Transform' is wrong on mechanism (there is no Transform) though right on consequence — do not copy that phrasing forward.

Also worth fixing while the notes move: kuluu-96ev cites CYySoundElem.cpp:33-38 for the constants, which actually sit at :35-38, and cites kuluu-render/src/audio.rs:513-541 for the invented curve, which is now the comment block at :519-529 plus sfx_attenuation at :530-543.

title: Melee crit / additional-effect / spikes branches never fire — 0x11 is a comparison OPERATOR, not a context variable
description:
SETTLED for the implementable majority (retail reversing, 2026-07-31), by disassembling the routines out of the retail install itself (TIER 1: ROM/0/0.DAT), which is the oracle the research/ tier list points at where XIClient stubs the area.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG
0x11 is **not** a context variable. It is a **comparison-operator code** occupying the words==3 operator slot. The variables in play are field indices into the client's `BattleResult`:
  0x28 resolution · 0x2B info · 0x2D value · 0x2F proc_kind · 0x33 react_kind

ROUTINE STRUCTURE (retail bytes)
- `dada` -> { `atpr`, `crtl`, `dam0` }
- `atpr` dispatches on VAR(0x2F) = proc_kind over 1..23  (the additional-effect leaves)
- `dam0` holds two siblings under one block:
    * a spikes chain on VAR(0x33) = react_kind 1..10 -> `sb00` .. `sb09`
    * `react_kind == 0x3F -> cnt0`, whose **ELSE** branch holds the resolution chain. So on a counter retail runs **only** `cnt0`, suppressing `damg` / `sway`.

EVIDENCE
- TIER 1, independently re-derived twice: ROM/0/0.DAT chunks `dam0`@0x7F900, `crtl`@0x80070, `atpr`@0x80180, `dada`@0x81800
- vendor/server/src/map/enums/action/proc_kind.h:28-60 (1..23), react_kind.h:27-41 (1..10 + Counter=63), resolution.h:28-34 (0..4) — tier 2, pins the enum anchors
- vendor/server/scripts/globals/job_utils/corsair.lua:117-123 — d6 roll written to `action:info`, pinning 0x2B = info

LAND NOW (fully pinned)
`atpr` 23 additional-effect leaves; `sb00..sb09` spikes; cnt0-suppresses-reaction.

DEFERRED — see the two blocking sub-questions in NOTES.
design:
- ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:222, 302 — keep the 0x6B payload; expose 0x64/0x67/0x69/0x6A as StageKinds.
- kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:372-378 — replace the `has_control_flow -> continue` bail with an r0/r1/op evaluator; :944-952 delete hit_reaction_routine; :1037-1044.
- kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:3885-3893 — widen decode_battle2_header. The exact bit widths already exist at :3939-3964, currently `_`-discarded.
- kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:900-908 + kuluu-session/src/wire_translate.rs:316 — carry proc_kind / react_kind / resolution across the snapshot boundary.
notes:
TWO OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS (neither blocks the majority above)

1. What is comparison operator 0x11?  Retail bytes prove only that it occupies the words==3 operator slot.
   XIClient stubs it (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Game/Scheduler/Tags/0x6B.cpp).
   XIM disagrees and admits it: research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/resource/EffectRoutineInstance.kt:74
   -> `r0 == r1 // made up for now` (TIER 6, do not trust).
   `(r0 & r1) != 0` and `r0 >= r1` are indistinguishable from both live call sites.
   NEEDS: FFXiMain.dll disassembly of the scheduler condition evaluator.
   PRACTICAL UNBLOCK: implement as `(info & 2) != 0` for the melee case only — safe over the documented
   0..3 info range (research/XiPackets/world/server/0x0028/README.md:309-320, tier 3) — comment the
   uncertainty and do NOT generalize the operator.

2. What is VAR 0x3B (the `damh` vs `damg` selector)?
   Exhaustive scan: exactly 16 sites across all 52,576 retail DATs, always `if (0x3B == 1)`, never written.
   Absent from XIClient (no battle path), XiPackets (struct only), and cexi-docs.
   NEEDS: retail-observe capture of a melee log + video, correlating `damh` (target plays `chih` = `efhl`+`sehl`)
   against the packet; or the FFXiMain.dll condition-variable resolver.
   MEANWHILE: leave false (today's behaviour) behind a named const.

3. TIER-6 ONLY, verify before building: does VAR(0x38) == 2 mean "attacker is a PC" (the hi14-vs-hi29
   crit-particle selector)?  Sole source is research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/game/AttackContext.kt:91-93.
   VAR(0x38) is read exactly once in the entire ROM tree, so no corroborating usage exists.
   NEEDS: retail-observe — crit a mob as a PC vs. observe a mob critting you, compare the particle.

GUARD-TEST WARNING: the existing flat test at ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:748-758 cannot see the cnt0 /
resolution nesting and would keep passing through a wrong implementation. Add a nesting-aware test.
