title: Auto-attack rounds with multiple results stomp the single-slot ActiveScheduler
description: One 0x028 BATTLE2 carries up to 8 results per target, but decode_battle2_header reads only the first and ActiveScheduler is a single component slot, so a multi-hit round plays one swing routine. research/xim ActorRoutineQueue enqueues them serially at a playback rate derived from the attack interval (Actor.kt:858-871). Needs a routine queue component. Follow-up to kuluu-yjlf.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Verified (audit 2026-07-31). LSB side: vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x028_battle2.cpp:56-64 caps results at 8 per target, and vendor/server/src/map/entities/battleentity.cpp:2989-3001 packs an entire multi-swing round as repeated `list.addResult()` on ONE target block — the extra swings are extra RESULTS, not extra targets, so the queue is fed by re-walking the first target's result list. Client side: kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:3884-3893 keeps only `first_result`. Note the fix crosses the wire boundary too: kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:901-909 ViewerEvent::ActionStarted carries a single `result: Option<(u8,u16)>`, so a routine queue needs a per-swing list there as well. XIM confirmation for the playback rate: Actor.kt:859-874 derives it from the auto-attack recast / (totalAttacksInRound+1) clamped to 30..60 frames, and ActorRoutineQueue.kt:38-73 is an ArrayDeque that starts one routine at a time.

title: SfxEvent is non-spatial: SoundOnCaster vs SoundOnTarget indistinguishable at playback
description: ffxi-viewer-core/src/audio.rs SfxEvent carries only se_id + volume. dispatch_sound_stages resolves on_caster and drops it, so a victim's impact sound and the attacker's whoosh mix identically and distant swings do not attenuate. Needs an emitter (Entity or world position) plus spatial mixing; changes the mix for every existing caller (spells, footsteps, ambience), not just melee. Follow-up to kuluu-yjlf.
close_reason: Fixed in 51c862c: SfxEvent gained an optional emitter position (existing 2D UI callers unchanged by construction) and dispatch_sound_stages stopped discarding resolve_stage_to_se's on_caster flag — SoundOnCaster/SoundOnTarget now resolve their origin through ActionTarget, honouring the target_link_context flip. Gain is dry within 8 yalms then 1/r windowed linearly to zero at the LSB entity streaming radius, scraped at build time from zone_entities.cpp rather than hand-copied. Distance is measured from the player, not the chase camera (the LSB bound is player-to-entity, and a camera anchor swung SE loudness ~17 dB with the mouse wheel). Single loudness authority: rodio's Spatial would stack a second distance law, so with_spatial stays off — STEREO PANNING IS NOT IMPLEMENTED and would have to come from its pan term alone. Pinned by system-level tests that drive dispatch_sound_stages through a real App plus a real-DAT cull test. Live audio observation was blocked by a locked macOS session.

title: Melee: dual-wield/H2H swing routines (bti0/cti0/dti0) and movement-direction variants (atf0/atb0/atl0/atr0) unresolved
description: dispatch_melee_action_started falls back to ati0 whenever the AttackAnimation-specific routine is absent from the attacker's battle dirs. ROM/32/13.DAT (HumeM weapon-motion base, file 9672) has ati0/atf0/atl0/atr0/atb0/cn*0 but NO bti0/cti0/dti0 — research/xim Model.kt:284-291 getSubBattleAnimationDirectory uses a separate dual-wield offset DAT. Also, retail picks atf0/atb0/atl0/atr0 by the attacker's movement direction at swing time (Actor.kt:864-903); we always use ati0. Follow-up to kuluu-yjlf.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: DAT-verified (audit 2026-07-31): file 9672 resolves through VTABLE/FTABLE to ROM/32/13.DAT, whose `hm_b` directory holds routine chunks (kind 0x07) ati0/ati1/ati2/atf0/atb0/atl0/atr0/cnb0/cnf0/cni0/cnl0/cnr0/cnt0/atk0/in 0/in 1/out0/out1 — no bti0/cti0/dti0 (btl0/btl1 there are 0x2B animation clips, not routines). The off-hand dir is not merely unresolved, it is never loaded: kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:443 `let _ = sub_weapon;` discards it before :511-529 builds the single main-hand motion-DAT chain (combat_stance.rs:13-24 maps skel 7072 → base 9672), so the dual-wield offset table from research/xim Model.kt:284-291 has no caller yet. Precision on the fallback: scheduler_runtime.rs:1024-1027 tests the MERGED lookup (actor dirs + global ROM/0/0.DAT), not the attacker's battle dirs alone.

title: dispatch_action_started re-reads 3.3MB of VTABLE/FTABLE per action event on the render thread
description: kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs dispatch_action_started calls DatRoot::from_env_or_default() per event, which re-reads/parses all 20 VTABLE/FTABLE files (3,291,030 bytes; measured ~1.5ms warm-cache), then does a blocking std::fs::read + parse_action_bytes on a ~38KB DAT. Order 2-3ms per action on the render thread. Hoist DatRoot into a cached resource (same shape as MainDllCache) and move the read+parse to an AsyncComputeTaskPool task like the actor-load path. This is a frame hitch, not the timing drift (kuluu-k6tz).
notes:
VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Verified 2026-07-31, unchanged: kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:780 opens a fresh DatRoot per ActionStarted event, :786 does a blocking std::fs::read, :789 parses it, and the system is registered in Update at :1385. The 3.3 MB figure reproduces exactly — DatRoot::open walks 1..=MAX_ROM_INDEX (ffxi-dat/src/archive.rs:8,41-58) and the install's 20 VTABLE/FTABLE files total 3,291,030 bytes.

Two notes for whoever takes it: (a) the same per-event pattern also lives at scheduler_runtime.rs:1355-1366 load_emote_scheduler (called from dispatch_entity_emoted), so the cached-root fix should cover both call sites; (b) MainDllCache (:718-723) is used as a system `Local`, not a Resource — a Local is per-system, so a shared Resource (or the load_global_effect_dir task shape at :554-573) is the better hoist target.
2026-09-09 landed on main (24967b36, 64acd2fb) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Review follow-up commit e0b141f2 on wt/kuluu-mxfm.

Semantics decision worth recording: `ActionDatRoot(None)` now means "the host has no install" and reads nothing, rather than falling back to `DatRoot::from_env_or_default()`. Rationale is not only consistency with the other `*DatRoot` resources -- kuluu opens its root via `resolve_dat_root` (kuluu/src/main.rs:203) and the settings reload (launcher_ui/settings.rs:365) and calls `overlay_store::apply_saved` on it, so an env re-open would silently serve an overlay-less install, and on the startup path it would just re-run the call that already failed.

Second decision: `ActionMainDll` is now dropped on a DAT-root swap instead of being kept warm. The dll produces the *file id* (`base_weapon_skill_index`/`base_emote_index`); keeping it across an install change meant computing ids from the old install's tables and resolving them through the new root. Cost of the fix: for the frames between the swap and the new dll landing, weaponskill dispatch drops the event and emotes fall back to `play_local_emote_clip`. `ActionDatCache::adopt_root` now also clears `pending` for the same reason (deferred dispatches hold old-install file ids).

Ordering: `adopt_action_dat_root.before(poll_action_main_dll)` closes the same-frame cancel window; verified that Bevy 0.19 auto-inserts the sync point between explicitly ordered systems, so adopt's freshly spawned `ActionMainDllTask` is visible to poll rather than being removed by poll's queued `remove_resource`.

The dead-wiring class now has both halves pinned: kuluu-render `the_plugin_loads_the_main_dll_from_the_wired_root` (plugin registers the systems) and kuluu `insert_dat_roots_hands_the_scheduler_runtime_the_shared_root` (host wires the root).
Unknowns left open: The shared target dir /tmp/kuluu-wt-target intermittently produced an unrelated E0425 'cannot find function zones_with_maps in module ffxi_dat::map_image' at kuluu-render/src/hud/map_screen.rs:526 -- that symbol exists in this worktree (ffxi-dat/src/map_image.rs:28, added by 89367829 on main) and th | The new plugin guard test relies on `set_error_handler(ignore)` to tolerate the dispatchers' missing session resources. If someone later gives those dispatchers required params that panic outside the error-handler path, the test would need real resources instead. | Dropping ActionMainDll on adopt means a settings-screen DAT reload has a few frames where a weaponskill event is dropped and an emote plays the local clip. That is the deliberate tradeoff (correctness over warmth); it has not been observed live, only reasoned from the code.
close_reason: Landed on main 24967b36, 64acd2fb after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed and how it was verified.

title: Defer BATTLE2 damage/battle-message lines to the routine's 0x2B DamageCallback stage
description:
Retail appears to defer the damage number / battle message to a DamageCallback stage (opcode 0x2B) inside the effect routine. SOURCE CAVEAT: that semantic mapping currently rests only on research/xim (EffectRoutineParser.kt:219-222 -> EffectRoutineInstance.kt:956-959 invokeCallback), which is tier 7 and not trustworthy for predicates. The higher tier does not settle it: research/XIClient has the tag (Game/Scheduler/SchedulerTagCode.h:48 SCH_TAG_0x2B) but Tags/0x2B.cpp is `XICLIENT_CODE_MISSING`, so its behaviour is unrecovered. Retail-observe is still required before building on this.

What the retail install DOES confirm is the structure, not the meaning: ROM/0/0.DAT chunk `mdam`@0x81780 parses to exactly one stage with opcode 0x2B (plus the 0x01 prologue and 0x00 terminator), and the melee root `dada`@0x81800 carries its own 0x2B alongside its atpr/crtl/dam0 sub-routine links. Sampled spell DATs (ROM/10/9.DAT, ROM/10/10.DAT, ROM/10/18.DAT) each reference the ASCII id 'mdam' — a 3-file sample, not proof of 'every spell routine'.

kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:990-992 emits the decode_battle2_action chat lines the instant the BATTLE2 packet is decoded, so the damage line lands ~3.3s before the effect resolves.

CORRECTION to the original text: StageKind::DamageCallback parses (ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:156) and IS already consumed renderer-side — kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:1052 dispatch_damage_callback_stages, registered at :1401, landed in 9be628a (2026-07-24, kuluu-yjlf) — but only to start the victim's PendingHitReaction routine. There is no chat-line consumer and no floating-number widget anywhere in kuluu-render, so the deferral this bead asks for is unbuilt; the work is to add a SECOND consumer of the same stage, not to add the stage.

Cross-boundary: chat lines are produced session-side, the stage fires renderer-side. Needs (a) retail-observe verification of whether the CHAT LOG line — not just the floating number — is deferred, and (b) a fallback that flushes pending lines when no routine starts within a bounded time, or a dropped effect DAT swallows the battle log.

title: Effect routines: 0x3B/0x3C sub-routine calls must block the parent timeline
description:
research/xim EffectRoutineParser.kt:270-274 parses 0x3B/0x3C as LinkedEffectRoutine(blocking = true), and EffectRoutineInstance.kt:400 (`blockers += newSequences`) stalls the parent while blockers is non-empty (runEffects loops only while blockers.isEmpty(), :284; update() early-returns at :240). Confirmed at tier 2: research/XIClient Game/Scheduler/Tags/0x3B.cpp executes the child then `newTask->SetParentTask(schedulerTask); schedulerTask->SuspendTask();`, and ~CMoSchedulerTask resumes it (CMoSchedulerTask.cpp:320-321 `this->return_parent->ResumeTask()`); the non-blocking Tags/0x03.cpp just Executes with no suspend. (Tags/0x3C.cpp is XICLIENT_CODE_MISSING, so 0x3C == 0x3B blocking is still XIM-only.) flatten_routine (kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs:368-377) inlines a BlockingSubRoutine child at its call frame exactly like a non-blocking 0x03, so the parent's later stages never wait. StageKind::BlockingSubRoutine distinguishes them (ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:122,160 — kuluu-k6tz); the timeline model does not.

CORRECTED 2026-07-31 by direct retail-byte parse. The blocking chain is three tiers deep, and all three resolve today (RoutineLookup = spell DAT + actor + GlobalEffectDir, scheduler_runtime.rs:794-800, whose comment already describes it): Poison (file 3020 = ROM/11/93.DAT) main@6096 --0x3C 'shbk'--> the caster's shbk (ROM/27/82.DAT@6720) --0x3B 'wash'--> global wash (ROM/0/0.DAT@529584); Cure (file 2801 = ROM/10/9.DAT) main@3424 takes the same route via 'shwh' (ROM/27/82.DAT@6528). The impact is NOT small: 'wash' is not a single delay-0 stage — its section-2 bytes are `01 02 …` / `59 02 … dur 60` (AnimationLock) / `56 03 … dur 60` / `2e 02 … delay 60 dur 60` (MovementLock) / `00 02 …`, and the header's totalDelay field is 0x3C = 60 frames. That earlier reading was an artifact of the then-current 12-byte minimum stage gate (ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs@7edfc01:188 `if stage_bytes >= 12`), which saw only the 12-byte 0x56; 1918365 (2026-07-30) lowered it to 8 bytes. Faithful blocking would therefore stall Poison/Cure's main ~60 frames (~1s at 60fps) before its 0x53/0x31/0x03 tgt0/0x32 stages — sized work, not a rounding error, and semantically it is the retail post-cast animation/movement lock.

A naive 'shift downstream stages by the child span' is still an approximation that could over-delay branching routines: 0x64/0x67/0x69/0x6A/0x6B are now DECODED and DETECTED (ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs:27-31 named consts, :228 block-open/close delay forced to 0, :302-310 has_control_flow) and routines carrying them are skipped rather than inlined (scheduler_runtime.rs:369-376), but they are still not EVALUATED — a faithful port needs a real sequence tree.

title: Cast routine drops 0x75 SetModelVisibility (hwmg) — weapons stay visible while casting
description: research/xim: HumeM 7072 cast routines call SubRoutine hwmg, which in the global effect dir (ROM/0/0.DAT) is three 0x75 SetModelVisibility stages (hidden=1, slots 0/1/2 — hide main/sub/ranged while casting). ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs maps 0x75 to StageKind::Unknown, so the stages are parsed and dropped: a casting PC keeps its weapons drawn where retail hides them. Split out of kuluu-ky8c (929fd71), which landed the routine plumbing that now delivers these stages to the runtime. FIX: add StageKind::SetModelVisibility (slot + hidden flag from the stage payload) and honour it in ffxi_actor_render's equipment visibility.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: DAT-verified (audit 2026-07-31): ROM/0/0.DAT chunk `hwmg` (offset 0x81ac0, kind 0x07) is exactly three 0x75 stages — hidden=1 for slots 0,1,2 — and the payload has a fourth field the fix must carry: hidden(u32,+8) / slot(u16,+12) / ifEngaged(u16,+14). hwmg sets ifEngaged=1 for slots 0 and 1 and 0 for slot 2, and research/xim ActorModel.kt:276 (`if (override.ifEngaged && !engaged) continue`) skips such an override while the actor is not engaged — so StageKind::SetModelVisibility needs {slot, hidden, if_engaged}. Callers confirmed: file 7072 = ROM/27/82.DAT, dir hm_s, routines cabk/cawh/casm/canj/cait/cabl/cafa (+ the sh** twins), each a 0x03 SubRoutine naming hwmg. Fix-scope note: kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs has no per-slot equipment identity today — load_pc:476-491 flattens every equipment DAT's meshes into one `skel_meshes` Vec and ffxi-dat SkelMesh (skel_mesh.rs:90-94) carries only id/meshes/occlude_type — so honouring the stage requires tagging meshes with their source slot first.

title: StaticMesh particle texture resolves by 4-byte DatId, not by texture name
description:
ffxi-viewer-core/src/particle_sim.rs resolve_mesh StaticMesh (0x0B) arm resolves its texture via assets.images[d3m.texture_name[8..12]] — i.e. by the Img chunk's 4-byte DatId, a THIRD naming convention alongside images_by_name (local token) and images_by_qualified_name (namespace+local, added in kuluu-7jpq). It only works when the chunk DatId happens to equal the local name token. Same class of latent bug as kuluu-7jpq; should route through the qualified-then-local tiers instead.

Related: ffxi-dat texture::extract_texture_tokens accepts only type 0xA1 (imginfo::FLG_DXT), while research/xim TextureSection.kt:28 also accepts 0x91 and 0xB1. Any sprite sheet whose backing Img is a palettised 0x91 will still miss. Not the case for file 3020 (all four Imgs are 0xA1).
close_reason: Fixed in abe671f: the StaticMesh arm tiers qualified name -> local name -> DatId, mirroring the SpriteSheet arm, and extract_texture_tokens accepts the palette Img headers 0x91/0xB1 alongside 0xA1. Measured install-wide (file ids 0..=12000) with a probe that mirrors production (decode-gated, last-wins) and scores by RESOLVED CHUNK IDENTITY, not hit-count: 16,911 named d3m links, 16,787 resolved before / 16,898 after; VISUAL BLAST RADIUS = 324 links now draw a different image (a further 121 change chunk but decode to identical pixels), chiefly clod_a/t/str/hit/enw families; 75 of the 324 come from the flag widening alone. The DatId tier stays last because 3 links (file 173 cld1-3 -> clo1/kumori) resolve only that way. The widening also lifts SpriteSheet links, which have no DatId tier, from 3338 to 4236 of 4250. NOT DONE: a visual comparison against retail — the change is pinned by real-DAT tests but nobody has eyeballed the 324 changed effects (GUI observation was blocked by a locked macOS session).

title: Lamp fixtures don't read as light sources: overbright emitter path misses them
description:
ORIGINAL HYPOTHESIS DISPROVEN. There is no emissive/additive bit in the MMB material flags word. We decode two (ffxi-dat/src/mmb.rs:373-376): 0x8000 alpha-blend, 0x2000 cull-disable. XIM decodes the same two (research/xim/.../ZoneMeshSection.kt:79-80) and although its RenderState carries an additive blendFunc member (MeshBuffers.kt:33), ZoneMeshSection.kt:130 never sets it.

CONFIRMED AT TIER 2 (XIM is not authoritative for bit-level, per research/AGENTS.md). Retail decodes FOUR bits from that word, not two — research/XIClient/src/XIClient/include/Resource/Derived/MeshBlockResource.h:34-39: 0x80000000 SubMeshIsTransparent, 0x40000000 SubMeshProperty4, 0x20000000 SubMeshDisableCulling, 0x10000000 SubMeshProperty1, vertex count = & 0x0FFFFFFF. But the zone draw loop consumes only transparent + cull (ZoneRenderer.cpp:2377, :2379-2390) and sets the blend func GLOBALLY (:2441-2442 SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA), never per-submesh. So retail lamp glow is not a material flag. The two bits we don't decode are not glow either: the only other per-submesh flag read in the render path is `subMesh->field_26` at ZoneRenderer.cpp:2333, gating an unrelated branch. (Which XIClient accessor maps to field_22 vs field_26 is inferred from declaration order in MeshBlockSubMesh.h:24-27, not stated.)

WHAT ACTUALLY CARRIES IT: the per-vertex RGBA overbright channel (raw/128, kuluu-render/src/dat_mmb.rs:259-270), doubled again by zone_ffxi.wgsl:233. zone_lights.rs:137-188 already mines exactly this: cluster_overbright() finds overbright vertex clusters and spawns an unlit AlphaMode::Add billboard + PointLight AS A CHILD OF THE MESH at cluster.local — the glow is positioned by the fixture geometry and cannot drift from it. That is the correct architecture for 'the lamp is the emitter' and it already exists.

THE GAP: the path is gated to DynamicLights::Enhanced (kuluu-render/src/graphics/settings.rs:144-146 — note the crate path; kuluu/src/view_native/launcher_ui/settings.rs is a different file) while the default is Vanilla (settings.rs:119-123 `#[default] Vanilla`), and it found zero clusters in the Port Windurst tunnel (zone 240) whose lanterns prompted this. DAT 340 has only 30 of 277 models with any vertex over 1.0, so at the default threshold of 1.15 (settings.rs:366) most lamp fixtures are invisible to the clusterer.

STEPS 1-2 CLOSED. dat-mmb-overbright now filters on the MMB header name (bytes 16..32) instead of the 4-char chunk name, so placement ids like wi_k_ramp match (ffxi-dat/examples/dat-mmb-overbright.rs:42-52, commit 111574b). Per that commit's recorded measurement, wi_k_ramp reads peak=1.000 (raw 128) with 0/204 verts over 1.0 across DATs 338/339/341 — no overbright data, so the emitter miner can never see these lanterns at any threshold. Threshold tuning and per-zone calibration are both ruled out for them. (Re-run `dat-mmb-overbright 340 wi_k_ramp` to reproduce; the figure lives only in the commit message, not in a test.)

REMAINING (step 3): decide whether the overbright emitter path is worth keeping/enabling in Vanilla at all, given it can only ever fire on the ~11% of models that do carry overbright verts. If not, this closes as 'retail-faithful already' and the Enhanced path stays an addon.
close_reason: Superseded by kuluu-ym64 (86ac6fd1): the overbright emitter path is retired; the DAT's own flames/glows (kuluu-8ifu) and 0x47 point lights are the faithful lamp rendering, and Enhanced now means point-light shadow maps

title: zone_clouds renders only cld1/cld2 by name; per-weather cloud variants (e.g. ~4cl) not drawn
description: After the follow_camera gate in dat_mzb, camera-relative cloud variants like ~4cl (DAT 202, model=rain, attach=0x00 follow_cam=true) are correctly kept OUT of world geometry, but zone_clouds only renders generators literally named cld1/cld2, so these variants aren't drawn as the camera canopy either. Faithful behavior (research/xim EnvironmentManager.updateWeatherEffects) registers ALL weat/<type> EffectResources via EffectManager, dispatched by attach type (0x0=cloud camera-follow, 0xE=sun, 0xF=moon) — not a name allowlist. Follow-up: render cloud canopies by attach==None+follow_camera+linked-dome-mesh, taking care not to sweep in the star/pole generators (which share attach/follow but live in the star/ subdir and link sta1/sta2). Belongs with the weat/ particle-VM effort. Not a double-render (single/no consumer); a missing-subtle-cloud fidelity gap.

title: Faithful stop-cast interrupt clip (sp<suffix>) instead of hard-clearing the pose
description:
kuluu-yned clears the looping cast pose on interrupt (fixing the 60 s stuck cast): the self path cancels a cast_pose ActionPlayback in tick_live_ffxi_actors (kuluu-render/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs:2198-2208) and the observed path drops actor.action when the BATTLE2 FourCC is an interrupt (ffxi_actor_render.rs:2274-2285). Retail is more faithful: research/xim Actor.kt:290-303 interruptSkill enqueues a distinct stop-cast model routine — DatResource.kt:135-138 stopCastId = 'sp'+suffix (spwh/spbk/spsm/spnj/spso/spbl/spge/spfa), 'spte' for JA/mobskill, 'spit' for items, 'splg' for ranged. Corroborated server-side at vendor/server/src/map/enums/four_cc.h:32,34,36,46-53. Follow-up: play the stop-cast routine on interrupt instead of snapping to idle. Nothing plays one today (workspace-wide grep for spte/spit/splg/spwh/spbk hits only ffxi-proto/src/magic.rs).

NOT blocked on the spell-DAT magicType parser — the suffix arrives on the wire. vendor/server/src/map/action/interrupts.cpp:268-287 MagicInterrupt pushes ActionCategory::MagicStart with actionid = PSpell->getFourCC(true), delivered CHAR_INRANGE_SELF, which vendor/server/src/map/zone_entities.cpp:1443-1451 explicitly falls through to CHAR_INRANGE (so the caster gets its own copy), and ffxi-proto/src/magic.rs:54-65 already decodes it into MagicRoutine{id, interrupt}. At ffxi_actor_render.rs:2280 the exact 'sp*' DatId is already in hand: resolve it the same way the cast branch does — routine_motion_clip(&actor.routines, DatId::from_name(&m.id)) (helper at ffxi_actor_render.rs:1303, used at :2301) — and enqueue it with looping=false, cast_pose=false, remaining = clip length. cast_pose=false matters: the self-path cancel at :2198-2208 only clears actions tagged cast_pose, so the stop clip survives the same frame's tick. Drop the kuluu-4u1j dependency; the DAT magicType parser is needed only to predict the interrupt clip locally before the server packet lands.

JA/mobskill/item/ranged interrupts (spte/spit/splg) arrive on their own action categories; action_routine (ffxi_actor_render.rs:1314-1334) maps only kinds 1/7/8/9/10/12 and has no interrupt branch, so those need separate handling.

title: Commands menu opens on page 2 on first '-' (open key double-processed as page flip)
description: Observed in live GUI verify (2026-07-21): pressing '-' from the world opens the Commands menu already on page 2/2 instead of page 1/2. Likely the same '-' keypress that fires Action::OpenMenu (World->Menu at Root cursor 0 = page 1) is ALSO handled by handle_menu_key's Minus arm on the same frame, flipping to page 2. Fix: consume the open key so it isn't re-processed as a page flip on the opening frame (OpenMenu path in view_native/input.rs + handle_menu_key in text_input.rs). Minor; the single-pane two-page rework itself is verified correct (kuluu-v4pd, commit 9c0af00).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified 2026-07-22 (commit 9dd8aeb): single '-' now opens Commands on page 1/2 (Map is on page 1); a second '-' flips to 2/2. MenuStack.absorb_open_minus one-shot flag swallows the opening keypress. Evidence: artifacts/verify/page1-on-open.png, page2-after-flip.png.

title: Map: zone-line exit markers (deferred)
description: Render up/down exit arrows on the map from existing zone_lines.rs trigger-volume data (ZoneLineDescriptor) as a marker source for the shared overlay helper. Deferred out of the initial epic scope.
notes: VERACITY SWEEP 2026-07-31: Re-grounded 2026-07-31, still unimplemented. Anchors: descriptor kuluu-render/src/zone_lines.rs:14 (line_id/from_pos/to_zone/scale_x/scale_z/rotation), live source kuluu/src/view_native/mod.rs:525 (ZoneLineResolver over kuluu_nav::zone_lines_for), shared marker helper kuluu-render/src/minimap/overlay.rs:291 (sync_marker_layer, "the single marker code path both surfaces share") with the category enum at overlay.rs:37 — an Exit category has to be added there so the legend/filters (kuluu-y5z9) pick it up, and it must be rendered by BOTH surfaces the helper drives. title: Parse item activation/cast time from DAT to complete retail recast bracket [max_recast, use_time]
description:
Follow-up to kuluu-ng3o. The retail item tooltip recast line is <cur/max HH:MM:SS/[max_recast, use_time]>, e.g. the user-screenshot case <1/1 22:55:57/[24:00:00, 0:30]>. kuluu-ng3o shipped everything except the second bracket value — kuluu-render/src/hud/item_detail.rs:56-66 formats "<{charges}/{max} {}/[{}]>" with one element — because ffxi-dat/src/item_dat.rs discards the fields it would need.

LAYOUT CONFIRMED (audit 2026-07-31). vendor/POLUtils/PlayOnline.FFXI/Things/Item.cs:741-744 gives the armor/weapon tail as MaxCharges u8, CastingTime u8, UseDelay u16, ReuseDelay u32 (research/xim InventoryItemParser.kt:383-386 agrees). ffxi-dat/src/item_dat.rs:97-101 reads max_charges and then `off += 1 + 2` — that is TWO fields, not one: CastingTime (u8, quarter-seconds; POLUtils Item.cs:364 formats it /4.0) and UseDelay (u16, seconds). Correct the LEAD accordingly.

WHICH FIELD FEEDS THE BRACKET: UseDelay, not activation/cast time. In vendor/server/sql/item_usable.sql every row with reuseDelay=86400 (58 of them, e.g. :2540 moogle_suit 1,2,0,0,1,30,86400,0) has useDelay=30 while activation is only 2, 3 or 8; no row in the whole table has activation=30 (the max is 16, :2791 mamool_ja_earring). A cast time can never render as the screenshot's 0:30. So thread the u16 UseDelay through ItemStatic -> item_meta -> format_charge_line as the second bracket element. Carry CastingTime at the same time — it is the client-side cast/use delay the cast-bar work wants and it is free once the offset is threaded.

STILL OPEN: the display format of that element. hhmmss() would print 0:00:30; retail shows 0:30, which is 30 s under M:SS or 30 min under H:MM. Nothing at tier 1-4 settles it (research/XIClient has no item-tooltip code) — take a retail capture of an enchanted 24 h item before choosing.

NOTE: POLUtils also has an ActivationTime u16 (¼-s), but only in the UsableItem branch (Item.cs:785-791) — plain consumables, not the equipment block item_dat.rs parses — so "the usable-item activation field" is a real field that is simply not in play for the charge line.

NO EXISTING ORACLE TO ASSERT AGAINST: contrary to an earlier audit note, ffxi-proto does NOT scrape activation/useDelay — parse_usable_row (ffxi-proto/build.rs:676-685) reads only itemid/validTargets/maxCharges and ffxi-proto/src/item_usable.rs:11-19 keeps only those three. Adding useDelay to that scrape is extra work, but it would give an independent LSB oracle to pin the DAT read in a unit test. Do NOT ship a guessed magic offset.

title: Retail key-layout parity: arrows move the character (not camera), numpad4/6/8/2 camera orbit/tilt, numpad5 first-person toggle
description:
TITLE: Retail key-layout parity: bind numpad5 first-person, numpad9/3 zoom, and decide the Shift+numpad strafe (Standard preset already matches retail's numpad-move/arrow-camera default)

DESCRIPTION:
Retail default key layout, per the disassembly-grounded client (this SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-19 HorizonXI observation, which recorded that server's shipped key config rather than the retail default):
- Numpad drives the CHARACTER: NUMPAD8/2 = forward/back, NUMPAD4/6 = turn left/right (research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Input/InputManager.cpp:400-414).
- Arrows drive the CAMERA: LEFT/RIGHT = camera yaw, UP/DOWN = camera pitch (same function, :416-431).
- Caveat on authority: XIClient's LogicalAnalogType names are the reimplementer's labels, so the identification is corroborated structurally rather than by name — in GetLogicalAnalogValue (InputManager.cpp:308-360) the numpad axes fall back to the MOUSE character-move (GetMoveH/GetMoveV) and are the only axes gated on NUMLOCK (:299-306,363-365), while the arrow axes fall back to the mouse CAMERA drag delta and getPointCameraH/V. The arrow analog is also suppressed whenever a UI window is active (AnalogCallbacks.cpp:28-45), matching retail's arrows-drive-the-menu-cursor behaviour.
- Shift + NUMPAD4/6 = strafe (InputManager.cpp:432-441, LogicalAnalogType::CharacterStrafe). Nothing in XIClient's port consumes CharacterStrafe (it appears only in LogicalAnalogType.h:8 and that switch arm), so whether retail additionally gates it on lock-on is unconfirmed.
- Zoom: NUMPAD9/PAGEUP in, NUMPAD3/PAGEDOWN out (InputManager.cpp:443-447; shortcut keys PERIOD/COMMA at research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/Input/ActionDefinitions.cpp:167,:169).
- First person = V *or* NUMPAD5 (ActionDefinitions.cpp:41, ACTION_016, ActionFilter::CameraControl).
- Autorun = NUMPAD7 (ActionDefinitions.cpp:65); "Select active window" = F or numpad + (ActionDefinitions.cpp:43).

Current state (re-grounded 2026-07-31): Kuluu's Standard preset ALREADY matches that table — Numpad8/2 move, Numpad4/6 turn, arrows camera yaw/pitch, Numpad7 autorun, NumpadAdd select-active-window (kuluu-render/src/keybinds/presets.rs:133-147), pinned by standard_uses_numpad_movement (presets.rs:200-229), and present since the initial commit. The compact presets keep WASD+QE with arrows on camera (presets.rs:99-131) as the no-numpad variant.

REMAINING:
- NUMPAD5 is not bound as the alternate first-person toggle; only V is (presets.rs:62).
- NUMPAD9/NUMPAD3 are not bound as zoom aliases; only Period/Comma are (presets.rs:64-65). PageUp/PageDown are already taken by Action::PageUp/PageDown (presets.rs:84-85), so decide the conflict.
- Strafe stays unbound in every preset (asserted at presets.rs:177,:196,:222) while retail binds Shift+NUMPAD4/6; bind it or drop the actions once the lock-on question is settled.
- No in-game per-action rebind path: /keybinds takes preset|list|reset only (kuluu/src/view_native/slash_commands.rs:2976-2997), even though PersistedKeybinds::overrides already round-trips per-action binds from the config file (kuluu/src/keybinds_store.rs:9-24) with no writer outside its own tests. This is the prerequisite for any user-facing layout work.

Retest note: re-observe on a retail-default client (not HorizonXI's shipped config) before reshaping any preset. The 2026-07-19 session also reported "A turns view in FP" — A IS bound in retail's default table (ActionDefinitions.cpp:127, ACTION_059, Shortcut modifier), but the port does not label that action's semantics, so what it does is unconfirmed.

title: Entity-stream NPC name labels shifted (name_extraction_miss): wrong names attached to nearby NPC ids
description: Observed live 2026-07-19 (kuluu-76z verify, zone 230): 37 name_extraction_miss events; id 17719636 labelled 'Rolandienne' is actually Voidwatch_Purveyor per vendor LSB npc_list.sql; the real Rolandienne 17719638 was labelled 'A.M.A.N. Reclaimer'. Names appear shifted across adjacent ids — likely an off-by-one/misalignment in NPC-name resolution (DAT name table vs act_index/id mapping). Misleads targeting for agents and players. Evidence: artifacts/verify/kuluu-76z/events-phase1.jsonl.
close_reason: Fixed in 5f7cba3: npc_names.rs addresses the table by each record's embedded entity id (LE u32 at offset 0x1C) instead of record index. Measured: 27,202/104,624 records (26%) have slot != index; all 251 zone tables affected. Against LSB npc_list.sql over 246 zones / 27,937 rows — embedded id 14184 correct vs record index 6121; on the 19,405 contested rows the verdict is 8379:316 for the embedded id. Those 316 are era skew (kuluu-j0nd), not mis-resolution: 316/316 have the LSB name on another record of the same table, clustered at +1/-1/-6 drift. LIVE VERIFIED headless in zone 238: Machitata, Synergy Engineer and Synergy Enthusiast all resolved correctly through the fixed path; zone-230 probe reproduces the filed bug byte-for-byte (old addressing gives 17719636 -> 'Rolandienne', new gives 'Voidwatch Purveyor'). title: Event watchdog force-ends open VM dialogs in user-driven mode (drains pending_event_end but not dialog_session)
description: Observed live during kuluu-76z verification (artifacts/verify/kuluu-76z/events-phase3.jsonl): with user_driven_events=true, the 10s PENDING_EVENT_END_GRACE watchdog auto-flushed a pending EVENT_END while the player still had the dialog open, and it drains pending_event_end but NOT dialog_session — a later Esc then sends a stale 0x05B that LSB rejects ('Not in an event', ValidatedPacketHandler:220). Harmless to session health but a GUI dialog left open >10s gets force-ended under the player. Fix: suspend the grace timer while dialog_session is user-driven-open, or clear dialog_session together with the flush.
close_reason: Fixed in 672a67d: the flush decision is a pure function over named inputs — the grace watchdog no longer force-ends an event while a VM dialog frame is open in user-driven mode (retail never times a dialog out; the escape hatches with a frame up are walking away and /endevent). Clearing the VM session is scoped to the walk-away path AND to the drained entry the open dialog belongs to, so !user_driven consumers (agent_io, agent_socket, ffxi-mcp, headless) keep walking the dialog tree — an adversarial review caught an earlier unconditional clear() that would have destroyed multi-frame dialog playback for every non-GUI consumer. take_pending_event_end makes the pending entry the authorization to send a 0x05B, so the local walk cannot resend one LSB would drop on the EventPara mismatch (validation.cpp:58-77). NOT DONE: the 20s-open-dialog GUI observation — blocked by a locked macOS session.

title: Dev-stack era skew: LSB text ids vs HorizonXI-era client DATs (TALKNUMWORK ids ≥~6425 off by varying amounts)
description:
Live verify of the 0x02A TALKNUMWORK chat path showed zone 230 !addkeyitem rendering 'Lost key item: X.' instead of 'Obtained key item: X.': the vendored/live LSB pin (c39004ce, 2026-04-26) uses text ids synced to a NEWER retail client than the installed HorizonXI-era DATs. Client indexing is identity-correct and must NOT be patched with an offset. Remediation is environmental: either era-match the dev LSB pin to the install's client era, or update vendor/game-files DATs to LSB's target client.

Evidence (reproducible from the install; the original artifacts/verify/parity3-events.jsonl no longer exists and never could be re-checked — artifacts/ is gitignored at .gitignore:87). Zone 230's dialog DAT is file id 6650 -> VTABLE/FTABLE -> ROM/25/39.DAT (ffxi-dat/src/zone_dat.rs:56 zone_id_to_string_file_id; generated STRING_DAT_TABLE row `(230, 6650)`). Installed entries: 6437 'Obtained key item: {KeyItem}.', 6438 'Lost key item: {KeyItem}.', 7062 'Tallying conquest results...', 7385 'Trick or treat...'. Modern LSB: vendor/server/scripts/zones/Southern_San_dOria/IDs.lua:17 KEYITEM_OBTAINED=6438, :37 CONQUEST_BASE=7071, :40 TRICK_OR_TREAT=7394 — SE inserted entries and the delta varies by range (1 in the 64xx band, 9 in the 70xx/73xx bands), so no constant base reconciles. The -1 offset is consistent across the whole 64xx band above the insertion: LSB 6431/6433/6435/6436/6438/6439/6440/6441/6449 each equal the install entry one lower.

Threshold: the insertion sits somewhere in install indexes 6425..6430 — it cannot be pinned tighter because install 6428 and 6429 carry the SAME English text ('You cannot obtain the <item>. Come back after sorting your inventory.', differing only in inline-tag kind 0x23 vs 0x25). LSB 6424 (ASSIST_CHANNEL) still matches at zero offset; the first unambiguous divergence is LSB 6431 (CANNOT_OBTAIN_THE_ITEM), which is install 6430. So: every TALKNUMWORK id >= ~6430 mis-texts by a range-dependent amount on the dev stack (retail-era clients would show the same).

UNVERIFIED sub-claim: 'LSB b3af49c62ae2 (2023-05-25) matches this install byte-for-byte' cannot be checked from this tree — the vendor/server submodule is a shallow clone and `git cat-file -t b3af49c62ae2` reports 'Not a valid object name'. Re-check against a full LSB clone before acting on that pin.

Test anchors: ffxi-dat/src/dmsg.rs:809 real_zone230_keyitem_obtained_decodes_marker (ZONE230_KEYITEM_OBTAINED_MAY2023 = 6437 at :802), kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:6570 talknumwork_composes_real_keyitem_line_from_zone_dat (constant at :6552).
notes:
Second instance of this skew class, measured 2026-08-04 - this time in the entity-id/name binding rather than text ids, and it reinforces the same conclusion (client indexing is identity-correct; do NOT patch with an offset).

Findings from the installed HorizonXI tree (vendor/game-files):
1. The base install is essentially stock: 52414 of 52432 .DAT files share one 2024-01 mtime. Eighteen do not, and those are the server's client-side edits: ROM/26/104.DAT (file id 6887 = NPC-name table, zone 167 Bostaunieux Oubliette), ROM/27/0.DAT (6911 = zone 191 Dangruf Wadi), ROM2/13/95.DAT (6833 = zone 113 Cape Teriggan), ROM2/17/114.DAT (6601 = dialog/string table, zone 181), ROM/286/72-73 (55548/55668, 17MB each), ROM10/42/20-25 + ROM10/1/67 with REBUILT FTABLE10/VTABLE10 (added files, not just replaced).
2. Diffing the patched zone-191 name table against LSB npc_list shows a systematic +1 shift: the DAT record carrying embedded id N+1 holds the name LSB assigns to N (Ramblix/Goblin Footprint at 375/376 vs LSB 374/375, ~190 such rows). Zone 109, whose name table is NOT patched, agrees with LSB exactly. So the servers re-author name DATs to line up with their own npc_list, which is a different id numbering from both retail and stock LSB.
3. Separately, servers ship client changes as an overlay rather than by editing the install at all: XI-Pivot (config/pivot/pivot.ini, polplugins/DATs/<overlay>/ROM*/...) with 22 override files across 3 overlays. Tracked as kuluu-gp3s.
4. And they rename entities over the wire: LSB isRenamed/packetName in 0x0E (vendor/server/src/map/packets/entity_update.cpp:539-587), plus a custom s2c 0x1FF name table consumed by the dynamic_entity_renamer Ashita addon.

Consequence for this bead's remediation options: 'era-match the LSB pin to the install' is weaker than it looks, because private-server installs are not a single coherent era - they are retail-era base DATs plus per-zone re-authored tables plus an overlay. The durable answer is the same one this bead already reaches for text ids: trust the install's own indexing, and where the server offers authoritative data on the wire, prefer it. Do not backfill names from the baked LSB npc_list - verified wrong on the case in kuluu-i7ry, where LSB has the id as an unnamed Conquest_Banner.

title: Build-script scrape counts: add zero/low-count sanity signal (canary) now that counts are quiet
description:
Follow-up to kuluu-d33k: the 'scraped N entries' lines were demoted from cargo:warning to plain build-script stdout (e.g. ffxi-proto/build.rs:118), which removed their incidental canary value.

Already covered — and predating this bead (all three guard families came in with the initial public commit 4c403ad, 2026-04-27): kuluu-nav/build.rs:135-137 bails on 'parsed zero zonelines'; ffxi-dat/build.rs:136 bails on zero zone rows (this one really fails the build), while :214 and :258 bail on zero map / dialog-string entries but the callers at :28-49 catch that Err and downgrade to `cargo:warning=ffxi-dat: skipping ... scrape` with an empty emitted table — i.e. those two already satisfy the bead's 'or emit a real cargo:warning' branch. ffxi-proto/build.rs carries 13 `if out.is_empty() { bail!(...) }` guards (e.g. :542-543 enum scrape, :570-571 packet ids).

Remaining gaps:
1. ffxi-audio/build.rs has NO count check at all — a scrape() that returns Ok(vec![]) on format drift in vendor/AltanaListener/AltanaListener/track_names.json silently emits an empty MUSIC_CATALOG (:12-18 handles only the read/parse error; :29-37 writes whatever it got; :39-42 just prints the count).
2. ffxi-proto/build.rs prints 24 scrape counts but only 13 scrapes have empty guards — audit the unguarded ones (spell/ability/item/emote sub-tables at :214,226,238,251,263,286,298,310,324,347,361,370) and add the same bail.
3. Nothing anywhere flags a suspiciously LOW but nonzero count (partial format drift). ffxi-proto/build.rs:27-30 + :475-477 (MIN/MAX_PLAUSIBLE_YALMS) is the only sanity-band precedent — generalize that shape to counts, with per-scrape floors rather than one global threshold.
4. d33k leftover: ffxi-proto/build.rs:378-381 still prints the item_usable count as `cargo:warning=`, so one informational line was never demoted.
Keep normal success output on plain stdout.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (b3d1fcd3, c54282e9, 37e6f1c0) after adversarial review (rounds: needs_fix, needs_fix, approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
2026-09-09 (round-2 review response, worktree /tmp/kuluu-wt/kuluu-m4yk, branch wt/kuluu-m4yk)

Round 2 raised one issue and it was a commit-message accuracy defect, not a code defect: a451a0fe's closing "Verified:" paragraph claims "all 33 ffxi-vocab / 7 ffxi-proto / 1 ffxi-audio counts print and pass". The ffxi-vocab number is 27.

Verification method (re-done from scratch, not taken from the review): touched the three build scripts to defeat the shared /tmp/kuluu-wt-target cache, ran `cargo build -p ffxi-vocab -p ffxi-proto -p ffxi-audio`, confirmed the log showed "Compiling ... (/private/tmp/kuluu-wt/kuluu-m4yk/...)", then counted the "scraped" lines in the build-script output whose mtime matched that build. Result 27 / 7 / 1.

Why 27: ffxi-vocab/build.rs has 24 check_scrape_count call sites; the one at :136 is inside the loop over the 4 msg.lua sub-tables, giving 24 - 1 + 4 = 27 printed lines. `mod floor` carries 26 consts rather than 27 because floor::JOB_NAME is deliberately shared by the two sites at :192/:198 (job_name entries and job_name abbreviations come from the same file with the same row count). The figure was already 27 at a451a0fe - `git show a451a0fe:ffxi-vocab/build.rs` also has 24 sites - so the later commit 9b383600 is not responsible.

How the correction landed: as an extra tip commit cb0c8b3e (empty, message-only), NOT as the amend the review asked for. Every history-rewriting command was denied by the session permission classifier (git rebase -i, git reset --hard, git commit-tree/update-ref), so probing further would have been working around a denial. The prepared corrected text for a451a0fe sits at /tmp/m4yk-msg.txt; whoever pushes this branch can `git rebase -i c443301a`, reword a451a0fe with that file, and drop cb0c8b3e if a cleaner two-commit history is preferred.

No source changed in this round. Re-ran fmt --check, checks.sh style, cargo test -p lsb-scrape -p ffxi-audio -p ffxi-vocab (106 tests, 0 fail) and clippy -p lsb-scrape -D warnings: all green. Branch remains unpushed.
Unknowns left open: The correction is an extra tip commit, not an amend of a451a0fe, because this session's permission classifier denied git rebase -i, git reset --hard and git commit-tree. A human (or a session with those permissions) should decide whether to squash it in before push; the prepared reworded message is  | cb0c8b3e is an empty commit. If the project would rather not carry one, dropping it and rewording a451a0fe is the equivalent outcome.
close_reason: Landed on main b3d1fcd3, c54282e9, 37e6f1c0 after adversarial review; gate green. See notes for what landed, how it was verified, and what stays open.

title: weather.rs: global ClearColor written by weather fog with no reset path for weatherless zones
description: Code review nit from the kuluu-ehye/weather session: weather.rs now writes ResMut<ClearColor> as a horizon backdrop when fog is active, but zones/weather states without fog never restore the previous ClearColor, so a stale horizon color can leak across zone lines or weather transitions. Fix: capture/restore a default, or write ClearColor every frame from current weather state including the 'no weather' branch. Verify with a zone-line crossing from a foggy zone to a clear zone.
close_reason: apply_zone_weather previously wrote ClearColor only inside the volumetric-fog-with-record branch and early-returned when zone_weather.current was None, so a painted fog horizon leaked across zone lines into weatherless zones and survived the volumetric-fog toggle. Fix: added a DefaultClearColor resource that captures the app's startup backdrop in PreStartup, extracted a pure zone_clear_color(rec, volumetric_fog, daylight_smooth, default) selection function, and restructured apply_zone_weather to compute and write the desired ClearColor every frame BEFORE the no-record early return (change-detection-guarded write). Volumetric+record paints the daylight-scaled zone fog color as before; every other state (no record, wasm, DistanceFog mode) restores the captured startup default.

title: Build-output noise: demote 'scraped N entries' info from cargo:warning; fix clang -ffp-model/-ffp-contract override in vendored recastnavigation-rs
description: (1) ffxi-dat/ffxi-proto/ffxi-audio/ffxi-nav build.rs emit success telemetry ('scraped N entries', 'generated X with N zones') via cargo:warning=, rendering as warnings on every fresh build. Move to plain build-script stdout (visible with -vv); keep genuine skip/failure messages as cargo:warning. (2) vendor/recastnavigation-rs/build.rs passes -ffp-model=precise then -ffp-contract=off; clang emits -Woverriding-option once per TU because precise implies contract=on. clang's default model is already precise, so drop the redundant model flag — identical FP semantics, no warning.

title: MH interior: giant glowing green 'T' + ring artifact fills the room
description:
In the Mog House interior (S. San d'Oria model 289, DAT 389), a huge green bloom-heavy 'T' shape hovers mid-room floor-to-ceiling and a giant green ring arc clips the bottom-right of the screen (screenshots 2026-07-14, /tmp/mog-01-login.png — since deleted; artifacts/ is gitignored at .gitignore:87, so a fresh capture is required). Only observed inside the MH.

Suspect narrowing from a code read (2026-07-31, no runtime repro):
- RULED OUT — the client-synthesized zone-line marker. kuluu-render/src/zone_lines.rs:118-123 returns before spawning any marker when state.snapshot.myroom.is_some(); the marker material is amber (:71-78, base_color srgba(1.0,0.75,0.20,0.55)); and zone_line_display defaults to Off in every graphics profile (graphics/settings.rs:513,543,573,607). The MH suppression predates the sighting (3149c20, 2026-07-13).
- RULED OUT — the placeholder orb for the door entity. It does spawn (kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs:5802-5819 makes the door an EntityKind::Npc with look: None, and kuluu-render/src/scene.rs:304-307 suppresses the orb only for Door/Transport looks), but the Npc orb material is yellow (scene.rs:134) and sphere-shaped.
- WEAK, colour only — the 'Door: To Town' nameplate billboard. The Npc plate colour is green (nameplate_billboard.rs:136, srgb(0.55,1.0,0.55)) and the plate does spawn for the door (scene.rs:346-359). But the geometry does NOT support a floor-to-ceiling quad: `world_height = world_width / aspect_ratio.max(0.01)` (:216) is driven by the rasterized text image size (:79), and rasterize_text_to_image floors width at 9 px (:297, max(1) + 2*pad with OUTLINE_RADIUS_PX = 3) against a ~90 px height at NAME_PX = 64 (:17), so aspect_ratio bottoms out near 0.1 — a ~14-yalm quad only for an EMPTY name. For 'Door: To Town' the raster is much wider than tall, so the plate is a fraction of a yalm high. Do not treat this as the likely cause without a capture.
- NO CANDIDATE — the 'green ring arc'. There is no ring/torus/annulus mesh anywhere in kuluu-render; a zone particle generator or misplaced MMB/D3M geometry is the more plausible family and has not been examined.

Next step (needs a live MH session): capture inside the Mog House, toggle nameplate billboards off to test the plate hypothesis, and log the BillboardAspect width/height plus the resulting Transform.scale for MH_DOOR_ENTITY_ID; separately dump the spawned zone-particle generators and MMB draw list for the MH interior.

title: Zone-teardown despawn flood: guard recursive double-despawns with try_despawn
description: During zone teardown, renderer teardown systems call bare commands.entity(e).despawn() on entities Bevy already freed as descendants of a recursively-despawned parent (index reused -> 'generation 2'). Produces thousands of 'Entity ... is invalid; its index now has generation 2' WARN lines per zone-in from bevy_ecs::error::handler. Harmless (Bevy logs and continues) but noisy + adds error-handler overhead to the teardown frame. Fix: swap the bare .despawn() at renderer teardown sites for the fallible try_despawn() (audio.rs:938 already does this). Adjacent to the zone-change-not-clean-lifecycle behavior.
close_reason: despawn_ingame_entities now uses commands.entity(entity).try_despawn() so recursively-despawned children freed by a parent earlier in the query no longer flood bevy_ecs error-handler WARNs during zone teardown. Verified by new unit test zone_teardown_tests::teardown_tolerates_recursively_freed_children_without_warns (parent+child both InGameEntity; counts error-handler warns via BevyEcsWarnCounter): fails with bare despawn(), passes with try_despawn. cargo test -p ffxi-client zone_teardown --features native-window green; scripts/checks.sh fmt clippy green. Live visual confirm pending.

title: Event/status packet paths swallow diagnostics (pre-existing, surfaced by PR #111 review)
description:
Three pre-existing silent-failure gaps found while reviewing PR #111 (not introduced there, not fixed by the stacked follow-up PR alexcstark/kuluu-ffxi#1):

1. event_dialog.rs load_event_dat/load_strings collapse missing-file, IO error, and parse error into None (.ok()?). With auto-release in place, a bad FFXI_DAT_PATH now auto-skips EVERY cutscene in a zone with 'not yet supported' chat lines, indistinguishable from an unimplemented opcode. Log once per zone on load failure.

2. ffxi-event vm.rs:154-157: exec_pointer running past the end of bytecode reports a clean Done, indistinguishable from OP_END — exactly the failure mode that hides a wrong opcode skip size. A distinct StepResult (or debug log) for 'ran past end without END' would make size bugs discoverable. Same for eventgetcode's unwrap_or(0) OOB reads.

3. session.rs handle_sub_packet: every 'if let Ok(x) = decode::X::decode(...)' silently drops decode errors; CHAR_STATUS now also loses the speed sync when it fires. A dedup'd tracing::warn on the Err arm would cost nothing.
close_reason: (1) event_dialog.rs: DAT load failures now log once per zone with the resolved FFXI_DAT_PATH file path and the underlying error (dedup'd per zone id). (2) vm.rs: added a distinct StepResult::RanPastEnd path when the exec pointer runs past the end of bytecode without an explicit OP_END, logged separately from a real END; eventgetcode out-of-bounds reads (the unwrap_or(0) sites around lines 283-299) now emit a debug log with pc/index before falling back. (3) session.rs: all 23 'if let Ok(...)' decode arms in handle_sub_packet (22 decode::* plus the from_utf8 arm) now route the Err through .inspect_err into a new warn_decode_err(opcode, err) helper that warns once per opcode (process-global OnceLock<Mutex<HashSet<u16>>> gate) and logs repeats at DEBUG, so dropped packets are no longer silent.

title: Alliance-aware party list (3x6 columns) + leader dots (party list + nameplates)
description:

Current state (re-grounded 2026-07-31):
- Roster widget renders one flat row list: kuluu-render/src/hud/roster.rs:117-118 (spawn loop), spawn_member_row roster.rs:154-177; no alliance partitioning — party is a single Vec<PartyMember> (kuluu-session/src/state.rs:318; wire kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:366).

- The alliance party index is ALREADY on our wire, just discarded. LSB's GP_GROUP_ATTR is `PartyNo : 2` in bits 0-1 of the GAttr word (vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x0dd_group_list.h:31, set at 0x0dd_group_list.cpp:40), and in an alliance LSB pushes a 0x0DD GROUP_LIST for every member with PARTY_SECOND/PARTY_THIRD in the flags (vendor/server/src/map/party.cpp:880-913). ffxi-proto/src/decode.rs:1579 already reads that u32 and extracts only bits 2-3 — so step one is `party_no = gattr & 0x3` plumbed onto PartyAttrs/PartyListExtra → wire PartyMember, not a new packet. (Retail also gets the same index from s2c 0x0C8 GROUP_TBL, GroupTbl[20] with PartyNo:2 — vendor/server/src/map/packets/s2c/0x0c8_group_tbl.h:29-43,52, pushed at party.cpp:887 — which Kuluu does not decode at all: no const in ffxi-proto/src/map.rs (only GROUP_LIST 0x0DD at :443 and GROUP_ATTR 0x0DF at :445) and no handler in kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs (:1314, :1326). Adding it is optional, not a prerequisite.)
- CORRECTION (previous text claimed "retail shows HP/MP only"): retail is not HP/MP-only. XIClient (tier 2) draws party TP as a right-aligned NUMBER next to MP, gated on a config bit — research/XIClient/src/XIClient/source/UI/Windows/InGame/Party/PartyList.cpp:247-249 ((FsConfig::GetConfig(FS_CONFIG_174) & 1) != 0 && !IsPartyDataActorIndexReady → DrawPartyTacticalPoints), definition PartyList.cpp:91-100 (0x80606060, 0x802060D0 at TP>=1000), alongside DrawHPBar/DrawMPBar and numeric HP/MP in DrawInfoParty (PartyList.cpp:222+). Our divergence is (a) TP drawn as a bar instead of a number and (b) no config gate — not the presence of party TP. title: Small ~28ms frame blip exactly every 10.0s (cpu-heavy + periodic 1MB image re-upload)
description:
Post kuluu-996 fix, perf logs show a residual single-frame ~28ms spike at an exact 10.00s cadence: cpu 11-17ms + rprep up to 17ms, churn img+1 (1024KB) in nearby windows, std+4 on spike frames. Repro: run instrumented client (perf summary/spike lines in view_native/perf_hud.rs, FFXI_GPU_TIMING=1), stand idle in Port_Bastok.

The cadence is real, not a logging artifact: LOG_COOLDOWN_S = 1.0 (perf_hud.rs:16) and the printed `after {interval}s` is read from secs_since_spike (perf_hud.rs:419), which is reset for every DETECTED spike (perf_hud.rs:442) before the cooldown early-return (perf_hud.rs:444).

Minimap ruled out on gating, not on size (re-grounded 2026-07-31). The 1024KB figure IS consistent with a retail minimap image — those are 512-px maps (minimap/retail.rs:33 MENUMAP_TEX = 512.0; minimap/mod.rs:106), so 512*512*4 = 1,048,576 B. What rules the minimap out is that neither path fires periodically while idle: the retail map DAT is loaded once per zone and early-returns thereafter (minimap/retail.rs:204-206), and the TopDown bake is change-gated on geom/policy/zone/lighting-bucket with a deliberately coarse 12-bucket lighting trigger over a ~57-real-minute Vana'diel day (minimap/topdown.rs:89-113, :34) — and its target is 256x256 = 256KB anyway (minimap/mod.rs:14, topdown.rs:253-269).

Unconfirmed candidate for the 1024KB: a Bevy font atlas. bevy_text 0.19.0 (Cargo.lock:1731) keeps the atlas Image CPU-persistent as Rgba8UnormSrgb (font_atlas.rs:47-53) and sizes it at a minimum 512x512 = 1,048,576 B (font_atlas.rs:159-160), and track_asset_churn bills the whole CPU buffer on any AssetEvent::Modified (perf_hud.rs:166-181), so one new glyph would read as 'img+1 (1024KB)'. This is a size match only — NOT established. Next step before optimizing an upload that may not exist: log the AssetId/handle behind the img churn and whether the event is Added or Modified.

The std-churn follow-up is partly addressed: 144145f (2026-07-16) epsilon-gates the sun/moon StandardMaterial writes (CELESTIAL_COLOR_EPS at sun_moon.rs:163, gate at :880-885) and adds FFXI_FREEZE_CELESTIAL_MAT=1 as an A/B (:867). Re-measure std+/5s before chasing it further; the comment at sun_moon.rs:864-867 still narrates the pre-fix unconditional-write behaviour. The water suspect named in the original text is untouched.

The spike itself has not been reproduced or fixed; this bead stays open on that.

title: Fountains & waterfalls: zone-static particle generators (gravity spray + UV-scroll sheet)
description:
Fountains & waterfalls: zone-static particle generators (gravity spray + UV-scroll sheet)

Fountain/waterfall spray is a zone-static Generator-chunk effect registered once at zone load (research/xim/src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/poc/Scene.kt:125-126 — `registerEffectsRecursively` filters `it.particleGenerator.autoRun` and calls `EffectManager.registerEffect(ZoneAssociation(this), effect)`), anchored at the generator base_position — the same DAT family that drives braziers/lamp point-lights (ffxi-dat/src/generator.rs).

LANDED since this bead was filed (2026-06-30) — the original three "concrete gaps" are all closed:
1. sec3 VelocityAccelerator (gravity) IS applied. ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:150-154 declares `accel: Option<[f32; 3]>` and :351-356 parse opcode 0x03; kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:458-467 integrates it per particle (`p.vel += a; p.pos += p.vel * frames`). Pinned by ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:596 `assert_eq!(def.accel, Some([0.0, -0.02, 0.0]), "0x03 -> accel")`.
2. sec3 TextureCoordinateUpdater UV-scroll IS applied at render time. ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:349-350 (0x27 -> U, 0x28 -> V) and kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:456 `g.tex_translate += Vec2::from_array(g.def.uv_scroll) * frames`. (Both shipped under kuluu-8i3, 2026-07-21.)
3. Zone-static fountain/waterfall generators ARE placed and spawned. kuluu-render/src/zone_particles.rs:23-25 WATER_MESH_PREFIXES (incl. "taki", "sib", "spl", "spr"); :52-62 `water_spray_mesh` gates on auto_run + non-zero base_position + life>0 + water-named mesh/texture; :102-117 spawns each at `mzb_to_bevy(base_position)` via `spawn_zone_particle_generator`. The Lower Jeuno tki1-5 / sibj cascade was live-verified under kuluu-czc6 (closed 2026-07-23).

REMAINING GAP (the whole of this bead now):
Lower Jeuno (zone 245) fountain basin renders DRY — the basin's still-water surface is never spawned (bare rock/gravel shows). The generator-driven model-spawn water-sheet path that draws canal/harbor water is kuluu-render/src/dat_mzb.rs:917-985; it rejects any model-spawn with `ms.uv_scroll == [0.0, 0.0]` (:943) and any non-singleton generator (:949-955). LEADING HYPOTHESIS (not yet confirmed against the DAT): a still, non-scrolling basin sheet would be rejected by the first of those filters. Next step: dump the Lower Jeuno zone DAT's Generator chunks and establish whether a basin sheet chunk exists at all and which filter (if either) drops it, before deciding whether the zero-scroll rule needs a water-texture escape hatch.

BIT-LEVEL CAVEAT: the 0x27/0x28 (TextureCoordinateUpdater) and 0x03/0x06/0x09 (VelocityAccelerator) opcode assignments rest solely on research/xim (src/jsMain/kotlin/xim/resource/ParticleGeneratorParser.kt:356, :400, :401). research/XIClient ships no particle system (only MonoRenderTarget.h even mentions "particle") and research/cexi-docs/fx documents only the effect/spell system, so no tier-2 or tier-4 corroboration exists in-tree — treat the opcode numbers as XIM-sourced and unconfirmed against retail.

CITATION CORRECTIONS: research/xim/src/Notes.txt:24 ("3. The fountain in [Metalworks]") and :26 ("5. The 0.5f step in [Northern San d'Oria] near the fountain") sit under the `### Interesting Collision Locations` heading at Notes.txt:21 — they are collision notes, not fountain-rendering evidence. The old "Parsing landed: ffxi-dat/src/generator.rs:99-250 (uv_scroll)" pointed at the CLOUD generator (CloudGeneratorDef :87, parse_cloud_generator :126); the model-spawn water-sheet uv_scroll is ModelSpawnDef :385-402 / parse_model_spawn :409 (fields :389, sec3 walk :472-503), and the particle uv_scroll is ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:153 / :331-350.

title: macOS: go universal (lipo x86_64 + arm64)
description: macOS ships arm64 only, excluding Intel users: the hand-rolled leg builds `Build (aarch64 macOS)` on macos-14 (release.yml:91-94) and the dist target matrix lists only `aarch64-apple-darwin` (Cargo.toml:119-123). NOTE dist 0.32.0 cannot lipo: the 0.32.0 binary contains no `lipo` codepath and `universal` appears only in its release.yml.j2 comment about universal *installers*, and `dist plan` emits exactly one archive per entry in `targets`. So adding `x86_64-apple-darwin` produces a SECOND download (`kuluu-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz`), not one universal binary. Pick a path before starting: (a) ship two per-arch archives and let dist's shell installer select by arch — cheapest, but drops the "single notarized download" goal and doubles the notarization work in kuluu-1qq; or (b) add x86_64-apple-darwin to `targets` and a dist custom job that lipos the two binaries into a universal one, re-signs and notarizes it, and attaches it as an extra asset. Linking: no verification step is needed for empty RUSTFLAGS — the dev lld pin in .cargo/config.toml:39-40 is scoped to `target.aarch64-apple-darwin`, and build-setup.yml already clears RUSTFLAGS on every macOS runner.

title: Particle VM: shared/global billboard meshes + sec3/sec4 updaters (Phases 4-5)
description:
Particle emission VM (kuluu-uvm) renders local-mesh effects. Remaining:

(1) Shared/global billboard meshes: some effect DATs reference meshes (e.g. Boost g004 'hi14', JA impact 'hi22'/'hi16') not stored in the per-action DAT. spawn_particle_generators already picks whichever asset tier holds the generator DEF (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:149-157 assets_holding), but resolve_mesh then looks the mesh up in that same single tier — `assets.d3ms.get(&def.mesh_id)?` (particle_sim.rs:676) — so a def whose mesh lives in another dir still drops silently. Needs a cross-tier mesh loader.

(2) sec3 updaters beyond scale/alpha are not parsed. ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs:329-360 walks section 3 (offset at body 0x78) for 0x27/0x28 uv_scroll and 0x03 accel only. Missing: rotation 0x05 (research/xim ParticleGeneratorParser.kt:357 RotationUpdater) and 0x56-0x58 (:462-464, rotation.x/y/z += v * PI), oscillation 0x29-0x2B (:403-405 OscillationApplier X/Y/Z).

(2b) CORRECTION — child generators are a SECTION 2 setup, not sec4. Confirmed at tier 2: XIClient's CYyGenerator::Preset walks the four scripts separately, and in the Script2 walk `case 0x3C: case 0x44: case 0x53: case 0x6A:` resolve a `ResourceType::Generater` (CYyGenerator.cpp:2314-2347), while the Script4 walk resolves a Generater on `case 1` and a Scheduler on `case 2` (:2412-2427). XIM agrees: 0x44/0x53 -> ChildGeneratorSetup live in sec2Handler (ParticleGeneratorParser.kt:238, :256) and sec4Handler carries only 0x01 EmitChildHandler / 0x05 RepeatExpirationHandler (:504-507). Beware the byte collision: in sec3, 0x44 is a dampening updater and 0x53 an occlusion updater (:442, :457), so the opcode must be read per section. We parse neither the sec2 setup nor the sec4 0x01 emit handler, so no child generator is ever spawned.

(3) CORRECTION — non-flat meshes (maz2 = 144 verts) ARE instanced with their full vertex list (particle_sim.rs:647-665 sprite_template). The actual defect is narrower: camera-billboard particles collapse the depth axis — particle_sim.rs:587-593 uses `sz = 1.0` unless the generator has a fixed orientation, so a 3D particle mesh is drawn as a flat card facing the camera.

(4) velocity units + base_position x/z need live tuning.

Evidence: kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs, ffxi-dat/src/particle_gen.rs.
notes: Implemented 2026-07-21: ParticleGeneratorDef sec3 walk (0x27/0x28 uv_scroll, 0x03 accel) + particle_sim tex_translate/accel apply + D3M Repeat sampler. Committed. Tests green. Visual unverified (headless has no particle sim).

title: Render scale: FSR1 (EASU+RCAS) WGSL upscale pass to replace bilinear
description: Follow-up to kuluu-aoc. The render-scale composite currently upscales the off-screen 3D image with a plain bilinear sampler (kuluu-render/src/graphics/render_scale.rs:119 `image.sampler = ImageSampler::linear()`, displayed by the full-window `ImageNode` spawned at :222-235 under the `Camera2d` composite at :198-206). Replace with an FSR1 spatial upscaler (EASU edge-adaptive upsample + RCAS sharpen) for far better quality at <100% scale. FSR1 is MIT/public-domain shader code with no temporal/motion-vector dependency, so it runs cross-platform (Metal/Vulkan/DX/web) — ideal for the macOS + Steam Deck (AMD) targets where Bevy's DLSS can't run. Wiring note: the composite is a Bevy UI node, not a 3D mesh, so `MaterialPlugin` (the FfxiZoneMaterial pattern at kuluu-render/src/ffxi_zone_material.rs:529-531) does not apply to it — use `UiMaterialPlugin` on the display node, a Material2d fullscreen quad under the composite camera, or a render-graph post-process node. The `embedded_asset!` + plugin-registration shape of FfxiZoneMaterial still carries over. LABELS: roadmap, enhanced, world-rendering (retail has no render-scale upscaler, and the roadmap convention wants vanilla/enhanced + an area label alongside `roadmap`).

title: Vanilla moon should use retail 12-frame sprite sheet, not procedural shader
description:
Vanilla sky draws the moon with a procedural shader (ffxi-viewer-core/src/moon.wgsl: hash noise + 3 gaussian maria + an in-shader ellipse terminator for phase; driven by MoonMaterial params in moon_material.rs). Retail FFXI instead draws the moon as a 12-frame sprite sheet, one baked image per phase, indexed by phase (confirmed via research/xim: EnvironmentManager.MoonPhase 0..11; MoonPhaseSpriteSheetUpdater sets particle.spriteSheetIndex; SpriteSheetMeshProvider returns spriteSheet.meshes[index]). Sprite sheet lives in environment DAT Section 0x21 (SpriteSheetMesh) referenced from Section 0x2F (EnvironmentSection), textures in Section 0x20.

Current infra (per audit): ffxi-dat texture.rs decodes DXT1/DXT3/palettized/0xA1/raw; zone_texture::decoded_texture_to_image bridges to bevy Image. ffxi-dat/src/weather.rs parses ONLY the 176-byte lighting/color header of 0x2F (skybox_colors/altitudes/fog/light), NOT the sprite-sheet refs. Section 0x21 is NOT in kind.rs and not parsed. moon_material.rs currently loads a single static texture by hardcoded file ids [55660,55780,56200,55540] via map_image::scan_graphics — a stopgap, not the phase sprite sheet.

Work: add ChunkKind 0x21 + sprite_sheet.rs parser (frame count, per-frame texture/UV), walk 0x2F->0x21->0x20 to locate the moon sprite sheet, expose 12 frames to the renderer, drive frame by VanaSky.moon phase, and have Vanilla moon sample the chosen frame instead of the procedural path. ~500-800 LOC + reverse-engineering the 0x21 binary layout. Re-express XIM logic in our own code; do not copy.
notes: Implemented in 47cce4b. ffxi-dat: ChunkKind::SpriteSheet(0x21) + sprite_sheet.rs::extract_moon_sprite_sheet (12-frame moonshap sheet -> UV rects + matched 256x256 texture via scan_graphics). Format validated against real DATs (dat-spritesheet-probe example) and research/xim. ffxi-viewer-core: MoonSpriteFrames resource + zone-driven loader in moon_material.rs (FFXI half-scale alpha expanded), moon.wgsl samples the phase frame's sub-rect, sun_moon_system selects frame via moon_phase_frame() (unit-tested 0=new/6=full). Procedural disc remains indoor fallback. PENDING: visual verification on running client — confirm (a) correct phase frame shows, (b) crescent waxing/waning direction (u-axis) not mirrored, (c) opacity looks right. Quick tweaks if off: flip u or v in moon.wgsl sprite branch; adjust alpha_remap.
close_reason: 0x21 chunk SpriteSheet parsed with 12 frames; moon_phase_frame() maps phase to retail index; shader branches on frame vs procedural

- kuluu-render/src/scene.rs:305-307 — a mesh-less world entity IS spawned for Door/Transport (placeholder orb suppressed, kuluu-kau5); it stays mouse-pickable via picking.rs's hitbox

- kuluu/src/view_native/slash_commands.rs:2204, :2350, :2856 — the remaining references are diagnostic look labels ("tx", "transport size=", "look: TRANSPORT")

description:
Auction House
Re-grounded 2026-09-08 (supersedes the 2026-07-31 grounding, every clause of which is now false). The AH is implemented end-to-end and awaits live acceptance:
- proto: search-server transport + AH list/history codec (3c04ef0a, kuluu-hay9); map 0x04C decode + 0x04E builders (c5dfec43, kuluu-yhlh); list/history u32s are open-listing counts, not prices (8972e1dd) — ffxi-proto/src/map.rs:129,484, ffxi-proto/src/search.rs
- session: search client, AuctionFlow, Ah* AgentCommands (5006d56d, kuluu-30ej) — kuluu-session/src/state.rs AuctionUi / AhCatalogView / AhHistoryView / AhSaleStatus / AhFeeQuote
- snapshot: SceneSnapshot.auction (AuctionUi, wire v16) (96029b97, kuluu-umuj) — kuluu-snapshot/src/lib.rs:740
- HUD + input: kuluu-render/src/hud/auction.rs (root menu, category dock, catalog, price history, digit spinner, sell flow, sales status) and kuluu/src/view_native/text_input/auction.rs (228f57e9; 47e9e4d2 spinner borrow/carry; 0122e745 catalog paging via TCP_AH_REQUEST_MORE)
Oracle: .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/auction-house.md (b45bbb87).
Remaining under this epic: the live acceptance passes on kuluu-gxm1 (browse screens side-by-side with the retail recording) and kuluu-oqdr (sell a stack + a failing bid against live LSB; chat lines match retail). Nothing else is unimplemented.
design: Gold-standard observation: .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/auction-house.md (2026-08-05 recordings, Bastok Mines AH). Architecture: two transports. (1) Map packets c2s 0x04E / s2c 0x04C (vendor/server/src/map/packets/{c2s/0x04e_auc,s2c/0x04c_auc}.{h,cpp}): Open 0x02 arrives after triggering the Auction Counter NPC (lua_baseentity.cpp sendMenu case 3); WorkCheck 0x0A on open; AskCommit 0x04 = fee quote; LotIn 0x0B = sale confirm; Bid 0x0E; Info 0x05 + LotCheck 0x0D = 7-slot sales status; LotCancel 0x0C. ItemStacks: 1=single 0=stack. (2) Search-server TCP (vendor/server/src/search/search_handler.cpp): TCP_AH_REQUEST/_MORE = category item list (cat id @0x16, sort params @0x18+8i; response type 0x95, 20x 10-byte items: itemid + cheapest single/stack price); TCP_AH_HISTORY_SINGLE/STACK = last-10 sales. Framing: u16 len, IXFF magic, blowfish over MD5(static 24-byte key in search_handler.h [build-time scrape] + trailing 4-byte packet key), MD5 hash at len-0x14. 'Natural' sort = ascending itemid (server always appends item_basic.itemid to ORDER BY). GUI reuse: LocalMenuSession -> DialogState -> hud/dialog.rs pattern (delivery box precedent), widgets/text_field, hud/item_detail, hud/shop, hud/menu paging. New: search TCP client, digit-spinner gil widget, category tab dock, price-history table.
notes:
2026-08-05: browse timed out for every category with >20 items ("AH browse: AH
list request timed out"). The search server answers TCP_AH_REQUEST with page 0
and then waits — each later page must be pulled with TCP_AH_REQUEST_MORE under
the connection's ORIGINAL client key (re-splicing a key makes the next response
fail the integrity check). Fixed in 0122e74; measured 270 rows / 14 pages in
~0.5s for category 18 vs HorizonXI. Only Crystals (8 items, one page) ever
worked, which is also all the live test covered — auction_search_live.rs now
browses a multi-page category too. Paging semantics recorded in
.agents/skills/retail-observe/references/auction-house.md.

title: Widen extract_texture_tokens to 0x81 Imgs, or record why they stay unlinkable
description:
kuluu-0itr widened the Img header accept-set to 0x91/0xA1/0xB1 (ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs:86). Imgs with flag 0x81 stay out of the name tiers, yet decode_texture reads them with FLG_PALETTE's layout so their pixels load (texture.rs:165-167). Confirmed in retail data: ROM/0/28.DAT offset 3389984 holds `81 'effect  smoke01 ' 28 00 00 00 80 00 00 00 80 00 00 00` — flag byte, a well-formed 16-char qualified name, the 0x28 SubsequentDataSize word, then Width=128 Height=128 (the same name appears behind flag 0x01 at ROM/0/29.DAT offset 3269136). Any sprite sheet or d3m naming smoke01 therefore resolves to no texture on the name tiers, and the SpriteSheet arm has no DatId fallback at all (kuluu-render/src/particle_sim.rs:694-706, vs the StaticMesh arm's `.or_else(|| assets.images.get(&d3m.texture_dat_id()))` at :691).

The 'record why' half is ALREADY DONE in-tree and predates this bead: texture.rs:88-91 carries the citation and texture.rs:523-529 pins it with extract_texture_tokens_rejects_the_unverified_palette_flags (both landed in abe671f, 2026-07-25 16:13 PDT; this bead was created 16:18 PDT).

What remains is the widening decision, and tier 2 settles the NAME question. research/XIClient/src/XIClient/include/Rendering/Texture/ImageData.h:5-36 lays the header out as `unsigned char Format; ResourceID TextureName (Category[8]+Identifier[8], ResourceID.h:5-13); unsigned int SubsequentDataSize ('observed to be consistently 40' = 0x28); Width; Height; …`, and GameTexture::ConfigureFromImageData copies TextureName as its very first statement, before any format branch (GameTexture.cpp:191); the switch at :211-244 then handles `case 0: case 1: break;` explicitly. So the name field is unconditional across Format bytes — 0x81 (compressed, format 0) and 0x01 (uncompressed, format 0) name themselves exactly where 0x91/0xA1/0xB1 do. XIM's rejection at research/xim TextureSection.kt:27-31 is an unhandled-case `warn(...)`, not evidence of an absent name (research/AGENTS.md: XIM tier 6, XIClient tier 2).

Proposed: fold FLG_PALETTE_UNVERIFIED into NAMED_HEADER_FLAGS keyed on the XIClient layout, flip the two guard tests accordingly, and give the SpriteSheet arm the same DatId last tier the StaticMesh arm already has.

Separate, do-not-conflate caveat surfaced while grounding this: per IsCompressed() = Format>>7, 0x81 IS compressed and 0x01 is not, yet texture.rs:165-167 decodes both with the identical palettised layout; retail's compressed path reads a DXT fourcc after the pixel data (GameTexture.cpp:290-300). Widening the name set does not validate that shared pixel path — file it separately if 0x81 pixels ever look wrong.
notes:
2026-09-09 landed on main (57820042, c324ce43, 09771b28) after adversarial review (round-1 needs_fix, round-2 approve); full fmt/clippy/test gate green on main.
Follow-up bead to file (finding 4, not fixed here -- widening the name set made a pre-existing decode gap newly reachable):

TITLE: decode_palettized ignores ColorFormat/BitDepth and the trailing DXT fourcc

ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs decode_palettized always reads 8-bit indices behind a 1024-byte BGRA palette at PALETTE_OFF. research/XIClient (pinned aba6c816) GameTexture.cpp:249-285 instead branches on ColorFormat, and inside Indexed4Bit/Indexed8Bit on BitDepth: Indexed8Bit skips 512/768/1024 palette bytes for BitDepth 16/24/32 (:266-270), Indexed4Bit 32/48/64 (:254-258), and the Direct16/24/32 cases carry no palette at all (:274-282). GameTexture.cpp:291-300 then re-points PixelData past a trailing DXT fourcc whenever IsCompressed() (Format >> 7) is set.

Install-wide census (my own run, 52,662 DATs; matches the reviewer's independently):
- 480 named format-0 Imgs: (0x01, CF 8, BD 32) 203, (0x81, CF 8, BD 32) 269, (0x01, CF 8, BD 16) 6, (0x81, CF 32 Direct32Bit, BD 32) 2.
- The 8 non-(8,32) ones now decode to garbage where before the widening they were merely unlinkable by name -- that is the newly reachable part.
- Same latent bug already covers 17 0xB1 Imgs (12 ColorFormat 4 / Indexed4Bit, 5 ColorFormat 32 / Direct32Bit), so it is pre-existing; this change only widened exposure.
- All 271 0x81 Imgs carry a trailing DXT3 fourcc that we ignore, so we currently render retail's non-DXT3-hardware fallback twin: same image content, lower fidelity. Fixing this is the higher-volume half of the bead.

Also worth carrying in the bead as a build gotcha: the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/kuluu-wt-target held a stale pre-change ffxi-dat rlib for kuluu-render's unit, so `cargo test -p kuluu-render` silently exercised the OLD NAMED_HEADER_FLAGS while `cargo test -p ffxi-dat` passed. `touch ffxi-dat/src/texture.rs` forced the rebuild. Anyone re-verifying real_dat_sprite_sheet_resolves_a_format0_texture in a shared target dir should force-touch first, or the test proves nothing.
