title: Animation: generic entity-state routine driver (init/iniN/dead/in/out), refcounted AnimationLock, mob-skill file ids, retire BurrowPhase
description: Retail FFXI has no per-mob animation code: every model DAT ships the same ~36 scheduler routines and the client turns wire inputs into routine names via a fixed rule set (F11, F35-F42, F46-F58 in docs/ffxi_disassembly.md section 9; observation record at .agents/skills/retail-observe/references/worm-burrow-routines.md). Kuluu has the routine interpreter and most combat rules but is missing the entity-state half (spawn/appear, animationsub, death, view-range respawn), several scheduler opcodes, the mob-skill (cat 11) file-id base, and still carries a worm-specific BurrowPhase FSM. Implement patches 1-7 from the design in order, one commit each; patch 5 (retiring BurrowPhase) is gated on KULUU_BURROW_LOG=1 verification of the Carrion Worm under the generic path.
design:
## 1. What we are doing, in one paragraph

Retail FFXI does not have per-mob animation code. Every model DAT ships the same ~36 scheduler
routines (`init pop0 dead corp atk0 ati0..atiN atf0 ldam damg sdam gurd pary shld sway cate cast*
shot sh?? v???`) plus its own specials (`ini1..ini3` for burrowers, `sp??` clips, `fsh0..3`, `wep0..8`).
The client turns wire inputs into **routine names** through a small fixed rule set, resolves each name
against the actor's DAT then ROM/0/0.DAT, runs whatever it finds, and does nothing when the name is
absent. Kuluu already has the routine interpreter (`ffxi-dat::scheduler`, `kuluu-render::scheduler_runtime`)
and most of the combat rules (melee, casts, WS/spell/JA finish, hit reactions). What is missing is the
**entity-state half** (spawn/appear, `animationsub`, death, view-range respawn), a few scheduler
opcodes the mob routines use, the mob-skill (category 11) file-id base, and removing the worm-specific
`BurrowPhase` FSM once the generic path plays the worm correctly. Result: worms, hares, crabs, wyverns
and everything else animate from their DAT, no mob scripting.

---

## 2. The retail model to implement (validated facts, with finding ids)

**Where names live.** Model DAT chunk types: `0x07` scheduler routine, `0x2B` motion clip, `0x3D`
sound sample, `0x20` skeleton, `0x2A` mesh, `0x45` Info (`cib` bytes), `0x05` generators where present
(F54). Scheduler body = stage stream; per stage `op u8, len u8 & 0x1F dwords, delay u16 @+4, dur u16 @+6`;
delay accumulates, 60 ticks/s (F46, F57). Every model ships the standard set above (F54/F55).

**Resolution order** (SE `SetAction`, xim `findResource`; F56/F58): routine's own directory → model
DAT root → the target's DAT for 0x09 target calls → ROM/0/0.DAT (`syst`, the global effect dir) →
not found = **do nothing, warn once**. `hwat aloc mloc rloc wash waso proc dcnt hw??` exist in no
DAT anywhere; they are dead references. Do not implement built-ins.

**Rules, wire input → routine name:**

| Input | Routine(s) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| actor first appears, or reappears after status 3 / view-range despawn (no actor yet) | `init` (`ini0` if the DAT has one); `pop0`/`spop`/`pop1` per the existing PopEffect/spawn flags | F11, F35, F39, F53 |
| 0x0E `animationsub` changed on a live actor | `[init, ini1, ini2, ini3][sub & 3]`, index with the **raw 3-bit** value; the mod-4 wrap is what absorbs the spawn flag 0x04 | F37, F47 |
| 0x0E status 3 | drop the actor (kuluu keeps a hidden stand-in; treat as "actor gone" so the next visible status re-runs `init`) | F11 |
| 0x0E status 2 | despawn | F49 |
| 0x0E animation byte engage / disengage | `in<n>` / `out<n>`, n = weapon anim subtype digit from the Info chunk (`GetBattleInSchResId` = `'in ' + '0'+cib[4]`) | F56 |
| death (HP 0 / anim 3) | `dead`, fallback `dea<appearanceState>`; `corp` holds the corpse | F49, F58 |
| 0x28 cat 1 actor | `atk0` non-blocking (voice) + swing: random `ati0..N` standing, `atf0/atl0/atr0/atb0` moving fwd/left/right/back; off-hand `bti0`.., kicks `cti0/dti0` | F50, F58 |
| 0x28 cat 7/8/9/10/12 | play `cmd_arg` as the name (`cate`, `cawh`, `calg`...) on the caster; it is a FourCC (LSB `enums/four_cc.h`) | F51, F56 |
| 0x28 cat 3/4/6 | effect DAT by file id (already implemented) | existing |
| 0x28 cat 11 (mob skill) / 13 (pet) | effect DAT: file id = `anim + 0x0F3C` (anim < 0x200), `+ 0xC1EF` (< 0x600), `+ 0xE739` (< 0x800), else `+ 0x14B07`; run its `main` (xim `MobAbilityTable.kt`) | F58 |
| 0x28 per target result | resolution 0 Hit → damage reaction (existing `dam0` switch), 1 Miss → nothing, 2 Guard → `gurd`, 3 Parry → `pary`, 4 Block → `shld`; knockback > 0 → `sway`; info bit Defeated → death follows on 0x0E | F58, LSB `enums/action/*.h` |
| routine completes | `hen0` if present (one-shot) | F37 |
| mid-routine `animationsub` → 0 | ignored, never cancels | F42, F48 |

**Locks.** Op `0x07` and `0x59` are AnimationLock with `dur` ticks; the lock is a **refcount**
(ActionTimer1 reached 2 and 3 on retail when a hit reaction overlapped a swing), and a routine
without a lock stage does not lock (`cate`, `atk0`) (F49, F55, F57). Retail measured: hare swing 50
ticks, damage reaction 28 to 30, worm dig 112, pop 188.

**Op corrections vs current kuluu parser** (F57, SE names from the PS2 decompile): `0x5F` =
StopRoutine(name) (dig's `ini1` stops `init`, pop stops `ini1`); `0x21/0x25` = flinch source/target
(direction picks dfi/dbi/dfm/dbm clips); `0x5E` = knockback; `0x78` = display dead; `0x28` =
transition to idle; `0x29/0x2A` = actor colour fade (RGBA payload); `0x1F/0x20` = LockActorStatus;
`0x24` = suspend parent on result; `0x2F` = facing lock; `0x32` = broadcast off; `0x3D/0x50/0x3E` =
random-child group (already parsed).

**0x28 result bit layout** (LSB `packets/s2c/0x028_battle2.cpp`): header `actor u32, trg_sum 6,
res_sum 4, cmd_no 4, cmd_arg 32, info 32`; per result `resolution 3, kind 2, animation 12, info 5,
hitDistortion 2, knockback 3, param 17, message 10, modifier 31`, then proc `6/4/17/10` and spikes
`6/4/14/10` behind 1-bit flags. Check `ffxi-proto::melee` against this; wormwatch's old 5-bit
"reaction" was `resolution | kind << 3`.

---

## 4. Patches, in order. One commit per numbered item unless noted.

### Patch 1: `ffxi-dat` scheduler opcodes (domain truth crate, cite F57 + xim)

File `ffxi-dat/src/scheduler.rs`.

Add to `StageKind`:
```rust
    /// 0x07 / 0x59 - AnimationLock for `duration_frames` ticks (SE: `BondageActor` /
    /// `LockCasterMagic`; xim treats both as AnimationLockEffect). Retail's ActionTimer1 lock;
    /// refcounted across overlapping routines (F49, F55, F57).
    AnimationLock,
    /// 0x5F - StopRoutine: stop the running routine named by `id` (xim EffectRoutineParser.kt:400).
    /// The worm's `ini1` stops `init` and `init` stops `ini1` this way (F46, F57).
    StopRoutine,
    /// 0x21 (source) / 0x25 (target) - flinch; SE `GetDamageDirId` picks the dfi/dbi/dfm/dbm
    /// front/back clip by hit direction (F57).
    FlinchOnCaster,
    FlinchOnTarget,
    /// 0x5E - knockback (SE tag table, F57).
    Knockback,
    /// 0x78 - DisplayDeadRoutine (xim EffectRoutineParser.kt:466): the actor is dead from here on.
    DisplayDead,
    /// 0x28 - TransitionToIdle (xim :205), f32 transition time in the payload.
    TransitionToIdle,
    /// 0x29 (source) / 0x2A (target) - ActorFade to the RGBA at +8 over `duration_frames`
    /// (SE `ActorColorDriveTask`; 0x80808080 is the neutral tint the worm's `init` uses).
    ActorFadeOnCaster,
    ActorFadeOnTarget,
```
Add the arms to `StageKind::from_stage`: `0x07 | 0x59 => AnimationLock`, `0x5F => StopRoutine`,
`0x21 => FlinchOnCaster`, `0x25 => FlinchOnTarget`, `0x5E => Knockback`, `0x78 => DisplayDead`,
`0x28 => TransitionToIdle`, `0x29 => ActorFadeOnCaster`, `0x2A => ActorFadeOnTarget`. Keep
`raw_type`. For the fade kinds read the RGBA the way `ScreenColorDrive` reads its colour (id is
the payload, so set `id = NO_STAGE_ID` and add `actor_fade: Option<[u8; 4]>` or reuse `screen_color`
with a comment; pick whichever keeps `SchedulerStage` Copy).

Tests: extend the existing scheduler tests with a synthetic body containing `0x0307 dur 0x70`,
`0x045F 'init'`, `0x0429 0x80808080` and assert kinds + durations. Real fixtures: the worm dig
record bytes are in `Other_part3.md §G.1` (Shane can paste them), or any mob DAT's `dead` routine
(`ded?` motion + `0x78`).

### Patch 2: mob skill / pet skill effect DAT file ids

File `ffxi-vocab/src/action_anim.rs`: add
```rust
/// research/xim MobAbilityTable.kt getFileTableOffset - a mob skill's `animation` id (LSB
/// mob_skills.animation, carried per result in s2c 0x028 category 11) is an FTABLE index with a
/// range-dependent base. The DAT at that index holds the skill's `main` routine, whose 0x05 stage
/// names the caster's own `sp??` clip (F51, F58).
pub fn mob_skill_file_id(animation: u16) -> u32 {
    let a = animation as u32;
    a + if a < 0x200 { 0x0F3C } else if a < 0x600 { 0xC1EF } else if a < 0x800 { 0xE739 } else { 0x14B07 }
}
```
File `kuluu-render/src/scheduler_runtime.rs` `action_dat_file_id`: add
`11 | 13 => Some(ffxi_vocab::action_anim::mob_skill_file_id(animation?))`. Check that
`dispatch_action_started` does not filter category 11/13 out before reaching it, and that the
`main` routine of that DAT is what gets run with caster = the mob and target = the packet target.
Test: Foot Kick (mob skill 259, animation 3) → file id 0xF3F.

### Patch 3: refcounted animation lock, multiple concurrent routines

`ActiveScheduler` is one component per entity, so a hit reaction landing during a swing currently
replaces or is dropped. Retail runs both (ActionTimer1 counted 2 and 3, F49/F52).

- Change the runtime so an entity can hold several running routines: either a
  `Vec<ActiveScheduler>` inside one component (`ActiveSchedulers`) or child entities per routine.
  Prefer the Vec: `tick_active_schedulers` iterates the vec, removes finished entries after the TTL,
  and removes the component when empty. Update every `Query<&mut ActiveScheduler>` /
  `from_routine` call site accordingly (grep `ActiveScheduler`).
- Add `AnimationLock { count: u16, until_tick: Vec<u32> }` (or a simple per-routine
  `lock_until` inside each running routine) and expose `fn is_animation_locked(&self) -> bool`
  = any routine's lock interval covers the current tick. The AnimationLock stage sets the interval
  `[stage.frame, stage.frame + duration_frames)`. A routine with no lock stage never locks.
- Handle `StopRoutine`: remove the running routine with that name from the same entity.
- The pose pass (`selected_animation` in `ffxi_actor_render.rs`) must not override a motion while
  `is_animation_locked()` is true; while locked the routine's `Motion` stage owns the clip. This is
  what lets `burrow_holding` go away in patch 5.

### Patch 4: entity-state routines (the generic driver)

New module `kuluu-render/src/entity_routines.rs` (product machinery), fed from the snapshot diff
where the burrow FSM runs today (`ffxi_actor_render.rs` ~2880 to 2930). Pure decision function in

`ffxi-actor/src/actor_state.rs`, add:
```rust
/// FFXiMain.dll .data @RVA 0x35AF60 (F37): the `animationsub` -> routine table the client indexes
/// with RF1 bits 1-3, i.e. the raw 3-bit wire value. Entries 4..7 repeat 0..3, which is how the
/// server's spawn flag 0x04 is absorbed without masking (F47).
pub const SUB_ROUTINE_TABLE: [&[u8; 4]; 8] =
    [b"init", b"ini1", b"ini2", b"ini3", b"init", b"ini1", b"ini2", b"ini3"];

pub fn sub_routine(animationsub: u8) -> [u8; 4] { *SUB_ROUTINE_TABLE[(animationsub & 7) as usize] }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct EntityAnimObserved { pub status: u8, pub animationsub: u8, pub animation: u8, pub hp_zero: bool, pub has_actor: bool }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntityRoutineEvent { Init, Sub(u8), Dead, Engage, Disengage, DropActor, Despawn }

/// Retail's per-entity update (F11, F36-F42, F49, F53): compare last frame's observed state with
/// this frame's and emit the routine events the client would dispatch, in retail order.
pub fn entity_routine_events(prev: EntityAnimObserved, now: EntityAnimObserved) -> Vec<EntityRoutineEvent>
```
Semantics of `entity_routine_events`:
- `now.status == 2` → `Despawn`.
- `now.status == 3` and `prev.has_actor` → `DropActor` (kuluu keeps the hidden stand-in but marks
  `has_actor = false`).
- `now.status != 3 && !prev.has_actor` (first sight, or back from 3, or back in view range) → `Init`.
  The create path also resets the client's stored sub to 0, so **do not** emit `Sub` for whatever
  `animationsub` the appear packet carries (F39/F47: the worm pops up with sub 5 in the packet and
  the routine that runs is `init`, not `ini1`).
- `now.animationsub != prev.animationsub` on a live actor and `(now.animationsub & 7) != 0` →
  `Sub(now.animationsub)`. A change **to** 0 emits nothing (F42/F48).
- `now.hp_zero && !prev.hp_zero` (or animation byte 3) → `Dead`.
- animation byte 0 ↔ 1 → `Disengage` / `Engage` (feeds the existing `EngageMachine`; only emit if
  that machine does not already derive it, avoid double `in 0`).

Bevy side (`entity_routines.rs`):
- keep `HashMap<u32, EntityAnimObserved>` as a `Local`/`Resource` (replaces `burrow_mem`).
- for each event, resolve and enqueue a **full** routine (motion included, not effects-only)
  on the entity via the patch-3 runtime: `Init` → `init` (try `ini0` first when the DAT has one,
  F29), `Sub(s)` → `sub_routine(s)`, `Dead` → `dead` then fallback `dea<state>`, `Engage`/`Disengage`
  → `in<n>`/`out<n>` where n comes from the Info chunk byte (for mobs read chunk 0x45 +0x24, until
  then `'0'`). Missing name → `tracing::debug!` once per (model, name), no error.
- `RoutineLookup` order must be routine dir → model root → target DAT (0x09) → `GlobalEffectDir`.
  Verify `RoutineLookup::get` does exactly that; fix if the global dir is consulted first.

### Patch 7: decode and use the result fields kuluu currently throws away (crits, knockback, kills)

Checked 2026-09-09 against the tree: `kuluu-session/src/session/mod.rs` (~5030) reads the per-result
bits and discards `_info` (5), `_scale` (5 = hitDistortion 2 + knockback 3), `_kind` (2), `_modifier`
(31); `kuluu_snapshot::ViewerEvent::ActionStarted` carries only `result: Option<(resolution, animation)>`
for category 1. Consequences today: a critical hit looks exactly like a normal hit, knockback never
plays `sway`, and the killing blow is not distinguishable from a hit until the next 0x0E.

- Session: keep `info`, `hit_distortion` (2 bits), `knockback` (3 bits), `kind` per result; extend
  `ActionStarted` (bump the snapshot version the way v9/v12 did) with
  `info: u8, hit_distortion: u8, knockback: u8` for the first result, and ideally a
  `Vec<ResultSummary>` per target for AoE.
- Render (`hit_reaction_routine` and its caller `dispatch_damage_callback_stages` /
  `dispatch_melee_action_started`): resolution Hit → `ldam` when hit_distortion == 3 (Heavy, the
  crit case; `ldam` = 0x09 `lhit` + `sdam` + `vdam`), `sdam` when 0 or 1 and the model ships it,
  `damg` otherwise (F54; xim leaves the damh/damg var 0x3B unhandled, so `damg` stays the default);
  knockback > 0 → also `sway` (F52's swy1..3 voice + the 0x5E stage); info bit 1 (Defeated) → let
  the death path start immediately instead of waiting for the 0x0E anim=3 (retail: StatusServer
  flips on the same frame as the HP packet, F49).
- HUD: info bit 2 (CriticalHit) drives the damage number style / "Critical hit!" line
  (`msg 67`); this is `kuluu-render/src/hud`, not the animation driver, but the field has to
  exist first.
- `ffxi_actor_render::action_routine`: category 7 currently maps to `ati0` (an attack swing).
  Retail plays the packet's FourCC, `cate` (F51/F56; LSB `FourCC::SkillUse`). Make categories
  7/9/10/12 use `cmd_arg` the way category 8 already does (`magic_start_routine` reads it; the
  same "ca??" / "sp??" prefix logic generalises: `cate/cait/calg` start, `spte/spit/splg` interrupt),
  and keep the hard-coded fallbacks only for a missing/unknown FourCC.

What is already right and should be left alone: spell casting. Category 8 reads `cmd_arg`
(`cawh/cabk/...`), interrupts (`sp??`) drop the cast pose, the fallback uses the spell table's
magic type, and category 4 runs the spell's effect DAT `main` with the `mdam` damage callback
driving the target reaction.

Evidence log: artifacts/verify/motion_west_saruta.log (~3 min, 11 mobs, West Sarutabaruta zone 115).

Measured: median server-update spacing while moving = 0.4s (gaps up to ~77s between movement bursts); all 42 snaps caused by stale-dt alone (dt_srv > DT_SERVER_CEIL=1.0), zero by jump distance (median snap-time jump ~0.3-0.6 yalms); moving-toggle rate up to ~16/min per mob (~50/min aggregate; one entity flapped 32x in ~2 min, speed oscillating 0.34<->3.87 across both hysteresis thresholds and WALK_RUN_BOUNDARY=3.0); 11 heading-mismatch events (diffs 85-97 deg). Packet speed byte stable at 40 (=4 yps retail decode) while differentiated velocity ~2.2-2.5 and 0 during gaps.

Root cause (single): snap/stale-velocity tuning vs LSB's actual roaming cadence: (1) burst-resume updates hit DT_SERVER_CEIL -> full snap + vel-zero on tiny corrections = "rebound before starting"; (2) stale dr_velocity extrapolates up to ~0.6s past the true stop, then CORRECT_TAU pulls back = "rebound after stopping"; (3) snap-zeroed velocity makes smoothed speed flap the gait hysteresis -> idle/walk/run stutter = "frozen, no animation".

Proposal (user decides; nothing wired yet): replace raw staleness snap with a speed-aware test (snap only when the jump exceeds what the entity could cover at its known packet speed during the gap; keep SNAP_DIST_SQ as absolute teleport floor); shorten/cap stale-velocity extrapolation; feed gait selection from the 0x0E speed byte while updates are fresh (work order: LSB speed 40 = run, mob roaming uses half speed = walk - need a rule before wiring); consider faster heading turn or velocity-directed facing while moving.
